items.statement: Management targets double-digit consolidated revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: we had taken a target of a double-digit growth in the current year, and we maintain that we will have a double-digit growth in the current year revenue.

items.statement: Management expects margins to be better than last year and accretive to top-line growth for the full year
items.quote: we are confident that our margins are better than last year and should be accretive to our top line growth also for the full year.

items.statement: Greenfield expansion in Tamil Nadu will consume INR400-500 crores globally
items.quote: We're anyway coming with greenfields of Tamil Nadu. In T amil Nadu, which will consume ca sh. So, another INR400- INR500 crores goes in cash globally

items.statement: Management is actively talking to 2-3 D2C companies for potential acquisition
items.quote: we're talking to 2 or 3 companies.

items.statement: Operating margin grew 11% and PAT increased 15% in Q1 FY27, both ahead of top-line growth
items.quote: margin grew by 11% and profit after tax increased by 15%, both ahead of the top line

items.statement: Hair oil growth split 50% volume (8%) and 50% price due to LLP/crude-linked inflation
items.quote: it is coming out of GST price -- GST-driven price increase and inflationary price incre ases. And there is an 8% volume growth, which is backing this growth of around 18% in overall hair oil

items.statement: Brands have strength to pass on inflation via price increases, but Middle East war impact on crude-linked inflation is being watched
items.quote: we feel that our brands have got strength to pass on this inflation in ter ms of price increases to the co nsumer. But we are vigilantly, watchfully watching this whole Middle Eastern war situation to see that inflation steps are taken to mitigate the inflation

items.statement: Rural demand grew ~550 bps ahead of urban in Q1 FY27; monsoon deficit now only 14-15% supporting Kharif season
items.quote: rural is growing ahead of urban at 170 basis points for the Nielsen as a categor y and also for us as far as our business is concerned, we have a rural growth of around 550 basis points, which is ahead of the urban growth

items.statement: Premiumization driving strong results: active juices +40%, coconut water +70%, gaining 600 bps and 344 bps market share respectively
items.quote: Our premiumization strategy continued to deliver strong result s with active juices growing by over 40% and coconut water registering a growth of over 70% dur ing the quarter. We continue to outperform the category, gaining around 600 bps market share in active juices and 344 bps in coconut

items.statement: Siens nutraceutical brand grew 3x in Q1 FY27, targeting ~INR50 crores ARR exit run-rate
items.quote: we will see an exit of roughly around INR50-odd crores of ARR that we will have at the end of the year with Siens.

items.statement: Badshah business expanded from 2 states to MP, Rajasthan, Delhi NCR; e-commerce/quick commerce now 6% of turnover growing triple-digit
items.quote: We've expanded beyond Gujarat and Maharashtra to MP, Rajasthan and now to Delhi NCR. So that's significantly picked up, and there's a good traction that we are seeing despite tast e being a little disparate in these

items.statement: Geopolitical developments in Middle East warrant close monitoring; war continuation creates wait-and-watch situation for inflation and profitable growth
items.quote: If the war ends tomorrow, then I think the petroleum prices will come down, and therefore crude-linked inflation will come down, and we'll be very confident on delivering a double-digit profitable growth in line with top line. If the war continues, then it's a wait and watch situation...

items.statement: Capital allocation: ~INR9,000 crores net cash (INR6,500 crores in India); 100% of India profits paid as dividend; M&A for mid/large scale or D2C foot-in-door
items.quote: We are approximately sitting with almost INR9,000 crores net de bt, and out of that, roughly INR6,500 crores is in India. The re would be three, four capital allocation strategy. First, obviously, being acquisition. Acquisition will be either a mid to large scale company or a foot in door into D2C

items.statement: Double-digit volume growth expected for next 9 months of FY27
items.quote: But this year, with a lot of confidence, we are saying next 9 months, we'll have a double -digit growth. Double -digit volume growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 18% to 19% for full year FY27
items.quote: So we are looking at an EBITDA margin about 18% to 19% for the entire year.

items.statement: Targeting INR 1,000 crores plus EBITDA for FY27
items.quote: We are looking at INR1,000 crores plus EBITDA overall.

items.statement: Capex plan of roughly INR 400 crores for FY27 including maintenance
items.quote: This year, we are looking at a capex of roughly INR400 crores because part of the capex which we are doing in 2 plants partly will come here, partly will come next year.

items.statement: Srikalahasti expansion of 10 million sqm at INR 210 crores and Gailpur expansion of 11 million sqm at INR 165 crores
items.quote: First is the Srikalahasti expansion in South at a cost of INR210 crores, which we announced in the last Board meeting. And second is the expansion at Bhiwadi factory in Rajasthan at a cost of INR165 crores

items.statement: Major breakthrough with two very big builders for lion's share of projects
items.quote: I will not -- just to give you the information that we have just had a major breakthrough with two of the very, very big builders of India, where we are getting a lion's share.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 19.60% vs 16.72% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 19.60%.

items.statement: Price hikes of 10-11% in North and South plants, 40-45% in Morbi plants due to gas cost differential
items.quote: In North and South from our plants, which we are manufacturing, we have raised prices by anywhere between 10% to 11%.

items.statement: Price gap between Kajaria and Morbi narrowed from 40% to below 20%
items.quote: Again earlier, as was said, the price differential between Kajaria and Morbi was 40%, which has come below 20% as of now.

items.statement: Demand recovery in May, June, July after soft April due to Morbi shutdown, pre-buying, labor shortage
items.quote: Already in the month of May and June things have started positively, and so is in the month of July, which is just about to close. So demand at the local -- at the normal level in the domestic market is very, very -- looking very optimistic.

items.statement: Bathware revenue grew 33% to INR 122 crores; Adhesives revenue grew to INR 45 crores from INR 25 crores
items.quote: Bathware segment registered a 33% growth in revenue, reaching INR 122 crores in Quarter 1, F '27 compared to INR 91 crores in Quarter 1, F '26. Revenue from Adhesives grew to INR45 crores in Quarter 1, F '27 as compared to INR25 crores in Quarter 1, F '26.

items.statement: Bathware targeting 35-40% value growth for FY27 with mix of price and volume
items.quote: But looking for this entire year, we are definitely looking at about 35% to 40% value growth, which will be a combination of both price increase and volume growth.

items.statement: Gas prices volatile due to war; Morbi gas prices went from INR 48 to INR 86-88 per SCM
items.quote: What has happened in Morbi, the gas prices went up from literally about INR 48 to INR86 to INR88 per SCM, whereas in North, the price hike was approximately about 10% to 12%?

items.statement: Exports less than 1% of turnover; no focus on export market
items.quote: We are a domestic consumption story. We don't want to go to exports. Our exports are less than 1% of our overall turnover.

items.statement: Outsourcing to increase to ~40% in FY27 due to capacity constraints, then decrease when new plants online
items.quote: So looking at that, we have to do more outsourcing to meet that requirement of sales. That is for this year. Next year, the percentage will go down when the manufacturing facility will come.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved by 5 days to 46 days as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: As of 30th of June '26, the working capital cycle also improved by 5 days to 46 days compared to 51 days on 31st of March '26.

items.statement: Targeting 8% volume growth for FY27
items.quote: And therefore, it gives me a good level of confidence to continue with our estimation and guidance of 8% growth, which we are targeting for this financial year.

items.statement: Targeting total cost of INR 4,250 per ton by end of FY27
items.quote: I again reemphasize all these initiatives are fundamentally reshaping our cost curve and reinforce our confidence in achieving total cost of 4,250 PMT by end of '27.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 is closer to INR 6,500 crores
items.quote: So, capex is overall, say, closer to INR6,500 crores and which is well between the growth and the efficiency capex, but that's like we are working on.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex spend around INR 1,500-1,600 crores (~25% of annual plan)
items.quote: So, I would say that we are well in terms of almost closer to 25%, which is like it's balancing out for me for the year actually. So 25% is there around closer to INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores, which we have invested.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved 331 bps sequentially to 16.7%
items.quote: Revenue of INR9,500 crores, operating EBITDA of INR1,589 crores, EBITDA margin, which has improved 331 basis points to now 16.7% EBITDA per ton of INR931 net cost reduced by INR206 per metric ton sequentially, PAT of INR660 crores and net worth of almost INR72,000 crores.

items.statement: Gray cement EBITDA per ton is INR 911 for Q1 FY27
items.quote: My EBITDA per ton for the gray cement is INR911 per ton. Yes, that's the number I have. Basically RMX and gray cement. So like gray cement is INR911.

items.statement: Net operating cost reduced to INR 4,241 per ton in Q1 FY27, down INR 206 sequentially
items.quote: Net operating cost reduced to INR4,241 per metric ton, a reduction of INR 206 PMT from the previous quarter. Thus, it puts us firmly in terms of our guidance to achieve INR 4,250 per ton for this financial year.

items.statement: Expect additional savings of INR 130-150 per ton from structural initiatives in FY27
items.quote: In all, these initiatives are expected to deliver savings of almost INR130 to INR150 per ton, providing a strong visibility towards our cost leadership target and enhancing long-term competitiveness.

items.statement: Trade sales share improved to 78% from 74% sequentially; premium products 34% of trade sales
items.quote: Trade sales share has actually improved from 74% to now 78% of our overall sales. Our premium strategy continues to gain traction with premium products comprising 34% of our trade sales.

items.statement: Blended cement share increased to 85%
items.quote: During the quarter, our clinker factor improved by approximately 3% to now 64%, while share of blended cement increased 85%, improving both profitability and sustainability.

items.statement: July trade volumes up 8% YoY; seeing good momentum in North, West, Central, East
items.quote: As we speak in the month of July, and I would not shy highlighting that we are already seeing an 8% improvement on the trade volumes.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia could increase costs by ~INR 100 per ton; mitigated by inventory and cost initiatives
items.quote: But I mentioned to you, I'm holding an inventory of clinker of almost a month, and I'm holding the coal inventory of almost 3 months. So I'm very well mitigated from that perspective. And on top of it, the initiatives to bring down the cost by INR100 to INR150, which will be a good mitigation to absorb any kind of surprises from any external factors.

items.statement: RE power capacity at 973 MW, targeting 1,122 MW by FY28; WHRS at 228 MW, targeting 376 MW
items.quote: Our RE power capacity is now at 973 megawatts, up almost 500 megawatts over past 1 year. WHRS capacity stands at 228 megawatts, and this has helped us to reduce our unit of power cost from INR5.9 per kWH to almost INR4.9.

items.statement: AFR/TSR target 12-15% for FY27, up from current ~7%
items.quote: So immediately, right now, for example, in this fiscal year, we are targeting to hit almost 12% to 15%.

items.statement: First coal block operational in ~30 months; 3 coal blocks in focus
items.quote: The first one will be operationalized in, say, 2, 2.5 years' time. And just to circle back on the AFR, I think needful investments have already been made. Therefore, the confidence to hit, say, 15% is hig h. Yes. So coal block, the first one gets operationalized in, say, about 30 months from now

items.statement: Installed capacity to reach 119 million tons by end of FY27 with 10.2 million tons addition
items.quote: These projects will increase our installed capacity to 119 million tons by end of this financial year, and it will also help us to improve on our efficiency and overall costs.

items.statement: Cost per ton guidance for FY27 is INR 4,250; target to reduce cost by another INR 250 by end of FY28 to reach INR 4,000 or below.
items.quote: And with a high element of confidence, we are giving a guidance for INR4 to INR5 a ton for the FY27, number one. And the way we have worked upon is the next year also, we want to bring another INR250 reduction in the cost so that by end of FY28, we reach up to INR4,000 or below in terms of cost per metric ton.

items.statement: Capex run rate of INR 6,000-7,000 crores per year expected for FY28.
items.quote: Yes. Yes. On a run rate, yes.

items.statement: Maratha clinker unit (4 mt) commissioning expected in Q1 FY28; Jodhpur clinker (3 mt) trials started, stabilizing in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Maratha, we are expecting to commission next year. And that is what, for example, we have planned. So far as Jodhpur is concerned, we already have seen trials started. And in Q2, which is in this current quarter, it will start stabilizing and supplying to my grinding units.

items.statement: Mundra clinker project expected in 18-24 months (around 2029).
items.quote: Mundra is expected about, say, 18 to 24 months from here. So 2029 basically.

items.statement: Fly ash sales ~INR 15 crores in Q1 FY27 vs ~INR 50 crores in Q4 FY26; RE power sales 45 crore units in Q1 FY27 vs 24 crore units in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: Rahul, it is ~INR15 crores for the first quarter, and you are right, around INR50 crores for the last quarter.

items.statement: Cost reduced QoQ by INR 206/ton to INR 4,241; INR 45 crore RE power sales and fly ash sales netted off in cost.
items.quote: Yes, it is netted off. It is very much part and parcel of my overall, say, opex only. This is netted off.

items.statement: Green power cost ~INR 3.3/unit vs grid power INR 7-8/unit; 50% of 45 crore units to be consumed in Q2, rest sold; long-term fly ash agreement in place, 30% consumed internally.
items.quote: See, my blend of power, if I look at the overall, say, grid power, that comes almost at, say, INR7 to INR8 a unit. And that is the first opportunity for us to basically replace with this green power. And hence, you know the math, for example. So I think I mentioned in my previous question also, I mentioned that it is always beneficial for me to consume the power first and only for any reason, surp

items.statement: Targeting 8-10% volume growth in FY27 driven by trade segment; 75%+ sales mix to be trade.
items.quote: When I'm adding 10% almost 10 million capacity, say, every year. So from a capacity addition perspective, we are growing almost say, 8% to 10%. And that is what, for example, we would be targeting to grow in terms of our growth plan on the trade side, especially.

items.statement: Curtailed ~1 mt low/negative EBITDA volumes in South; focus on shifting to trade segment; South trade sales now picking up.
items.quote: So we actually curtailed the low and negative EBITDA volumes, and this is almost like closer to 1 million, for example, which was which we actually reduced.

items.statement: Maintenance cost accounting under review with auditors; currently reporting actuals, not amortized over 4 quarters.
items.quote: I think we are still engaging with our auditors on this point because from the accounting standard perspective, they are deliberating on this point that how we basically equalize over the four quarters. Until that time happens, we have continued with the reporting on the actual basis on the O&M cost.

items.statement: RE power transition: 1 GW capacity (700 MW Khavda, 300 MW Rajasthan); target 100% in-house consumption in 3 quarters, ~10-15% surplus sold.
items.quote: The ultimate goal is to consume everything in-house. It is a transition phase because we have as we as a lot of our systems come online. So, for example, in RE, a lot of a few of our plants, we need to connect to the central grid. So they don't have the connectivity to the central grid, which programs are under execution.

items.statement: WHRS capacity to increase from 228 MW to 376 MW by FY28 across existing and new kiln lines (Assam, Mundra, Maratha, Penna, Jodhpur, Bhatapara, Sanghi, Penna).
items.quote: So it's a combination of both the existing kiln lines and the new kiln lines basically. So in terms of the clinker new capacities coming up, say, Assam, we have announced and then Mundra, for example, then Maratha is expanding and so is the Penna, Jodhpur, which has come up now. Then Bhatapara, we have already expanded, for example.

items.statement: Orient Cement acquisition justified via MSA benefits; standalone numbers misleading due to inter-company arrangements.
items.quote: No, Rajesh, I think you are looking at the stand-alone numbers of Orient and then giving this remarks, I think always there's an element of MSA between Orient and Ambuja. Therefore, when I look at in totality, Orient assets are delivering us decent margins and justifies the valuation.

items.quote: And therefore, it gives me a good level of confidence to continue with our estimation and guidance of 8% growth, which we are targeting for this financial year.

items.quote: Thus, it puts us firmly in terms of our guidance to achieve INR 4,250 per ton for this financial year.

items.quote: We remain well positioned to outperform industry growth, expanding installed capacity to 119 million tons with the addition of 10.2 million tons, which I mentioned before.

items.quote: My EBITDA per ton for the gray cement is INR911 per ton. Yes, that's the number I have. Basically RMX and gray cement. So like gray cement is INR911.

items.quote: WHRS capacity stands at 228 megawatts, and this has helped us to reduce our unit of power cost from INR5.9 per kWH to almost INR4.9. So by INR1, actually, it has come down with these improvements.

items.statement: Seeing good demand traction in North, West, Central and East regions
items.quote: So for me, the key market remains, Manish, North, West, Central and East. All of them, for example, we are seeing a good traction. And that's how with confidence I mentioned to Navin also in terms of our estimates of guidance on the volume growth.

items.quote: Trade sales share has actually improved from 74% to now 78% of our overall sales.

items.statement: Target utilization 70-75% on expanded 119 mt base; next capex leg triggered at this value-focused utilization level.
items.quote: I think our targeted utilization now that our focus on value and all in that background, I'm saying around 70% to 75%. And this is like all value-focused capacity utilization, point number one.

items.statement: Maintenance cost accounting under review with auditors for quarterly equalization; currently reported on actual basis.
items.quote: I think we are still engaging with our auditors on this point because from the accounting standard perspective, they are deliberating on this point that how we basically equalize over the four quarters. Until that time happens, we have continued with the reporting on the actual basis on the O&M cost.

items.statement: Annualized capex will be around the depreciation number, aiming not to exceed it and be below it for FY27
items.quote: Our annualized capex will be around the depreciation number. We will try not to exceed it, in fact be below that.

items.statement: Salt plant in India 82.5 KTPA operational by year-end, supplying market by Q1 next financial year
items.quote: The salt plant in India 82.5 KTPA, that should get operational by this year-end. So, you should start it supplying to market by first quarter of next financial year.

items.statement: 210 KTPA Salt plant in South India and 50 KTPA silica plant have 24-month execution timeline, operational during 2028
items.quote: The 210 KTPA Salt plant in South India, has a 24-month execution time. Similar is the execution timeline for 50 KTPA silica plant. So, they will become operational sometime during 2028.

items.statement: Sustainable India EBITDA margin around 18%, with gross contribution margin of 32% to 33%
items.quote: In terms of sustainable margin it would be around 18% which you referred to. ~32% to 33% GC margin.

items.statement: India soda ash spot price increased by INR 2,000 per tonne; contracts reviewed quarterly
items.quote: India has taken a price increase of about INR 2,000 per ton ne, which is spot price, but the contracts are quarterly as you know, and they get reviewed with the customers

items.statement: Chinese soda ash export prices at USD 160-180 FOB, translating to USD 170-190 CIF in Southeast Asia; pricing expected to remain subdued
items.quote: Chinese soda ash export prices are in the range of USD 160 to 180 FOB, translating to USD 170 to 190 CIF in Southeast Asia, which is where the most, which remains the most challenging markets for us.

items.statement: Living Essentials (salt, bicarbonate, FOS) stable demand growing with premiumization; prebiotics expected to grow faster on health and wellness
items.quote: In Living essential, mainly the food, feed, pharma, the core products which are salt, bicarbonate, and FOS, they continue to have a stable demand continuing to grow with supported by premiumization in this segment.

items.statement: Industrial Essentials (soda ash) near-term outlook challenging due to global oversupply from China and elevated raw material and freight costs from Middle East tensions
items.quote: Industrial essentials, which is mainly soda ash, the near -term outlook, unlike the previous one, is challenging due to global oversupply, especially coming out of China, and also eleva ted raw material and freight costs which are caused by the geopolitical tensions in Middle East

items.statement: India farm sector outlook moderately positive supported by improved irrigation; monsoon variability and El Niño conditions monitored
items.quote: In terms of Farm essential, Indian farm sector outlook remains moderately positive, supported by improved irrigation technology supplies.

items.statement: Key cost risks: Kenya HFO prices hedged until October, India limestone imports from Middle East if war drags beyond October, energy logistics costs in India and US
items.quote: Clearly watch out for Kenya HFO, India limestone beyond October, and energy cost increases in India mainly driven by logistics cost and the cost increase in US driven by again logistics cost.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR 5,692 crores QoQ and INR 300 crores vs March due to land sale and share sales; further non-core land monetization planned in H2
items.quote: We have sold some land in Q1 and we sold some of the shares we were holding, and that contributed to the debt coming down in Q1.

items.statement: Strategic focus shifting capex towards Living Essentials and Farm Essentials; Industrial Essentials focus on silica to de-commoditize portfolio
items.quote: We will be sort of focusing our capex more towards what you explained, that we drive growth in food, feed, and pharma and also specific segments within the industrial essentials and try to de-commoditize our portfolio as much as we can.

items.statement: Sodium-ion battery pilot testing underway for stationary storage applications; piloting to finish in 6-9 months, full-scale plant two years after
items.quote: We expect the piloting to finish in about 6 to 9 months so that we at least get a clear understanding of what is the customer responsiveness. After that, we'll come back to you.

items.statement: IMACID did not produce in Q1 due to high sulfur prices; operations restarted in current quarter, expected to be profitable for the year
items.quote: IMACID did not produce during the quarter because of high sulfur prices. They have just begun operations during this quarter. So, we'll see how it progresses, but certainly that part of the business is under pressure in terms of margin, but they'll be profitable for the year.

items.statement: UK business had one-offs of GBP 2.4 million (EU ETS loss and prior period adjustments); expected EBITDA positive and PBT breakeven from next quarter
items.quote: UK had fundamentally two big events which were one-offs of adding up to about GBP 2.4 million. One was on the loss on sale of EU ETS. This is likely to come back by October quarter because we go through a cycle.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 volume growth guided at 8-10% band
items.quote: At the current stage, we are looking at the band of 8-10% for the full FY27.

items.statement: PBDIT margin guidance maintained at 18-20% band
items.quote: We are still garnering around the guidance of 18-20% of our PBDIT margins holds.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin was 45.6% in Q1 FY27, down from previous quarter but up YoY
items.quote: If you look at it from a standalone perspective, the overall gross margin trend has also been fairly strong. There was some pressure on gross margin; we were at about 45.6% in the last quarter. However, we are still higher if you look at it on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Weighted average price increase of ~7% taken in Q1 FY27 across April, May, June
items.quote: While we took price increases in April, May and June, the overall weighted average price increase was around 7%.

items.statement: Material inflation was ~25% in Q1 FY27, significantly higher than price increases taken
items.quote: The material inflation was still very high to the extent of about 25%. That is something which is an area we will have to look at going forward, how it impacts us going ahead.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volume growth of ~9% with rural markets outperforming urban markets
items.quote: Overall, we are at about a strong 9% volume growth. The growth has been across the months in this entire quarter.

items.statement: Rural market growth better than urban; B2B growth driven by urban government expenditure
items.quote: Overall, we are seeing good volume growth. We have seen that growth in rural markets has been much better compared to urban markets. This was a trend that we also saw in Q4, and trend continues to strengthen. However, the B2B business continues to be driven by good growth in urban markets.

items.statement: Premiumization drive contributed ~3% positive mix impact in Q1 FY27
items.quote: There is almost about 3% impact, which is coming higher because of the better mix of what we have been able to sell.

items.statement: New products launched in last 3 years contribute 17% of overall revenues
items.quote: New products within the portfolio contribute 17% of our overall revenues. That's a pretty high number in terms of contribution.

items.statement: VAM-VAE manufacturing ecosystem Phase 1 to commence by August 2024
items.quote: The first phase of this initiative will commence by August. We believe this is a very significant area that we will be entering.
