items.statement: Renewable energy projects: 18 MW Gujarat commissioning Q2 FY27, 67 MW Gorakhpur commissioning Q4 FY27
items.quote: Our renewable energy program, 18 megawatt at Gujarat and 67megawatt at Gorakhpur remains on track for commissioning in Q2 and Q4 respectively of the current financial year.

items.statement: Captive iron ore mines in Rajasthan and UP targeting FY28 operationalization
items.quote: Work continues on our captive iron ore blocks in Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, with FY28 remaining our internal target for these to become operational.

items.statement: Ash handling daily volume target of 90,000 tons by Q4 FY27
items.quote: Target is there to close to 90,000.

items.statement: Wind business revenue target of INR 1,700-1,800 crores for FY27
items.quote: Yes, it should be close to 1,700, 1,800.

items.statement: Wind business net margin target of 5-6% for FY27
items.quote: It should be around 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Ash and coal handling EBITDA margin guidance of 15-18% and net margin of 10-12%
items.quote: We always maintain that EBITDA margin will be 15% to 18%, and net margin will be 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Silvassa assembly plant capex of INR 3.5-4 crores with 1 GW capacity potential
items.quote: Currently in Silvassa, it's a leased facility. We are not the total capex done by us is only on the a little bit of repairs and maintenance, which is close to about INR3.5-INR4 crores. It has a capability of about 1 GW of manufacturing capability.

items.statement: Ash handling operating at 42 thermal plants covering 30-35% of India's thermal capacity
items.quote: Currently, we are working in 42 thermal power plant, and penetration is we are working in 30%-35% of the thermal power plant in India today, and there is a lot of potentials for the future opportunities.

items.statement: Diesel supply constraints and logistics disruptions from geopolitical developments in Q1 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, we also witnessed intermittent diesel supply constraints and logistics disruptions arising from ongoing geopolitical developments.

items.statement: Wind turbine localization targeting 85% component localization within 12 months, blades to be manufactured in-house
items.quote: I think 12 months from now, we'll have about 85% of the components localized, so we can see a similar margin 2 years down the line when the localization and the plant capacity increases.

items.statement: Promoter stake increase through market purchases when opportunities arise
items.quote: When opportunity comes, we'll keep acquiring from the market, Miten bhai. As of now, we see when there is an opportunity, we'll keep acquiring the shares from the market.

items.statement: Ash handling realization varies from INR 450-1,200 per ton per km based on distance and volume
items.quote: It is per kilometer per ton. It varies from 450 rupees to 1200 rupees. It is it is purely a distance and the volume.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 ash handling volumes to slow down, Q3 and Q4 to scale up
items.quote: Q2 will be little slow, Q3 and Q4 will be scaling up.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 10%-15%
items.quote: We continue to maintain our FY27 guidance of 10%-15% revenue growth, gross margins in the range of 35% and remain focused on strengthening our long-term growth platform through sustained investment in our registration pipeline.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 18%-20%
items.quote: It will be in the same range of 18% to 20%.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance unchanged at around Rs.500 crores, Q1 was Rs.273 crores due to data compensations
items.quote: we have not revised our CAPEX investment for this year. Just by seeing what has happened in the first quarter. First quarter has been a little unusual. Because we had to spend very heavily on some data comp ensations. But that is not going to repeat in the rest of the year

items.statement: FY27 capex could be Rs.480-550 crores
items.quote: It could be 500, it could be 550 or it could be 480.

items.statement: Region-wise Q1 FY27 gross margins: Europe 44.2%, NAFTA 32.8%, LATAM 16.9%, Rest of World 30.8%
items.quote: In Europe, our gros s margin has been 44.2% and NAFTA, 32.8%, LATAM, 16.9% and rest of the world, 30.8%, total, 36.7

items.statement: Europe volumes softened due to heatwave and distributor destocking; situation now normalized
items.quote: The main reason behind this was the distributors' cutback on the stock largely because of unusual heatwave conditions and swept across parts of Europe this summer.

items.statement: Europe restocking has improved and reached normality
items.quote: It has improved and has reached to normal. In most of the cases, it is reaching the normality.

items.statement: Europe volume recovery expected in next 3 quarters
items.quote: As I have told you, in the first quarter it has not been good. Not because of any human factors. This is the effect of mother nature. So, we cann ot predict. But as the things are predicted, the next 3 months, the 3 quarters will be better than the first quarter

items.statement: Prices have stabilized and are slowly improving after severe beating two years ago
items.quote: Yes, sir. This is a very pertinent question and the answer is the prices are improving. The prices have taken a very severe beating 2 years back and now they got stabilized and they are slowly improving.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 product mix impact -2.1%; Europe margin improvement driven by product mix and some price increase
items.quote: I would say product mix and also to some extent price increase. But mainly because of the product mix.

items.statement: Registration process full of uncertainties; timing and cost unpredictable
items.quote: the process of registration is fu ll of all the uncertainties. can say when will you receive the registration and at what cost. So, it's full of uncertainties, but still our efforts are very much there and very strongly there

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected 18%-20% on annualized basis; Q1 FY27 higher at 26%
items.quote: So, our effective tax rate on annualized basis could be in the range of 18% to 20%, which you will find in the earlier years al so. Because we are having diff erent tax rates applicable to our overseas subsidiaries vis-à-vis our Indian holding company. So, more or less, the rate will be in the range of 18% to 20%. Though the current quarter, there coul d be a higher rate, but this will get normali

items.statement: Depreciation and amortization expected around Rs.370-375 crores for FY27
items.quote: So, on annualized basis, could be around Rs. 370-375 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 started encouragingly with releases like Alpha, Dhamaal 4, Jana Nayagan; positive outlook supported by upcoming slate including Batwara 1947, Toxic, Haiwan, Awarapan 2
items.quote: Q2 FY27 has commenced on an encouraging note with the release of films such as Alpha, Dhamaal 4 and Jana Nayagan. The outlook for the remainder of the quarter remains positive, supported by an exciting slate of upcoming releases, including Batwara 1947, Toxic, Haiwan, Awarapan 2 and others.

items.statement: Healthy content pipeline across languages and improving advertiser sentiment give confidence in advertising growth over coming quarters
items.quote: Looking ahead, a healthy pipeline of releases across languages, coupled with improving advertiser sentiment, gives us confidence in the growth prospects of advertising over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Advertisement revenues grew 33% year-on-year in Q1 FY27 driven by blockbuster momentum and improved advertiser participation
items.quote: The continuing blockbuster performance of Dhurandhar: The Revenge along with performance of select Hindi and regional titles supported improved advertiser participation, contributing to a 33% year -on-year growth in our advertisement revenues.

items.statement: Advertising revenue mix historically 30-40% annual deals, balance tactical; Dhurandhar was an outlier with unusually high tactical spending
items.quote: Over the years, we have seen that around 30 40% of our advertising revenue comes from annual deals or annual advertisers, while the balance is contributed by tactical advertisers or short -term, seasonal spending around specific films or seasons.

items.statement: Maintains Rs 1,000 crore revenue target for FY28 despite Q1 shortfall, refuses to revise guidance downward
items.quote: we would not like to revise the guidance as of right now. we'd like to because if we lower it we are not even then striving for it. So, we would still like to strive for it and hoping that we are still able to make it happen through some measures.

items.statement: Targets 10-12% top-line growth YoY for FY27, confident on domestic but export dependent on global situation
items.quote: Yes, we are hopeful that we will be able to still go there. Yes, we everyday keep our fingers crossed that at least domestic and India numbers we are much more confident and the export numbers, yes, depends on our situation, but we are hoping for the best. But still, we will maintain that kind of top line guidance.

items.statement: Sanand plant FY27 revenue target Rs 40 crore, on track after Q1; expanded from 2 to 3 operating lines
items.quote: So, for the Sanand unit, we have the yearly target of Rs. 40 CRs, which is the minimum we want to do. And looking at the performance which we could achieve in the 1st Quarter, I think we are on track. So, that is possible.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin expanded 317 bps QoQ to 12.51% driven by better price realization, lower RM cost, improved operational efficiency
items.quote: EBITDA margins improved to 12.51%, representing an expansion of 317 basis points quarter-on-quarter. This improvement was primarily driven by better price realization, lower raw material cost and improved operational risk efficiency.

items.statement: Passed on RM cost increases to customers in Q1 for own brand; white-label pass-through lagging due to long-term contracts, expected to complete within FY27
items.quote: whatever cost increase was there, we have been able to pass on this to the customer, and we took this exercise at the beginning of the quarter itself. Right? So, there is no under recovery there.

items.statement: Europe demand recovering after weak H2 FY26; targeting double-digit growth in Europe for FY27 vs FY26, new customer wins in UK, Southern Europe, Germany, Russia
items.quote: I think it's getting better. It was in a pretty bad shape earlier. I think that part is probably gone and we are getting better. There are more orders which are flowing and there's more positivity around the India-EU trade deal.

items.statement: Value-added products now 60-70% of sales; launched EN812 bump caps, FR workwear (EU/US certified), gumboots at Sanand; focus on hazard-based product development
items.quote: So, at this point, I think almost 60% or 70% of what we would be selling is more value added products than the regular products, and the idea is to get into more product development, do more market research, learn from the developed countries, and quickly adapt it.

items.statement: Export orders 60-70% planned/contract, 30% spot; Europe inquiries rising due to India-EU/UK FTA prospects; some customers waiting for FTA implementation to place orders
items.quote: Roughly, I would say 60% or 70% is something which are planned and the rest is something that are based on spot sales.

items.statement: Port congestion delayed raw material procurement and customer deliveries in Q1; US market uncertain due to changing tariff/news; West Asia crisis disrupted international revenues
items.quote: Congestions at major seaports resulted in delays in the procurement of certain critical raw materials as well as the customer deliveries, impacting operational timelines.

items.statement: Domestic revenue Rs 64 crore in Q1, up 10% QoQ, highest ever Q1 domestic revenue; India/export mix approaching 50-50 by FY27 end
items.quote: Further, during the quarter, domestic revenue stood at Rs. 64 crores, registering a growth of 10% quarter-on-quarter and achieving the highest ever 1st Quarter domestic revenue for the company.

items.statement: SMILE reseller program expanded distribution to 1,000+ resellers across India, improving market reach
items.quote: Another key highlight during the quarter was the overwhelming response to our "SMILE" Reseller program, which has helped expand our distribution network to over 1,000 resellers across India, significantly improving our market reach and customer accessibility.

items.statement: Working capital borrowing to remain at same level in FY27; term loans taken for Sanand CAPEX and incentive claims
items.quote: So, in case of working capital, it should be same, because we are still continuing to do some investment, not now in building or land, but into increasing our capacity, so in machinery.

items.statement: No FOREX gain in Q1 margins as exposures are hedged; margin improvement purely operational
items.quote: So, there is no FOREX gain because in our case, mostly we are hedged. So, whatever cost we have we are hedging. So, no FOREX gain there.

items.statement: No plans to acquire European distributors due to cannibalization risk; inorganic focus on developing markets instead
items.quote: Not as of right now, because it's traditionally been a market where our customers are present, and we run the risk of cannibalizing our market if we go and acquire some company and start our own distribution there.

name: S H Kelkar and Company Ltd

items.statement: Expect double-digit revenue growth and improved margins for full year FY27
items.quote: Notwithstanding these quarterly variations, the current business momentum keeps us on track to deliver double-digit revenue growth and improved margins for the full year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 13.4% from 12.6% YoY; expect similar absolute EBITDA if double-digit growth sustains
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA rose 21% to Rs. 89 crore with EBITDA margin improving to 13.4% from 12.6% in the corresponding quarter last year, aided by operating leverage on the higher revenue base.

items.statement: Flavours Q1 revenue Rs. 112 crore includes ~Rs. 15 crore preponed orders; normalized run-rate ~Rs. 95-96 crore/quarter
items.quote: We did Rs. 112 crore revenue for Flavours this quarter and ballpark Rs. 95 crore would be on a normal basis. We expect that 1-odd month or 2 or 3 weeks of preponement of orders by clients given that the lead times and shipping times were not normal.

items.statement: Passed on cost inflation to customers; ~95%+ of clients accepted price corrections; held back supply where negotiations incomplete
items.quote: We have corrected the pricing to our customers based on the cost inflation that we have ourselves received as a result of the geopolitical effect. We have passed it on. I think almost 95% plus of the clients, we were able to get reasonable price corrections.

items.statement: Flavours demand strong with repeat orders and new product adoption; Fragrance India soft due to high base and low-margin exit; Europe/US traction building
items.quote: We continue to see the growth. So, at the moment, we are quite bullish on how the flavour business is evolving. Quarter 1 is, I would say, very strong. We may not see the same sort of momentum in the remaining quarters, but it is doing exceedingly well.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility in West Asia keeps energy, freight and trade uncertainty high; macro disruptions could affect pipeline and growth
items.quote: Geopolitical developments in West Asia have kept energy, freight and generally trade volatility remains high. At this time, the fundamental demand drivers of our industry in the consumers' preferences of fragrance and taste across personal care, home care and food categories have remained intact and continued to grow,

items.statement: Net debt rose Rs. 65 crore to Rs. 852 crore due to strategic inventory buildup and capex; debt expected to stay at June level in Q2 then reduce ~Rs. 25 crore/quarter from Q3
items.quote: On the balance sheet, net debt increased by Rs. 65 crore during the quarter to Rs. 852 crore as of June 2026. This reflects 2 conscious decisions: strategic inventory buildup to ensure supply security for our customers in uncertain geopolitical environment and continued capital deployment towards capacity expansion and

items.statement: Vanvate factory commissioning targeted for Q3 FY27; depreciation run-rate expected to rise to Rs. 38-39 crore/quarter post-capitalization
items.quote: Right now, we are at around Rs. 35 crore per quarter. And once we do Vanvate capitalizations we will move into that, we are expecting somewhere Rs. 38 crore, Rs. 39 crore per quarter kind of a run rate.

items.statement: Target ROCE >15% in 3-5 years, long-term target 20%; Europe ROCE target 17-18%; new market investments (Germany, US, UK) expected to breakeven by year 3
items.quote: So, I think we should have excess of 15% ROCE as our target. Our long-term target is 20%. But at the moment, we will see 3 to 5 years of slow traction towards the 15%. And then as the sales ramp up in the new initiative areas post breakeven and EBITDA plus and then we will reach that 20% ROCE level.

items.statement: Insurance claim Rs. 30 crore received in Q1; further Rs. 50-60 crore expected within FY27
items.quote: I think Rs. 50 crore to Rs. 55 crore, Rs. 60 crore is the claim amount pending. So, we will continue to chase the insurers to fulfill the claim in this year.

items.statement: No impact from Gujarat floods on manufacturing or supply chain
items.quote: So far, we had no impact.

items.statement: Expects clients to remain on path through H1 FY27 with 17,500 open positions and healthy pipeline
items.quote: we are at this point, carrying an open position of 17,500 and a healthy pipeline, and we expect clients to remain on the path through the first half

items.statement: General staffing EBITDA margin to stay flat at ~1% in Q1-Q2 FY27, expansion expected in Q3-Q4 FY27
items.quote: Q2 will also be flat, more or less at the same EBITDA percentage. Q3, Q4, we will demonstrate the margin expansion

items.statement: Specialized staffing EBITDA margin target 8-9% stable state in 4-5 quarters
items.quote: Directionally, we think about 8% to 9% is the stable EBITDA margin in our specialized staffing business, which would take us another maybe 4 to 5 quarters to get there

items.statement: RegTech EBITDA margin expected ~8% for full year FY27
items.quote: RegTech also in the similar range, about 8% of EBITDA margin is what we are expecting on a full year basis

items.statement: Investing in sales, hiring engines, data lake, and automation in Q1-Q2 FY27 to drive future growth
items.quote: our priority this year is that between Q1 and Q2, we make some investments, which will help us to accelerate our growth rates as well as make our entry into some of these adjacencies productization of high-margin verticals

items.statement: 17,500 open positions and healthy pipeline across the group
items.quote: we are at this point, carrying an open position of 17,500 and a healthy pipeline

items.statement: Business EBITDA (ex-corporate) grew 18% YoY led by specialized staffing and HR services
items.quote: the business EBITDA without corporate or unallocated costs grew 18% year-on-year, mainly led by specialized staffing and HR services

items.statement: General staffing EBITDA margin currently at 1%
items.quote: staffing is currently at 1% EBITDA

items.statement: 65%+ of new general staffing logos under variable markup or outcome-linked pricing
items.quote: over 65% of the new logos this quarter came in under variable markup or outcome-linked pricing

items.statement: Retail inflation at 4.38%, weak monsoon, trade term uncertainties creating demand variability
items.quote: retail inflation has risen to 4.38%. Monsoon has not been that good this year. Trade terms and there are a lot of other uncertainties

items.statement: Management expects 10-15% annual revenue CAGR going forward, down from prior 20% target due to capex hold
items.quote: on an average CAGR should be anywhere between 10%-15%.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin target of 13-14% under normal circumstances
items.quote: 13%-14% is a pretty reasonable ask to achieve for us under normal circumstances.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin expanded to 37% from 29% YoY driven by patented product mix and price increases
items.quote: Gross margins improved to 37% from 29%, reflecting a favorable product mix, selective price increases, and our continued focus on procurement and manufacturing efficiencies.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin reached 20% vs 12% YoY; Q2 expected similar, H2 depends on monsoon
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved significantly to 20% compared with 12% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Patented portfolio contribution rose to 65% of branded sales in Q1 FY27 from 45% YoY; medium-term target 60-70%
items.quote: we believe it would be anywhere between 60 to 70% where our patent portfolio should remain out of our total branded sales.

items.statement: Implemented two rounds of price hikes in April and May; passed on significant portion of raw material cost inflation
items.quote: in first week of April, even before the season started, we had increased our prices. And then for further few of the products, we did a second round of increase in first week of May.

items.statement: Delayed monsoon subdued Q1 demand; expect herbicide, insecticide, fungicide and PGR demand to improve from Q2 as crops enter vegetative phase
items.quote: As crops move into vegetative and reproductive cycles, we expect demand for herbicides, insecticides, fungicides, and PGRs to improve during the following quarters.

items.statement: Created Rs 60 cr sales return provision (20% of sales) at higher gross margin to buffer Q3/Q4 volatility
items.quote: we have taken a number of say 20% as expected sales return and we have done a provision of around Rs. 60 crores.

items.statement: Branded sales volumes grew 13% YoY; patented product volumes surged 37% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: our patented portfolio delivered an impressive 37% increase in volumes, reflecting the strong acceptance of our differentiated products.

items.statement: Inventory reduced 6% YoY to Rs 764 cr; working capital improved with creditor payments normalized and better advance collections
items.quote: Inventories stood at Rs.764 crores as of 30th June compared to Rs.812 crores a year ago, representing a reduction of around 6%.

items.statement: India volumes growing 20%+ since March except April; post-June also 20%+ minimum
items.quote: Even post-June, we are looking at a 20% plus growth at least minimum.

items.statement: International volumes up 38.4% YoY including 11.8M cases from Twizza South Africa
items.quote: International markets also delivered a healthy growth with volumes increasing by 38.4% including the contribution of 11.8 million cases from Twizza in South Africa.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin improved 44 bps YoY to 55%; India EBITDA margin up 38 bps
items.quote: Gross margin improved by 44 basis points year -on-year to 55% supported by a higher mix of international business.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin declined 76 bps YoY to 27.7% due to Twizza consolidation at lower margins
items.quote: EBITDA margin declined by 76 basis points year-on-year primarily due to consolidation of Twizza business which currently operates at lower margins.

items.statement: Raw material cost impact averaged in Q2; enough stock for Q3; pricing unchanged; no large overall effect
items.quote: Our pricing would remain same and overall effect would not be large because we have averaged out the pricing.

items.statement: Low-sugar, no-sugar products contributed ~73% of consolidated volume in H1 2026
items.quote: Low-sugar, no -sugar products contributed approximately 73% of the consolidated volume during the period.

items.statement: VAD growing >40%; Nimbooz growing >30%; both 3x-4x overall business growth
items.quote: VAD is growing at over 40% for us and Nimbooz is growing at more than 30% for us.

items.statement: H1 2026 net capitalized capex ~Rs 9,500M; CWIP ~Rs 4,900M; inorganic capex Rs 11,314M for Twizza acquisition
items.quote: During H1 2026, net capitalized capex amounted to ~Rs. 9,500 million.

items.statement: Acquired Devyani Food Industries (Kenya) Limited for ready GTM to expand into CSD and energy drinks
items.quote: We also entered into an agreement to acquire the business of Devyani Food Industries (Kenya) Limited , which will provide us with the ready GTM in Kenya for expansion into carbonated soft drinks and energy drinks.

items.statement: Energy drink label change: remove word 'energy' within 90 days per FSSAI guideline; temporary dip in June-July, volumes recovering
items.quote: They have come out with a clear guideline that we should have the word energy removed within next 90 days.

items.statement: Extended exclusive PepsiCo bottling license in India until April 2049; removed SPV restrictions for operational flexibility
items.quote: We also extended our exclusive bottling and trademark license agreement with PepsiCo in India until April 2049 and removed the earlier restrictions requiring VBL to operate solely as the S PV for PepsiCo business.

items.statement: Strategic alliance with Asahi Group Holdings to introduce CALPIS fermented dairy beverage in India
items.quote: We also entered a strategic alliance with Asahi Group Holdings to introduce the iconic CALPIS brand in India, marking our entry into the value-added fermented dairy beverage category.

items.statement: Interim dividend 25% of face value (Rs 0.50/share); total cash outflow ~Rs 1,691M
items.quote: the Board of Directors has approved an interim dividend of 25% of face value, i.e., Rs. 0.50 per share, resulting in total cash outflow of ~Rs. 1,691 million.

items.statement: Food distribution and manufacturing in Africa growing ~50%
items.quote: That is also growing well for us. That is growing at about 50%.

items.statement: Confident of sustaining growth trajectory leveraging expanded capacities, diversified portfolio, distribution network; strong execution capabilities
items.quote: We believe our strong execution capabilities will enable us to deliver consistent performance going forward.

items.statement: Comfortable maintaining margins even in worst geopolitical cost environment; margins will improve when wars stop
items.quote: We can comfortably maintain our margins even in a year, which is the worst year for the geopolitical reasons and all the costing has gone up internationally.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin target is 12.5-13% blended margin to maintain market share
items.quote: Our ideal margin level for normal operations should be as I have always maintained between 12.5-13% which is the steady state margin so that we are not losing business, maintaining our share of business

items.statement: Expect to recover lost EBITDA margin of ~1.5% over next two quarters via indexation and price increases if rupee stable
items.quote: If things remain as it stands, we believe at least another percentage, half of EBITDA is still there in the system to be had through price increases and indexation from the customers.

items.statement: DICVS revenue target Rs 8000 cr by FY31 (Calendar Year 30) via organic and some inorganic growth
items.quote: We have also in the past given a revenue guidance for our DICVS business and we have said we hope to achieve Rs. 8000 crores by a combination of primarily organic and some amount of inorganic growth for Calendar Year '30 or FY31 of Rs. 8000 crores and I continue to maintain that.

items.statement: Polymer business has won significant new business; capacity additions across 6 plants (Hosur, Mysore, Aurangabad, Sanand, Bhiwadi, NCR) to unlock revenue from FY28
items.quote: We have won a lot of business for which we are creating capacity, but that will take the next 9-12 months to mature, after which that business also will maintain a very healthy (+20%) growth rate.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 11.41%, down ~160 bps YoY due to polymer/LPG/freight/wage cost spikes; Polymer division EBITDA 7.8%
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our revenue from operations has been about Rs.1083.58 crores with an EBITDA of Rs.123.69 crores with an EBITDA margin of 11.41%

items.statement: ~75% of revenue gets quarterly indexation in Q2, balance in Q3; minimum wage increase ~Rs 21 cr/yr under negotiation with customers
items.quote: At least about 75% of our revenue, Q2 we will get some indexation and the balance will go to Q3 because of the half yearly indexation which also we are trying to improve. It will help, but the minimum wage cost increase of about approximately 21 crores per annum because of the government regulation, we are still navigating with the customers to see how much we can absorb and how much they are goin

items.statement: Demand robust; industry grew ~22% YoY in Q1, PRICOL grew 26% YoY outperforming by 4%; two-wheeler industry grew 23%, PRICOL 28%
items.quote: All the industry put together weighted average grew by 22%. We grew by 26%. We have outgrown industry growth by 4% across all our divisions.

items.statement: DICVS and ACFMS each grew ~25% YoY in Q1; Polymer revenue Rs 249 cr; TFT penetration in 2-wheelers ~7-8%, expected to double in 2-3 years; hybrid clusters emerging
items.quote: The growth of both DICVS and ACFMS has been around 25%. Both of them have equally grown because we supply to the same set of customers both these vertical of products.

items.statement: EBITDA under pressure for next couple of quarters due to rupee at all-time low, crude oil rising, freight rates high for 4+ quarters, memory chip prices surging from AI demand
items.quote: We are mitigating some of these increases through VAV, value analysis and value engineering and productivity enhancement activities and also requested customers for offsetting part of these costs, but some degree of cost will be unrecovered and there will continue to be impact on EBITDA till all these global crises resolve and there is some semblance of normalcy returning to the world.

items.statement: Polymer capacity to double from ~Rs 1000 cr to ~Rs 2000 cr turnover post Rs 400 cr capex; centre of excellence operational by May 2027
items.quote: With the capacity that we are creating, we should comfortably go to about Rs. 2000 crores of turnover from our current Rs. 1000 crores of turnover that we are capable of producing.

items.statement: New customer wins in Polymer: Ather, River, Simple Energy, Raptee, Honda, Royal Enfield, Yamaha (final stages); Switches: Suzuki; ACFMS: disc brakes production started for major Indian OEM, export discussions with EU/US customers
items.quote: We have acquired business from Ather. We have acquired business from River. We have acquired business from Simple Energy. We have acquired business from Raptee. We have acquired business from Honda. We have acquired business from Royal Enfield. We are just on the final stages of acquiring business from Yamaha.

items.statement: Internal benchmark to open around 15% of store base annually; actual may vary a few percentage points higher or lower due to real estate realities
items.quote: internally, our benchmarks will remain that we should be opening around 15% of our store base as the number that we want to increase annually

items.statement: Building management bandwidth and capabilities across all levels; upgrading key technology and data systems for tighter operations
items.quote: we will be investing heavily in building management bandwidth and capabilities across all levels of the organization. Another big priority for me will be modernizing our technology and data stack

items.statement: Pipeline to build stores is strong and confident in maintaining 15% annual store growth over coming years
items.quote: our pipeline to build so many stores is strong, and we are confident in maintaining this over the coming years

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 16 bps to 14-15% range; EBITDA margin flat at 7.85%; net margin target around 5%
items.quote: our healthy gross margin is in the range of 14% to 15%, which keeps us very, very competitive, and that's the moat that we look at

items.statement: Staff cost increased significantly due to capability building ahead of volume growth; permanent headcount up ~4,000, contractual up only 2,200 despite 85 new stores
items.quote: we have driven productivity initiatives for the manpower in the stores as well as the warehouses. So those counts are inclusive of that

items.statement: Metro stores seeing slowdown due to saturation, high throughput, capacity constraints and competition; Tier 1/2 stores performing better than metros
items.quote: we are seeing, especially in metros like Mumbai, Bangalore, et cetera, where we have stores which are, one, very old and also very dense, with very high throughputs. And so therefore, to some extent these stores are reaching a saturation point

items.statement: Category contributions steady; slight dip in non-food, marginal increase in food; garments/apparel stable at 22-23% range; no intent to push to historical levels
items.quote: we expect this particular part of the business to be somewhere in that 22% to 23% kind of a range. And it is, as I said earlier also, it is doing quite well compared to our total business

items.statement: Quick commerce competition impacting metro same-store growth; impact expected to persist for next few years; not changing store expansion strategy based on QC presence
items.quote: I'm suspecting that that's not going to change over the next few years. And so therefore, that impact would remain while we of course continue to keep driving our own assortment

items.statement: DMart Ready focusing on 11 key cities to prove sustainable profitable model; improving assortment, 6-hour delivery, user experience; no plan to integrate with physical stores
items.quote: We made a conscious choice to double down on DMart Ready in 11 key cities where the vast majority of our online business comes from. We want our team to be laser-focused on proving that we can run a truly sustainable, profitable e-commerce model here

items.statement: 68 stores on long-term leases (15 of 85 new stores last year); open to leasing where land acquisition difficult; lease costs under AS 116 hit below EBITDA
items.quote: last year, for example, we now have about 68 stores -- 65 stores which are on long leases. And so therefore, it's not a very small number, it's a reasonable number in the overall store count of 500 plus

items.statement: Same-store sales growth for older stores likely to hover at current 7-8% range; not expecting considerable improvement; new stores in Tier 1/2 performing better
items.quote: same-store growth would possibly be hovering more in the range that we are seeing today, and we are not likely to see that go up considerably, all things being constant

items.statement: Internal store expansion target is 15% CAGR, could be a couple of percentage points higher or lower depending on real estate execution
items.quote: the internal number or internal ambition that we will look at will be that 15% number. And again, depending on how the situation turns out on the real estate development, the permissions, etcetera, it could be a couple of percentage points higher or lower.

items.statement: Same store sales growth expected to be around last financial year's level for the coming financial year
items.quote: I think we've said that it will be around the current trend, what we have been seeing over the last few years.

items.statement: Capex was upwards of INR 4,000 crores last year; NCD approval of INR 1,000 crores to manage capex and reduce borrowing cost
items.quote: If you see last year, capex was upwards of INR4,000 crores, and with the increasing store count that we want to pursue, we will need some capex - that is the plan.

items.statement: NCD approval of INR 1,000 crores may take total borrowing to INR 2,000 crores by year-end; existing stores expected to fund expansion in 2-3 years
items.quote: So we might go to an INR2,000 crores borrowing by the end of the year, but that is all going towards managing capex.

items.statement: Gross margin target range 14-15%; any sourcing or productivity benefits within this range passed to customers
items.quote: wherever we will be getting, any benefit which might be on account of sourcing, productivity, etcetera, and if it is in that ballpark 14% to 15% type of a range, we will pass that on to customers.

items.statement: Monthly shopping in metros remains stable and strong despite quick commerce; Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities show good traction
items.quote: We are actually seeing that to be, quite stable and strong. And we're continuing to see, good traction in all our Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities.

items.statement: Quick commerce impact seen mainly in dense metros with infrastructure challenges; minimal impact in other cities
items.quote: this seems to be more of an impact in, let's say densely populated metros with some of the infrastructure challenges and so therefore, I think that is where we see a little bit more. And wh atever impact, if at all, would be quite minimal in other places

items.statement: Piloting fresh fruits in some Mumbai stores with strong results; no plan for full-fledged fresh portfolio currently
items.quote: There are some pilots that we are doing in some of our stores with some fresh fruits, for example, in Mumbai, which is giving some strong results. But, is there a plan to have a full -fledged fresh portfolio in DMart stores at this point of time? No.

items.statement: DMart Ready consolidated to 11 cities from 18; 165 pickup points currently; efficiency gains expected FY27 onwards
items.quote: We currently have 165 pickup points.

items.statement: Of 85 stores opened in FY26, 15 were leased; lease model challenges remain around finding right property
items.quote: Of the 85 stores that we opened last fiscal, 15 were leased.

items.statement: Employee cost up 33% in standalone financials due to wage code implementation from December 2025 and March quarter
items.quote: On the absolute number of employee cost per se, there has been a slight impact also of the wage code that we implemented from December 2025 and the March quarter. So that also has contributed to the 33% hike in employee cost in the standalone financials.

items.statement: Organized trade including quick commerce and e-commerce still in early teens; huge runway for all formats
items.quote: total organized trade including quick commerce and e -commerce still is roughly in the early teens. Yes, and this includes the brick-and-mortar as well.

items.statement: Not tracking customer shopping behavior shifts to quick commerce; no consumer insight studies conducted
items.quote: No, we haven't done that, and I think possibly you are aware as well that we do not really track customer data, especially in our brick-and-mortar stores.

items.statement: Land acquisition pipeline of 2-3 years; conversion timeline 2-3 years depending on store complexity
items.quote: we are sitting on a project execution pipeline of next two to three years of stores that we will open and i t takes as Anshul mentioned earlier, it takes varying amount of time based on complexity and the local micro-market dynamics.

items.statement: Property conversion rate steady over years; manpower increased to support store openings
items.quote: the conversion has m ore or less remained steady. So, we shortlist a lot of properties, we do diligence, some properties fall off because the documentation is not clear and some landlords also are hesitant to sell every thing and all that.

items.statement: Offline customer data not collected to keep checkout simple and fast; DMart Ready has customer data
items.quote: Offline, we do not, collect the data because I think, one of the values that this organization is built around is simplicity. We want to make sure that the experience is simple enough.

items.statement: H2 FY27 will be better than H1; return to growth in H2 led by Q4
items.quote: During the outlook, we have just mentioned that H2 will be better than H1, and we will return to growth in H2 by Q4, driven by the Q4 performance and our profitability will return largely when the revenues come.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue expected to be flattish; significant growth expected in Q4 FY27
items.quote: Yes. I mean frankly, the large part is related to the growth and it really depends on that. But yes, fundamentally, if you look at the way the cost structure, and to tell you clearly, the European cost to take out takes much longer time than the other parts.

items.statement: USD 257 million deal wins in Q1 FY27 across connected cars, aftersales transformation, autonomous
items.quote: On the back of that, what was still good was KPIT could do USD 257 million worth wins during the quarter, which was across the world, but mainly driven through connected cars , then after sales transformation and autonomous

items.statement: EBITDA 17.2%, EBIT 12.3%, PAT INR 1.17 billion in Q1 FY27; margins to improve incrementally until revenue growth returns
items.quote: In terms of profits, the EBITDA was at 17.2%, EBIT at 12.3% and PAT at INR 1.17 billion .

items.statement: Medium-term aspiration of 22-24% EBITDA by FY29 remains; driven by product/solution revenue growth and fixed-price model
items.quote: I would say the medium-term outlook remains good for two, three reasons. I will not just make a statement. There are two, three things. As I said, we believe that our product revenues will grow and the solutions revenue will grow exponentially.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle segment to return to growth next quarter (Q2 FY27) after one-time license deal in prior quarter
items.quote: On the commercial vehicle, we will be on for growth next quarter. Actually, this quarter also, there was one specific thing what has happened was a quarter before we had one significant revenue in a particular place.

items.statement: Europe revenue impact ~4% in Q1 FY27; further impact expected in Q2 FY27 at geography level, offset by US and SIMA growth
items.quote: So I think we saw a reasonable impact in Europe, which was about 4% for the quarter, about 4% or so. But we also see, as you would look at this impact for the next quarter will not be at a company level.

items.statement: Broad-basing revenue: expanding wallet share in existing OEMs, adding new passenger car OEMs in Japan/Korea/Europe, growing off-highway/trucks (SDM), scaling products/solutions (N-Dream, i-Dart, Technica, Cymotive, Beacon)
items.quote: The first thing is on the existing OEMs. In the existing OEM, apart from focusing on increasing our wallet share in the areas in which we work , by getting a larger responsibility of the programs and through multiple ways, we have also added many newer areas of practice or offerings, which we provide to the client, which will help us.

items.statement: European OEMs discussing 30-40% product and production cost reduction with KPIT; shift to fixed-price contracts increasing 600-700 bps
items.quote: In their journey, given our relationship with them, the conversation has shifted towards how does KPIT help these OEMs reduce the cost of their product by at least 30% to 40%.

items.statement: Two major SDV programs ending: one European program reaching start of production, one Japanese program cancelled last minute; revenue impact to continue into Q2 FY27
items.quote: So one program from Europe is almost getting over now. We'll go to start of production, but that's been planned. The one in Japan that was actually cancelled at the last minute.

items.statement: Europe cost reduction takes longer than other regions; Qorix share of loss to continue for next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: the European cost to take out takes much longer time than the other parts. So, I think considering that at the cost of some of those, time as well as the cost will be longer from that perspective.

items.statement: Continued investment in R&D for products/solutions (N-Dream, i-Dart, Technica, Cymotive, Beacon platform, Microsoft partnership)
items.quote: We have multiple products and solutions. Again, we have made multiple investments in research and development. – One of the a few latest ones is N-Dream. The second I talked about is Aftersales Transformation which we brand as -Dart, Technica products, and then Cymotive, the cybersecurity company.

items.statement: China strategy: engaged with two Chinese OEMs, one nearing meaningful engagement; traction for products/solutions; leveraging global OEM partnerships in China
items.quote: And so we have engaged with two Chinese OEMs. And at least one of that we are about to get to a meaningful engagement in that case. The third is that we do believe that we have found a reasonable traction for our products and solutions in China.

items.statement: Wage hikes delayed; will be implemented in stages starting with junior grades, senior grades over period
items.quote: This is the first time we have delayed. But we will do it in stages. And we will give it to the some of the younger grades soon. The senior people will get over the period.

items.statement: Deep tech exploration: hydrogen tech (long-term), drones, humanoid, production floor automation, data center opportunities with clients like Cummins
items.quote: So I think these are some of the areas which we are exploring right now. Also some other areas where we are looking at and we see an opportunity. Again, these are some initial efforts, but we believe the opportunity there is big.

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: Confident of delivering 25% AUM growth while maintaining focus on profitability, portfolio quality and operating efficiency
items.quote: We remain confident of delivering 25% AUM growth while maintaining our focus on profitability, portfolio quality and operating efficiency.

items.statement: Long-term spread guidance maintained at 5% to 5.25% on blended basis
items.quote: We are committed to maintaining that 5% to 5.25% basis points spread.

items.statement: Full year Opex to Assets guidance in region of 2.6% to 2.7%
items.quote: I think full year guidance would be in the region of 2.6% to 2.7%.

items.statement: Net interest margin improved to 6.0% from 5.9% previous quarter
items.quote: Net interest margin was 6.0%, up from 5.9% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing reduced 10 bps sequentially to 7.8%, incremental borrowing cost at 7.6%
items.quote: On the liability side, proactive management of our borrowing mix led to a further 10 basis point sequential reduction, bringing cost of borrowing down to 7.8%. Incremental borrowing cost during the quarter remained favo urable at 7.6

items.statement: Demand across markets is healthy, growth supported by disciplined underwriting and scalable platform
items.quote: The affordable housing opportunity remains compelling. Demand across our markets is healthy, and our growth is supported by disciplined underwriting, a granular portfolio, stable asset quality and scalable operating platform.

items.statement: Added 4 branches in Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh; net addition of 133 employees
items.quote: During the quarter, we added four branches, one each in Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Madhya Pradesh, taking our network to 175 branches and 373 touch points. We made a net addition of 133 employees, largely in customer-facing roles, taking the total headcount to 1,988.

items.statement: AUM at INR16,938 crore, up 25.7% YoY and 6.7% QoQ; disbursements at INR1,628 crore, up 31% YoY and 3.6% QoQ
items.value: INR16,938 crore AUM, INR1,628 crore disbursements
items.quote: AUM stood at INR16,938 crore as of Jun'26, growing 25.7% year-on-year and 6.7% sequentially. Disbursement at INR1,628 crore is up 31.0% year-on-year and 3.6% sequentially.

items.statement: Committed to maintaining 5-5.25% spread; will pass on borrowing cost changes to customers in floating rate book
items.quote: We are committed to maintaining the yield of about 5% to 5.25%. Based on rate movement, we will convey the same thing to the customers.

items.statement: Disbursement growth 50% from unit volume increase, 50% from ticket size increase
items.quote: Lot of productivity improvement, but there is obviously increase in units as well. I would put it at around 50-50. There is 50% of the growth is coming from increase in units and 50% is coming from ticket size.

items.statement: 1+ DPD flat at 4.7%, 30+ DPD flat at 3.2%, Gross Stage 3 flat at 1.8%; stable asset quality
items.quote: Asset quality remained stable during the quarter. Our 1+ DPD remained flat at 4.7%, 30+ DPD remained flat at 3.2% and Gross Stage 3 remained flat at 1.8%.

items.statement: Targeting USD 100 million revenue from Kothavadi project by FY29 and on track
items.quote: I'll reiterate that we have targeted USD 100 million sort of revenue in FY '29. We are on track for that.

items.statement: Expect 30% of heavy engine production by FY28 and 50% by FY29 with full revenue from FY30
items.quote: I would say 30% of the production will be productionized by FY 28 and another 50% will come into FY 29, I would say. So, FY 30 will be the first year of seeing that full revenue.

items.statement: Sunbeam restructuring 90% complete by December with mid-teens EBITDA margin by Q4
items.quote: I'm very confident about Q4 mid-teens sort of an EBITDA margin for Sunbeam.

items.statement: DR Axion approved capex plan of INR 430 crores for this year, may spill to next year
items.quote: The approved plan is around INR 430 crores capex for DR.

items.statement: Standalone capex averaging more than INR 1,000 crores and will continue
items.quote: Standalone, we have been averaging more than INR 1,000 crores, I think, capex, and that will continue.

items.statement: Consolidated capex conservatively INR 1,500 crores but may increase if traction continues
items.quote: Conservatively, yes. But the traction what we see, if this -- we thought because of the Iran crisis, everything will slow down and stop that was when the capex plans were made.

items.statement: Aluminium segment on growth path for many more quarters due to massive recent investments
items.quote: Aluminium, we are on a growth path, and this growth journey will continue. The aluminium segment's pace of growth or the absolute growth and even percentage growth, all of that will beat the other segments.

items.statement: Powertrain EBIT margins may look depressed initially on new capacity until utilization improves but return ratios similar in couple of years
items.quote: But our confidence is that the return ratios will be among similar lines on the current powertrain within a couple of years.

items.statement: Confident all customers will align to pass-through of alloy prices though some taking time
items.quote: we are confident all customers will need to align to the new reality that this sort of a situation, suppliers have to be fairly compensated for the al loy prices, which should be a pass -through

items.statement: Heavy horsepower engines: 5 of 6 large customers orders received, first USD 100 million target filled
items.quote: With the first 4 customers itself, we have filled in the first USD 100 million sort of revenue target, which we had set up for FY '29-'30.

items.statement: Global problems and Iran crisis create uncertainty; operating in wait-and-watch mode on capex acceleration
items.quote: But as of now, we don't see much need to react very quickly because still we have global problems. Yes. I mean, we are in a wait-and-watch mode.

items.statement: Sunbeam exiting legacy negative-margin businesses (10-20% revenue reduction) but replacing with higher value-addition aluminium business
items.value: 10%, 20% sort of reduction in the top line
items.quote: Revenue, there may be a 10%, 20% sort of reduction in the top line, but there will be an increase in the gross margin or value addition.

items.statement: Land deal for monetization close to signing
items.quote: Yes, it is gaining traction. I think something is happening. I think we are close to signing a deal, I would say.

items.statement: Capex cycle started in India and will continue long term across OEMs and Tier 1/2 companies
items.quote: The capex cycle has started in India. I think this capex cycle is going to continue quite for a long time, I would say, in general, not only the OEMs, but also Tier 1, Tier 2 companies.

items.statement: KFC SSSG target of 5% to 6% to reach 105k-110k ADS in 1.5-2 years
items.quote: we are looking at a SSSG of about 5% to 6% for KFC. And therefore, if I were to take that, obviously, it will be almost like 1.5 -2 years kind of scenario.

items.statement: Merger with Sapphire Foods expected to complete by end of FY27
items.quote: As Mr. Jaipuria mentioned, our proposed merger with Sapphire Foods remains on track, and we continue to expect completion of the merger by end of the current financial year.

items.statement: No significant change in capex intensity despite dine-in shift; current store formats to continue
items.quote: Not much change in capex, so whatever format we are opening currently, that is what is going to be happening for future also.

items.statement: KFC Brand Contribution margin target of 20% at 105k-110k ADS threshold
items.quote: once we cross a threshold of 105,000 ADS to 110,000 ADS, we will be able to cross 20% Brand Contribution margins in KFC as we have demonstrated that in the past.

items.statement: Dine-in channel focus and technology adoption to drive margin improvement
items.quote: We have experimented in this quarter and we have seen some positive results on the dine-in channel. So, that will be another lever that can push the margins up.

items.statement: Slight price increases taken in KFC and Pizza Hut to mitigate LPG and wage cost inflation
items.quote: We have taken slight price increases in KFC and Pizza Hut to mitigate the cost impact, and we are monitoring the raw ma terial and packaging prices as we go

items.statement: Stable demand trends with positive July trends, though Shravan timing creates Q2 drag
items.quote: broadly, in terms of trends, we have seen a positive trend in the month of July, and we are on track.

items.statement: KFC dine-in saliency target of 59%-60%, up from current 57%
items.quote: our target remains to get to a number of 59%-60%.

items.statement: Global KFC initiatives (Kwench beverages, sauces, boneless) to roll out in India starting with Kwench test launch
items.quote: one after the other, all of those initiatives will come to India. India is part of the pipeline.

items.statement: Opened 11 net new KFC stores and 3 net new Biryani By Kilo stores in India in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We opened 11 net new KFC stores in India and added 3 net new Biryani By Kilo stores in India.

items.statement: Total store count reached 1,855 in India and 2,255 globally as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: We ended the period with 1,855 stores in India and 2,255 stores globally, as of June 30, 2026.

items.statement: Macro volatility (rupee, oil, LPG) and El Niño risk to consumption recovery cited as key risks
items.quote: the operating environment has remained volatile, along with the usual seasonal complexities. While the demand has remained stable so far, the forecast of a below-normal season, combined with El Niño risk, is a reminder that consumption recovery in India rarely moves in a straight line.

items.statement: Biryani By Kilo target to become INR 1,000 crore brand in next few years
items.quote: our objective is to make sure that this brand gets to INR 1,000 crore brand in the next few years.

items.statement: Technology platform buildout with new CTO and Cognizant partnership to complete pre-merger
items.quote: we have decided to build a core team in -house and then outsource the buildout to Cognizant Technologies. So there fore, as a combination of these two, we are very confident that we will be able to achieve a faster rollout and we should be on track before the merger

items.statement: Crop Protection segment expected to grow top line in double digits over next 2-3 years with EBITDA margin at or above industry average of 15-17%
items.quote: For the Crop Protection segment, we have been telling we'll be growing in double digit over a period of next two to three years' time. At the same time, we'll be maintaining the healthy profitability, which is industry average is in the range of 15% to 17%. We will try to be in this range or maybe above this range for

items.statement: Pigment segment annual revenue guided at INR500-600 crores with target EBITDA margin near 10%
items.quote: For the Pigment segment, demand or the growth will not be significantly heavy because little less growth-oriented industry. Over there, we believe our revenue will be somewhere in the range of INR500 crores to INR600 crores. We are not doing any big capex in this segment, and we will try to improve the profitability co

items.statement: Crop Nutrition segment expects couple of INR100 crores revenue over next 2-3 years from nano fertilizers
items.quote: So from the future perspective, we have a very, very optimistic plan for this segment, nano fertilizer. So there will be couple of INR100 crores revenue coming from this segment over a period of next two to three year's time.

items.statement: No heavy capex planned for next 1-2 years; focus on debt repayment
items.quote: At the same time, there will be continuous repayment because we are not going to do heavy capex for next one or two year's time. So as we are growing in terms of top line and bottom line, we'll be continuously reducing the debt.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 18% from 10.9% YoY; standalone EBITDA margin 18%
items.quote: EBITDA margin on consolidated basis stood at 18% as compared to 10.9% in the corresponding quarter previous year.

items.statement: Pigment margin expansion driven 5-6% by better realization and balance by operational efficiencies
items.quote: So yes, definitely about 5% to 6% is because of the better realization, and the balance is because of the better efficiency.

items.statement: Food and FMCG revenue growth guided at 18-20% for rest of FY27
items.quote: Revenue guidance would be in and around, I think between 18%- 20% is something we should continue to deliver.

items.statement: Food and FMCG EBITDA margin guidance based on average of last 4-5 quarters, not 6%
items.quote: EBITDA margins, I would rather say, we should not be looking at a 6% EBITDA margin for this quarter, what we should be looking at is the average of last four quarters.

items.statement: Edible Oil volume growth expected at 5-6% for rest of FY27
items.quote: I think rest of the nine months, I think we should grow in a moderate single digit, which can be anywhere between 5%-6% kind of number on volume.

items.statement: Edible Oil EBITDA per metric ton expected at INR 4,000-4,500 for FY27
items.quote: In Edible Oils, we expect volume growth of around 5%- 6%, with EBITDA expected to remain in the range of INR 4,000-INR 4,500 per metric ton.

items.statement: Industry Essentials volume growth expected at 8-9% with EBITDA at INR 3,000-3,500 per metric ton for FY27
items.value: 8-9% volume growth; INR 3,000-3,500 per metric ton EBITDA
items.quote: For Industry Essential s, we continue to expect volume growth of around 8%-9% while sustaining EBITDA in the range of INR 3,000-INR 3,500 per metric ton.

items.statement: Consolidated volume growth guidance of 8-9% for FY27
items.quote: I think 8% -9% is something which we are saying, and this is the AVVL Agri business guidance also we are giving it for quite some time. So, w e should continue to deliver that

items.statement: Annual capex run-rate of around INR 700 crore for modeling purposes
items.quote: A steady state for a modeling purpose, if you really want, I think you can continue to assume a CAPEX of anywhere between INR 700 crore kind of number for every year.

items.statement: Madhur brand targets 20,000 tons/month by end of FY27, full-year revenue INR 700-800 crore
items.quote: Our target is to scale it up further and make it close to 20,000 tons a month, by end of the year. Therefore, average revenue that this brand today is generating or will continue to generate will be in the range of close to maybe. For the full year it can be close to INR 700 crore-INR 800 crore kind of number.

items.statement: Food and FMCG segment EBITDA margin at 6% in Q1 FY27, viewed as right trade-off during investment phase
items.quote: Segment EBITDA came in at INR 104 crore with margin at 6%. We see this as the right trade-off.

items.statement: Royalty of 0.5% on sales payable to Shree Renuka Sugars for Madhur brand license
items.quote: We will be paying a royalty of 0.5% on the sales that we will do for this Madhur brand.

items.statement: Quick commerce channel grew 56% year-on-year in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Quick commerce continues to be particularly exciting for us, recording a growth of 56% year-on-year.

items.statement: Food and FMCG business is 80% B2C and 20% B2B
items.quote: I think for the Food , 80% is actually B2C. In fact, more than 80% is B2C, hardly 15% is B2B.

items.statement: Edible Oil import dependence remains at ~70%, with ~1/3 sourced from Wilmar
items.quote: I think for Edible Oil, it's close to 70% we import. I think little more than 70%, in fact, is imports. Of that 70%, close to one third is Wilmar.

items.statement: Raw material stock held at 30-35 days due to 35-40 day voyage period for imported oils
items.quote: Stock days are anywhere between 30 to 35 days, given the fact that most of our raw material is imported and there is a voyage period of 35, 40 days.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected in 20% range for Q2 FY27 and above 20% thereafter
items.quote: The first quarter delivered strong growth, and while the base will naturally become higher going forward, we remain confident of delivering revenue growth in the 20% range during the second quarter as well. We expect growth to remain above 20%.

items.statement: Target to double revenue over next four years from FY27 base
items.quote: Based on our current trajectory, we expect to cross INR 2,000 crores in revenue by the end of this financial year. Looking ahead, over the following four years, we believe we have the potential to double that revenue.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to return to 24%-25% range on pre-Ind AS basis by end of FY27
items.quote: Our long-term guidance remains unchanged. We continue t o expect EBITDA margins to return to the 24% –25% range on a pre -Ind AS basis by the end of the year

items.statement: Plan to add 2,500 beds over next 5 years with estimated capex of INR 2,200 crores
items.quote: Over next 5 years, we plan to add 2,500 beds to expand our network capacity to 5,000 beds through an estimated capex of investment around INR 2,200 crores.

items.statement: Invested INR 56 crores in capex during Q1 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, we invested approximately INR 56 crores towards capital expenditure, primary focused on expanding and strengthening capabilities across our existing hospitals and upcoming projects in line with our long-term growth strategy.

items.statement: Visibility of 1,200 beds under various stages of development
items.quote: We already have visibility of 1,200 beds under various stages of development, giving us confidence in our expansion road map.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 28.6% despite initial rating losses at new hospitals
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter amounted to INR 134.6 crores, registering a 30% year -on-year growth despite the initial rating losses at the newly commissioned hospitals. We maintained a healthy EBITDA margin of 28.6%.

items.statement: Rajahmundry hospital at breakeven; Electronic City Bangalore expected to reach breakeven in 2-3 months
items.quote: Rajahmundry is broadly at breakeven. As for our Electronic City hospital in Bangalore, we expect it to reach breakeven over the next two to three months.

items.statement: ARPOB improved 6% year-on-year in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We also delivered a 6% improvement in ARPOB while maintaining an efficient average length of stay.

items.statement: ARPOB growth driven by pricing and case mix improvement
items.quote: I think it's a combination of -- combination pricing as well as the case mix. These are 2 reasons.

items.statement: Inpatient discharges up 28%, outpatient consultations up 25%, deliveries up 23% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Inpatient discharges, outpatient consultations and deliveries grew by 28%, 25% and 23%, respectively.

items.statement: Expansion into Gurugram and Mumbai with tertiary/quaternary care to drive higher ARPOB
items.quote: Markets such as Gurugram and the broader NCR region have higher pricing points, which should support better realizations.

items.statement: Actively evaluating government scheme participation but cautious on reimbursement rates and economics
items.quote: This is something we are actively evaluating. In markets where we have excess capacity or available beds, we may consider allocating a portion of that capacity to government -funded healthcare schemes. However, the decision will depend on the reimbursement rates and overall economics.

items.statement: Mumbai entry faces higher cost structure; EBITDA margins expected above 20% eventually but too early to estimate stabilization
items.quote: Given the higher cost structure, I am not in a position to provide a pr ecise margin expectation today. However, I am confident that EBITDA margins should eventually be above 20%, although it is too early to estimate where they will ultimately stabilize.

items.statement: Digital transformation initiatives including CRM, HIS, BI platform and data lake to be substantially implemented in 3-4 months
items.quote: This transformation journey has already commenced, and we expect most of these initiatives to be substantially implemented over the next three to four months.

items.statement: New Bengaluru hospitals (HRBR and Electronic City) expected to break even within 12-15 months, broadly within 18 months
