items.quote: So INR660 crores, I mean originally, we had given a split of about INR500 crores for consumer and INR160 crore s for aerospace. We may see some acceleration in aerospace capex and that may be compensated by some reduction or saving & optimization in consumer

items.statement: 5-year capex plan FY27-31 of USD350-400 million
items.quote: we have laid down a plan from this year to FY31 for the next five years investing about USD350 Million to USD400 Million of overall capex

items.statement: Hosur ecosystem investment of INR1,900 crores over 10 years including JVs
items.quote: We have committed about INR1,900 crores in in total investment in that, including, investment into JVs what we have.

items.statement: Aerospace segment EBITDA margin 23% in Q1 FY27, above 20% target
items.quote: Q1 delivered 40% growth at a 23% segment margin.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA improved 3.5x sequentially from INR42M to INR148M, margin from 1% to 4%
items.quote: Excluding other income, ope rational EBITDA increased from INR 42 million in Q4 FY '26 to INR148 million in Q1 FY'27, an improvement of approximately 3.5x with the margin increasing from 1% to 4%.

items.statement: Consumer EBITDA loss narrowed by INR112M sequentially (24% improvement) to INR361M loss
items.quote: Sequentially, the consumer EBITDA loss narrowed by INR 112 million or approximately 24%, supported by increasing production volumes and improving operating performance.

items.statement: Consumer demand is structural, not inventory restocking; all production is shipped
items.quote: This all driven by the customer demand basically. Whatever we are producing, we are shipping. There is no issue of the demand.

items.statement: Consumer revenue grew 16% QoQ at similar utilization, driven by better throughput, mix and execution
items.quote: The consumer segment achieved 16% quarter-on-quarter revenue growth while operating at a similar capacity utilization level as Q4. This reflects enhanced throughput, better product mix and improved execution

items.statement: Raw material sourcing 99% imported; no qualified Indian sources for aerospace alloys
items.quote: I think our raw material is like 99% is imported. So, I don't think there is any possibility of changing that anytime soon, because we don't have any qualified sources in India for that to change.

items.statement: Likely USD150 million raise needed over 5 years, not planned for FY27 unless capex acceleration or inorganic opportunity
items.quote: We did communicate that most probably about USD150 million kind of a raise we'll have to do. We are not planning to do anything this year unless there is advanced pull-in of capex or inorganic piece, you know.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin expected 25-27%, PAT margin 22-23% after 2-3% dent from marketing spend in Q2-Q4
items.quote: So, EBITDA margins, so the current EBITDA margins that we are talking about is 29% and the PAT margins are around 23%. Like I said, 2% to 3% dent here, so anything between 25% to 27% on yearly basis and something between 22% to 23% on PAT basis is what we are expecting.

items.statement: Plan to open 9 COCO stores in Year 1 post-IPO (2 already open), 7 in Year 2, total 15 stores funded by IPO proceeds
items.quote: As outlined in prospectus, we plan to open nine stores during first year of following IPO with remaining stores to be opened in second year. As on date, we remain on track to execute the expansion plan as communicated and expect to complete the rollout within the stated timeline.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue INR118 cr, up 119.5% YoY; diamond caratage volume growth >50% YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, revenue from operations stood at INR118 crores registering robust 119.5% year-on-year growth, driven largely by higher volumes in terms of diamond caratage and highlighting the strength of our core diamond jewellery business.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin 35.46%, EBITDA margin 28.76%, PAT margin 23.06%; full-year EBITDA 25-27%, PAT 22-23% after marketing spend
items.quote: The gross profit for the quarter stood at INR41.83 crores, reflecting the growth of 147.25% Y-o-Y with gross margins of 35.46%. The EBITDA stood at INR33.92 crores, recording a growth of 192.88% Y-o-Y, while EBITDA margins stood at 28.76%. The PAT stood at INR27.21 crores, growing it by 265% Y-o-Y with PAT margins at 2

items.statement: Better price realization on diamond caratage contributed to margin expansion; gold price correction expected to support demand
items.quote: And the better price realization for diamond on caratage base was also a contributor there. So that's why the GP margins went up and accordingly our EBITDA and PAT margins also went up.

items.statement: Healthy consumer demand across all 21 cities; Akshaya Tritiya revenue INR12.7 cr vs INR3.5 cr YoY (268% growth); gold price correction supports wedding/festive season
items.quote: During Akshaya Tritiya alone, we recorded revenue of INR12.7 crores compared to INR3.5 crores in corresponding period last year, reflecting a robust 268% year-on-year growth. This continued traction highlights the increasing customers' preference for certified natural diamond jewellery and growing acceptance of Reva Di

items.statement: 97% of business in star-melee/minus-two diamonds where lab-grown price differential only 10-15%; minimal lab-grown competition impact
items.quote: So, the competition from lab-grown is not that significant because predominantly we are dealing in star-melee and minus-two kind of diamond. So, in that particular category, the price differential between the lab-grown and natural diamond is not more than 10% to 15% on a product basis.

items.statement: Marketing spend ramp-up in Q2-Q4 to dent PAT by 200-300 bps; EBO fixed costs minor impact as most open in H2; trade payables fell INR32 cr to INR20 cr due to payment cycles
items.quote: So, the 200 or 300 basis points that we are talking about is large will be largely impacted by the marketing expenditure that we will take in Q2, Q3, Q4 where the main seasons would start. And obviously there will be some dent by, you know, fixed cost of some EBOs, but that won't be like very material because most of t

items.statement: EBO break-even: 1 year in Maharashtra, 15-18 months outside; target EBO contribution 20-25% of revenue in 2-3 years from current 95% SIS dependency
items.quote: And obviously eventually after two to three years, the EBOs also will be consider if they reach to a stock turn of like 1.25 to 1.5, they will also start significantly contributing to the PAT level. So, I don't think so there would be any revision at PAT levels that can be ascertained right now.

items.statement: Short-term debt INR166 cr at FY26 end (WCDL for BTA settlement), INR120 cr repaid, balance ~INR120 cr; future EBO expansion funded primarily from internal accruals
items.quote: So, it was WCDL taken at the start of I think a year for the procurement of for the BTA settlement and that is been now I think repaid. 120 is part of it is repaid and currently it is around INR120 or something.

items.statement: No upward revision to guidance despite strong Q1; management prefers to under-promise and over-perform; confident of delivering previously promised targets
items.quote: So we -- honestly I think Modak sir would have been a better person to answer that. As he always said that we want to under-promise and over-perform. So this is what I think that -- there is no different guidance that I have received from him. So, I think the guidance remains same, but at least we are more confident on

items.statement: H2 typically 65% of annual revenue (Q3/Q4 strongest); Q2 better than Q1 historically; expect similar seasonality this year
items.quote: So usual bifurcation is that almost 35% would be H1 and 65% should be the H2. And that has been the, general rule of thumb when it comes to jewellery and that is what has happened also with Reva in previous year.

items.statement: FY27 AUM growth guidance of upwards of 40% for next 12 months; confident of over-delivering
items.quote: last quarter we had said our overall growth for the next 12 months will be upwards of 40%.

items.statement: FY27 credit cost guidance of 15% reduction; tracking well and holding firmly
items.quote: We firmly hold to our guidance which we gave last quarter, which is 15% reduction in credit cost , and we are tracking well on that.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing to drop by minimum 100 bps in H2 FY27 as old debt runs off
items.quote: our guidance for FY, particularly H2 of FY27, that you will see the cost of borrowing dropping by 100 basis points and it will only increase as we, as the old debt basically runs off the book

items.statement: AUM at INR 8,001 crores, up 61% YoY and 13% QoQ; disbursements INR 3,812 crores, up 37% YoY
items.quote: AUM stood at, as I mentioned, INR 8,001 crores, up 61% year-on-year and 13% quarter-on-quarter. Disbursement for the quarter were INR 3,812 crore s, up 37% year -on-year

items.statement: Total income yield fell 249 bps QoQ deliberately due to higher share of high-quality lower-risk customers and rising off-book mix (49.7% to 53.6%)
items.quote: As a share of average AUM, total income fell 249 basis points over the quarter. This drop is very deliberate and is part of a conscious and concerted strategy from our part.

items.statement: Registered users grew 33% YoY to 74.6M; served customers up 26% YoY to 12.25M; organic sourcing share rose to 31% from 27% QoQ
items.quote: organic channel contributed to 31% for quarter one. They were 27 odd percent last quarter. The total average of organic channel for the entire year FY26 on an average was close to around 23-24 odd percent.

items.statement: Paused lending in 450 pin codes last quarter; reopened 180 (40%) as signals turned modestly positive; remaining 270 still paused
items.quote: last quarter, out of caution, we paused lending across roughly 450 pin codes based on what our early warning system had flagged. We have re-examined those pin codes since. The signals have turned modestly positive , and we have reopened approximately 40% of these pin codes already.

items.statement: IPO completed May 2026 raised ~INR 850 crores; NBFC capital adequacy rose to 40.2% from 25.3%; net worth INR 2,245 crores (4x March 2023)
items.quote: Capital adequacy in our NBFC subsidiary rose to 40.2% from 25.3% last quarter. Net worth grew to INR 2,245 crore s, nearly four times its level in March 2023, built on retained earnings, organic profitability, and the IPO completed in May 2026

items.statement: Expect INR5,000 crores revenue from On-Highway tires by 2030
items.quote: I think the vision statement states that INR5,000 crores revenue from On-Highway tires by 2030, we're standing on that figure. I think that should be achieved.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR1,500-2,000 crores additional, total INR3,000 crores balance
items.quote: Around additional about between INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Total capex plan INR6,800 crores, INR3,800 crores spent, INR3,000 crores balance
items.quote: capex is INR6,800 crores. Out of that, we have spent roughly INR3,800 crores, INR3,000 crores is balance.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 20.61%, impacted by raw material prices and higher India mix
items.quote: The stand-alone EBITDA for the quarter was at INR703 crores with a margin of 20.61%. The margin was particularly impacted on account of raw material prices due to geopolitical situation globally and its impact on supply chain.

items.statement: 5% price hike taken in Q1, full pass-through expected in Q2; raw material cost up 5%, sales price impact ~3%
items.quote: So we have taken on a price hike of about 5% scattered across the various parts of the quarter, you will see the full pass-through coming in this quarter.

items.statement: Raw material price increased 5% on cost basis, ~3% sales price impact, may impact 2% margins in coming quarter
items.quote: The raw material price has increased by 5% on the cost basis of the raw material. The impact on the sales price is approximately 3%. Out of that, we are expecting it may impact 2% of our margins in the coming quarter.

items.statement: OHT volume grew 16% YoY to 93,770 MT, highest ever quarterly sales volume
items.quote: For the quarter, our OHT segment volume stood at 93,770 metric tons, a growth of 16% year-on-year.

items.statement: India OHT grew exceptionally well despite high base, driven by infra capex and market share gains
items.quote: India performed exceptionally well in Q1 despite of a high base from last year. Our marketing efforts along with superior product range is helping us gain market share. The growing infra capex in India is also aiding to our performance.

items.statement: Americas growth momentum expected to sustain with 10% tariff settlement and sharper go-to-market
items.quote: In the Americas, with the tariff rate settling at 10% levels, we have seen a better performance led by the U.S.A. With a sharper go-to-market strategy and stable end markets, we expect growth momentum to sustain.

items.statement: Carbon Black Phase II commissioned, total capacity 360,000 MTPA; captive power increased to 64 MW
items.quote: In this quarter, we commissioned our Phase II of Carbon Black plant, taking the total capacity to 360,000 -MTPA. For the energy circularity model, we have al so increased our captive power plant to 64 megawatts.

items.statement: On-Highway TBR and 2-wheeler launched in domestic market, gradual ramp-up expected from Q2
items.quote: Having seeded the business in Q1, we expect a gradual ramp-up starting Q2.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty, supply chain disruptions, vessel/container availability, freight costs, weather challenges in Europe, sketchy monsoon in India are key near-term variables
items.quote: For upcoming quarters, we would like to highlight geopolitical uncertainty with supply chain impacts on both availability of mate rials as well as the costs, availability of vessels, containers and freight costs as well. These, along with weather challenges in Europe and the sketchy monsoon expected in India, are key variables towards near-term performance -.

items.statement: Freight rates may increase further if current scenario continues, will attempt to pass on
items.quote: We may see some change if the scenario continues the way it is now with the stop in the peace process. So we may see some impact coming.

items.statement: Net debt INR1,725 crores as of June 30, 2026 (gross debt INR4,690 crores, cash INR2,965 crores)
items.quote: As on June 30, '26, gross debt and cash and cash equivalents were approximately INR4,690 crores and INR2,965 crores, respectively. Accord ingly, we have a net debt of approximately INR1,725 crores.

items.statement: First interim dividend of INR4 per equity share recommended
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a first interim dividend of INR4 per equity share.

items.statement: Full-year revenue growth guidance of approximately 12% including retail business.
items.quote: We have given a guidance earlier in the last quarter of about approximately 12% revenue growth with a 14% kind of EBITDA margin with a drop of 150-odd basis points of the retail business.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 14% for FY27, including retail drag.
items.quote: I believe that in terms of the EBITDA guidance of about 14% that we give, we feel confident that we will remain with that kind of guidance and apart from the drop of the retail business.

items.statement: Retail business to cause about 150 basis points annual EBITDA margin drop, including all store costs.
items.quote: We have already given an indication of an annual drop in EBITDA by about 150 basis points. We hope to be well within that budget.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at about INR100 crores, with INR40-50 crores for retail.
items.quote: The capital expenditure that we had envisaged for this year, as indicated earlier, was close to about INR100 crores with about INR40 crores to INR50 crores going into the retail project.

items.statement: Retail revenue expected to reach about INR160 crores in FY27, up from INR80 crores last year.
items.quote: As indicated earlier, the revenue expectation from the retail business, we did about INR80 crores last year, and we hope to close this year around INR160 crores.

items.statement: Some raw material cost pass-on done in Q1; more may follow if input costs stay high.
items.quote: Some pass on was done in the first quarter. If raw materials remain high and margins start getting shrunk, then some might continue to be passed on, which is the general standard that we follow.

items.statement: Positive sentiment on upcoming festive and wedding season; confident of achieving guidance.
items.quote: The sentiment towards how the season will go is very positive. Overall, everyone is very hopeful that this year also goes as planned. We are very positive on reaching the guidance that we had indicated.

items.statement: Real estate project construction to start this quarter, completion expected in 24 months.
items.quote: In this quarter, we expect to start construction, and we expect 24 months for this project to be completed.

items.statement: ZECODE stores expected to reach profitability in 1.5 to 2 years; some already EBITDA positive.
items.quote: And we've indicated about 1.5 to 2 years for store profitability. For some of the stores that we've opened, we have seen very positive results, and I've indicated earlier that some stores have turned EBITDA positive, but it's too early to come to those conclusions.

items.statement: Preference share bonus scheme effective; record date 22 August 2026; redemption taxed as dividend.
items.quote: The company has also fixed 22nd August 2026 as the record date for determining the eligible shareholders entitled to receive these redeemable preference shares under the scheme.

items.statement: ZECODE store format evolved from 4,000 sq ft to average 7,000 sq ft with better results.
items.quote: Now we have an average size of approximately 7,000 square feet. We've seen better results in these larger stores because the product portfolio that we cater to now is better displayed in the larger format stores and also the consumer experience that we are able to offer is far greater.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 EBITDA per ton guidance for carbon black maintained at INR16,500-17,000, implying 14-15% improvement over FY26 average
items.quote: On a full year basis, if you refer to our last quarter's investor call, we had given a guidance of 14% to 15% improvement over our FY26 average EBITDA. With which will be somewhere around, say, INR16,500, INR17,000 per ton. So we stick to that.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 volumes may be temporarily lower due to cautious customer procurement, but management expects strong volume recovery in H2 FY27
items.quote: In the very near-term, the operating environment remains dynamic and some customers have adopted a more cautious procurement approach than we could have temporarily -- that will probably have a temporary effect on volumes in Q2. We see this as a timing effect, not a demand effect and therefore, remain constructive on the second half of FY27.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR300 crores (+/- INR50 crores), mainly maintenance and productivity enhancement; strategic capex limited to ~INR100 crores as Andhra greenfield spend shifts to next year
items.quote: Capex outlook this year, we are largely through with our ground field expansion. Small capex here and there, which is more like maintenance capex plus some new developments for productivity enhancement, yield improvement, etc.. My sense is that it should be somewhere around INR300 crores, maybe plus-minus INR50-odd crores.

items.statement: Coal tar distillation project business plan under review with OEM suppliers; approval and capex details expected within a month
items.quote: We are progressing very well on the definition of the project for the coal tar distillation. The business plan is being checked, and we are also in talks with the OEM suppliers of equipment, etc.. By this quarter, we should be looking at getting an approval -- on all the capexes that are required as we refine the business model.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 carbon black EBITDA per ton at INR22,900 boosted by ~INR70 crores low-cost inventory gain; ~INR40-50 crores may reverse in Q2
items.quote: For the quarter, we did about INR22,900 a ton. On a full year basis, if you refer to our last quarter's investor call, we had given a guidance of 14% to 15% improvement over our FY26 average EBITDA. With which will be somewhere around, say, INR16,500, INR17,000 per ton. So we stick to that.

items.statement: Management targets gross profit per kg of INR36-38 for next 9 months through pricing discipline and bottom-slicing low-margin volumes
items.quote: Yes, that's kind of right. But again, it will be a trade-off between volumes and margins. So we'll hold on to pricing discipline as long as we can see that our ability to push volumes in market is high. But it will also depend on demand and supply scenario, Sanjesh.

items.statement: Cost pass-through mechanism working on formula-linked contracts with contractual lag; spot market (30% of volumes) monetized effectively during crude spike
items.quote: On the formula linked portion of our business, the pricing mechanism works exactly as designed. Input cost movements are passed on to our customers with a contractual lag.

items.statement: Logistics surcharges recovered from most customers but not 100% due to delivered-price competitiveness; approach varies by customer
items.quote: In most cases, we have managed to get surcharges from our customers based on the fact that logistics costs have gone up. So most of the time we try to recover it, but are we able to recover 100% of it? The answer is no, because we have to be competitive at a delivered price level.

items.statement: Domestic tire industry grew 7-8% in FY26; similar high single-digit growth expected FY27-29 driven by aging fleet, premiumization, EV penetration; tire makers at ~90% utilization with fresh FY27 capex
items.quote: Closer home, Indian tire sector is on a healthy growth path after a solid 7% to 8% this fiscal, industry estimates for growth is in a similar high single-digit range over FY '27 to '29, supported by a growing aging vehicle fleet, premiumization and rising EV penetration.

items.statement: Export volumes deliberately diverted to domestic spot market in Q1 due to high freight; significant international volume growth expected Q2-Q4 as freight normalizes and FTA benefits take hold
items.period: Q2 FY27, Q3 FY27, Q4 FY27
items.quote: As freight normalizes and the tariff and FTA tailwinds I spoke about earlier take hold, we see significant headroom to scale our international business from here. You should see those volume flows happening quarter 2, quarter 3, quarter 4 onwards.

items.statement: Nanovace pilot plant operational; individual equipment testing progressing; first customer sampling batches expected in coming weeks of August
items.quote: The pilot plant is up now. As I mentioned earlier as well, at an individual equipment level, the testing is progressing extremely well. We now need to line balance it and ensure that the flows are managed well. That process is ongoing and in the next few weeks we are committed to sort of starting producing the first batch of products which will go to customers with whom we have already been engagi

items.statement: 1,000 MTPA super-conductive specialty black facility in Palej commissioned; market development started across battery, conductive polymers, electronics
items.quote: To address growing demand from battery semiconductors and advanced polymer applications, we have set up a 1,000 metric ton per annum super-conductive specialty black facility in Palej and have commenced market development activities across battery, conductive polymers and electronic applications.

items.statement: Acetylene black modular facility engineering completed; product development initiated with technology collaborator
items.quote: Engineering for the first phase of the modular manufacturing facility has been completed, and we have initiated product development activities with our technology collaborator.

items.statement: Green chelates order booking running ahead of current capacity; new facility under discussion; qualified with key accounts P&G, Reckitt, Henkel
items.quote: On green chelates, order booking is running ahead of our current capacity, and we are now getting qualified with key accounts like P&G, Reckitt and Henkel. To build further on this shift towards green chelates, we are in discussion around a new facility.

items.statement: Logistics costs remain high and erratic due to Middle East crisis; port disruptions may cause temporary volume losses
items.quote: It continues to be erratic. It's a reflection of how the Middle East crisis keeps ebbing and flowing. And -- so we are quite agile in looking for capacities as well as prices. So we'll just need to be agile and nimble on this one.

items.statement: US tariff refund application filed for PCBL and Aquapharm; expected refund INR40-45 crores within 2-4 weeks
items.quote: Between Aquapharm and PCBL, the amount would be somewhere between INR40 crores to INR45-odd crores. We have already made application, and we are tracking it very closely. My own sense is maybe in next 2 to 4 weeks' time, we should be receiving that refund.

items.statement: Targets 20% consolidated EBITDA margin, expecting to achieve in next financial year.
items.quote: So with that being said, yes, we will be -- very soon, we'll be achieving the 20% margin. Will that be next financial year? Yes, I remain positive to that.

items.statement: Barium EBITDA margin to remain at 25% going forward.
items.quote: I think we believe the EBITDA margins will continue to remain at 25% moving forward.

items.statement: Barium and strontium combined EBITDA margin to remain over 20%.
items.quote: It will still remain over 20% for the consol, I mean, consolidate -- I mean, removing stand-alone, combining barium and strontium, it will still remain 20%.

items.statement: Total capex outlay for this year is INR200-250 crores.
items.quote: This year, we are -- we have a total capital outlay, capex outlay of close to about INR200 crores to INR250 crores.

items.statement: DMSO project capex estimated at INR205-240 crores, INR68 crores spent up to June 30.
items.quote: In DMSO, our total project estimated capex is between INR205 crores to INR240 crores, of which we have spent close to about INR68 crores up to 30th June.

items.statement: Chromium derivative expansion to invest about INR50 crores.
items.quote: Chromium, we are expanding our derivative base. Almost INR50 crores will be invested over there.

items.statement: Barium backward integration investment of about INR40 crores.
items.quote: Barium business, we are expanding our backward integration line, and we are likely to see an investment of close to about INR40 crores to complete these projects.

items.statement: Solar project capex of INR5-6 crores, rest under SPV model.
items.quote: The total capex outlay for solar will be close to about INR5 crores to INR6 crores, and the rest will be under the SPV model, wherein we will be able to buy the solar at a fixed price on the longer term.

items.statement: Barium division expected to grow 15-20% this year.
items.quote: Things we remain positive, and we expect it to grow 15%, 20% this year in the barium division as well.

items.statement: Higher value-added derivatives contributed nearly 50% of chromium sales in Q1 vs 40% in FY26.
items.quote: And the higher value -added derivatives contributed to nearly 50% of our sales in the quarter gone by as comp ared to, say, 40% in FY26 as a year.

items.statement: Higher sea freights challenging to pass on completely; focusing on domestic sales and higher value products.
items.quote: For the current quarter, I mean, there are certain headwinds related to higher sea freights, which we are finding it a bit challenging to pass on com pletely.

items.statement: Strontium capacity utilization at 50%, targeting 65-75% by year-end.
items.quote: We are currently operating at 50% utilization over there. And we would like to end the year at close to about 65% to 75% capacity utilization.

items.statement: ECU expected in range just below INR30,000 or higher; chlorine price currently minus INR7,000 to minus INR8,000
items.quote: current ECU is in the range of just below INR30,000. So, we expect it to be in this range or higher. As for the chlorine price, currently it is in the minus INR7,000 to minus INR8,000 range.

items.statement: PVC demand expected to remain soft in Q2 FY27 due to monsoon onset
items.quote: With the onset of the monsoon, demand is expected to remain soft in Q2 financial year '27.

items.statement: Sugar prices expected to remain firm for next couple of months
items.quote: We expect it to, it is difficult to say, but it should be firm for next couple of months, yes.

items.statement: Capex of around INR1,000 crore planned for FY27
items.quote: we do have capex of around INR1,000 crore this year.

items.statement: Fenesta order book close to INR1,000 crore, up 4%
items.quote: The total order book is close to around about INR1,000 crore if I put all together.

items.statement: Fenesta PBDIT grew 13% YoY to INR40 crore, partially offset by product mix change and higher fixed expenses
items.quote: On profitability, PBDIT for the quarter grew 13% year-on-year to INR40 crore. The contribution from higher volumes was partially offset by a change in product mix along with higher fixed expenses towards setting up new revenue platforms and elevated marketing expense.

items.statement: Bioseed Kharif season impacted by 15-20% sowing acreage shortfall; large part of season lost despite July rains
items.quote: large part of it is lost. I mean, monsoon has been decent in the month of July, but as Chairman mentioned in his opening remarks as well, that it is patchy and in our region where we sell our products or our products are suitable for that region, there the sowing has been lower than 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Urea business saw sharp increase in natural gas prices due to West Asia conflict; focused on energy efficiency and cost discipline
items.quote: The Urea business witnessed a sharp increase in natural gas prices following supply disruptions arising from West Asia conflict. We remain focused on improving energy efficiency, maximizing urea production, and maintaining strict cost discipline.

items.statement: Chemicals advanced materials portfolio (glycerine to ECH to epoxy) meaningful contributor to 33% revenue growth
items.quote: The advanced materials portfolio, spanning the glycerine to ECH to epoxy value chain, was a meaningful contributor to this top-line performance.

items.statement: Demerger application targeted to be filed with government in FY27
items.quote: objective is yes, we make the application to the government in this financial year.

items.statement: Effective cash tax outgo expected at 19% for at least 5 years due to MAT credit utilization
items.quote: effectively for, you know, let's say anywhere between 5 to 10 years, at least 5 I can see in the foreseeable future, my effective tax rate will be 19% or tax outgo will be 19%.

items.statement: Aluminum chloride and calcium chloride projects at Bharuch in final pre-commissioning; commercial production expected Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our projects in aluminum chloride and calcium chloride at Bharuch are in the final stages of pre-commissioning, and commercial production is expected to commence during Q2.

items.statement: 68 MW peak hybrid renewable power project at Kota under commissioning with 25 MW average injection in July
items.quote: The 68-megawatt peak hybrid renewable power project at Kota is currently under commissioning with average power injection of 25 megawatts for the month of July.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties may impact LNG availability and lead to higher subsidy outstanding for Fertilizer business
items.quote: Going forward, continued geopolitical uncertainties may impact LNG availability and lead to higher subsidy outstanding.

items.statement: Solar opportunity expected to contribute 4-5% of total volume over next 2-3 years

items.statement: Group shared services company formed to consolidate HR, IT, branding across APL Apollo, Apollo Pipes, SG Finserv, SG Mart
items.quote: This is a small company we have started since we have many common activities like HR, IT, branding. We want to deal with all these by gathering them at the group level so that our cost from it -- currently every company has a separate HR head, every compan y has a separate IT

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at INR4,400-4,500 crore, average growth over 25%.

items.statement: Labor requirement to increase by 3,000-4,000 in next 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: So in peak, if you can say, still 3,000 to 4,000 number will still be added in next one or two quarters.

items.statement: Precast plant capacity INR200 crore, expected to execute INR150-200 crore annually.
items.quote: So, throughout the year, Precast plant capacity is, in the range of INR200 crores, so we'll be executing about INR150 crores to INR200 crores throughout the year whatever may be the project.

items.statement: Tax rate for full year to be slightly higher than 25% due to non-deductible expenses.
items.quote: No, it will be slightly on the higher side because there are certain expenses which are not deductible in tax, so it's a permanent difference. So for the year it will be slightly on a higher side.

items.statement: ARPP introduced as new metric; Q1 FY27 ARPP INR201,891 broadly similar to prior year
items.quote: For Q1 FY27, ARPP stood at INR201,891, broadly similar to the number achieved in the corresponding period last year, reflecting stable realization despite the continued ramp-up of newer and existing facilities.

items.statement: Ambition to double revenue from Rs.1,000 crores to Rs.2,000 crores by FY29.
items.quote: And also, our ambition is to double our revenue, right, from Rs.1,000 crores to Rs.2,000 crores by FY29.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin for this year expected at 14-15%.
items.quote: We think the normalized margin for this year will be about 14%-15%.

items.statement: When ready-to-cut fabric supplier, normalized EBITDA expected 16-18%.
items.quote: So, let us say when we are vertically integrated and have become ready-to-cut fabric, we can expect a normalized EBITDA of about 16% to 18%.

items.statement: About Rs.350 crores CAPEX planned for ready-to-cut fabric production facilities.
items.quote: But as we have sort of said earlier as well, we almost have about Rs. 350 crores of CAPEX to be deployed, primarily for our ready-to-cut fabric production facilities, which is what we are focusing on now.

items.statement: This year's total CAPEX including modernization expected Rs.100-120 crores.
items.quote: So, this year, our CAPEX , all projects put together, including modernization, replacement of capital equipment, I think will be about Rs.100, 120 crores.

items.statement: Spreads in Q1 FY27 were about Rs.155 per kilo with packing, up from Rs.138 in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: So, with packing, it is about Rs. 155 per kilo is what our current spread for the last quarter was. And this is sort of a jump from about Rs. 138 per kilo, which was there in Quarter 4 FY26.

items.statement: Full year spreads will be better than last year; Q2 may be slightly lower than Q1.
items.quote: This definitely for the full year will be better than that, right, at least from a demand situation point of view, that looks to be continuing.

items.statement: Fabric share of total sales to rise to 30-40% in three years from 15-16% now.
items.quote: Fabric will become a significant part of our overall top line, probably in the region of about 30% -40%, which is right now at 15% -16%. But this is after three years is what I am talking about.

items.statement: Remaining 25 knitting machines to be commissioned by Q3 FY27 end.
items.quote: The rest 19-machines to be received in FY27 Quarter 2, Quarter 3. So, by Quarter 3 end we will have this 25-machines commissioned.

items.statement: 11 MW solar project commissioning delayed to December, saving Rs.6 crores annually.
items.quote: The commissioning date is in December now. So, that project would give a benefit of about Rs. 6 crores per year, but the full benefit will only come next year.

items.statement: Demand tailwinds strengthening from FTAs and domestic growth; order book healthy at 1.5-2 months.
items.quote: So, the order book is healthy. We usually maintain about one and a half to two months of forward booking, which we are able to maintain as of now as well.

items.statement: US-Iran conflict and US tariff policies remain key headwinds.
items.quote: The evolving US-Iran situation remains a key headwind trigger, along with the US tariff policies and related investigations.

items.statement: PM MITRA Park project completion targeted by CY28.
items.quote: So, it will be in CY ' 28, we have to start building it, bu t yes, in CY '28, we will sort of plan to commission it and initiate it.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu incentives expected Rs.100-125 crores capital subsidy on Rs.1,000 crores investment.
items.quote: And in terms of the total investments of around Rs. 1,000 crores, almost around Rs. 100 crores, Rs.125 crores kind of capital subsidy and other benefits will be there.

items.statement: Full year net new money guidance: INR20,000-24,000 crores from Wealth and Private combined; INR3,500-5,500 crores from AMC
items.quote: Broadly, Sanketh, and these are obviously indicative numbers, but the way we are seeing it is that between wealth and private, both INR 10,000 - 12,000 crores. So a range of INR 20,000 to 24,000 crores and AMC, we are seeing anywhere between INR 3,500 to 5,500 crores.

items.statement: Full year Asset Services revenue growth expected at 20-25% despite Q1 moderation
items.quote: But on a full year basis, we are confident that revenue growth will be more than 20 -25% here.

items.statement: Full year cost-to-income ratio expected around 55%
items.quote: Having said that, on a consolidated basis, our cost-to-income ratio is around 55% and maybe for the full year, this will remain around this level only.

items.statement: Full year opex to revenue ratio expected at 15-16%
items.quote: If you look at the overall full year opex, I would imagine it will still be in the range of 15-16% for the full year.

items.statement: Asset Management cumulative loss expected at INR35-40 crores for FY27, breakeven path starts after
items.quote: So this year, we will end up at a cumulative loss of around INR35 crores to INR40 crores. And subsequent to that, you will see the path to breakeven start.

items.statement: Private Wealth cost-to-income target 60-62% over next 3 years
items.quote: And overall, as you rightly said that 60% to 62% medium term, that target also remains over the next 3 years.

items.statement: Private Wealth RM addition target 15-16% annually if market allows
items.quote: RM addition essentially our desire always is to basically keep adding 15 -16% every year, provided the market allows us to do that at costs which are not upsetting to the overall business.

items.statement: Capital Markets full year cost-to-income expected 36-40% range
items.quote: But I think overall full year basis, anywhere between 36% to 40% range is what will remain here.

items.statement: New office lease under evaluation; upfront Ind AS 116 charge will be over and above usual opex growth
items.quote: There's one more update on the opex side, which I would like to highlight is that we are looking for our new office because our current lease is coming for renewal. And as you guys know that under Ind AS 116 when you do a lease accounting, there will always be some charge which comes upfront.

items.statement: PRIME Commercial Real Estate Fund closed at INR4,000 crores vs INR3,000 crores target; 40% deployed, targeting 70% by end Q3
items.quote: We successfully closed our first commercial real estate fund. It's branded as PRIME (PRIME Offices Fund). We closed at around INR4,000 crores. We had initially launched with a target of INR3,000 crores. We've completed deployment of around 40% across 3 to 4 marquee assets between Chennai , Delhi, Pune and we are on the verge of completing a few other transactions. And the target is to deploy about

items.statement: Crossover 4 Private Equity Fund raised INR300-350 crores so far, targeting INR700-1,000 crores
items.quote: We are in the process of raising our fourth fund, it's branded as Crossover 4. We've done about INR300 crores to INR350 crores. We are targeting anywhere between INR700 crores to INR1,000 crores there.

items.statement: Lending book steady-state margins 30-40 bps above current 3.7-3.8% due to hedging gains on MLD book
items.quote: So about 30 -40 bps higher than this because like I mentioned in a few calls, our cost of debt basically moves a bit up and down because of the hedging gains and losses, which comes on our MLD book. Our overall borrowing has about 25%, which is the MLD on which we keep hedging. On a full year basis, we are able to save around 50 basis of cost.

items.statement: Private Wealth ARR yield range 80-90 bps; advisory yield similar to combined transactional+ARR yield ex-NII
items.quote: I've always maintained Sanketh, that between 80 to 90 at this point in time is what we are able to see. It depends on the product mix of ARR, what gets done or what proportion of product of between AIF II, AIF III, MF, PMS become heavy in a quarter.

items.statement: Q1 opex up 24% YoY but down 4% QoQ; seasonal marketing expenses INR10-12 crores; underlying opex growth 14-15%
items.quote: Opex is up by 24%, but compared to Q4, it is down by 4%. So there are a few seasonal expenses which comes in this quarter. They will be towards the marketing expenses and business promotion expenses. That will be around INR10 crores to INR12 crores. If I remove that, the opex would have grown by around 14 -15%.

items.statement: Primary market IPO activity selective in Q1 (8 IPOs vs 15 in Q4); pent-up demand with many documents filed; expecting better activity in balance 9 months
items.quote: Primary market activity was very, very selective. The total number of IPOs, which we saw in Q1 were 8 as compared to 15 in Q4 and maybe 14 -15 last year. And even the total amount of fundraise fell by around 60 -65%, both against Q4 and last year Q1. But now we are seeing that activity come back. And there is a lot of pent-up demand. A lot of documents have been filed. So I think the balance 9 mon

items.statement: Managed accounts/ARR asset mix: 30-35% equity, 65% non-equity (fixed income plus alternatives like credit, real estate, infrastructure)
items.quote: broadly for us, it remains in the managed products and ARR segment between 30% to 35% would be equity and 65% will be non -equity. So it's not fixed income. It will be fixed inco me plus alternatives like credit, real estate, infrastructure, so products that could deliver clients returns ranging from 7 - 8%, right up to 18-20%, but non-correlated with the equity market performance

items.statement: Derivative regulations (STT, intraday financing, bank guarantee collateral) impact being monitored; not expected to be very significant
items.quote: There is one key monitorable, which basically on the new regulations which have come around derivatives, which is STT and on intraday financing and bank guarantee collateral around these two. We've seen the numbers. We've ran through the numbers. At least we don't feel that there's going to be a very, very significant impact, but we'll closely monitor on that.

items.statement: Full-year Classic Vacations EBITDA margin expected around 2.5%
items.quote: Yes, I think that is a fair assessment.

items.statement: Steady-state scaled platform businesses normalize at 45-60% EBITDA margins, significant runway from current levels
items.quote: Those businesses are starting to normalize anywhere between 45 % to 60% EBITDA margins, which we are not at all.

items.statement: AI initiatives (VOYA, CX, sales productivity) are lean, in-house, minimal capex sitting in intangibles, not impacting cost structure
items.quote: It is a lean team as is the modern AI native projects. So, it is not impacting on our cost structures in any way at this point, but it is creating optionality on the other side.

items.statement: Middle East situation extremely fluid, impossible to predict recovery, treating any growth as optionality
items.quote: I would really not hazard a guess on what is going to happen in the Middle East and when it comes back to growth. We are just thinking of that as optionality now that should that growth come in, that helps us accelerate bottom line growth even faster, but given where the situation is, it is very hard to back on it.

items.statement: Organic growth expected to return to pre-war Q3 FY26 levels when normality resumes, timing uncertain
items.quote: We would absolutely expect to get back to that when things get normal. The "when is a big when" and we really don't have an answer for it.

items.statement: Europe and APAC leading growth charter; North America like-for-like growth expected from Oct-Dec on large base
items.quote: Europe and APAC are leading the growth charter right now. We are also expecting to see reasonable growth like-for-like basis in North America as well starting whenever October, November, December when it's a like-for-like comparison admittedly on a very large base in a very tough market, but we are looking for growth levers over there as well.

items.statement: Classic integration three-pronged: North America sales hiring mostly done, CRM/back-office automation underway, platform migration targeted by calendar year-end
items.quote: The third is platform integration, which is the big one and which we are likely to finish by CY end of this current calendar year. This is what will allow one seamless integration of the TBO platform into the Classic ecosystem and secondly a more seamless selling and buying between the two platforms.

items.statement: Middle East crisis unpredictable, changes hourly; inbound businesses under serious stress, potential attrition if not revived
items.quote: situation is extremely fluid, and the fact that the Middle East was flat is quite an achievement in all honesty given that is the eye of the crisis right now. It is also very hard at this point , we have given up on predicting what is going to happen because the situation literally changes every hour

items.statement: Q2 QoQ growth expected to be better than Q1 as July is heaviest northern hemisphere travel month
items.quote: On a QoQ basis, Karan, historically, Q2 is bigger than Q1 and you would expect it to be same way and that is what we are really anchoring around that just like last quarter we said that let's aim for QoQ growth and YoY growth. We continue to aim for that.

items.statement: Organic SG&A growth ~4% YoY CC in Q1; may expand slightly in short term due to increments and opportunistic market development but remains below top-line growth
items.quote: I think it will expand a little bit from here in the short term. One, because it is also increments season in Q2. Secondly, as business recovers, there will be opportunities for us to opportunistically do a little bit of more market development exercise. I would say that it will be range bound, but it may be the SG&A growth may slightly increase, but not at the pace of top line.

items.statement: Hosting/bandwidth expense fell 14% QoQ due to technical optimization and shift to self-managed infrastructure; new baseline established
items.quote: We had made significant investments in terms of technical investments to make sure that we optimize our traffic. Also, on the infrastructure, we essentially try to move away from expensive solutions, infrastructure solutions to solutions that we manage oursel ves to essentially bring that cost down. So, that is the new baseline that we can assume from now

items.statement: Constant currency reporting to continue directionally each quarter given recent 11% FX gap vs 3% prior quarter
items.quote: Directionally, yes. As Gaurav pointed out in the initial comments as well, we had seen a wild fluctuation in this quarter. That is the reason we wanted to transparently show the numbers in the constant currency so that, we have the real picture of the numbers. So directionally, yes, we would tend to show the numbers in the coming quarters as well.

items.statement: GTV split remains broadly 50-50 retail vs B2B/API, consistent with prior quarter
items.quote: GTV numbers would broadly be between 50-50 only as the last quarter.

items.statement: Classic standalone enterprise-level growth a few quarters away; opposing forces of Middle East normalization vs Classic seasonality make blended GP growth hard to predict for Dec quarter
items.quote: I think the first thing to acknowledge is that for Classic, which is a business that we have just recently acquired, it will be a period before we get Classic standalone. I am not saying North America as a whole, but Classic standalone to start delivering enterprise level growth. I think we will have to find those levers. We are confident we will find them, but that is definitely a few quarters aw

items.statement: Quick commerce contribution margin guidance for Q2FY27 is 0 to -100 bps, assuming no change in competitive intensity.
items.quote: Even the guidance that we've given is highly range-bound. We closed the last quarter at -0.2%, and we're talking about -100 bps is the range. So obviously, we've assumed no change in competitive intensity.

items.statement: Food delivery YoY growth guidance maintained at 18% to 20%.
items.quote: But if you've seen the momentum over the last 3-4 years, it's been on an upward trajectory, and we continue to maintain guidance of YoY growth between 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Quick commerce NOV growth expected to be at least double-digit sequentially in Q2FY27.
items.quote: So we are cautiously optimistic of being able to deliver at least on this double-digit growth on a sequential basis, and hopefully more.

items.statement: Quick commerce store additions in Q2FY27 will exceed total additions of the last four quarters, within existing top 8 cities.
items.quote: Our guidance for the current quarter is that seeing some of this growth, that we are going to add more stores than we have added in the last four quarters, in this quarter itself.

items.statement: Quick commerce contribution margin improved to INR30 per order over last 5 quarters; Q1FY27 closed at -0.2%.
items.quote: When we look at the quality of the business going into the future, we have absolutely moved close to INR30 in contribution over the last 5 quarters.

items.statement: Food delivery margin currently at ~3%, targeting 5% steady state.
items.quote: We are currently at about 3%. We have told that we will be getting to 5%, and that steady growth you will continue to see.

items.statement: Take rate improvement driven by brand margin negotiations, advertising revenue, and user fee monetization; deemed sustainable.
items.quote: So the combination of these three levers, we have been able to increase the take rate significantly and a large part of our improvement over the last 4-5 quarters to help us get to the CM break-even was also led by the monetization efforts.

items.statement: Monetization runway: ~INR20 from product margins/mix and ~INR10 from advertising to reach EBITDA breakeven; further INR25-30 for steady EBITDA.
items.quote: Again, INR20 roughly, that is going to come from the monetization side, roughly broken half and half between, say, the product margins that we make from the brands or the mix of our business, as well as roughly, say INR10 from the advertising side of the business.

items.statement: Quick commerce 4-week cumulative NOV growth at 10% vs 1% prior period; M1 user retention at highest in many quarters.
items.quote: So, Abhisek, I can clarify that it is a four week cumulative number. So not just a week, but a four week cumulative number over the previous 4 weeks. This is the latest available data that we have of the previous week

items.statement: Quick commerce added more orders in last 4 weeks than previous 6 months combined.
items.quote: So even over the last four weeks, we've added more orders than in the previous 6 months.

items.statement: Differentiated assortment via strategic brand partnerships (mix of proprietary, large brands, D2C) with many exclusive SKUs; 'Switch to Better' campaign live.
items.quote: The way we are working is we work with a mixture of both incumbent and large brands in some of the categories, as well as challengers like D2C brands to create a distinctive value proposition of better quality or great quality at great prices.

items.statement: Competitive intensity in quick commerce remains high with 7-8 players expanding networks; no noticeable change in competition recently.
items.quote: We're not seeing anything noticeable in changes, Sachin. Harsha here.

items.statement: Value-seeking consumers acquired via low MOV/zero fee propositions will churn quickly if value proposition changes.
items.quote: So any player that has to make these choices is going to see significant dips in volumes, and then you need to make up for it, and then more with organic drivers of growth.

items.statement: No capitalization of employee costs, store pre-opening costs, or indirect costs; all expensed to contribution margin.
items.quote: Absolutely not. For all the line items that you mentioned, and there are a lot of them, we do not capitalize any of these. All of these are booked as part of the -- especially also new stores when they open, even if there are 30-60-90-day period, all of that gets baked into our contribution margin.

items.statement: Consolidated cash breakeven expected in next 2 quarters (excluding platform innovation burn), funded by food delivery margin expansion and treasury income.
items.quote: So we expect to, over the next two quarters, be able to break even at the overall cash level, while we continue to support the Quick Commerce business during its EBITDA profitability journey.

items.statement: Toing food delivery model uses lower commissions than Swiggy to enable everyday low prices; different AOV economics; 1/3 users overlap with Swiggy.
items.quote: I think, firstly, we are still in early days on the Toing business. But definitely, I think commissions do need to be different from the Swiggy platform to enable our restaurant partners to offer everyday low prices.

items.statement: Target pre-sales of approximately Rs 6,500 crores for FY27, ~23% growth over FY26
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY27, we target closing the year with pre -sales of approximately Rs. 6,500 crores which would be a growth of ~23% over

items.statement: Net debt/equity ratio expected to improve from current ~2.0x due to profit recognition at end of FY27
items.quote: However, the net debt / equity ratio is expected to improve from current levels of ~2.0x due to recognition of profits at the end of FY27.

items.statement: Company will complete around 15 million square feet of ongoing projects across FY27, FY28, FY29
items.quote: In closing, I wish to state that company would be completing around 15 million square feet of ongoing projects in FY27, FY28 and FY29 gradually.

items.statement: Target 5.5 million square feet of project completion in FY27
items.quote: We are well on track to deliver on a target of 5.5 million square feet of completion this year.

items.quote: We have a strong pipeline of launches spread over approximately 5 million square feet and worth approximately Rs. 7,800 crores this year and we hope to carry this momentum into other project phases when we launch them.

items.quote: I am pleased to share th at we have secured a development agreement for the redevelopment of five societies in Ashok Nagar, Kandivali. This project is situated on approximately 2.8 -acre land parcel and has a GDV potential of Rs. 1,250 crores

items.statement: Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin ~20%
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA during the quarter was Rs. 95 crores with the margin of ~20%.

items.statement: Pricing trend stable and strong; price increase quantum to be known by Q2
items.quote: We are seeing a positive trend towards walk-ins and conversion and also the pricing is looking stable and strong.

items.statement: Sales momentum at Kalpataru Park City Thane expanded significantly with pre-sales surging ~350% year-on-year
items.quote: Sales momentum at Kalpataru Parkcity, Thane expanded significantly this quarter, with pre-sales surging ~350% year-on-year compared to Q1 FY26 on a low base.

items.statement: Launched two projects/phases with total potential of 1.25 million square feet saleable area in Q1 FY27
items.quote: we launched two projects/ phases which have a total potential of 1.25 million square feet of saleable area. This includes Tower C of Estella at Kalpataru Park City Thane and our luxury development Kalpataru Vian, Hrushikesh, Lokhandwala in Mumbai.

items.statement: Refinanced debt of approximately Rs 1,800 crores in Q1 FY27 giving estimated annual savings of Rs 55 crores in finance cost
items.quote: during this quarter, we have refinanced a debt of approximately Rs. 1,800 crores which wi ll give us an estimated annual savings of Rs. 55 crores in a finance cost

items.statement: Weighted average cost of borrowing now ~11% per annum, down ~200 basis points since listing
items.quote: Hence, our weighted average cost of borrowing now stands at ~11% per annum down by approximately 200 basis points since the listing.

items.statement: Debt may increase slightly or marginally within quarters due to spend on ongoing or new projects but trend is downside year-on-year
items.quote: Directionally, it is going to be on the downside, year on year. Periodically, within quarters, it is possible that it may increase slightly or marginally due to the spend or investment or capital allocation on to the ongoing projects or the new projects which are acquired under new BD.

items.statement: Monetized commercial office property Kalpataru Infinia in Pune for ~Rs 119 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, we have monetized our commercial office property Kalpataru Infinia located at Shivajinagar Nagar in Pune for a consideration of ~Rs. 119 crores.

items.statement: Received occupation certificate for ~0.79 million square feet across 668 units in Q1 FY27
items.quote: during the quarter we received occupation certificate for ~0.79 million square feet across 668 units, continuing a strong track record of project execution and handovers.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 25-30% from earlier 25%, and PAT margin expansion guidance to 0.5-1% from earlier 0.5-0.75%
items.quote: In terms of specific guidance, we would like to revise our revenue guidance from earlier 25% to 30% and at the PAT level margin growth, we would like to increase it from 0.5% to 0.75% -1%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin expanded to 24.65%, up 329 bps YoY and 542 bps QoQ
items.quote: Gross margin expanded to 24.65%, improving by 329 basis points over last year and 542 basis points over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 12.8%, up 156 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR52.8 crores, with EBITDA margin at 12.8%, an improvement of 156 basis points year-on-year compared to 11.3% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Memory prices rose 5-10% in Q1 FY27; 8GB DDR5 at $126 and 16GB DDR5 at $231 as of June 30; prices up 5x since Oct 2025
items.quote: Memory prices have risen a further 5% to 10% in the last quarter alone. 8GB DDR5 now stands at $126 and 16GB DDR5 at $231 as of June 30th. Since October 2025, these prices have more than doubled.

items.statement: Entry-level new laptop prices rose from INR40,000 to INR48,000
items.quote: Price of an entry-level 8GB RAM and 512GB SSD laptop has further risen from INR40,000 to INR48,000.

items.statement: IDC projects global PC shipments to decline 11.3% in 2026, with 20% YoY decline in H2 2026; ~30 million unit decline in two quarters
items.quote: IDC now projects global PC shipments to decline 11.3% for full year 2026 with conditions expected to worsen in the second half, driving a 20% year-on-year decline in that period alone.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volume grew 18% YoY to 150,000 units (108,000 laptops + 42,000 desktops/others)
items.quote: Total number of laptops is 1,08,000 and desktops and others is 42,000.

items.statement: Laptop ASP increased 12% YoY to INR30,763; desktop ASP increased 10% YoY to INR19,300
items.quote: In terms of ASPs, in terms of laptops during the quarter, we have an ASP of about INR30,763. If you were to compare this to the corresponding quarter, it is about it was about INR27,500.

items.statement: India gross margin 21% vs international ~30% in Q1 FY27; international revenue share 64% (US 24%, Europe 23%, Middle East 12%, Others 5%)
items.quote: 21% being the gross margin in India and international going to almost touching 30% in the quarter, right And see, the acceptability of the product is increasing and getting deeper both in India as well as in the international markets.

items.statement: No disruption to UAE refurbishment facility or logistics despite Middle East tensions; UAE remains insulated
items.quote: There is no disruption at all in our UAE facilties, all our facilities are up and running and the shipments are also going. Shipments are through air and there is no disruption at all.

items.statement: Inventory at INR700 crores end of Q1 FY27, down from INR740 crores end of FY26; strategic inventory held for margin advantage
items.quote: The inventory at the end of Q1 is about INR700-odd crores. This has gone down, this has gone down from about INR740-odd crores at the end of the year.

items.statement: No fixed capital investment; business is working capital heavy with no machinery involved
items.quote: Also, in our business, we don't have any fixed capital worth talking about, there are no machinery involved, there are no other things, so the business is working capital heavy.

items.statement: Effective tax rate guidance 10-12% for FY27 on consolidated basis
items.quote: The tax rate you should assume on a similar basis at between 10% to 12% for the full year on a consol basis

items.statement: Refurbished laptops priced at ~30% of new laptops; potential to reach 50% as trust grows, implying significant margin expansion
items.quote: Currently, we are pegging our product, we are around 30%, right? When you compare that with phone or car market, the refurbished phone or refurbished car, they are like 50% of a new phone or new car.

items.statement: Supplies to 49 countries (up from 46), 5,130 customer touchpoints, 773 suppliers, 2,420 employees as of June 2026
items.quote: As of end of Q1 FY27, Electronics Bazaar supplies to 49 countries, up from 46 at the end of FY26. Customer touchpoints have grown to 5,130 and our supplier base now stands at 773, reflecting deeper and more diversified sourcing across geographies.

items.statement: Procurement prices trailing new laptop price increases; companies deferring purchases or extending leases may reduce disposition volumes
items.quote: Second, obviously, companies are, there are two things happening: company might defer their purchases, or the leases might get extended. Will it make the disposition overall pie lower, absolutely, yes.

items.statement: Standalone margins moderated due to front-loaded investments in technology resilience, cyber security, operational automation, and talent acquisition.
items.quote: I wish to highlight that our standalone margins have seen some moderation compared to the previous periods. This is largely on account of the investments that we have been our focus areas which we have been talking to you about which is strengthening technology resilience and cyber security, enhancing customer experiences through greater operational automation and increase in talent pool by addres

items.quote: The bank margins during the period was impacted by the upfront onboarding revenue sharing associated with a specific partner project that the bank won and started implementing during that quarter. items.statement: Capitalized INR 7-8 crores on technology in Q1 FY27 versus full year FY26 capitalization of INR 106 crores.
items.quote: On the technology front, we have capitalized INR7 to INR8 crores during Q1 FY27 versus full year capitalization in the previous year of INR106 crores.

items.statement: Added 3,600 unlisted companies in Q1 FY27; total issuers now over 115,000.
items.quote: the number of companies that joined this quarter was 3,600 companies. And in terms of the component of the joining fee, we typically charge INR15,000 per company as a processing charge at the time of joining.
