So, both sequential and Y-o-Y basis, there is clear improvement. This improvement reflects a steady pickup in accounts addition and the various works that we've been doing to add new DPs and improve our customer experience and add APIs

items.statement: FinTech brokers now contribute ~20% of incremental demat additions vs ~2% a few quarters ago; Yuva and Women's Demat plans together account for 18-20% of incremental additions.
items.quote: In fact, just for information, that number few quarters back was about 2% of our total addition was coming from FinTech and 98% was coming from non-FinTech. Now, that number of FinTech too has gone to almost 20%. And the numbers have increased. So, that is the sort of change in the sort of color of the onboarding new customers that are joining us.

items.statement: Technology investments driven by regulatory expectations for resilience, market expectations for customer experience, internal automation needs, and hardware refresh cycles (every 5-8 years).
items.quote: One of the themes is from a technology resilience. So, technology resilience is an expectation from regulators. And at the same time, it is an expectation from the market, to say, it is purely regulatory driven may not be accurate. At the same time, to say, it is purely market driven is not accurate. I think both legs are sort of overlapping in this particular them e. And that is a sizable area of

items.statement: E-voting events increased to 900 in Q1 FY27 from 794 in Q1 FY26; e-voting market share rose to 64% from 61% YoY.
items.quote: Our e -voting platform has helped many leading companies to offer e-voting services to their shareholders, empowering them to exercise their voting rights electronically with a number of events conducted during the quarter increasing to 900 compared to 794 that we did same time last year, same period last year. And our e- voting market share as a result increased to 64% in Q1 FY27 from 61% in Q1FY

items.statement: NSDL Payments Bank retail customers grew 1.7x to 49.5 lakhs in Q1 FY27 from 28.3 lakhs in Q1 FY26; ranked 6th as payee PSP among top 15 banks.
items.quote: Retail customers have increased by 1.7x from 28.3 lakhs Q1 FY26 to 49.5 lakhs in Q1 FY27. Coming to our database management, our other subsidiary. During the quarter, NDML welcomed Mr. Rajeev Gupta as the MD and CEO, succeeding Mr. Gupte who completed his full term as MD and CEO of NDML.

items.statement: Joining fee for unlisted companies is INR 15,000 per company; contributed INR 5-6 crores to transaction charges in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: And in terms of the component of the joining fee, we typically charge INR15,000 per company as a processing charge at the time of joining. So INR15,000, I mean, let me just look at the number here. Yes, that should be in the range of about INR5 to INR6 crores.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks revived in July (West Asia conflict) after easing in Q1 FY27; FPIs remain net sellers for third consecutive quarter.
items.quote: renewed hostilities in July have revived geopolitical and crude price risks. But during the quarter, what stayed consistent was that who was buying and who was selling. FPIs remained net sellers for the third consecutive quarter, and DIIs remained strong buyers with continuing to provide support to the markets

items.statement: NDML diversified across 5 businesses (KRA, SEZ Online, Insurance Repository, etc.); KRA price cut impact offset by SEZ business growth.
items.quote: So, as we had explained to you, Sanketh, the NDML business is more diversified compared to our competition. So, to measure us purely and solely on behalf of the performance of demat account and KRA downloads may not be a very accurate way of looking at it, because we have about 5 businesses there which includes SEZ online, which includes your KRA business and which includes insurance repository am

items.statement: Board approved 20% stake investment in IIBH (associate in GIFT City); appointed Subhash Kelkar as Executive Director, Critical Operations.
items.quote: Further, during the quarter, the board approved an investment in IIBH, which is a subsidiary in the GIFT City, which is an associate, I'm sorry, in the GIFT City with NSDL holding 20% stake in that company. We also recently welcomed Mr. Subhash Kelkar as our Executive Director, Critical Operations.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 38%-40% from previous 27%-30%
items.quote: We are now revising our FY27 revenue growth guidance from 27% to 30% that we had given earlier to 38% to 40%.

items.statement: Margin trajectory unchanged despite higher growth guidance
items.quote: Having said that, our margin trajectory remains unchanged, suggesting faster growth with the same disciplined path into profitability.

items.statement: Q1 capex of INR60 crores, 77% allocated to network and automation
items.quote: 77% of the capex that we are talking about has gone into network and automation.

items.statement: Order volumes reached nearly 25 crores in Q1, growing 83% year-on-year
items.quote: Order volumes reached nearly 25 crores, growing 83% year-on-year.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 4.9% in Q1 from 4.7% in Q4
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA rose to INR67 crores, with margins expanding to 4.9%, which was 4.7% last quarter.

items.statement: Chose to lag diesel price pass-through by 5 days to support customer relationships
items.quote: On diesel price, many of our contracts allow us to pass increases straight to our customers, and we had every right to take that hike on day one, but we chose to lag it by 5 days and carry it on ourselves.

items.statement: Lost shipment debit cost reduced to 5.5% of revenue from 6.1% in Q4
items.quote: Our lost shipment debit cost, came down to 5.5% of revenue, which was 7.9% a year ago and 6.1% in the last quarter, Q4.

items.statement: Prime D2C business grew 2.7x year-on-year, crossed 400 D2C customers
items.quote: Prime grew almost two and a half times last year. It has accelerated to 2.7 times year-on-year this quarter, even at a much larger base.

items.statement: Prime Large expanded to 10,000 pin codes in Q1, exceeding full-year FY27 target; new target 12,000 pin codes
items.quote: We have already expanded to 10,000 pin codes, which was our full year target for FY27. We hit that number within the first quarter. We are now raising our FY27 target for Prime Large to 12,000 pin codes.

items.statement: Shadowfax 360 onboarded 1,200+ transacting sellers within one quarter of launch
items.quote: Within one quarter of the launch, we already have more than 1,200 transacting sellers, and this number is compounding every single week.

items.statement: Hyperlocal grew 53% year-on-year and 17% quarter-on-quarter; category expanding across verticals
items.quote: Hyper-local has grown about 53% year-on-year, and 17% over the last quarter itself.

items.statement: 47 dark stores live as of June 30, another 20 on the way; target 100 for FY27
items.quote: We are super proud to communicate that out of thos e 100 dark stores, 47 are already live as on 30th June, and another 20 are on the way to go

items.statement: Minimum wage hikes in four states causing INR2-2.5 crores monthly impact
items.value: INR2 crores to INR2.5 crores a month
items.quote: Yes, we have roughly taken about between INR2 crores to INR2.5 crores a month impact because of minimum wage impact coming from various states.

items.statement: Full-year margin guidance unchanged at 100-200 bps expansion; excess profits reinvested or passed to customers
items.quote: While we are catching up on growth faster, we still want to maintain the margin guidance that we had given at the start of this year.

items.statement: Amazon Now partnership scaling; Amazon entered top 10 customer club; Express volumes also started
items.quote: Amazon has now, entered the top 10 customer club for us.

items.statement: Geographical coverage expanded to 16,372 pin codes, adding 716 in Q1 (8 per day)
items.quote: We ended the quarter at about 16,372 pin codes, where we opened about 716 pin codes over the last 90 days, almost 8 pin codes every single day.

items.statement: New urea plant expected to be commissioned by 2030
items.quote: In my opinion, even with today's situation in terms of stressed timelines for critical equipments, we should be able to deliver it within 2030.

items.statement: New urea plant project cost around INR 10,000 crores
items.quote: You would understand that projects of this type, almost INR 10,000 crores, they go through several phases in terms of preparation.

items.statement: Financial bids for new urea plant expected by mid-October
items.quote: The financial bids after equalization of the technical requirements should be available to us by may be middle October or so.

items.statement: New urea plant EBITDA per ton estimated at INR 12,000
items.quote: I would say we will be still around INR 12,000 a ton.

items.statement: 8.5 lakh tons of NPK tied up with vendors
items.quote: I think till date we have tied up, Ashish, about 8.5 lakh tons.

items.statement: July urea sales at 3.8 lakh tons and NPK at 92,000-93,000 tons
items.quote: This month itself, we have had almost 3,80,000 tons of farmer sales of urea and almost 92,000 -93,000 tons of NPK sales in this month alone.

items.statement: Q2 expected to progress well with channel liquidation creating second round of demand
items.quote: Yes, we feel that Q2 will also progress well and the liquidation from the channel is also happening, which will create the second round of demand.

items.statement: Launched 7 new crop protection products and 2 new seed varieties in Q1
items.quote: Our crop protection chemicals and special ity business continued to strengthen its product portfolio with the launch of seven new products across herbicides, fungicides, and insecticides during the quarter.

items.statement: TAN project progressing with WNA, Ammonium Nitrate Melt and HDAN nearing commissioning
items.quote: Our Technical Ammonium Nitrate project progressed well during the quarter with production commencing of Weak Nitric Acid and Ammonium Nitrate solutions, while the high- density Ammonium Nitrate moves closer to commissioning.

items.statement: IMACID JV impacted by Sulphur shortages and high prices, production resumed in July
items.quote: Our joint venture, IMACID , was impacted during the quarter due to Sulphur shortages and elevated Sulphur prices, which resulted in temporary production shutdown to avoid operating at negative margins.

items.statement: NPK subsidy rates for Kharif do not reflect subsequent cost escalations from West Asia tensions
items.quote: While the nutrient-based subsidy rates for Kharif were revised upwards by around 10%, these were announced prior to the sharp increase in global prices following the geopolitical developments in West Asia and therefore do not fully reflect the subsequent cost escalations.

items.statement: Q1 standalone EBITDA rose 12% to INR 851 crores with margins expanding to 17% from 13%
items.quote: On a stand- alone basis, revenue from operations stood at INR 5,000 crores as compared to INR 5,700 crores, lower by about 12% . EBITDA , however, rose 12 % to INR 851 crores, with margins expanding to 17%, roughly from 13%, an improvement of about 350 basis points.

items.statement: Complex fertilizer segment EBIT rose 67% to INR 239 crores due to advance purchases
items.quote: On the complex fertilizer segment, revenues stood at INR 1,737 crores, against INR 2,131 crores, lower by 18%, reflecting a measured approach to placement in a season where sowing was delayed. Segment EBIT rose 67% to around INR 239 crores.

items.statement: Crop protection segment EBIT grew 13% to INR 108 crores with margins improving to 25%
items.quote: The crop protection chemicals, special ity nutrients and seed segment recorded revenues of about INR 430 crores, as against INR 458 crores, lower by 6 %, reflecting deferred farmer purchases. Segment EBIT, however, grew 13 % to INR 108 crores, with margins improving to about 25%.

items.statement: Progress made on overseas phosphatic JV, will inform when materialized
items.quote: On t hat line, I would say that some progress has been made and we are proceeding ahead with certain actions. So, as and when we come to that situation, we will definitely inform you on that also.

items.statement: Net borrowing of INR 200 crores as of Q1
items.quote: We had net borrowing of about INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Management will not provide full-year revenue guidance due to market visibility and base effects
items.quote: For the full year, I will not be able to give you a guidance, Vibhav, because for 2 reasons. One is that everything is not visible at this moment how the market will look like.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 20 bps YoY and 70 bps QoQ to 12.4%
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR655 crores, up 19.5% year-on-year, with EBITDA margin at 12.4%. The margin expanded by 20 basis points on a year-on-year basis and by around 70 basis points on a sequential quarter basis.

items.statement: Price increases of 4-6% taken in Q1 FY27 across categories; Q2 decision pending
items.quote: So I can tell you on Q1, on year-on-year basis, the price correction would be in the range of 4% to 6% across categories. There are multiple categories. It is not uniform across, but around 4% to 6% in various categories, we took price increases.

items.statement: Board approved INR1,400 crores capex for lithium-ion giga factory in FY27; INR100 crores invested in July
items.quote: We have already got an approval from our Board for INR1,400 crores for this fiscal year. But we'll review again -- this is required and we'll let you know. As of now, it's INR1,400 crores. Out of that INR100 crores has gone in July.

items.statement: Annual core lead-acid capex of ~INR500 crores for manufacturing technology, automation and capacity expansion
items.quote: every year, we keep INR500 crores, around INR500 crores for our core lead acid business, sometimes for manufacturing technology, sometimes for automation and sometimes for capacity expansion.

items.statement: Revenue from Bangalore giga factory expected to commence in FY27 shortly; first NCM cylindrical line started customer sample deliveries
items.quote: We expect revenue contribution from the Bangalore plant to commence during FY27 shortly. Localization runs through all of this. What we are building is a genuinely Indian advanced chemistry cell platform, multiple chemistries, multiple form factors, strategic sourcing partnerships for raw materials, automation -led manufacturing and a global technology partnership.

items.statement: Automotive OEM demand sustained; replacement market robust; inverter battery seasonality 15-25% of revenue
items.quote: Yes, it will anywhere range between 15% to 25% based on the season.

items.statement: Engaging 3 major 2-wheeler OEMs covering 80-85% of EV market; 2 lines (NMC & LFP) starting commercial production in FY27
items.quote: We are talking to all the major OEMs, legacy as well as new. About 3 OEMs, I can tell you. And all these 3 contribute to about, let's say, 80% of the EV volume of the country.

items.statement: Chinese export controls on raw materials from November may require higher inventory; technology transfer embargoes a future risk
items.quote: Right now, no, because this export control announcements of Chinese government does not cover raw material as of yet. It will be from November. I think they have deferred it. We'll see what to do. This is not a ban. This is only additional approvals, which is required, it is a kind of export control.

items.statement: Target 50-60% bill of material localization in 2-3 years; electrolyte likely first component to be localized domestically
items.quote: our target or wish list, you can say, is to go to about 50% to 60% of bill of material localized in next 2 to 3 years. That's our road map. And that's why we are talking to multiple companies, everybody I'm ta lking to them, both for electrolyte for positives, for negatives

items.statement: Vacuum Salt and Bromine projects to reach full utilization in FY28, generating INR150-160 crore revenue with 40-45% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Roughly it will be around INR150 crores, INR160 crores of revenue and the margin will be in the range of around 40% to 45% kind of EBITDA margin.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR140-150 crores, mainly for Vacuum Salt and Bromine projects plus regular maintenance.
items.quote: Capex plan in FY27 will not be big, but roughly around INR140 crores, INR150 crores kind of a number, which is primarily in these two projects and the second will be some infrastructure projects in the factory and regular capex.

items.statement: Margins to moderate from current elevated levels and normalize on annual basis, not to be read as new run rate.
items.quote: Going forward, we expect margin to moderate from current level and revert to more normalized trend driven by the domestic demand, higher captive industry production and softening realization.

items.statement: Solar glass soda ash demand to rise from 1.5 lakh tonnes to 3.5 lakh tonnes as new capacities commission by Jan-Mar quarter.
items.quote: roughly 1.5 lakh tonnes of the soda ash gets consumed into the solar glass, which will go to roughly around 3.5 lakh tonnes once all the new capacity which has been planned, which is under implementation.

items.statement: Vacuum Salt and Bromine commercial production to start in Q2 FY27, with gradual ramp-up; full utilization in FY28.
items.quote: Both these projects, commercial production is expected in Q2 of this year.

items.statement: Global soda ash oversupply and weak prices persist; China demand recovery slow, high inventories, capacity rationalization delayed.
items.quote: Global soda ash market continues to face pressure with supply exceeding demand and price remains weak.

items.statement: Energy and raw material costs likely to rise in coming quarters due to ongoing global conflict.
items.quote: The ongoing global conflict is likely to feed into our energy and raw material costs over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Indian soda ash demand soft near term due to monsoon and higher imports, but structural demand from solar glass to improve over time.
items.quote: This situation may continue to persist in the near term with the onset of the monsoon season and some increase in imports.

items.statement: Greenfield soda ash project delayed due to land acquisition challenges; no timeline provided.
items.quote: the challenge which we are facing is more towards the -- major challenge is more towards the land acquisition and which I have mentioned in the past also. And at this point of time, I'm unable to give you a ki nd of a time line when this issue will get resolved.

items.statement: Imports from US, Turkey, China at landed cost $180-190; no anti-dumping duty, base duty 7.5%.
items.quote: Landed cost will be the same range of around, you can say, $180, $190 kind of a cost of those products to India.

items.statement: Monthly average soda ash imports rose to 73,000-74,000 tonnes in Q1 FY27 from 45,000-46,000 tonnes in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: which is again now elevated to 73,000 to 74,000 kind of a number. And these are the monthly average.

items.statement: Chinese synthetic soda ash producers making cash losses, leading to some long shutdowns and capacity regulation.
items.quote: as per our understanding, they are making cash losses at this point of time. That's the reason some of the plant has kind of taken a long shutdown to kind of regulate the capacity or the inventory part of it.

items.statement: Safeguard quantitative restrictions on soda ash imports under government consideration; no current restrictions.
items.quote: Safeguard quantitative restrictions is still under consideration of the government. So we will wait for that outcome of that.

items.statement: Net cash surplus over INR1,000 crores at end Q1 FY27; supports strategic capex and growth.
items.quote: We have net cash surplus of more than INR1,000 crores at the end of Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Guided FY27 India cement volume at 40 million tons; on track with 10.4-10.5 mt in Q1 and 9-9.5 mt expected in Q2
items.quote: I had guided in March concall that we should do 40 million tons in FY '26-'27. We have already done from Indian operation about 10.4, 10.5 in Q1. We are on track to do 9 to 9.5 in Q2.

items.statement: FY27 India capex guidance maintained at INR1,500 crores; INR456 crores spent in Q1
items.quote: Total capex I had guided Q4 about INR1,500 crores. For in Q1, we have done INR456 crores. I maintain my guidance at about INR1,500 crores for the year.

items.statement: Consolidated operational EBITDA per ton fell to INR1,111 in Q1 FY27 from INR1,339 in Q1 FY26 due to fuel and gypsum issues
items.quote: Operational EBITDA per ton was 1,339. Whereas this quarter, we have done 1,111, four times 1. So though we have taken the beating on EBITDA per ton

items.statement: Blended fuel cost peaked at INR1.95/kcal in Q1; may rise marginally by INR0.02-0.03 in Q2 but expected to stabilize or decline
items.quote: We are looking at 1.95 today. It may hardly go up by INR0.02, INR0.03 but that doesn't materially change the cost equation.

items.statement: Industry expected to grow 7-8% in FY27; Shree Cement targeting ~10% volume growth
items.quote: Pan-India, the industry is expected to grow at about 7% to 8%. We hope to catch up with 10%.

items.statement: Trade sales mix dropped to 62% in Q1 from 71% a year ago; blended ratio fell to 60% from 70%; aims to return to 70/30 trade/non-trade
items.quote: 62% is the trade against 71% in June '25. And 60% blended ratio against the 70% of June '25.

items.statement: Middle East war disrupted pet coke and gypsum supply, forcing shift to higher-cost coal and domestic gypsum, raising costs and lowering conversion factor
items.quote: Three things happened. Number one, the Pet Coke which were contracted for could not reach us, which had to make us shift the fuel from Pet Coke to coal.

items.statement: Consolidated volume reached 11.45 mt in Q1 FY27 vs 9.96 mt in Q1 FY26; consolidated operational EBITDA INR1,272 crores
items.quote: If you look at the consolidated, the volume stands at 114.5 for the quarter. Rajesh Ravi: Okay. Ashok Bhandari: The operational EBITDA without other income, repeat, without other income, stands at 1,272

items.statement: Freight lead distance reduced sequentially from 459 km to 445 km in Q1 FY27
items.quote: First on the lead distance, it has come down from 459 to 445.

items.statement: No plans for inorganic growth; not interested in buying assets at high valuations
items.quote: No, no, no. We are not in the inorganic game at all, my friend. As I said, we don't have the heart to buy a $5 EBITDA capacity at $110

items.statement: Depreciation guided at INR2,400-2,500 crores for FY27; tax rate ~30%
items.quote: INR2,400 to INR2,500 crores is the depreciation number, and tax rate would be about 30%.

items.statement: RMC revenue INR109 crores in Q1 FY27 (vs INR90 crores in Q4 FY26); currently profit-neutral, targeting 5% EBITDA margin eventually
items.quote: RMC revenue is INR109 crores for this quarter, INR90 crores for March '26, and INR40 crores for June '25.

items.statement: Renewable energy share increased from 61% to 66% in Q1; deploying 100 e-commercial vehicles and testing BESS
items.quote: You'll be surprised to know that our renewable energy component to total energy has increased from 61% to 66% in this quarter.

items.statement: Expect better profitability from Q2 onwards if Middle East situation remains stable; cost peak likely in Q1 not Q2
items.quote: I think we have almost peaked out in Q1. And if anything untoward doesn't happen in Middle East, this cost should more or less stabilize or rather go down.

items.statement: Northeast project approvals confirmed in place as of July 31 morning; media reports of protests dismissed
items.quote: Today morning 8:30, there was a meeting and all approvals are in place. This is as of today morning 8:30 meeting. So all your media reports you can put to you can snub them.

items.statement: UK EBITDA breakeven target pushed to 3Q or 4Q FY27 from earlier 2Q expectation
items.quote: It may be pushed by one quarter and may not be in 2Q but 3Q or 4Q. In the second half, we should be able to be closer to breakeven.

items.statement: Board approved 4.8 MTPA expansion at NINL for Rs 33,873 crores, taking site capacity to 6.2 MTPA
items.quote: The Board yesterday accorded the final investment approval for the 4.8 MTPA expansion in long products capacity covering wire rods and rebars, including solutions beyond that, at the NINL site for an investment of Rs. 33,873 crores towards the core project of the steelmaking steel capacity expansion.

items.statement: Maharashtra project recalibrated to 5 MTPA per blast furnace phase, targeting 15 MTPA total across three phases
items.quote: If you look at it from a productivity point of view and from an asset efficiency point of view, our view is that we will copy the 5 MTPA plants that is the reason, so the total Maharashtra volume eventually in phases can take in somewhere around 15 MTPA.

items.statement: India EBITDA per ton improved to Rs 19,162 in 1Q FY27 from Rs 15,907 in 4Q FY26
items.quote: India continues to deliver industry-leading margins. EBITDA per ton improved significantly from about Rs. 15,907 per ton in 4Q to about Rs. 19,162 per ton in 1Q.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA per ton tracking close to Rs 13,000 (15% margin) after Rs 1,200 crore unplanned cost increase from West Asia conflict
items.quote: On per ton basis, 1Q EBITDA improved by about Rs. 2,400 per ton YoY and by about Rs. 1,490 per ton on QoQ basis and is presently tracking close to about Rs 13,000 per ton consolidated levels, which is effectively a 15% margin.

items.statement: India realisations increased ~Rs 6,000 per ton QoQ offsetting lower volumes
items.quote: We were able to offset the impact of the lower volumes because of an increase in the reali sations to the tune of about Rs. 6,000 per ton, or Rs. 5,990 per ton to be more precise over 4Q

items.statement: European prices expected to rise incrementally in phases due to structural changes from CBAM and quota reductions
items.quote: I think there is still fairly a long runway as far as price increases are concerned in the European market. But it will happen in phases, incrementally, rather than a sharp uptick, because this is a structural change that is happening in the European market.

items.statement: Automotive & speciality business delivered best-ever 1Q volumes with 21% YoY growth in high-end sales
items.quote: The automotive & speciality business delivered best-ever 1Q volumes. It had a 21% YoY growth in high-end sales.

items.statement: Netherlands Direct Sheet Plant (20% of volumes) shut since April due to chrome emissions; 4-week trial restart approved from August 5
items.quote: The temporary shutdown of our Direct Sheet Plant has weighed on the operational performance because the Direct Sheet Plant, or DSP as we refer to it, is about 20% of our production in Netherlands, and that has been closed since the first week of April.

items.statement: Reassessing DRI-EAF investment in Netherlands due to regulatory uncertainties and need for viable risk-return profile
items.quote: We are currently reassessing the situation with all stakeholders to understand the investability of the DRI – EAF, the regulatory framework within which there is not just an investment case but also a sustenance case because these investments are done for 20 – 25 years.

items.statement: Capex spend of Rs 3,579 crores in 1Q FY27, majority in India; downstream expansions in tinplate, HRP galvanising, tubes on track
items.quote: We spent about Rs. 3,579 crores on capital expenditure during the quarter, of which the majority was in India.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs 84,000 crores, net debt/EBITDA at 2.3x within 2.5-3x target range; liquidity at Rs 45,950 crores
items.quote: On the balance sheet, net debt stands at about Rs. 84,000 crores and the net debt to EBITDA is comfortably at 2.3x, which is within our stated range of 2 .5 to 3 x through the

items.statement: Netherlands volumes and EBITDA expected to be better in 2Q than 1Q but lower than desired
items.quote: we expect volumes and EBIT DA to be better in 2Q than 1Q, lower than what we would like it to be, but certainly starting to move in the right direction

items.statement: NINL merger with Tata Steel expected to complete by end of FY27
items.quote: The merger process of NINL with Tata Steel is also progressing as per plan and is expected to be completed by the end of the current financial year.

items.statement: Indian operations resilient with 5.76 MT crude steel production; deliveries 5.17 MT after inventory drawdown in 4Q
items.quote: In India, crude steel 2 production was about 5.76 million tons, this was lower than the previous quarter because we had some shutdowns scheduled, and some operational issues which are behind us now

items.statement: India NSR expected to be Rs 1,500 per ton lower in Q2 vs Q1 FY27
items.quote: This quarter, we are saying will be about Rs 1,500 per ton lower than 1Q in India.

items.statement: UK NSR expected to increase £70-80 per ton in Q2 over Q1 FY27
items.quote: And as far as 2Q is concerned, it will be another £70 – £80 per ton increase is what we are expecting in 2Q over 1Q.

items.statement: Netherlands NSR expected to increase €10 per ton in Q2 over Q1 FY27
items.quote: this quarter the guidance is about €10 per ton increase.

items.statement: India EBITDA in rupee crore expected to be better in Q2 than Q1 FY27 despite margin compression
items.quote: we expect the rupees crore to be better in 2Q than in 1Q in India.

items.statement: UK spread expected to expand in Q2 FY27 between substrate and HR
items.quote: we will s ee spread expansion in UK in the second quarter between the substrate and the HR, because we are seeing improvement in the prices

items.statement: Netherlands spread expected to remain same in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The Netherlands spread is ballpark going to remain same

items.statement: India coking coal consumption cost expected at ~$184/t in Q2 FY27, up $5/t QoQ
items.quote: So, the consumption cost in 2Q for coking coal in India will be about $5 per ton higher

items.statement: Netherlands coking coal consumption cost expected up $10/t QoQ in Q2 FY27
items.quote: for Netherlands will be about $10 per ton higher.

items.statement: Ludhiana EAF plant built in 2 years with Rs 3,000 crore capex for 0.75 MTPA
items.quote: The other thing to keep in mind is the Ludhiana plant was built in two years. It is a 3,000-crore capex for a 0.75 MTPA plant, steelmaking and rolling plant.

items.statement: Planning similar EAF plants in west and south India, 0.8-0.9 MTPA each, 100-150 acres land, 2-year build
items.quote: Hence, we are also looking at building a similar plant in the west and in the south. And like I said, you need 100 – 150 acres of land, you can build it in two years and add point 0.8 – 0.9 million tons.

items.statement: Targeting EBITDA margin close to current levels despite iron ore cost increases via cost takeouts and downstream shift
items.quote: we are looking at how can you deliver an EBITDA margin close to what we are delivering today even if the iron ore prices go up. I think that is basically our objective.

items.statement: Netherlands DRI-EAF investment reassessment due to regulatory challenges, EU ETS dilution, CBAM impact, and social license concerns
items.quote: we are currently reassessing the situation with all stakeholders to understand the investability of the DRI – EAF, the regulatory framework within which there is not just an investment case but also a sustenance case

items.statement: Coke oven green push issue in Netherlands: currently at 98%+ reduction, but authorities pushing for zero green push and potential early closure by 2028-29
items.quote: today we are at 98% or 98%+ lower than what we were before. The requirement in Netherlands was to minimi se coke pushes, green pushes. And, but now that is being more specific to say there should be zero green push

items.statement: Depreciation to increase by Rs 300 crore per quarter (Rs 1,200 crore/year) due to accelerated amortization of mining assets ahead of 2030 reauction
items.quote: It will be about Rs 300 crores a quarter and Rs 1,200 crores every year additional depreciation in line so that there is not a big hit in 2030.

items.statement: Downstream focus: targeting 100kt shipbuilding steel in FY27 (domestic), growing to 0.5MTPA; expanding Tinplate, Tubes (1.5 to 4 MTPA), Wire (600kt to 1 MTPA); HR galvanizing line at Tarapur
items.quote: we are adding a HR galvani sing line in Tara pur, which is going to be state of the art hot roll ed galvanising line in India, nobody else has that, right, we are doubling our Tinplate capacity, packaging steel capacity

items.statement: India long products demand impacted by monsoon construction slowdown; auto demand strong supporting flat products
items.quote: Long products are impacted by construction activities slowing down during the monsoons. But I think we mentioned before, while there will be some margin compression in India, because there will be additional volumes in 2Q compared to 1Q

items.statement: Management expects mid-single-digit growth for the domestic tractor industry in FY27 and aims to outgrow the industry to gain market share.
items.quote: But yes, currently, we are looking at a middle or mid-single-digit growth for the financial year. So that is our current take as of now.

items.statement: Management expects tractor exports to be flat in FY27 and anticipates good growth in FY28, particularly if the North American market opens up.
items.quote: So this year, FY '27, we expect the export to be more or less flattish in nature. So even though Q1 has been down, but we think we'll be able to make it up in the balance 3 quarters.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 is INR 850-900 crores, including INR 450-500 crores for greenfield land acquisition and INR 350-400 crores for normal capex.
items.quote: So overall, you can say about INR850 crores to INR900 crores of capex for this year, including greenfield investment, which will happen.

items.statement: Tractor business faced ~5% commodity cost impact in Q1 FY27; an additional 1.5-2% cost pressure is expected in Q2, with potential reversal from Q4.
items.quote: Because 5% is still continuing. On top of that, we are talking about another 1.5% to 2% sort of pressure, which will be there. And we expect this will be a temporary phenomenon.

items.statement: A 1-1.5% price hike was taken in April for tractors; further price increases are under discussion for Q2 but quantum is not finalized and will not fully offset cost inflation.
items.quote: And then also one price increase we've taken in the month of April, which is about 1%, 1.5% sort of range, which also, to some extent, was able to offset this.

items.statement: Construction equipment prices increased ~6% effectively (including channel discount adjustments) in H1 FY27 due to commodity cost escalation; prices expected to stabilize in Q2.
items.quote: So price increase so far has been roughly about 5%, including the price increase, which we have taken in the month of January. Having said that, there is also adjustment of channel discounts, which have been done. So effectively, it is roughly about 6%, which has been passed on to the market.

items.statement: Domestic tractor industry grew 18.6% YoY in Q1 FY27 to a record 3.39 lakh units; management sees supportive underlying demand but flags monsoon distribution and festive season against high base as key monitorables.
items.quote: Following the strong industry performance in FY '26, the domestic tractor industry maintained its growth momentum in Q1 FY '27, achieving a record high first quarter volume of approximately 3.39 lakh

items.statement: Construction equipment industry expected to grow 12-15% in FY27, led by cranes and mini excavators; backhoe loaders and compactors seen growing 5-7% and 5-6% respectively.
items.quote: So we are anticipating anywhere around 12% to 15% overall in which there will be high growth for Mini Excavators and Cranes. We believe that backhoe loaders will grow at about 5% to 7% and Compactors also will grow at about 5% to 6%.

items.statement: New products driving share gains: Shaurya series in South, Promaxx contributing 20-22% of Farmtrac sales, Digitrac 4x4 contributing 23-25% of Powertrac portfolio; 4WD gap in 35-50 HP to be filled in coming months.
items.quote: Promaxx actually now contributes over 20% to 22% of the overall Farmtrac sales. And with Promaxx, we had been able to cater to the 4-wheel segment substantially, and that has helped us grow in the Farmtrac brand across the country.

items.statement: Dealer inventory at comfortable ~30 days; company plans to build stock for festive season starting October as agri demand is cyclical with big highs and lows.
items.quote: So you can look at about a 30 -day inventory with our dealers. And as we go forward into the season, this might see a change.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia disrupting supply chains and freight, causing commodity, logistics and imported component cost inflation; rupee depreciation adding to cost pressure.
items.quote: Geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia continue to disrupt supply chain and freight market. Shipping disruption and the depreciation of the Indian rupee against the U.S. dollar increased commodity, logistics and imported component costs.

items.statement: Captive finance penetration reached 10-12% in Q1 (15%+ in July) across 250 onboarded dealers; target 40-50% dealer coverage by FY27 and pan-India by FY28.
items.quote: So maybe by FY '28. But by FY '27, we expect almost 40%, 50% dealership will get covered. And then by FY '28, then we'll go pan-India.

items.statement: Component exports flat in Q1 FY27 at ~INR 160-170 crore base; management expects pickup in H2 and more than doubling over next 2 years.
items.quote: So last year, I think we did about INR 160 crores, INR170 crores in terms of overall numbers. So this year, so far, first quarter was more or less flat. But in the second half, we expect the pickup will start happening.

items.statement: Buyback scope limited due to promoter holding ~68% and total non-public ~70%; cannot exceed 5% without delisting; capital allocation strategy under review but requires promoter alignment.
items.quote: So the scope for further buyback is very limited. You can't go beyond 5% if you were to continue to be listed. So yes, possibility definitely exists, but this is one of our capital allocation strategy going forward.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA INR845 crore, up 65% YoY; PAT INR490 crore, up 101% YoY; net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.4x
items.quote: Operating EBITDA increased to a record INR845 crores, up 65% Y-o-Y and 139% sequentially, while EBITDA margin improved to 26% compared with 19% in the same quarter last year and about 12% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Capex of over INR500 crore incurred in Q1 FY27; total project spend till Q1 ~INR3,850 crore; both projects within approved envelope
items.quote: During the quarter, we incurred capex of over INR500 crores as we progress our strategic growth project. Even after these investment, net debt reduced to INR4,719 crores.

items.statement: Gopalpur TAN project ~96% complete, Dahej nitric acid project ~93% complete; both expected to commence operations in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Both of our projects are now in the final stage of execution. The Gopalpur TAN project is approximately 96% complete, and the Dahej nitric acid project is approximately 93% complete. Commissioning activities are underway, and both projects are expected to commence operations during Q2 FY 27.

items.statement: Equinor LNG supplies commenced in May; first cargo received; phase-in/phase-out of existing contracts to complete by Q4 FY27; Equinor gas commercially favourable with sizable savings
items.quote: One of our most important development during the quarter was the commencement of supplies u nder our long- term LNG agreement with Equinor, with the first cargo received in May. This mark s an important milestone in our integration journey

items.statement: Mining chemicals volume 130 KT in Q1, impacted by PESO portal changes; normalization expected; B2C revenue grew 42% to INR151 crore (17% of segment)
items.quote: Mining chemical delivered a resilient quarter despite temporary disruptions from the changes in PESO portal, while the volume were lower at 130 KT, stronger realization helped drive revenue to around INR911 crores, up 37% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Crop nutrition revenue INR1,367 crore, up 9% YoY; manufactured NPK sales grew 4%; specialty and Croptek products contribute 43% of segment revenue
items.quote: Crop nutrition operated in a challenging environment due to delayed monsoon, elevated input cost, and inadequate subsidy alignment. Despite these headwinds, the business remain resilient, delivering revenue of around INR1,367 crore s, up 9% Y -o-Y.

items.statement: Specialty and customized products driving customer stickiness and price premiums across all three businesses; B2C, Croptek, and downstream specialties improving earnings quality
items.quote: Last but not the least at all, is our growing core strength emerging from our transformative shift into specialty and customized products for all our three businesses. And this we see is increasingly coming out to be very strongly reflected in our results by way of the undercurrent of customer stickiness, customer preference, and above all, price premiums.

items.statement: Middle East war volatility strains phos acid, sulphur and raw material sourcing for fertilizers; needs faster government subsidy corrections; Russian FGAN export ban possible from October
items.quote: However, with the Middle East war scenario still hovering and bringing along with it its own set of volatility, somewhere sourcing and prices of phos acid, sulphur, and other raw materials for the fertilizer business will be under somewhat of a strain, and will need for faster decisions on the subsidy corrections by the government.

items.statement: Geopolitical supply disturbances can impact business; but structural changes (ammonia integration, Equinor LNG, new capacities, specialty shift) reduce severity of past volatility
items.quote: Now, with these things in place, what we are confident as a management, the kind of a volatility the business has seen in past, will not have a similar volatility. Yes, some volatility will continue. Deepak Fertilisers and That's business, and the business do depends on international, a lot of international factors which comes and impact

items.statement: Net debt INR4,719 crore; debt/EBITDA 1.4x; near peak debt; deleveraging expected to start as new capacities contribute EBITDA and cash flow from FY27 onward
items.quote: On the balance sheet, continue to strengthen despite being in peak of our investment cycle. During the quarter, we incurred capex of over INR500 crores as we progress our strategic growth project. Even after these investment, net debt reduced to INR4,719 crores, and our debt/EBITDA improved to 1.4x.

items.statement: DMSL explosives acquisition completed in May; upgrading facility for safety/quality; will roll out TCO-based mining solutions model; no decision yet on DMSL listing structure (IPO vs demerger)
items.quote: So, as you rightly mentioned, we completed the acquisition of an explosives company in May this year, which we had announced to the stock exchange as well. And the p urpose of that acquisition is to complete our value chain, make it even stronger as we develop the mining solutions business

items.statement: Industrial chemicals: nitric acid stable, contract-linked margins; IPA volume recovery expected as propylene availability improves; long-term average margins with quarterly volatility
items.quote: Nitric acid business is more, I'll say, majority of the capacity which is CNA is a long -term contract-driven business, broadly linked to, I call it in a linked to the feed stock. So, it's more stable business, comes with a stabl e margin, predictable business

items.statement: TAN margins expected to normalize to consistent medium-term levels; near-term elevated due to Middle East conflict; Russian export ban risk from October could sustain tight supply
items.quote: Tarun Sinha: Yeah. Thanks. This is Tarun here. Essentially, and this is a similar question which we have addressed in the in some of the prior calls as well, like this. We've always maintained that the medium-term to long-term horizon, you know, margin levels would be very consistent as far as TAN business

items.statement: Double-digit revenue growth expected to sustain in FY27, supported by full quarter impact of price increases in Q2, festive demand, and distribution expansion.
items.quote: Business outlook for ﬁnancial year 27, double-digit revenue growth expected to sustain, supported by the full quarter impact of price increases in quarter two

items.statement: Operating margins expected to remain within guided range of 15% to 17% for FY27.
items.quote: Operating margins are expected to remain within the guided range, which we have always said, that is between 15% and 17%.

items.statement: Monsoon progressing well with more dry days supporting exterior paint offtake; rural sentiment may improve.
items.quote: Well-progressing monsoon may support rural sentiment. Market competitiveness, however, is expected to stay elevated.

items.statement: Macro environment dynamic; crude oil, currency, and geopolitical developments being closely monitored.
items.quote: Macroenvironment remains dynamic, with crude oil, currency, and geopolitical developments being closely monitored.

items.statement: Tinting machine installations crossed 2,100 in Q1; target 10,000 for FY27, mostly in under-indexed markets.
items.quote: our aspiration is to try and touch 10,000 machines. 138 00:21:50.760 --> 00:22:05.700 Abhijit Roy: For the year. Last year, we were very close to that ﬁgure. This year, we expect that we should be able to again touch 10,000 numbers

items.statement: Operating margin expected to grow at a decent pace year-on-year in Q2 if raw material prices hold and selling prices are not dropped.
items.quote: That is why I'm saying there are too many ifs and buts, but in the second quarter, I expect that the operating margin will grow at a decent pace.

items.statement: Operating margin improvement in Q2 is year-on-year, not sequential, due to seasonally lower value sales in Q2.
items.quote: It is year-on-year that I am talking about.

items.statement: Price increases have been absorbed with volume growth intact, delivering double-digit value growth.
items.quote: And yet, you know, the entire pricing… price increase has been absorbed, and, you know, therefore the value growth is coming at a decent level in double digits.

items.statement: Sellout in July was much better than last year; August expected to be similar, overcoming dealer upstocking.
items.quote: But as I said, you know, much of it is also that the sellouts will be far better this year, which we saw in July also, the sellout was much better than last year .

items.statement: Volume growth improvement driven by favorable weather versus last year's excessive rains and early Diwali; price hike impact neutralized.
items.quote: In all possibility, even though the prices have gone up, and it should have impacted the volume growth, that impact will be more or less neutralized by these favorable weather conditions.

items.statement: Construction chemicals now 10-12% of decorative revenue, growing significantly faster than paint.
items.quote: Right? You know, as far as the, you know, percentage is concerned, it is in now, about 10-12% level.

items.statement: Mix shift toward low-value, high-volume construction chemicals creates 2-3% volume-value gap differential.
items.quote: So, that's the reason why you don't see the full extent of the volume-value gap, which otherwise should have reﬂected, you know, with the type of price increase that has happened.

items.statement: Price cuts post-Diwali possible only if raw material prices fall substantially and peace prevails; too early to comment.
items.quote: But as of now, very, very diƯicult to say, and I don't think anyone should comment at this stage what will happen in the second half is too far oƯ.

items.statement: Capex for the year estimated at Rs 600-800 crore as Panagar project starts at fiscal year-end.
items.quote: So, roughly it will be 600 to 800 rupees for the year.

items.statement: Backward integration pursued where feasible; emulsants, resins, thickeners now made in-house; Dow tie-up for Monsens to be manufactured at Sandhilla, Lucknow.
items.quote: Recently, we had a tie-up with Dow, for one of the Monsens, which we were buying from them, and now we are going to manufacture the same in our unit in Sandhilla, in Lucknow.

items.statement: Subsidiary margins expected to stay okay; corrective measures in Bollocks and STP should yield good results in Q2 and Q3.
items.quote: I think, you know, it should yield very good results, you know, in this quarter and going forward in Q1.

items.statement: Q1 market share gained slightly; growth higher in South, North, West; East muted, Northeast hit by floods, West Bengal in transition.
items.quote: Second question, answer is, you know, that, overall, you know, the growth rate has been higher, possibly in the south and the north, to some extent west. East has actually been a little bit muted.

items.statement: Industrial business (~20% of revenue) price increases delayed vs decorative; benefit flows into Q2, aiding margin vs peers.
items.quote: Also, the essential diƯerence is that we have a higher percentage of industrial business than them. It's almost 20% for us, and in their case, it might be much lower.

items.statement: Other income rose sharply due to higher cash balances and treasury income.
items.quote: So, it's out of our Treasury incomes.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected at 25% YoY, with volume growth possibly 30%.
items.quote: And for FY27, we expect a growth of 25% compared to last financial year.

items.statement: Targeting ~20% CAGR over coming years.
items.quote: targeting a growth trajectory of approximately 20% CAGR over the coming years.

items.statement: New plant targeted for commissioning by 31st March FY28.
items.quote: Our internal target date to commission the plant is -- 31st March FY28.

items.statement: New facility peak revenue potential ~INR300 crores.
items.quote: to answer your -- this peak question of the revenue potential from the new facility, it will be about INR300 crores.

items.statement: Margins likely to rise due to input cost pass-through and operating leverage; 28.5-29% possible.
items.quote: Yes, theoretically, that should happen, and this is what we are going to strive to achieve.

items.statement: Full pass-through of raw material and natural gas cost increases effective 1st July 2027.
items.quote: With increase in the input cost of various raw materials and natural gas, we would be having price correction on upward basis, and this will be effective 1st July '27.

items.statement: Sequential top-line improvement expected for several quarters; demand strong across 9 sectors.
items.quote: There will be a sequential improvement in top line from here on for several quarters.

items.statement: GET revenue share to rise from <1% now to 4.5-5% by FY29; FY27 ~3.5%.
items.quote: As of now, it's less than 1%. But by FY29, we expect this to reach 4.5% to 5%.

items.statement: U.S. railroad opportunity deprioritized due to better opportunities elsewhere.
items.quote: We are not pursuing the U.S. railroad for the time being because there are many opportunities in better markets, better products, better pricing.

items.statement: Defense given low priority due to high customer concentration risk and better pricing elsewhere.
items.quote: Defense side, we are pursuing, but we are giving that lately past 1 year a low priority because the opportunities, the pricing is far better than defense in what we are doing.

items.statement: Management reaffirms high single-digit revenue growth guidance for full year FY27
items.quote: Think we should stick on to the high single-digit growth for the full year.

items.statement: Organon acquisition expected to close in Q4 FY27
items.quote: We expect the acquisition to be completed in Q4 of financial year '27 and an integration management office has been working on day one preparedness.

items.statement: Gross margin at 80.5% in Q1 FY27, higher year-on-year due to better product mix
items.quote: Gross margin was at 80.5% for the quarter, higher than the same period last year, mainly on account of better product mix.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 28.9% in Q1 FY27, slightly lower year-on-year due to Lenalidomide benefit in prior year
items.quote: EBITDA margins came in at 28.9% while EBITDA margins were slightly lower, please note that Q1 FY26 had some benefit from Lenalidomide sales.

items.statement: R&D spend at INR 8,264 million (5.4% of sales) in Q1 FY27, with 30% for innovative medicines
items.quote: Consolidated investments towards R&D for Q1 FY27 stands at INR8,264 million or 5.4% of sales. Innovative R&D accounted for 30% of our total R&D spend.

items.statement: India formulations sales grew 16% year-on-year to INR 54,749 million in Q1 FY27, driven by volume and new products
items.quote: Sales of India formulations were INR 54,749 million for the quarter, recording a growth of 16%.

items.statement: U.S. business sales declined 9.7% year-on-year to USD 427 million in Q1 FY27 due to Lenalidomide erosion and generic competition
items.quote: Overall, the U.S. business reported sales of USD427 million for the quarter, declining by 9.7%.

items.statement: Emerging markets formulations revenue grew 4.2% year-on-year to USD 311 million in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our formulations revenues in emerging markets were USD311 million, up by 4.2% over quarter 1 last year.

items.statement: Innovative medicines sales grew 12.8% year-on-year to USD 351 million in Q1 FY27, driven by ILUMYA, ODOMZO and CEQUA
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, our innovative medicine sales were up 12.8% to reach USD351 million.

items.statement: Leqselvi surpassed 1,000 prescribers in June 2026 with strongest month since launch
items.quote: In the month of June, we surpassed 1,000 prescribers, and we also delivered our strongest month since launch, demonstrating increased adoption and growing confidence in the brand.

items.statement: Unloxcyt showing month-over-month growth as more cancer centers add to formularies
items.quote: Similar to Leqselvi, we continue to see month-over-month growth as more cancer centers and integrated health systems add Unloxcyt to their formularies.

items.statement: Organon acquisition-related costs of INR 1,617 million charged in Q1 FY27, with additional charges expected in subsequent quarters
items.quote: Exceptional items for Q1 FY27 include a charge of INR1,617 million towards Organon's acquisition-related costs. There would be additional charges on this account in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Emerging markets growth impacted by geopolitical issues and difficult macroeconomic conditions in certain countries
items.quote: I think emerging markets, I would characterize the impact as a combination of both the geopolitical issues and difficult macroeconomic conditions in certain countries.

items.statement: Net cash position of $3.4 billion at consolidated level as of Q1 FY27
items.quote: Balance sheet of Sun continues to be strong with a net cash of $3.4 billion at the consolidated level.

items.statement: Semaglutide auto-injector launched in India (March 2026), South Africa (launched), Brazil (expected shortly)
items.quote: Sun Pharma is the only company in India offering semaglutide auto-injector and the device has received a positive feedback from health care professionals for enabling smooth initiation and significantly reducing needle phobia.

items.statement: Ecosis recycling project to stabilize by end of FY27; FY28 utilization above 80%, reaching near 100% by year-end.
items.quote: FY28, I think our utilization should be close to above 80% a year as a whole, it will progress slowly. But year as a whole, I think we should be able to do 80%. And by the end of the year, we should be close to 100%.

items.statement: Ecosis to contribute INR80-85 crores EBITDA, primarily next year; other projects add INR140-150 crores this year.
items.quote: Ecosis, which is going to deliver around anything to INR80 to INR90 crores of EBITDA, that is going to come primarily in next year. But other than that, most of it will come in this year only.

items.statement: INR690 crores capex program progressing; PFI expansion 50% complete by Sep 2026, balance by Oct 2026.

The election and commissioning activities are in full swing. We expe

items.quote: By September, this should get commercialized. It was supposed to get commercialized in July, August, but due to certain hiccups, it got delayed by 1 or 2 months.

items.statement: Ecosis EBITDA margin minimum 30%, potentially higher.
items.quote: EBITDA margin will be minimum 30%, it can be more, but minimum 30% for sure.

items.statement: PFI expansion to add INR400 crores annual revenue; INR150-200 crores this year.
items.quote: So top line would increase by around INR400 crores, because some of it was already there in the chip form. So around INR400 crores, I think, top line should increase in the full year. This year, it might be around INR200 crores or INR150 crores, because this year will be hardly utilizing around 5 - 5.5 months.

items.statement: Raw material price increases passed on to customers, maintaining or improving margins.
items.quote: So this is like a price rise in the raw material prices only, for us because if the duty is not there, then the domestic prices also get reduced. Once the duty is incorporated, then the domestic players increase their prices, also the import prices increase. So we pass it on to the customers, and we have been successfu

items.statement: Demand stable with need-based buying; margins improved from May, July similar to June.
items.quote: Yes, July was also similar to June. And we see it improving only going further.

items.statement: Increasing FDY and cationic yarn production for value-added mix.
items.quote: Product mix changing, we've already explained. We are putting more FDY. We are going to increase our production of cationic yarn.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions and raw material volatility pose near-term risks.
items.quote: Although the intensity of the conflict in West Asia moderated from the disruption witnessed during the previous quarter, geopolitical tensions involving the United States, Iran and the broader Middle East continues to create uncertainty across global petro products and energy markets.

items.statement: Debt to increase to INR350-370 crores by year-end; net debt INR150-200 crores.
items.quote: By the end of the year, our debt would be in the vicinity of INR350 crores to INR370 crores from the -- but net debt, if you see, I think net debt, we might be around INR150 crores to INR200 crores.

items.statement: Inventory gains of INR15-17 crores in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: I think it could be in the vicinity of around INR15 crores to INR17 crores.

items.statement: Employee reduction of 180-200 to save INR4-5 crores annually.
items.quote: Yes, but overall, I think we should save in a year INR4 crores to INR5 crores, but it will enhance the quality of the products, maybe some productivity will also increase. So that's why we have undertaken this. So we'll be able to reduce around 180 to 200 people.

items.statement: Ecosis product sold at INR140-150 per kg for chips.
items.quote: Chips could -- I mean, from what we have sold small quantities, the prices are very high. , and we have sold at around INR140, INR150.

items.statement: Management assures double-digit revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: I would like to stick to my statement saying that we will show double-digit growth no matter what.

items.statement: Three major capex projects ~70% complete; ~₹1,400 crores capitalized of ₹2,000 crores total
items.quote: So that's about, I would say, one that we declared to the stock market earlier was the 3 projects together about, if I remember correctly, ₹ 2,000 crores. So I would say 70% of that has been capitalized so far.

items.statement: Capitalized assets of ₹451 crores in Q1 FY27; CWIP at ₹2,034 crores as of June 30, 2026

items.statement: Three major dedicated projects in validation; commercial supply expected after regulatory approvals
items.quote: we have done -- we have gone through validations of the 3 large projects we have done and several other projects are on the pipeline

items.statement: Gross margin ~68% in Q1 FY27; full-year gross margin expected ~60%; EBITDA margin similar to last year
items.quote: At gross level, I would say it was approximately 60% all over the year. And frankly speaking, if I'm looking at EBITDA margin, it would be the similar as last year.

items.statement: Solvent costs remain elevated due to Middle East situation; price increases passed to customers where feasible
items.quote: While prices of certain raw materials moderated during the quarter, solvent costs remain elevated for a significant part of the period. We con tinue to engage closely with the customers to evaluate commercially appropriate mechanisms to mitigate these costs wherever feasible

items.statement: Generic pricing uptick driven by raw material cost pass-through, not market correction

items.statement: Custom Synthesis projects progressing across clinical, validation and commercial stages; peptides expanding with multiple 3,000L SPPS additions
items.quote: Peptides remain a strategic area of investment for the Company. items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue mix: Custom Synthesis 60%, Generics 40%; Nutraceuticals ₹298 crores
items.quote: The business mix for the quarter reflected Custom Synthesis contributing 60% of the revenue and Generics accounting for 40%, respectively.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty in West Asia affecting supply chains, freight rates, container availability and solvent pricing

items.statement: Maintaining 3-month rolling inventory buffer for critical materials to secure supply continuity
items.quote: We are currently stocking it on a 3 monthly basis. Like any given point of day for the next 3 months, are we secured for our production.

items.quote: In overall 3 to 4 -year period, we are looking at INR300 crores to INR350 crores of revenue -- additional revenue.

items.quote: So w here we are expecting for that particular product, we will be putting about INR25-odd crores.

items.quote: So Kemin, probably our offtake will increase by 20% to 40%.

items.quote: I think it should be sustainable, and we had no real advantage of cheap raw material.

items.quote: Wherever we had long -term contracts, we are respecting most of them. And -- so in that case, we are not able to pass on. And also, it is not like -- I mean, we were not able to pass on 100%.

items.statement: Demand environment steady; Q1 volume decline due to supply chain disruptions (2 weeks shutdown)
items.quote: The demand environment continues to be steady.

items.statement: HALS export mix ~50% in Q1 vs fully domestic first year; higher grade mix improving
items.quote: In contrast, the current quarter reflects a much more diversified geographical mix with exports contributing nearly 50% of the HALS sales.

items.statement: Raw material price volatility and shipping vessel availability remain key risks
items.quote: The issues which I mentioned with availability of -- the prices are volatile. That is still an issue, but the availability is there, which was not the case in quarter 1.

items.statement: Netherlands subsidiary operational from mid-September to serve Europe demand

items.quote: On the expense side, if you look at the current QoQ expense increase, that annualises to about 12.5%, so we’ll probably end up around 10% or so - that’s my sense - which is what you can expect.

items.statement: International impact expected much less than last year; planned initiatives should show better results in coming months.

items.statement: Closing-sales team to nearly double from ~34 to ~60 by December 2026.

items.statement: Historically converted up to 80% of incremental revenue into EBITDA; expects non-linear expansion once growth re-accelerates.
items.quote: However, historically, when growth accelerates, margins improve fairly quickly - we have converted as high as 80% of incremental revenue into EBITDA.

items.statement: In one recent year, top line rose 20 crore and EBITDA rose 15 crore, showing non-linear expansion.
items.quote: in one recent year, when the top line increased by 20 crore, our EBITDA increased by 15 crore in just one year.

items.statement: Quarterly contract prices increased; deferred revenue at all-time high; ASP saw minor increase, stabilising.

items.statement: VC was over a third of revenue at peak; now lower as IB and corporate sales grow share.

items.statement: Both IFM and BSS expected to grow low double-digit, around 9-12%, keeping revenue mix steady.

items.statement: Matrix EBGC margin profile believed sustainable for the year on volume growth and cost optimization.
items.quote: So for this year, we do believe that these volumes and these margins are sustainable.

items.statement: IFM margins believed to have bottomed and will not decline further.

items.statement: Cash of over INR300 crores to be used for inorganic, brownfield growth and shareholder rewards.

items.quote: Where we have declared a dividend of INR1 per share, which will take away about INR7 crores of cash.

items.statement: Labor shortage is real in southern, western and NCR markets; pass-through model used with customers.
items.quote: That said, labor shortages are real. And there are many areas, for example, if you look at Gujarat, if you look at some areas of Tamil Nadu, if you look at some areas of Maharashtra, finding labor is an issue.

items.statement: Audit and Assurance pipeline healthy from large multinational audits; results expected in H2 FY27.
items.quote: Results are expected in H2 of '27, and you will start seeing those trends.

items.statement: EBGC seeing green shoots with IT hiring pickup; subdued hiring in banking and BPO persists.

items.statement: Avon increasing contribution of higher-margin value-added services in enterprise transport and logistics.
items.quote: During the quarter, Avon also continued to strengthen its portfolio by increasing the contributions of higher -margin value -added services, particularly in enterprise transport and logistics solutions.

items.statement: IFM continuing to shift mix towards higher-margin specialized technical services.
items.quote: share with existing marquee clients and continuing to shift our mix towards higher -margin specialized technical services.

items.quote: Through agentic AI, it offers an opportunity for us to enter these segments without committing to large real estate and without committing to a large number of people, et cetera.

items.statement: GCC focus being added to business development; current GCC exposure limited.
items.quote: So right now, it's not impacting us too much, but we are looking at it. We have put in place a team which will start looking at growth opportunities, including GCC.

items.statement: No formal guidance given; Q1 numbers can be used as indicator to extrapolate.
items.quote: We normally don't give formal guidance. So I think we will continue with that. What we have said, I mean, you can take our Q1 number as an indicator.

items.statement: Expect organic growth in FY27 to be better than FY26 with acceleration in second half
items.quote: On that basis, we expect our organic growth in FY27 to be better than FY26, and we anticipate an acceleration in the second half.

items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter was INR1,795 million at a margin of 16.9%. On a reported basis, that is 50 basis points higher quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Continue to expense proprietary tech stack investments including data layer, Cortex platform, and agent layer to keep P&L clean
items.quote: We continue to invest heavily in our tech stack. This is our proprietary tech stack. We continue to invest in that. I would say we have ratcheted up the investments a bit over there because we're investing in a data layer where we have our own data integrating with various data sources.

items.statement: Signed 1 deal in $3-5M range, 4 deals in $1-3M range, plus sub-million deals with expansion potential
items.quote: In Enterprise Commercial segment, we signed 1 deal in the $3 million to $5 million range, where a top 5 customer selected us to migrate the ir content platform. We also signed 4 deals with annual contracts in the $1 million to $3 million range, three in commercial and one in medical

items.statement: Customer enthusiasm for AI is real but enterprise adoption remains measured; view this as opportunity
items.quote: Across our conversations, customers are genuinely excited about the potential of AI. And when they are ready to move, that excitement is translating to real expanding work. What we are also seeing is that while the enthusiasm is real, enterprise adoption remains measured and the pace of change on the ground is slower.

items.statement: Revenue from accounts beyond top 20 now 33.4% of total, up from 2.5x YoY; active clients 105
items.quote: Revenues from accounts beyond our top 20 has almost doubled year-on-year in rupee terms and now contributes 33.4% of total revenue.

items.statement: Key risk is US regulatory policy outlook; currently stable with drug pricing and MFN decisions largely behind industry
items.quote: What we keep a look out for is the regulatory environment and the policy decisions, especially in the U.S., which impacts this industry the most. But having said that, currently, the policy outlook is stable. The drug pricing and the MFN-related decisions are largely behind this industry, and the new launch pipeline is very healthy and robust.

items.statement: Gen AI driving price deflation but Indegene converts deflation into volume and share gains due to outcome-based model
items.quote: On economics, Gen AI is driving price deflation. Incumbents at very large scale lack the growth headroom to offset falling prices. We are the opposite. Large enough to serve global clients end-to-end, nimble enough to convert deflation into new volumes and share gains.

items.statement: Workforce transformation had one-time margin impact in Q1 but will reduce employee costs and temper wage hike impact going forward
items.quote: First, we have invested in workforce transformation that had a onetime impact on margins this quarter but will have a long-term impact in reducing our employee cost as well as tempering the impact of wage hikes going forward.

items.statement: Tectonic engagement expanded from Germany to Spain; omnichannel deal revenue recognition starts Q3 FY27

And with revenue expected to be recognized starting Q3 FY27, it adds to our H2 revenues with costs already being incurred in the P&L

items.statement: Revenue per employee ~$77,000 on trailing 12-month basis, up 25% over 2 years

items.statement: Currency volatility mitigated by designated hedge accounting adopted last quarter; undesignated hedges material till December 2025
items.quote: We have in the last quarter moved our accounting to the designated hedge accounting as per the accounting standards. items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crores

items.quote: Our order book stands at approximately INR61,500 crores, the highest in our history, up from INR50,000 crores just a quarter ago, with about INR16,000 crores in new orders won in this quarter alone.

items.quote: Our announced capex programs total around INR31,500 crores, of which we have already deployed around INR9,450-odd crores as of 30th of June. It is around 30% in FY27, roughly 40% in '28 and around 30% in FY29.

items.quote: Our overall realization and net EBITDA margin from U.S. facility can range somewhere between USD0.07 to USD0.08 per watt peak basis.

items.quote: If you look at the approval that we have taken from Board and shareholders to have around INR10,000 crores worth of fund raised through various channels, including equity. Right now, our balance sheet stands at around INR7,000 crores worth of cash available as of 30th of June.

items.statement: BESS Phase 1: 3.5 GWh cell, 5.15 GWh pack/container; 90-95% site construction done; commercial production within FY27
items.quote: Our capex of BESS cell manufacturing along with pack and container is well in shape and as per plan. We are already at the verge of starting our cell production over the next 2 quarters. items.statement: India solar additions growing from 38 GW in 2025 to ~100 GW by 2035 (10% CAGR); global additions 698 GW to 993 GW (4-5% CAGR)
items.quote: India additions are growing much faster from 38 gigawatt in '25 to around 100 gigawatt by 2035, are 10% CAGR over next 10 years.

items.quote: On the capacity, we commissioned an additional 3 gigawatt of module capacity at our SMS plant, Samakhiali, Gujarat in April '26 Waaree Energy Storage Solutions commenced the automated BESS container production at 5.15 gigawatt hours.

items.statement: Cell production ramp: 800 MW Q1, 1.2 GW Q2, 1.5 GW Q3, 1.5+ GW Q4; module utilization 70-75% in Q3/Q4
items.quote: As our cell capacity comes on stream, our cell production ramped sharply through the year from around 800 megawatts in Q1 FY27 to around 1.2 gigawatts in Q2, around 1.5 gigawatt in Q3 and over and above in Q4.

items.statement: Non-DCR market offtake delayed due to ALMM-II transition; 6-month extension given; offtake expected to ramp from Q2
items.quote: In India also, the non-DCR market where the ALMM -II facility came in 1 st of June. The order came in effect 1st of June. And now the government has given a window of around next five to six months of time, we are looking at large offtake from the customers

items.quote: So yes, INR75 crores EBITDA and INR40 crores PAT is the kind of numbers that we are fairly confident of achieving.

items.statement: Expects lending disbursements to reach INR1,000 crores per quarter in coming quarters.
items.quote: we feel very comfortable about generating at least a INR1,000 crores disbursal in every quarter going forward.

items.quote: on a long-range basis we believe that this will continue to be between 4.5% to 5.5%.

items.quote: Roughly INR25 crores is what we have available to buy more devices out of the IPO proceeds.

items.quote: Direct costs have been brought down 21% YoY. For payments side, the direct cost was down 15%. Lending side, the direct cost was down 40%.

items.quote: And we are targeting Punjab to give us next year about close to INR30,000 per ton.

items.quote: So this year, out of the 9,000 addition, we should do about 7,500 tons additional over last year's capacity.

items.quote: We have done, let's say, about last year, if I look at the entire year, we have done about INR11,000 and odd per ton at Silvassa.

items.statement: Spreads improved across all three verticals from Q4 to Q1.

items.statement: Management reiterated confidence in delivering double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for FY27.

items.statement: Management stated comfort with average net debt to EBITDA of 2.5x in coming years, up and down in some quarters.

items.quote: we already operate a very significant good EBITDA, we are around 50%, and we intend to maintain that and marginally grow it year-on-year as our RevPAR grows.
