items.statement: Cost of borrowing fell to 10.1%, a 64 bps year-on-year improvement and nearly 300 bps lower than FY2021 levels.
items.quote: During Q1 FY2027, our cost of borrowing stood at 10.1%, down 64 basis points year-on-year, and nearly 300basis points lower than the 13% level seen in FY2021.

items.statement: Healthy demand persists in MSME and micro-enterprise segments; disbursement growth driven by deeper penetration and expanded touch points.
items.quote: The sharp increase in the disbursements was primarily driven by the last few quarters execution of deeper penetration that we were doing through our increased touch points, which brought strong demand from the MSME and SME segment.

items.statement: FCCB conversion of ~$44 million underway; committee meeting scheduled for conversion which will reduce leverage further.
items.quote: we also have about $44 million worth of foreign currency convertible bonds due for conversion which can get converted at any point of time. And if you see today we have our committee meeting scheduled for the same for conversion of those bonds

items.statement: AI deployment expanded: 180k onboarding applications, 500k voice-to-data conversions, 200k daily outbound calls, and AI bots increased from 7 to 18.
items.quote: During the quarter, we processed approximately 1,80,000 customer on-boarding applications compared with about 1,60,000 applications in Q4 FY2026. We also completed approximately 5,00,000 voice-to-data convergence versus 3,50,000 in the previous quarter. AI-enabled outbound engagement increased to approximately 2,00,000 calls per day from around 1,50,000 calls per day in Q4 FY2026. In parallel, the

items.statement: Distribution network expanded to 5,995 touch points across 23 states, up 696 points over the last four quarters.
items.quote: As the end of Q1 FY2027, our network comprised of 5,995 touch points spread across 23 states, reflecting the scale we have built through a combination of branch-led expansion and asset-led operating model.

items.statement: Business correspondent franchise crossed USD 1 billion in gross transaction value.
items.quote: Our business correspondent franchise crossed USD 1 billion in gross transaction value. A powerful validation of the scalability of our asset-light distribution model

items.statement: Internal leverage comfort zone at 3.5x debt-to-equity; current level ~2.5x including unconverted FCCBs.
items.quote: we feel being somewhere between a three-and-a-half level is fairly comfortable for us. Because we also have if you may have missed on it, we also have about $44 million worth of foreign currency convertible bonds due for conversion which can get converted at any point of time.

items.statement: Co-lending with SBI remains at status quo pending bank-side compliance; disbursements slow but expected to progress soon.
items.quote: The lending status for the co-lending tie-up remains as that of last quarter itself. So we are at a status quo level. We are still awaiting the compliance to be completed at the bank side before we can start working on it.

items.statement: Promoters acquired 4.7% from open market in FY2027, nearing SEBI's 5% annual limit; pledged shares reduced quarter-on-quarter.
items.quote: promoters have already acquired4.7% from the open markets. SEBI allows the promoter and the promoter group to only acquire up to 5% equity by any of its equity instruments in one financial year, which we have largely exhausted. In terms of the pledge, if you see on a quarter-on-quarter comparison, adjacent quarters, the pledge has come down.

items.statement: Expect another quarter of sequential growth and confident of delivering top-quartile growth for the full year
items.quote: Even so, we expect another quarter of sequential growth. We have also crossed an annualized revenue run rate of over USD 500 million, an important milestone for the company. While quarterly growth will naturally vary, we see good client conversations, a healthy pipeline, and encouraging momentum.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 24% to 28% for the full year
items.quote: Despite all of this, we are confident of meeting the stated EBITDA range of 24% to 28% for the full year.

items.statement: Capex estimate for the full year is INR 130 crores to INR 150 crores
items.quote: No, whole year. INR 130 crores to INR 150 crores, let's say. And for the next three years, it depends on what we decide to do as a Board.

items.statement: New deal wins were USD 41 million, up 25% year-on-year; full year ACV aspiration is to exceed last year's USD 170 million
items.quote: New deal wins were USD 41 million, up 25% year -on-year, reflecting the momentum built over recent quarters.

items.statement: Q1 operating EBITDA margin was 23%, down 260 bps sequentially primarily due to wage increments of 210 bps
items.quote: Operating EBITDA Q-on-Q is down 260 bps, primarily because of wage increments, which contributed 210 bps out of the 260; spend on computers and network infrastructure contributed 40 bps, and this was partially offset by a reduction of 60 bps in S&D.

items.statement: Margin trajectory expected to improve from Q2 onwards as wage increments impact is behind and revenue growth continues
items.quote: Margins will continue to improve because this quarter is when we gave out the increments. So, from now on, if everything stays equal and there is revenue growth, then margin should improve.

items.statement: BFSI segment expected to turn positive from H2 FY27 with pipeline momentum and conversions
items.quote: I think we should see momentum build up and giving us benefits starting in H2FY27.

items.statement: Fashion and Luxury expects gradual improvement to continue in Q2 after flat sequential revenue
items.quote: Fashion and Luxury revenue was flat sequentially and up 2% year -on-year. We see some early signs of recovery and expect gradual improvement to continue in Q2.

items.statement: Analytics and Automation grew 7% sequentially, crossed USD 100 million annual run rate, growing faster than company average
items.quote: Analytics and Automation grew 7% sequentially, well ahead of the company average, and has now crossed a USD 100 million annual run rate, an important milestone for us.

items.statement: M&D and Retail verticals remain soft due to supply chain challenges from Middle East conflict causing cautious spending and longer decision cycles
items.quote: M&D and Retail, these verticals remain relatively soft. Clients continue to face supply chain challenges from the prolonged Middle East conflict, resulting in more cautious spending, longer decision cycles, and some delays in discretionary projects.

items.statement: Adding capacity across India delivery centers increasing seat count by about 1,600 seats over next three to four months
items.quote: We are, in fact, adding additional capacity across our delivery centers in India, that is, Mumbai, Pune, Chandigarh, Mohali and Coimbatore. These facilities will become operational in a staggered manner over the next three to four months and increase seat count by about 1,600 seats in aggregate.

items.statement: Seeing pricing pressure from increased competition including large players entering small and medium deals, but nothing untoward
items.quote: On the second question, are we seeing pricing pressure because more and more players, obviously, competition always determines the price at which you win the deal. Yes, there are pressures that we are seeing, but nothing untoward to say.

items.statement: Plan to host an Investor Day later this quarter to provide deeper understanding of capabilities, strategy, and leadership team
items.quote: Finally, we plan to host an Investor Day later this quarter, giving investors a deeper understanding of our capabilities, strategy, and the leadership team. We will share details soon with you all.

items.statement: Emerging business led by F&A delivered strong growth for fourth consecutive quarter, expanding into APAC region for a client
items.quote: Emerging business, led by Finance and Accounting (F&A), has delivered strong growth for the fourth consecutive quarter. For one of our clients, we are expanding F&A support into the APAC region.

items.statement: Roll-off trends volatile but generally 15% to 20% of revenues annually over a 4-quarter period, expected to hold this year
items.quote: But generally, if you look at it in a 4 -quarter period, then it is generally between 15% and 20% of revenues for the year. And we expect that, that should broadly hold up this year as well.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of minimum 25% and up to 40% YoY on FY26 base of INR396 cr
items.quote: Minimum 25% and upper side 40%.

items.statement: FY27 PAT margin target of 9-10% with improvement visible from Q3-Q4 as capacity utilization rises
items.quote: We are hoping 9% to 10% of PAT in this current year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to improve by approximately 1% over upcoming quarters due to better fixed cost absorption
items.quote: Higher operating volumes are expected to improve fixed cost absorptions and support an improvement in EBITDA margin of approximately 1% over the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: UAE capex of AED15M for third tempering line and fire-rated technology; commercial production expected in Q3 FY27; funded 50:50 internal accruals and AED7M bank debt
items.quote: Around AED15 million is the total capex for in UAE, including the third line and fire-rated.

items.statement: India capex minimal (<INR1 cr) for regular machine overhauling and realignment at Taloja and Erode
items.quote: In India, there are some critical capex which are not very huge in amount, maybe less than INR1 crores, which are regular realignment or overhauling of the machines which are required.

items.statement: Targeting 10% revenue from new verticals (railway, fire-rated, bulletproof) by next year; fire-rated production starts Q3 FY27 in UAE
items.quote: Next, we are targeting 10% of the revenue will come from that vertical.

items.statement: Geographical diversification underway: UAE share falling from 75% to 60-40% this year and 50-50 next year; expanding to Africa and Europe
items.quote: Last year there was a contributions of about 75% from UAE operation. This year it will be 60-40 and coming year it will be 50-50.

items.statement: Capacity utilization targets: Silvassa 85-90%, Taloja 75%, Erode 25-30%, UAE 85% (existing lines) by Q4 FY27; third UAE line 15-20% utilization in Q3
items.quote: Silvassa, we are expecting by year end we will be reaching at 85% to 90%. Taloja, we are expecting to reach at 75% in the next quarters. Erode, yes, we will target of around 25% to 30% in the next quarters. And UAE, we are already at 71%, so we are targeting to reach at 85%.

items.statement: Current blended capacity can support INR600-650 cr revenue; with UAE third line and India ramp-up, potential rises to ~INR725-750 cr
items.quote: Yes. So, whatever I was asking is if considering the present capacity utilization, am I right in understanding the maximum revenue that can be generated without any present ongoing expansion would be somewhere around INR600 crores? Amrut Gada: Yes.

items.statement: No equity fund raise planned; UAE capex funded 50% internal accruals, 50% via AED7M bank term loan
items.quote: We don't have any fund raising plan. Whatever the capex planning is there, which is within the internal profit and second, little bit of debt.

items.statement: India working capital ~98 days, UAE ~85 days; blended tax rate <9% (India has carry-forward losses for 4-5 years, UAE 9% corporate tax)
items.quote: In India, the working capital days are around 98 days, and UAE is around 85 days.

items.statement: FY27 production guidance toned down from 400,000 tons to around 380,000 tons due to transformer and gas cleaning plant constraints at KNR-2
items.quote: We had indicated 400,000 tons, but we going to tone it down a little bit because while we were able to switch on all furnaces at KNR-2 in the month of March and, in fact, got a little bit of production, but some of the transformers we have, we feel should not be loaded beyond a certain point.

items.statement: FY28 production target maintained at 475,000 to 500,000 tons
items.quote: We are still maintaining 475,000 to 500,000 tons for FY '28.

items.statement: Two sets of transformers plus a spare ordered for KNR-2; replacement expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27
items.quote: We have already ordered 2 sets of transformers plus a spare. Sometimes in Q2 or Q3, we will be looking to replace the 2 sets of transformers where we have a little bit of concern.

items.statement: Additional INR 15-20 crores approved for 50,000 ton furnace at KNR-2 pending environmental clearance
items.quote: In fact, at the current Board meeting, we have also approved a slightly higher budget because, again, when we do a more detailed review of what is the situation and what work remains to be done. So, a little bit of another INR15 crores, INR20 crores or so is what we have approved in this budget.

items.statement: Q2 average price realization expected to be more or less same as Q1 with marginal volume increase due to ferrochrome stock build-up
items.quote: For the quarter 2, the average price realization is expected to be more or less same. On the volume-wise, there will be some incremental volume, but since we are building up the ferrochrome stock, it is expected to be marginal.

items.statement: KNR-1 and KNR-2 more competitive than Therubali; margins expected to improve by INR 1,500-2,000 per ton once stabilized at 500,000 tons
items.quote: Both KNR-1 and KNR-2 are more competitive than Therubali in terms of cost of production. And therefore, once KNR-1 and KNR-2 all stabilize and we get to that 500,000 tons production in a smooth manner, then we will see our margins improve by about INR1,500 to INR2,000.

items.statement: Met coke prices moved up slightly due to Colombian currency depreciation; impact may be seen in Q3
items.quote: Actually, met coke prices have moved up a little bit. I don't know about coking coal, but as far as metallurgical coke is concerned, it's moved up a little bit on account of Colombia, etc., their currency depreciation.

items.statement: Global stainless steel production growing at 2.5-3%; ferrochrome prices supported by chrome ore cost pressures
items.quote: Stainless steel production has grown. I mean it may not be very aggressive growth, but about 2.5% to 3% growth is there globally if you look at it.

items.statement: Domestic sales around 19% in Q1; company can flex between domestic and export markets with price parity
items.quote: Yes, around 19% we have sold in domestic.

items.statement: South African ferrochrome restart with Eskom special tariff may create short-term glut if China does not cut output
items.quote: If ferrochrome production in South Africa goes up and China doesn't compensate in terms of lesser output, then you will see some sort of glut. And that is going to impact everybody, including the South African producers themselves.

items.statement: No impact from West Asia crisis as IMFA does not import from or sell to the region; freight costs up slightly but prices more than compensate
items.quote: Fortunately, for us, no impact of the West Asia crisis because we don't import anything from West Asia or sell anything to West Asia.

items.statement: KNR-1 first furnace heating refractory lining; first tapping expected around third week of July 2026; second furnace by end September or early October
items.quote: We are also looking to commission the KNR-1 greenfield project, where the first furnace we have already initiated the process of heating the refractory lining, so we expect first tapping around the third week of this month.

items.statement: Chrome ore inventory of approximately 6 lakh tons stacked to meet additional capacity needs for next year
items.quote: On the chrome ore, we have stacked up to meet whatever is our additional capacity requirement for next 1 year. So approximately chrome ore stock of 6 lakh tons is there with us.

items.statement: Ferrochrome inventory to be built up to 17,000-18,000 tons over next 1-2 quarters to support higher output from three locations
items.quote: We'll also have to build up a little bit of ferrochrome stock because that's about 17,000, 18,000 tons, which works well when we have only 2 locations. But now that we have a third location and higher tonnages.

items.statement: Coke consumption 0.65 kg and chrome ore consumption 2.5 tons per ton of ferrochrome
items.quote: So broadly, that's 0.65 kilograms of coke and broadly 2.5 tons of chrome ore.

items.statement: Critical minerals remain an area of interest; company has bid on blocks but not yet successful
items.quote: Critical minerals are something we are interested in because it's certainly adjacent to our skill set. We have looked at a couple of blocks but have unfortunately not been successful in the bid.

items.statement: Expects FY27 to continue strong after good Q1 start; footfall growth unpredictable quarter-to-quarter
items.quote: This year has started on a strong note. So I think we are hopeful that this year should continue.

items.statement: Chennai Park long-term margins expected at par with mature parks; currently tracking similar in Q1
items.quote: Chennai margin should be in line with other margins as it progresses. It's still the first year, so it's hard for us to kind of tell you how it's exactly going to be. But long term, it will give the same margins as other parks or at par.

items.statement: Maintenance capex 6-7% of revenue; expansion capex ~10% of revenue for new attractions
items.quote: Generally, we keep about 10% of our top line for the expansion purpose or maybe for adding new attraction to the existing park. 6%, 7% of my top line will be for the maintenance capital.

items.statement: July footfalls looking good so far but early to judge full quarter; Q1 benefited from favorable weather and no unseasonal rains in May
items.quote: So far, it's looking good. But again, like I said, July is just 1 month. So we'll have to wait and see for the remainder of the quarter and see how it goes.

items.statement: Targeting 40-50% non-ticket revenue mix (currently ~30%); non-ticket spend per guest grew 20% YoY to INR591
items.quote: Yes, your assumption is correct. That's it.

items.statement: Rainfall deficit and heavy rains in Kerala pose operational disruption risk; no government directives currently
items.quote: As of now, there is no issue. I think rainfall has been actually very strong in the last few days. But again, we can't predict these things. We'll have to wait and see. As of now, it's all fine.

items.statement: Corporate overhead increased INR6.5 Cr in Q1 for digital transformation (INR1.5 Cr) and marketing; marketing spend up INR5 Cr YoY excluding Chennai
items.quote: This is mainly the digital transformation expenses compared to the previous quarter because we started the new POS in our parks only from July month. So all those digital transformations has costed us about some INR1.5 crores incrementally.

items.statement: Average ticket price up 2% YoY to INR1,310; ARPU up 7% to INR1,901 driven by 20% non-ticket spend growth
items.quote: Our average ticket price for the quarter stood at INR1,310, registering a 2% Y -o-Y increase. Average non -ticket spend per guest increased by 20% Y -o-Y basis to INR591, reflecting a continued strength in our in-park spending initiatives. As a result, average revenue per user, the ARPU, increased by 7% Y-o-Y to INR1,9

items.statement: Aim to achieve at least INR 300 crores export revenue this FY
items.quote: Our assessment is that this year, export, we should try and achieve at least INR 300 crores plus.

items.statement: Target INR 10,000 crore order book despite heavy execution
items.quote: Our target of achieving INR 10,000 crore, and the interesting thing is that about 70% of these fresh orders are on a competitive basis.

items.statement: Red lines: 20% EBITDA margin and 15% PAT margin on consol basis
items.quote: Our red lines of 20% EBITDA margins and 15% PAT margin on a consol basis, we will definitely strategically pushing on the execution of some higher margin orders out of the 700 plus order that we are executing.

items.statement: Total order book INR 9,450 crore; RITES Videsh order book INR 2,100 crore as of 30th June
items.quote: We are now at INR 9,450 crore.

items.statement: Export order book INR 1,775 crore including INR 900 crore Bangladesh coaches and balance locomotives from Mozambique and Africa
items.quote: Out of that, about INR 1,775 is the export of rolling stock and out of that, about INR 900 odd crores is the order from Bangladesh, which is about 200 coaches.

items.statement: Bangladesh 200 coaches to complete by early Q2 or Q3 next FY; Mozambique locomotives may start deliveries by end of this FY
items.quote: yes, it will get completed in next FY, maybe somewhere the early Q2 or maybe Q3 of the next FY. As far as the locomotives are concerned, the Mozambique, yes, we are trying that maybe by the end of this FY, we could aim for beginning of the deliveries

items.statement: Turnkey 50% of order book at 1.5-2% margins; consultancy and export 50% at higher margins
items.quote: The Turnkey is about 50% of our order book, and it contributed roughly about 30-33% of the revenue of this quarter. Basically, they always remain in the range of about 1.5-2% margins.

items.statement: Employee cost increase 8-10% in FY28 due to pay revision and headcount growth
items.quote: Not really 20%. I would put it more in the range of about 8-10%.

items.statement: QA revenue about INR 70 crores this quarter; targeting double-digit growth for full year
items.quote: QA has been again a good steady growth and if you recall last FY, we touched the levels which we had touched about before the competitive were enough up about 2 years back. We are on track again. It's about in the same range of about INR 70 odd crores.

items.statement: REMCL profit INR 22 crores this quarter; 91% dividend payout; INR 10 crores dividend received
items.quote: REMCL has been steadily giving a good PAT and dividend to us. It's about 50% plus PAT margins. This quarter also, it gave a profit of about INR 22 crores. That's a good dividend payout ratio of about 91%. We've got a good dividend of about INR 10 crores from REMCL.

items.statement: Aim for one export order per quarter; got 35 million USD order for 9 locomotives to South Africa in July
items.quote: This quarter also, in July, we have got an order for about 35 million for nine locomotives to South Africa.

items.statement: Low CapEx and hardly any working capital requirement; debt free
items.quote: Once there is no major change, we can with the low CapEx and hardly any working capital requirement, debt free, we don't see any major shift in the dividend payout policy.

items.statement: Target double-digit revenue growth and incremental quarterly growth sequentially
items.quote: Definitely aiming that we have a double-digit growth on the revenue and have some incremental definitely growth in the quarter. That's the aim in the quarters on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Turnkey proportion not expected to exceed 50% of order book over 2-year perspective
items.quote: I don't think over a period of time, I see the Turnkey being more than 50 odd percent on an average basis of the total order book.

items.statement: Vande Bharat export prototype development on standard gauge initiated; early discussions with Indian Railways started
items.quote: The process of trying to develop a prototype on the standard gauge platform, the initial discussions with Indian Railways have already started.

items.statement: Current order book stands at ₹13,596 crore comprising 11 projects and 44 marine platforms, down from above ₹15,000 crore for the first time in 10 years due to strong execution.
items.quote: Our current order book stands at ₹13,596 crore and this comprises mostly of shipbuilding orders with shipbuilding divisions contributing to ₹13,296 crore and the other two divisions, the engineering and the engine divisions, contribute to the balance of the order book.

items.statement: Revenue recognition for the Next Generation Corvette (NGC) project will commence in FY28 assuming contract signing in Q2 FY27; project completion over 8 years with first delivery in 5 years.
items.quote: The first revenue recognition will commence next year, that is the Financial Year 2028. Revenue recognition will commence in Financial Year 2 028 when we will be utilizing the activities involved in design, then the binding data information which we need to progress with the preparation of compartment design and equipment layout

items.statement: Capex plan includes ₹200 crore for Kolkata Port facility revitalization (18 months), ₹2,200 crore for Raichak greenfield shipyard (3-5 years), and ₹2,000 crore for Gujarat total ship solution facility (3 years).
items.quote: And there the capital infusion is expected to be just about ₹200 crore and this will be completed within a year and half (18 months). Coming to the larger projects, we ar e just undertaking two projects, one in West Bengal, I mentioned it, towards the sea. The land is already with us again on a very long -term basis, a long-term lease from Kolkata Port Trust. Here we are creating a full -fledged s

items.statement: Defense pipeline of ~₹1.5 lakh crore: ₹80,000 crore live RFPs (NGC, 120 FIC, 31 FAC, 22 interceptor boats, 6 NGOPV, P-17B) plus ₹70,000 crore expected RFPs (12 MCMV, 4 LPD) in current calendar year.
items.quote: So, in a nutshell, if you are taking the defense sector alone, about ₹1,50,000 c rores worth orders are expected in the near future. Nearly 80,000 coming from the RFPs which are live and about Rs. 70,000 expected from the RFPs which are expected to be or likely to be published during the calendar year

items.statement: Commercial pipeline includes 4 MR tankers, 6 VLGCs, 6 Aframax vessels, and upcoming container ship tender; GRSE partnering with other Indian and foreign yards to bid.
items.quote: Six Very Large Gas Carriers, VLGC, six Aframax Vessels, and another tender, high-value tender for container ships is expect ed to come soon. So, in a nutshell, if you are taking the defense sector alone, about ₹1,50,000 c rores worth orders are expected in the near future

items.statement: Order book mix shifting: 74% from four naval projects, 25% from non-defence (research vessels, export orders); previously 98% defence.
items.quote: About 74% of the shipbuilding pie is from the four naval projects and the balance, 25% is coming from the non-defence sector. There was a period when 98% of the shipbuilding order book was comprised of defence orders, but now the split, the breakup has been different, mostly because we have been executing the research ship projects for various ministries, and of course the export orders.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 total income ₹1,914 crore (+38% YoY), revenue from operations ₹1,815 crore (+39%), PAT ₹173 crore (+44%), EPS ₹15.09 (+44%).
items.quote: Our total income stood at ₹1,914 crore, recording a year -on-year growth of 38% when compared to Q1 FY26 results and the revenue f rom operations has increased from ₹1,310 crore to ₹1,815 crore recording a growth of 39%.

items.statement: Employee cost may rise 15-20% due to upcoming pay commission; already factored into projections.
items.quote: Our anticipation is that it could be of similar range 15-20% which is normal in every pay commission. We don't see any abnormality, and we have already factored those in our, let us say, future projections and calculations.

items.statement: Capacity expansion from 28 to 32 concurrent platforms by end of calendar year; further to 43 platforms with new facilities enabling large commercial vessels (Aframax, VLGC).
items.quote: We intend, with the creation of these two facilities, the capacity constraint will be completely obliterated, and we will have the capability to build 43 platforms, and the 11 platforms, 11 types of platforms, that means from 32 to 43 platforms, there will be large vessels of Aframax and VLGC type.

items.statement: Navratna status granted on 19 June 2026 provides autonomy for expansion; GRSE intends to utilize this privilege fully.
items.quote: Navratna status definitely provides the autonomy for expansion, and we intend utilizing this privilege or the expansion autonomy to the hilt.

items.statement: Water metro projects emerging across states; order value ~₹200-300 crore per metro, potential ₹1,500 crore for 5 states (30-40 platforms).
items.quote: The order value could be to the tune of around ₹200 to 300 crore per metro. They are small platforms, but that but is the attractiveness or the overall necessity of a green platform. But here, again, the volumes are high. If for five states, let us say, going for this, the order value could be to the tune of around ₹1,500 crore. And in terms of numbers, it could range from 30 to 40 platforms.

items.statement: Next Generation Destroyer (NGD) RFP not expected before FY29 as DAC approval pending; 1.5-2 years after DAC for RFP issuance.
items.quote: I do not expect, in my appreciation again, that I do not expect the RFP to come out for NGD till FY29, because currently we are in FY27. Considering, depending upon the priority that Navy has got, even if a DAC approval is taken in the current financial year, it could take about a year-and-a-half for the RFP to come out.

items.statement: Other expenses dropped in Q1 FY27 vs Q4 FY26 due to absence of ship commissioning costs; contract worker costs vary sinusoidally with project execution phase.
items.quote: In the last quarter, we had three of the ships which were commissioned. So, the last phase of commissioning, a certain amount of expenditure was incurred for these activities. So, in the current quarter, we did not have such occasions. So, that has resulted in a drop in the other expenses.

items.statement: Indigenization ~80-85% by value on recent warships (ASW SWC, SVL); float 100%, fight ~60%, move (propulsion) not indigenous yet, survive ~70%; full indigenization may take 5-10 years.
items.quote: In the last few projects, two projects I will just take, which we have completed, the anti- submersible aircraft, then four ships already been delivered, we know exactly what is the kind of indigenization that they can achieve. And the survey vessels l arge, which we have already completed the project. There, we have plus 80% indigenization overall. This is for the ship building sector

items.statement: No decision on bonus or stock split; await instructions from Administrative Ministry and DIPAM.
items.quote: We are fully aware that this is controlled by the government department. We are waiting for t heir instructions on this. And whatever instructions come from the Administrative Ministry and DIPAM, we will abide by that. Let us wait for their directives

items.statement: Volume growth guidance maintained at 12-15% for FY27
items.quote: No. We will stick to our guidance on growth going forward.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 11-13% for FY27
items.quote: Our guidance is 11% to 13% kind of operating margin.

items.statement: Q1 capex of INR 40-42 crore spent on Bhuj plant second tranche; full year plan unchanged
items.quote: For this quarter, around INR 40 crores, INR 42 crores has been spent, and that has primarily been on the completion of second tranche of Bhuj plant takeover.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin at 13%, up 600 bps YoY driven by product mix and pricing
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 77 crores, a growth of 93% Y-o-Y, while margins stood at 13%, registering a 600 basis point growth.

items.statement: Plumbing share increased vs agri; CPVC/PPR/PP contribution improved vs PVC
items.quote: So one is agri versus building material and second is PVC versus CPVC, PP, PPR. So both product mix improvements at a segmental and at a polymer level has helped as far as gross margin is concerned.

items.statement: Channel restocking resumed in June-July after April destocking; MIP provides price floor
items.quote: In June and July, we saw better stocking from channel partners, which is more reflective of the secondary demand or the last mile demand.

items.statement: CPVC price hikes being passed on in phased manner over 1-2 weeks
items.quote: I think we are passing it on in a phase-wise manner. So usually, we give 1 to 2 weeks to the channel.

items.statement: Inventory days at 100 vs 65-75 guidance due to supply insecurity and volume miss; expects correction by Q2 end
items.quote: We should see immediate correction in inventory. This is not a structural thing. We will be back to our stated guidance by end of September quarter.

items.statement: Bathware revenue INR 13 crore, EBITDA loss INR 5 crore in Q1; expects INR 25 crore quarterly run rate by Q3
items.quote: In the December quarter, we should be doing INR 25 crores, which will be very close to break even.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 52-53%; 12-15% volume growth would take it to ~60%
items.quote: As of now, we are at around 52% - 53% kind of utilization. And what we have guided is 13% to 15% of growth in this year, which translates to, if the capacity is static, then we will reach to around 60% of utilization.

items.statement: Targeting industry-leading volume growth via network expansion, digitization, new products
items.quote: We are confident that more long-term initiatives like network expansion and digitizing of value chain, new product innovation. These are going to be the levers of sustainable growth going forward.

items.statement: DECILO PP drainage pipes launched at Haridwar; installed in residential, hospitals, hotels
items.quote: We have developed our polypropylene-based drainage system, DECILO, which is designed to deliver superior performance across these parameters.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 lowest quarter; expect improvement in Q2 FY27 and return to year-on-year growth from H2 FY27
items.quote: As we had indicated in our previous earnings call, Q1 of this year would be our lowest quarter ever, and that is how the quarter has played out. From here onwards, we expect improvement in Q2FY27 and the return to year-on-year growth from the second half.

items.statement: Sequential improvement in Q2 FY27 and movement towards year-on-year comparability by end of first half
items.quote: The recovery phasing outlined by Umang is in line with our financial framework. We expect sequential improvement in Q2FY27and movement towards the year-on-year comparability by end of the first half and a return on year-on-year growth from the second half.

items.statement: Margin recovery weighted towards second half of FY27; pace depends on revenue conversion, mix, utilization, and operating milestones
items.quote: Given the unusually low operating base inQ1FY27, margin recovery will be weighted towards the second half of the year. The pace of improvement will depend on the revenue conversion, business mix, utilization, and delivery against the operating milestones discussed today.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target closer to previous year margin percentage for current year; acceleration expected from FY28 onwards
items.quote: So Foram we should be looking at a number which will be closer to previous year margin percentage for the current year. And we should thereafter start accelerating from FY28 onwards.

items.statement: Restocking order received for one commercial molecule providing meaningful delivery visibility for Q4 FY27 and FY28
items.quote: For one commercial molecule that faced destocking last year, we have now received the restocking order, providing meaningful delivery visibility for Q4 FY27 and FY28.

items.statement: Robust API order book supporting outlook for the year
items.quote: These were largely timing-related factors, and importantly, the underlying demand remains healthy, with a robust API order book supporting our outlook for the year.

items.statement: Capital expenditure during Q1 FY27 was approximately INR 598 million
items.quote: Capital expenditure during the quarter was approximately INR598 million as we continue to invest in capabilities required for future growth.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin at 71.5% in Q1 FY27 vs 73% in Q1 FY26; decline due to product mix and lower high-margin Pharma CDMO contribution
items.quote: Consolidated gross margin was at 71.5% compared with 73% in Q1 FY26. The decline primarily reflected the product mix and the lower contribution from the high-margin Pharma CDMO business.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA at INR 92 million, margin of 2.2% in Q1 FY27; reduction reflects lower revenue base, negative operating leverage, and subsidiary consolidation impact
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA was at INR92 million, representing a margin of 2.2%. The reduction reflects the lower revenue base, negative operating leverage, and the impact of subsidiary consolidation.

items.statement: Standalone business generated revenue of INR 3,599 million and adjusted EBITDA of INR 332 million, margin of 9.2% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The standalone business generated a revenue of INR3,599 million and adjusted EBITDA of INR332 million, representing a margin of 9.2%.

items.statement: Passed on major chunk of raw material cost escalation to customers in API+ business during last quarter
items.quote: The price increase which happened during the last quarter, largely due to the larger raw material price escalations which we witnessed because of the geopolitical situation, we tried our level best in terms of transferring a decent portion of that increase to our customers.

items.statement: Sapala reported 2.5x revenue growth in Q1 FY27; supply commenced on specialized nucleic acid building blocks program
items.quote: In oligonucleotide segment, under Sapala, supply commenced on the specialized nucleic acid building blocks program during Q1FY27. As a result, Sapala reported 2.5x revenue growth in Q1.

items.statement: API+ portfolio increasingly focused on niche assets in CNS and controlled substances; targeting value maximization through value chain play
items.quote: The portfolio is increasingly focused on niche assets in CNS and controlled substances space, while targeting value maximization through our value chain play across intermediate, APIs, pellets, and formulations.

items.statement: USFDA inspection of Pashamylaram facility from 27th July to 5th August 2026 resulted in Form 483 with five observations; none relate to data integrity
items.quote: I also want to add that we have just announced that USFDA has completed an inspection of our Pashamylaram facility, which was conducted from 27th July to 5th August, 2026. Following this, we received a Form 483 with five observations. None of them relate to data integrity.

items.statement: NJ Bio revenue below expectations at INR 350 million; adjusted EBITDA loss of INR 328 million weighing on consolidated profitability
items.quote: NJ Bio, by comparison, reported revenue of INR350 million, lower than the corresponding period last year and below our internal expectations. It recorded an adjusted EBITDA loss of INR328 million.

items.statement: Expects gross margin to improve by at least 1% YoY in FY27 and settle between 40-42% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: We are very confident of the current margin levels, and we are also confident of improving from here. We hope that on a year-on-year basis, there is some headroom, and we will be able to improve at least 1% on gross margin year-on-year.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 14-15% in next 2-3 years from current 11.2%
items.quote: On the EBITDA margins, yes, that is where the endeavor is. We believe that we'll be able to grow at least a percentage even on the margin side year-on-year, which will ultimately in the range, in the next two to three years, we should be in the range of 14-15%.

items.statement: Expects export contribution (including IKEA) to reach 15% of revenue in next two years from ~12% currently
items.quote: As of last year, we had about 12% contribution to the revenue. As the company grows, we believe even in spite of the growth overall as a company, our export contribution in the next two years, that is the current and the next year, should get to 15%.

items.statement: Targets 500 standalone Pigeon exclusive outlets by end of 2027; added 17 stores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Further, we added 17 new stores under franchise model during the quarter, reinforcing our retail expansion strategy and advancing our long-term objective of establishing 500 standalone Pigeon exclusive outlets by the year end 2027.

items.statement: Expects Induction Cooktop contribution to stabilize at 20%+ of full year FY27 revenue
items.quote: We are confident of this, contribution from Induction Cooktop to be in the range of, at least 20% and a little above that as we progress over the year.

items.statement: Targets non-induction categories to grow at nearly 20% consistently
items.quote: Our endeavor is to actually take the non-induction growth to nearly 20% if possible, if you are able to do everything right.

items.statement: Expects Q2 FY27 to be as strong as Q1 with growth over high base of last year
items.quote: Historically, the Q2 is the strongest and we will continue to be there. Obviously, because the Q1 was stronger, the Q2 has to be in line with that. It may not be exactly at the same rate of growth of Q1, but definitely there is a very strong demand, that we are witnessing. So we believe that the Q2 will be as strong.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin expanded 127 bps YoY to 39.6%; EBITDA margin expanded 71 bps YoY to 11.2%
items.quote: Gross profit for the quarter stood at INR190.4 crores versus INR130.4 crores in Q1 FY26, a growth of 46% year-on-year. Despite ongoing supply chain challenges and elevated raw material costs. Also, gross margins expanded by 127 basis points year-on-year

items.statement: Increased domestic prices and export realizations to pass through input cost inflation; follows cost-plus model
items.quote: We have increased our prices for the domestic market. We also are, there's a favorable situation even in our exports. They have corrected their buying prices upwards to address the input cost.

items.statement: Induction Cooktop demand remains structurally higher than pre-war levels; expects annualized 2x growth vs last year
items.quote: On an annualized basis, we still believe that we will be a 2x of last year.

items.statement: Premiumization driving mix shift: stainless steel pressure cookers growing faster than aluminium; retail channel grew 86% YoY
items.quote: We have grown higher in our stainless steel pressure cooker versus our aluminium pressure cooker, which also means, I mean, it's the product mix which is contributing.

items.statement: IKEA supplies to begin in Q2 FY27; IKEA deemed export business expected to be 5-6% of revenue at full scale
items.quote: In this quarter, Q2 is when, IKEA business is starting.

items.statement: Chimney category revamped with BLDC motors; expects substantial growth from internal manufacturing and own retail
items.quote: What we have done is actually revamped the entire range from normal AC motors to BLDC motors, all but one. So that makes us extremely, current and in fact ahead of many of our competitors. And given that we've got our own retail also to drive this, we are very confident that the Chimney business is going to grow quite

items.statement: Committed to reaching 300 restaurants by FY27 with disciplined, calibrated pace
items.quote: We are committed to reaching 300 restaurants by FY27, and we'll build our portfolio from there.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR140 crores: INR120 crores for new outlets, INR20 crores for maintenance and ancillary
items.quote: We guided previously capex for full year would be around INR140 crores of which INR120 crores to the new outlet openings and INR20 crores towards the maintenance capex and our ancillary capex.

items.statement: 15 restaurants under construction to operationalize through Q2 and Q3 FY27
items.quote: As of today, we have 15 restaurants that are under construction, and these will operationalize through Q2 and Q3 of this financial year.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin improved to 8.1% in Q1 FY27, up 350 bps YoY and 260 bps QoQ
items.quote: Pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin for Q1 came in at 8.1%, which was around 350 basis points higher than Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Mature restaurant operating margin reached 16.2% in Q1 FY27, up 290 bps YoY
items.quote: Q1 FY27 matured portfolio Pre-Ind AS restaurant operating margin came in at 16.2%. This was again around 290 basis points higher than Q1 of last year.

items.statement: No price increase taken in Q1 FY27; growth entirely volume-led with average per cover spend reflecting mix changes
items.quote: Our growth continues to be entirely volume led. We have not taken any price increase during Q1, and our average per coverage spend continues to reflect changes in business segment mix.

items.statement: Consolidated same-store sales growth 28.7% in Q1 FY27; dine-in transaction volumes up 63.5% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated same-store sales growth for the quarter was 28.7%. Consolidated revenue grew 43.4% year-on-year to INR426 crores. Dine-in transaction volumes increased by 63.5%.

items.statement: Barbeque Nation India TAM revised to 600 restaurants from earlier 400-450; Big Buffet format enabling Tier 3/4 expansion
items.quote: Overall, if I look at the dynamics that we have with respect to the metro markets, the Tier 1 markets and the Tier 2, Tier 3 markets, I think at the current scale, the brand, which is Barbeque Nation India can take it up to around 600-odd restaurants.

items.statement: Net debt increased marginally to INR106 crores from INR102 crores due to capex investment
items.quote: Our net debt position has moved marginally up from INR102 crores at the end of FY26 to INR106 crores at the end of Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth expected to moderate in FY27 due to stronger comparatives, not demand change
items.quote: We are conscious that the same-store sales growth will moderate as we move through FY27. This again, is more mathematics than our comment on demand.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin in 66-67% range; India gross margin improved 130 bps sequentially, International softer
items.quote: I think the current levels of around 66% -67% range is a good operating band and we would expect to move directionally from here over time.

items.statement: Monthly active users on digital platform grew ~60% YoY to 1.4 million; captive channels contribute 65% of dine-in transactions
items.quote: Our monthly active users on our digital platform have grown to approximately 1.4 million, which is up by almost 60% year-on-year. Our captive digital ecosystem contributes to 65% of overall Barbeque India dine-in transactions.

items.statement: Expect to outperform underlying automotive industry by 1.5x to 2x in FY27
items.quote: Given our current b usiness visibility, healthy order pipeline, and execution capabilities, we continue to expect SJS to outperform the underlying automotive industry by 1.5x to 2x in FY27

items.statement: Target export contribution of 14%-15% of consolidated revenue by FY28
items.quote: We continue to focus on scaling our export business and remain committed to achieving export contribution of 14%-15% of consolidated revenue by FY28.

items.statement: New SJS Decoplast facility in Pune adds Rs 200-250 crore additional revenue capacity
items.quote: And B - this new capacity will add close to about 200 crs to 250 crs of additional revenue.

items.statement: Cover glass and display plant equipment on order; commercial supplies expected from Q2 FY28
items.quote: Equipment is on order. It will be shipped and installed. And sales out of this new plant will come in Q2 of next year. This is what is for FY28.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 239 bps YoY to 30% in Q1FY27
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 799.6 mn, reflecting a year-on-year increase of 36.2%, with EBITDA margin expanding by 239 bps to 30%.

items.statement: Adjusted PAT margin 19.3% in Q1FY27 excluding one-time gain
items.quote: Excluding this exceptional item, adjusted PAT increased by a healthy 45.2% to Rs. 502.5 mn, translating into an adjusted PA T margin of 19.3

items.statement: Input cost impact on profitability 0.5%-0.6% this quarter; pass-through with 1-2 quarter lag
items.quote: That would be somewhere between 0.5% to 0.6%.

items.statement: Automotive business grew 32.4% YoY vs industry 21.7% in Q1FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, our automotive business registered a year-on-year growth of 32.4%, significantly ahead of the 21.7% growth recorded by the combined passenger vehicle and two-wheeler industry.

items.statement: Strong order book with new wins from Mahindra, Tata Motors, TVS, Autoliv, Royal Enfield, Skoda, John Deere, Hero MotoCorp
items.quote: The company also secured new orders from leading customers, including Mahindra and Mahindra, Tata Motors, TVS, Aut oliv, Royal Enfield, Skoda, John Deere, Hero MotoCorp, amongst others, during the quarter

items.statement: New generation products contributed ~24% of consolidated revenue in Q1FY27
items.quote: New generation products contributed approximately 24% of consolidated revenue during Q1FY27.

items.statement: Non-compete with Walter Pack Spain expires January 2027; may enable global expansion
items.quote: We have an agreement with Walter Pack Spain on non-compete till January of 2027. At that point in time, we will take a call what we need to do.

items.statement: Walter Pack India operating at ~75% utilization; no major capex planned beyond maintenance
items.quote: As of now, the Walter Pack is operating around 75%. We are developing a couple of business there. So, we have the capacity available there. So, as of immediate basis, there is no further capex.

items.statement: Aspire to capture at least 10% of Indian display market by 2030 (estimated Rs 5,000-7,000 crore)
items.quote: Our estimate is it could grow be as large as maybe Rs. 5,000 crs. So, that is, and what I said earlier, 5,000 crs to maybe 7,000 crs. And what I said earlier is our aspiration is to be at least 10% of the market by 2030.

items.statement: Board approved wholly-owned subsidiary for cover glass and display business
items.quote: The Board has approved setting up a wholly-owned subsidiary for the cover glass and display business.

items.statement: In-house R&D Centre received DSIR recognition from Government of India
items.quote: Further reinforcing our commitment to innovation, our in-house R&D Centre received recognition from the Department of Science and Industrial Research, DSIR, the Government of India.

items.statement: Paisabazaar full-year EBITDA expected to be about half of ₹100 Cr target
items.quote: I don't think it'll be ₹100 Cr. I think we'll be, maybe, at about half of that.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT margin improved from 6% to 9% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The consolidated PAT increased 92% year-on-year, (which is, again, both going to the new business as well as the renewal business), to ₹163 Cr, while PAT margin improved from 6% to 9% year-on-year.

items.statement: Management prioritizes growth over margin expansion; willing to increase acquisition spends aggressively
items.quote: We are actually increasing our acquisition spends. We are going even more aggressive than ever before.

items.statement: Health and term insurance grew 53% YoY; new health grew 59% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: New health and term insurance grew at 53%, with new health growing at 59% year -on-year, for the core business.

items.statement: 82% of new business comes from customers who never had insurance before
items.quote: 82% of our business that's coming in, is new, in the sense they've never had an insurance policy in the past.

items.statement: Monthly payment mode now over 30% of health insurance business
items.quote: Almost over 30% of our business now comes on monthly mode.

items.statement: Hired 5,000 people at gross level in Q1 FY27 despite being seasonally weak quarter
items.quote: We hired, at a gross level, 5,000 people in Q1.

items.statement: Renewal revenue grew 55% to ₹1,003 Cr for last 12 months; renewal growth expected upwards of 50% for some time
items.quote: While our renewal revenue has grown at 55% to ₹1,003 Cr for the last 12 months, but now we're getting to a stage when you will see higher and higher growth in renewals.

items.statement: Regulator's effort-based commission framework legally requires brokers to put maximum effort; management sees no near-term threat
items.quote: Legally, as defined by the regulator, the largest amount of effort in any sale needs to be put by a broker, more than any other channel.

items.statement: Dark pattern allegations dismissed; mobile number collection is standard practice globally for insurance quotes
items.quote: Globally, if you look, if you look in the UK, there is nobody who is providing insurance quotes at scale, even in products like motor insurance, without collecting a mobile number.

items.statement: AI touches 30-40% of 10 Cr monthly customer interactions; 20-30% of interactions automatically handled by bots
items.quote: Roughly we handle 10 Cr customer interactions in a month, calls, emails, etc, etc. Of those 10 Cr, 30 -40% are now being touched by AI, and that number is growing.

items.statement: PB Partners: 78% GWP from Tier 2/3 cities; 1.13 lacs active partners (+55% YoY); top 100 partners share 16% of premium
items.quote: Our top 100 partners' share of premium is 16%. We will furth er work actively in reducing this

items.statement: UAE insurance premium grew 31% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our UAE insurance premium grew 31% year-on-year for this quarter.

items.statement: Motor business: direct grew over 30%, POSP grew close to 50% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our motor plus two -wheeler direct business grew over 30%. Our motor business in POSP grew close to 50%, almost.

items.statement: Targeting mid-double-digit overall growth for FY27, split between ASP and volume growth
items.quote: we are looking at a mid-double-digit growth as an overall annualized impact of a business. Closely split between ASP and volume.

items.statement: Expecting high single-digit volume growth for FY27, with ASP growth of 6-7% from Q2 onwards
items.quote: we will be close to double-digit. We cannot promise a double-digit volume growth, but it will be high single digits for sure, right? It will be a combination of both ASP and volume growth that will lead us to mid-double-digit overall growth, right, for the year.

items.statement: Confident of delivering full-year EBITDA margin of 17-19% for FY27
items.quote: Absolutely, Umang. Yes, we are 100% confident of delivering that. There is no reason not to deliver the margin.

items.statement: Implemented 8% MRP increase across key categories effective April 1, resulting in ~5% underlying ASP increase in core Stuck-On category
items.quote: During the quarter, we implemented MRP increases of approximately 8% across key product categories, resulting in an underlying ASP increase of around 5% in our core Stuck-On category.

items.statement: RM inflation fully absorbed by 8% price hike; no further MRP increases planned, benefit to flow back to P&L as market stabilizes
items.quote: RM inflation has been fully absorbed. And in fact as the volatility subsides we believe that and we will not be obviously taking the MRP increases correction again. Like we will not go down on the MRPs.

items.statement: Broad-based growth across channels, categories, geographies; strong momentum in women, kids, sneakers, school shoes
items.quote: Growth was broad-based across channels, categories and geographies, with particularly encouraging momentum in our women and kids' portfolio.

items.statement: School shoes revenue grew ~50% YoY, moved from DIP to Stuck-On, contributed ~40% of volume growth in Q1
items.quote: We have moved this entire business from DIP to Stuck-On, which has a much better ASP and is a margin-accretive category versus DIP.

items.statement: Sneaker portfolio grew ~12-13% of volumes in Q1, targeting ~30% growth for FY27
items.quote: We are looking, since the scale is now getting bigger, this year we are looking at a close to 30% growth on this category.

items.statement: New manufacturing facilities at Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar commissioned, added ~Rs 2.5 cr depreciation in Q1
items.quote: approximately Rs. 2.5 crores of additional depreciation arising from the commissioning and ramp -up of our new manufacturing facilities at P aonta Sahib and Pantnagar

items.statement: Record orders received at largest-ever distributor meet, giving strong visibility for festive season
items.quote: strengthened our partner ecosystem through one of our largest ever distributor meets, where we have received record orders giving us a very good visibility of the upcoming festive season.

items.statement: Temporary ASP dilution of ~4.5% from Walmart accounting change (2.5%) and school shoes mix shift (2%), normalizing from Q2
items.quote: combined just these two factors have had about a 4.5% to 5% impact on our growth which are temporary factors effective only to this quarter.

items.statement: Targeting 90-100 new EBO store openings in FY27, accelerated from 18 in Q1, driven by SOR model transition
items.quote: This year we are back on track with respect to at least 80 to 120 stores is what we are targeting. Let us say give more or less about 90 to 100 stores is what we should achieve by the end of this year.

items.statement: Elan by Campus launched in neo-casual segment (Rs 1,899-2,599), selling in 100-110 own stores and online, initial response extremely positive
items.quote: Elan is almost a two-month-old launch now, and it is doing extremely well. It is selling currently in about 100 or 110 of our own stores, as well as actively selling on Amazon, Myntra, and our own brand.com.

items.statement: Built highest-ever Q1 production and July production to prepare for festive demand; inventory under control, secondary sales tracking positive
items.quote: we recorded our highest ever Q1 production and continued this momentu m into July, being the highest ever production month ever, proactively building inventory to ensure superior availability across key channels and categories

items.statement: Minimum wage increase added Rs 5 cr to other expenses in Q1; employee cost impact 15% (10% annualization/increments, 5% new hiring)
items.quote: So, hi Umang, it is Neeraj. So, in other expenses, basically Rs. 5 crores is sitting for minimum wage increase for the quarter.

items.statement: Franchise model transitioned from outright to SOR across 158 stores, completed in Q1; Rajasthan first state to transition, showing strong SSG growth
items.quote: we have also transitioned over the last three months our entire franchise business from an outright business based model to an SOR model where we control the entire inventory and discounting of these products. It is a complete transition of our 158 franchise stores which is almost now completed.

items.statement: Management expects 18-20% revenue growth for FY27, with festive period in Q3 FY27 expected to be good
items.quote: So on an overall number, we can look at a good 18% to 20% kind of revenue growth. That should be very easily achievable.

items.statement: Post-Ind AS EBITDA margin for FY27 guided at 7.5-8%, not the 9% suggested by analyst
items.quote: Around 8% that's a -- I mean 7.5% to 8% is easily achievable, looking at the current trend.

items.statement: Gross margin for FY27 guided at 15-15.5%
items.quote: It will be about 15% to 15.5%.

items.statement: Capex of ~INR 100 crores for 25-30 new stores plus ~INR 50 crores for property purchases in Kolkata
items.quote: So, the capex that we plan to invest would be in the lines of around INR 100-odd crores for the upcoming stores, plus or minus INR 5 crores, INR 10 crores because as quickly as the store gets built or if it's built before 31st March, you know, so that way and another INR 50-odd crores would be the investment that would go through in buying out properties in Kolkata.

items.statement: Plan to open 5 stores in Kolkata by Diwali and 10-12 stores by end of Q4 FY27, targeting 30 stores in West Bengal over next 24 months
items.quote: 5 stores will be operational by Diwali. And by 31st of March, by end of Q4 FY27, we should be operational by 10 to 12 stores.

items.statement: Mature stores (96 stores >4 years) at 11.2% EBITDA margin; non-mature stores (131 stores <4 years) improved to 8.1% margin this quarter
items.quote: Our mature stores are already operating at an EBITDA margin of 11.2%. But what is encouraging is that our non-mature stores delivered an 8.1% margin this quarter, a meaningful step-up and proof that these stores are picking up pace faster than we had originally modeled.

items.statement: Gross margin expansion driven by cooling product mix and temporary price escalation advantage in IT products; mobile price benefit was periodic across brands/SKUs
items.quote: Sir one, majorly summer season cooling products definitely have a higher gross margin. items.statement: Strong AC season with consistent footfalls and healthy conversions; South cluster reaccelerated with Andhra Pradesh revenue up 62% YoY and SSG 49.1%
items.quote: The summer of 2026 has been good for us. Air conditioners had their best quarter yet, both in terms of volume and value. As demand stayed strong right through the quarter, footfalls in our stores were consistent and healthy through the quarter and conversions held up well even as we saw customers trading up within the category.

items.statement: Large appliances 48% of revenue (AC leading), mobile phones 39%; mix shifts seasonally with cooling products dominant in Q1
items.quote: More broadly, large appliances remained our largest contributor at 48% of revenue with AC leading, supported by continued traction in washing machine and refrigerators. Mobile phones contributed 39% to our revenue mix.

items.statement: North cluster market was negative for cooling products this year; Delhi NCR SSG lower due to weak AC demand in the region
items.quote: Delhi actually didn't perform this year for air conditioners and the cooling products. So if you see, cooling products between refrigerators, air conditioners and air coolers, all three and very negligible market de-grew, the entire North market was actually minus than 2024 as well if I look at the bigger cluster in 2024.

items.statement: Working capital days reduced sharply to 42 days from 73 days; working capital borrowings down to INR 97 crores from INR 658 crores at quarter start
items.quote: Working capital days reduced sharply to 42 days as of June 2026 compared to 73 days as of March 2026. This was driven by tight working capital management and strong seasonal sellout throughout the quarter.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS operating cash flow INR 631 crores, post-Ind AS cash flow INR 671 crores for the quarter
items.quote: During the quarter, pre-Ind AS operating cash flows and post-Ind AS cash flows were INR 631 crores and INR 671 crores, respectively.

items.statement: Interest cost for FY27 expected to be lower by at least INR 10 crores vs last year's INR 150 crores
items.quote: No, it will be in the same range like last year. I mean about INR10 crores will be less. It will be less by at least INR10 crores.

items.statement: Store payback: South cluster under 10-11 months, North cluster 16-18 months; breakeven South 30-40 days, North 2-2.5 months
items.quote: Okay. So sir, now because the company is established in South, we've been deeply penetrated in markets here, we would look at a payback period of around under 10 to 11 months here in this cluster in South, and this number up north would be around 16 to 18 months. And in terms of breakeven, South, we would look at 30 to 40 days and, say, under around a month. And up North, it would be around 2-2.5

items.statement: Plan to open 8-10 stores in NCR in FY27, 5 stores in South, 25-30 stores total including West Bengal
items.quote: So, sir, we plan to open around 25-30 stores in existing geographies as well as in Bengal for that matter

items.statement: Expect high-teen volume growth in FY27 with EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26 levels and potential for further improvement
items.quote: We continue to expect the business to deliver high teen volume growth during the year while maintaining EBITDA m argins broadly in line with FY 26 levels, with potential for further improvement

items.statement: Successfully negotiated price revisions with OEMs; benefits expected to fully reflect in P&L from Q2 FY27
items.quote: We have now successfully negotiated price revisions with OEMs and benefits from these revisions are expected to fully reflect in our P&L from Quarter 2 onwards.

items.period: next two years to three years
