items.statement: Commissioned 4,000-ton forging press line and added 7,200 metric tons machining capacity in Q1 FY27; total forging capacity now 152,000 tons, machining 75,200 tons
items.quote: We also added capacity during the quarter by commissioning another 4,000-ton forging press line, adding 4,000 tons of forging capacity. Besides this, 7,200 metric tons of additional machining capacity has been added during the quarter.

items.statement: 18,000-ton vertical upsetter line under commissioning; trials from Q3 FY27, operational from Q4 FY27
items.quote: Yes, we probably start adding from Q4 of this financial year. It is already under commissioning right now, and our trials will start from Q3 onwards.

items.statement: Captive solar power project on track; large part of capex done, clearances obtained, ROW work ongoing; power generation expected from Q4 FY27, full contribution from FY28
items.quote: We are hopeful that the project will be on stream from January onwards, and a large part of the capex is already done. And, so all the clearances have been obtained. Just some work on ROW, right of way, is going on.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 275 bps YoY to 31.3%, marking 4th consecutive quarter above 30%; PAT margin expanded 178 bps to 20.4%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs.141 crores, and EBITDA margin expanded by 275 basis points year-on-year to 31.3%. This marks the 4th consecutive quarter in which we have delivered an EBITDA margin in excess of 30%.

items.statement: Confident of sustaining 30%+ EBITDA margins going forward, aided by 1-1.5% benefit from solar power from FY28
items.quote: Yes, I'm very confident that we should be achieving that because we will be having a benefit of 1%, 1.5% from power as well. So I'm quite confident that, you know, we should be seeing upwards of 30% going forward.

items.statement: Machining contribution increased to 90% in Q1 FY27 from 88% in Q1 FY26; industrial and passenger vehicle revenue share rising
items.quote: Machining contribution increased to 90% in Q1 FY27 compared with 88% in Q1 FY 26. Furthermore, one of the key strategic developments for our business has been continued diversification of our revenue mix, as reflected in the increasing contribution from industrial and passenger vehicles.

items.statement: Industrial segment grew ~50% YoY in Q1 FY27 across domestic and exports; demand healthy across power generation, renewables, railways, oil & gas, digital infrastructure
items.quote: The industrial segments contributed 16% of our revenue during the quarter. We achieved around 50% growth across both domestic and export segments. Demand remained healthy across power generation, renewable energy including wind, railways, oil and g as, and digital infrastructure

items.statement: Export freight costs rose from ~$2,000 to ~$6,000 per container; ~75% pass-through, expecting 15-20% incremental cost hit
items.quote: You're right, the cost of, you know, container has gone up from roughly from USD2,000 to almost USD6,000, and a large part of it, the contract that we have, it's kind of a pass-through, or it is around 75% pass-through.

items.statement: Industrial revenue expected to double in 3-4 years; passenger vehicle revenue target 12-15% of total; combined industrial + PV to contribute 45-50% of revenue
items.period: next three years to four years
items.quote: We can safely say that, you know, industrial skills will grow from these levels, will double from these levels in next three years to four years. Also, the PV, we should be looking at 12% to 15% of our revenues. Both the sectors put together should be contributing around 45%, 50% to our revenues.

items.statement: Growth capex of Rs.350-400 crores annually expected to be funded largely from internal accruals; possible bridge loan for LCs for a year
items.quote: As of now, it looks like that we should be able to fund this growth on our own. Cash flows look very strong and the accruals will be even stronger going forward. So yes, we are also -- maybe there is some bridge loan for a year or so for opening up some letter of credit, but most of this will be funded from our own accruals.

items.statement: Open to inorganic acquisitions or JVs in energy and aerospace for technology and approvals; cautious on simpler businesses due to expensive valuations
items.quote: Yes, so we are quite like open for this and searching for it on especially on the energy and aerospace side where we are new in entering, and also the technology and approval process takes a lot of time. So we are open for that and are seeing an opportunity in that sector.

items.statement: Inventory days at 50 as of June 2026; receivable days improved, no big change in working capital cycle
items.quote: Inventory days. 50 days as on date.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 expected to show similar year-on-year growth trend as Q1, with price increase speed halving
items.quote: Q2 also similar trend will be there. The only correction will happen on the speed of the price increase. Price increase speed should be half.

items.statement: Full year FY27 expected to continue price uptrend with possible trajectory slowdown
items.quote: We are expecting similar trend to continue in the entire this financial year although the trajectory, there may be a little bit slowdown comparatively.

items.statement: Semiconductor JV targeting over $100 million revenue in next three years
items.quote: we are targeting in next three years maximum, we are targeting a revenue of more than US$100 million under the JV.

items.statement: Planning 50+ local engineering hires over next two years for semiconductor JV
items.quote: It also includes direct skill transfer from Japanese design expert who will train our engineers backing our 50 plus local engineering hires over next two years.

items.statement: Good pipeline of AI data center projects for next three quarters
items.quote: there is a good pipeline of these projects, which will continue to be there for next three quarters at least.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 3.38%, PAT margin 2.05%
items.quote: EBITDA grew 55% to INR 173 crores and EBITDA margins at 3.38%. Profit after tax surged 69% to INR 105 crores delivering a PAT margin of 2.05%.

items.statement: Annualized ROCE and ROE at approximately 19.5% and 19.8%, highest since listing
items.quote: we delivered the highest annualized ROCE and ROE since our listing at approximately 19.5% and 19.8%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 growth breakdown: 30-35% from price increases, 5-10% from new products/brands, 20-25% from volume growth
items.quote: broadly speaking, 30%-35% has come from the price increase. 5% to 10% has come because of addition of new products and new brands. And the balance 20%-25% has come by increasing the quantity.

items.statement: Entry-level laptops facing ~50% shortage; mid/premium available if price accepted
items.quote: entry level laptops, there is almost 50% shortage. But if I go for medium and premium notebooks, if we are able to accept the price, then so far availability is not a concern.

items.statement: Commercial segment 60-65% of business, growing strongly; consumer 30-35% facing affordability pressure
items.quote: about 30%-35% of the business is consumer centric. Balance 60-65% is commercial, which is split between SMB and enterprise.

items.statement: Unit volumes grew ~20% in Q1 FY27 excluding SanDisk brand impact
items.quote: the unit growth is 20% and balance growth is coming from the ASP increase.

items.statement: PES segment share increased, lowering gross margin vs LIT segment
items.quote: PES share has increased which is of comparatively low margin as compared to the LIT.

items.statement: Acquired 67% stake in VDA Infosolutions (FY26 revenue INR 850 crores) for enterprise services integration
items.quote: they did INR 850 crores. In this current financial year, obviously, there will be a substantial growth plan.

items.statement: Supply constraints tracked weekly; orange alert status but good allocations maintained via OEM relationships
items.quote: this is an orange alert for us. We track it on a weekly basis.

items.statement: Dell commercial business contributed ~5% of revenue in Q1 FY27, above target
items.quote: roughly about 5% business has come from the new Dell commercial business in the past quarter, previous quarter.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of Rs 1,500 crores plus for FY27 with EBITDA margin above 19%
items.quote: As we have told earlier, you know, we remain fully committed, fully committed for our top line of Rs. 1.500 crores plus and EBIDTA margin of more than 19%. 100% without any doubt in that.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 2,428 crores as of 30 June 2026 providing strong revenue visibility
items.quote: with a strong order book of Rs. 2,428 crores as of 30 June 2026, which gives us strong revenue visibility and a healthy project pipeline across key segments.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance of more than Rs 2,000 crores for FY27, with Rs 700 crores already booked in Q1
items.quote: Your first question, definitely yes, it may increase also. But your first question is absolutely inline, we are likely to get more than 2000 crores worth of inflow in this particular year.

items.statement: Anjar facility utilization at 60-65% in FY27, targeting 100% by end of FY28; no expansion planned for Thailand facility
items.quote: Sir, Whatever we have planned in this particular year, we shall be doing it. But, you know, in that also, we should be reaching at around maybe around 60% to 65% of our available capacities. And our plan is that by the end of next year, we should be utilizing almost 100% of the available capacity at Anjar.

items.statement: Healthy demand across power, oil & gas, process industries domestically and overseas; multi-year opportunity from India's capex cycle and global energy/infrastructure pickup
items.quote: Overall demand, visibility across our core end markets, particularly power, oil and gas, and process industries in India and overseas remains healthy and a strong order pipeline gives us confidence in delivering profitable growth.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 16.9% vs 16% YoY; improvement driven by capacity utilization, operating leverage, seamless pipe contribution; confident of >19% full year
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 49.7 crores with a margin of 16.9% compared with 16% in Q1FY26 and it is up by 38.7% year-on-year.

items.statement: Rs 25 crore dispatches deferred to Q2 due to Middle East situation affecting oil & gas export customers; material ready at company end
items.quote: Around Rs. 25 crores of dispatches scheduled for Q1 got pushed into Q2 primarily on the oil and gas side, where a few of our export customers deferred take-offs given the situation in the Middle East.

items.statement: Thailand facility revenue target Rs 170-200 crores (vs Rs 130 crore FY26); facility fully booked for 3 years; no expansion planned
items.quote: Sir, as we have been telling, last year we did around Rs. 130 crores, and the intention is that we have to keep that unit busy and target to achieve anything between Rs. 170 crores to Rs. 200 crores.

items.statement: Anjar facility peak revenue potential Rs 1,500 crores by FY28-29
items.quote: So, our plan is around Rs. 1,500 crores from Anjar facility only and by '28-29, we should be able to do it.

items.statement: BHEL order pipeline: Rs 200 crore last quarter, more tenders in preparation expected this quarter; L&T orders awarded, more discussing; JSW, Hindustan Energy discussions ongoing
items.quote: Last quarter also we got around Rs. 200 crores worth of order and few more tenders are in the preparation stage. We expect that those tenders should be in the market maybe in this quarter itself and they may get finalized in the next quarter.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 17-19%
items.quote: We have given the guidance of EBITDA margin of 17% to 19% year-on-year and which we maintaining for current year and for even for the next year.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 20-25%
items.quote: 20% to 25% guidance we always maintain, and we try to achieve that. So we are as of now quite sure we will be achieving or crossing that.

items.statement: New Wada land acquisition: 10.15 acres, ~INR40-45 cr capex planned for next FY
items.quote: A broadly INR40 crores something, INR40 crores to INR45 crores something will be there as a capex plan, which we will plan in the next year once we have a complete hold or ownership of this particular land parcel.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 16.51%, expected to improve with Chennai utilization and revenue scale
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at around INR12 crores, up 28% year-on-year, with EBITDA margins at 16.51%.

items.statement: Pricing stable; 10-20% cost advantage vs European peers; raw material pass-through with lag
items.quote: I think pricings are stable, and we are still able to offer between 10% to 20% saving to our customer, maintaining our margins. And for the price increases which are happening on account of raw material particularly and some other heads, we are also getting the pass-through with some lag effects from the customer.

items.statement: Strong order booking growth ~40% YoY; first bulk electrolyzer order secured
items.quote: We delivered robust order booking growth of approximately 40% year-on-year, providing greater visibility for the quarters ahead. We also secured our first bulk commercial order from one of the India's leading electrolyzer manufacturer.

items.statement: New products contribute 30-35% of order book; offshore wind fasteners targeting 10% of fastener sales by FY27 end
items.quote: I think totally newly launched products contribute about 30% to 35% of the order book, which includes bolts which we have started manufacturing in Chennai. This also includes smart fasteners again which we entered into the global market in offshore wind sector.

items.statement: Chennai Phase 2 mezzanine (10k sq ft) completing Q2; Phase 1 utilization 70-80% in Q1, targeting 80-90% in Q2
items.quote: Q1 Phase 1 capacity utilization is almost 70%-80%, and we are seeing in Q2, we should be touching 80%-90% of Phase 1. By the time we are working on the Phase 2 capacity, which should be there partly in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Chennai facility EBITDA parity with Wada expected by Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28 at 70-80% utilization
items.quote: Like, once we complete the Phase 2 and start utilizing approximately 70% to 80%, which should happen in Q4, so maybe in Q4 or next year Q1.

items.statement: Forward forex cover reduced from 70% to 40% due to euro volatility; rupee weakening bias
items.quote: Now we have reduced it to 40% of the total collection, primary because of the huge volatility in the foreign currency, especially as far as euro is concerned.

items.statement: KPMG working capital study initiated July; report expected Q2; action plan and targets by Q3
items.quote: They started this study in July, and we are expecting report by August end or this quarter, and based on that report, we will be planning the actions and targets in quarter 3.

items.statement: Wind turbine fasteners ~25-26% of Q1 sales; offshore wind fastener ramp-up to 10% of fastener sales by FY27 end
items.quote: I think in totality, wind turbine fastener contribution in total sales of quarter one will be approximately 25%-26% approximately.

items.statement: Maintain True North objective of at least INR3,000 crores EBITDA by FY30 with marginal dilution only for ESOPs and return to pre-TruBridge net debt
items.quote: I want to reiterate that we are continuing to maintain our True North objective of getting to at least INR3,000 crores in EBITDA by fiscal year '30, number one.

items.statement: Aspire to grow legacy IKS book at north of 12% constant currency and drive non-linearity in profitability
items.quote: I continue to say that, that should be our aspiration, that will be our aspiration that is not a guidance. I'm not good enough to predict that. I can tell you that we will aspire to continue to grow that $388 million book of business at 12% which is the legacy IKS business and continue to drive non-linearity as it relates to profitability in that growth

items.statement: Target blended EBITDA margin back to early-to-mid 30s over next couple of years from pro forma 26%-27% post-TruBridge consolidation
items.quote: Needless to say, perhaps any deal that has strategic rationale still has to work financially. And so, happy to note that we have our plan laid out for getting back to our early-to-mid 30% EBITDA margins after our pro forma drop post-consolidation of TruBridge initially to, you know, the 26%-27% range.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 reported EBITDA 33% at INR294 crores; adjusted for INR20 crores acquisition costs EBITDA ~35% at INR314 crores
items.quote: Happy to report another strong quarter of financial performance in which we've delivered 21% year-on-year growth for fiscal Q1, 12% in constant currency, resulting in revenues of about INR893 crores. And while doing that, we've been able to deliver 33% EBITDA at INR294 crores.

items.statement: Expect integration expenses similar to Q1 (INR20 crores) in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We do expect a little bit of integration expenses going into the next quarter as well. It's likely to remain in a similar range.

items.statement: Signed significant wins: large California health system Epic partnership, national musculoskeletal leader RCM deal, expanded Advocate Health Care partnership in revenue cycle and coding, StrideCare vascular surgery partnership
items.quote: Happy to announce that we've had a couple of very significant wins in that land-and-expansion strategy over the last couple of quarters, and I'll talk a little bit about those in the financials.

items.statement: Pricing pressure exists with competitive intensity but signing healthy priced deals including recent five-year lock-in at very healthy price
items.quote: Pricing. Look, I think with increasing competitive intensity, there is always going to be pricing pressure, but I will say that we are signing deals that are very healthy price. We just signed another deal recently that was a five year lock-in at a very healthy price.

items.statement: Market growing at ~8%, outsourced TAM at ~12%; competitive intensity increasing naturally
items.quote: The overall market is growing at close to 8%, and the outsourced TAM is growing at about 12%.

items.statement: Building proprietary SLMs from TruBridge's 5M+ patient dataset to reduce LLM dependency; deploying explainable AI via ARAI knowledge graphs; stratifying deterministic vs non-deterministic tasks for autonomy roadmap
items.quote: We've already well into our journey of starting to build that database. TruBridge has already started to do it. We're quickly bringing momentum to that, and as that structured database comes together, we will start training our own SLMs.

items.statement: TruBridge revenue base reset ~$40M annually due to conservative rev rec ($2-3M/qtr), exit unprofitable services ($8M/qtr), and customer discounts for transformation ($2-3M/qtr)
items.quote: We actually believe that the operating revenue that once translated into IKS on a steady state basis will be about $300 million a year. Again, we'll produce the same $68 million in EBITDA margin starting out at the $300 million a year than the $340 million a year that we were anticipating pre-close.

items.statement: Achieve INR3,000 crores EBITDA by FY30 without significant dilution beyond ESOPs and without expanding net debt beyond pre-TruBridge levels
items.quote: Number two, I also want to provide that we will be able to do that again with very marginal dilution, perhaps associated with ESOPs to incentivize our people, but outside of that, that objective is to achieve that without any further dilution to shareholders outside of ESOPs and getting back to that net debt position that we had prior to the TruBridge acquisition, right?

items.statement: TruBridge operating EBITDA confirmed at ~$68M annually on ~$300M revenue (22-23% margin); combined run-rate ~$688M revenue with ~INR1,800 crores EBITDA
items.quote: I think we're happy to confirm that that is the operating EBITDA that we are essentially inheriting through the TruBridge acquisition. So, very happy with that.

items.statement: Legacy IKS 10-year revenue CAGR ~29% with non-linear PAT growth; post-IPO 18-20 months: EBITDA from INR647 crores to INR1,148 crores (~40% CAGR)
items.quote: Just in the last, call it 18 to 20 months, with no dilution, we have basically taken that business of INR647 crores to INR1,148 crores on a standalone basis, pre-TruBridge, right? And so, that is about nearly a 40% CAGR when annualized in terms of growth between TTM September 2024 and TTM June 2026.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue INR893 crores (21% YoY, 12% CC); PAT INR193 crores (28% YoY); adjusted FCF yield 90%
items.quote: Happy to report another strong quarter of financial performance in which we've delivered 21% year-on-year growth for fiscal Q1, 12% in constant currency, resulting in revenues of about INR893 crores.

items.statement: Headcount grew 4.2% YoY (12,300 to 12,889) vs 12% CC revenue growth demonstrating non-linearity
items.quote: For example, our 12% year-on-year growth for this quarter that you've experienced has come on a people increase of only 4.2%, right?

items.statement: Tax rate 22.4% in Q1 FY27; legacy IKS expected 22-23% for rest of year; combined pro-forma tax rate to be discussed next quarter
items.quote: The Tax rate was higher this quarter. This is something we had discussed last quarter as well. Tax expenses were in the range of 22.4% this quarter. For legacy IKS for the rest of the year, this is likely to remain in the 22% to 23% range.

items.statement: Maintains mid-teens revenue growth target for FY27 despite Q1 impact from West Asia crisis; expects to make up lost revenue in H2
items.quote: We have tried to maintain a like-to-like growth of mid-teens in that mid-teens range. We will be able to do that and that's why if you look at it our top line increased by 5% but as I mentioned earlier we saw a INR14 crores impact in terms of cancellations of business in our books.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance of INR500 crores; INR53 crores spent in Q1, balance ~INR350 crores to be spent over next three quarters
items.quote: In the first quarter, we have spent around INR45 crores towards CWIP and renovation of INR3.5 crores and for the new restaurant Project Grain around INR4 crores. So put together is around INR53 crores and the balance amount will be spent over next three quarters.

items.statement: Total development pipeline capex of INR3,600 crores for ~1,700 keys by FY30; INR400 crores deployed by FY26, funding mix 60% debt / 40% internal accruals
items.quote: Our development pipeline entails a total Capex of approximately INR3,600 crores to build out ~1,700 upcoming keys by FY30 taking our portfolio from 1,600 keys to 3,300 keys. Of this, around INR400 crores had already been deployed by FY26.

items.statement: Luxury/upper-upscale mix to rise from 14% to 31% by FY29 and 38% by FY31 via Grand Hyatt, InterContinental, JW Marriott, Ritz-Carlton additions
items.quote: This will lift our luxury and upper upscale mix from 14% today to 31% by FY29 and 38% by FY31, positioning BHVL in the segment with the strongest pricing power and demand-supply mismatch.

items.statement: Portfolio ADR target above INR7,500 to offset GST impact; Q1 FY27 ADR at INR7,241 (+7% YoY); Kochi Courtyard expects minimum 10% ADR growth this year
items.quote: We had also mentioned we are doing our best to push the entire portfolio and each hotel above that INR7,500 so that that GST impact can also be negated.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 34.8% (+9% YoY EBITDA); GST 2.0 impact of 1.6% on margin; finance cost fell >50% to INR8.7 crores driving 140% PAT growth
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA increased by 9% year-on-year to INR46 crores with EBITDA margin at 34.8%. GST 2.0 had an impact of 1.6% on the EBITDA margin during the quarter.

items.statement: Courtyard by Marriott Chennai WTC (45 keys) to launch Q3 FY27; expects starting ADR INR9,000 and stabilized occupancy ~80%
items.quote: We do expect a minimum of a INR9,000 as a starting ADR and then we expect that to grow in the coming months. This is one hotel that we expect to stabilize quickly and should be continuously occupied through the week so we see stabilized occupancies at about 80%.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt launch delayed from FY28 due to approvals; JW Marriott Chennai and Trivandrum hotel targeting commissioning by 2030
items.quote: We had mentioned that there would be a slight delay in the Grand Hyatt which we had originally slated for FY28 but there is going to be a slight delay in the Grand Hyatt because we're waiting a few approvals there.

items.statement: Under discussion for hotel acquisition using IPO proceeds; hopes to conclude transaction in FY27 subject to due diligence
items.quote: Yes, we're under discussion. We're hoping to conclude a transaction in FY27. But it is subject to due diligence.

items.statement: Bangalore hotels: focus on maintaining occupancy while driving ADR growth over next three quarters; portfolio occupancy stable at 76% with 5 of 9 hotels above 80%
items.quote: Our focus over here is to maintain our occupancy now and focus on positioning only. We do see the market becoming stronger as months go by and we will have an increase in ADR over the coming three quarters.

items.statement: Net cash position INR108 crores as of June 30, 2026 after INR468.1 crores debt repayment from IPO proceeds; effectively no institutional debt
items.quote: As of 30th June 2026, we had a net cash position of INR108 crores reflecting the continued strengthening of our balance sheet. On debt and deleveraging post-IPO, we deployed INR468.1 crores of the proceeds towards debt repayment which has left us with effectively no institutional debt on our book.

items.statement: FY27 steel volume target of 1.2 million tonnes reaffirmed with 20% YoY growth expected
items.quote: We remain on course for our 1.2-million-ton steel volume target for FY27.

items.statement: FY27 non-steel revenue growth target of 25% YoY reaffirmed
items.quote: Going forward, we are confident of meeting our projections given in the last quarter, 20% growth in steel volumes and 25% in non-steel.

items.statement: Medium-term target of 4% EBITDA margin with 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth
items.quote: Yes, I think our target would be in the medium term to go to around 4% EBITDA and maintain our 20% volume growth for steel and 25% for non-steel.

items.statement: Added 3 fulfillment centers in Q1 FY27; plan to add 5 more in coming quarters
items.quote: We have added three fulfillment centers in Q1 and we have plans to add around five more in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 3.26%; normalized for Rs 10 cr inventory loss would be ~3.8%; steady-state target 3.5%+
items.quote: I think that resulted in erosion of around 10 odd crores, which I think if I factored that in, we would have obviously been at a much another 0.5% bps would have probably gone up in the EBITDA, EBITDA, which means we would have been around 3.8 or so.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin target of 3.5%+ for remainder of FY27
items.quote: Ideally, yes. And steady state, we are looking at 3.5% kind of EBITDA margin as we go forward.

items.statement: Steel demand recovery visible from June-July; industry activity points to recovery from Q2 FY27
items.quote: Industry activity in the past month points to a recovery in steel demand from Q2 and with prices now stabilizing, the operating backdrop for the remainder of FY27 looks distinctly better.

items.statement: Non-steel growth driven by 32% YoY growth in fittings & sanitaryware; tiles stabilizing; UPVC roofing gaining traction
items.quote: Our performance for the quarter was driven by a 32% growth in fittings and sanitary ware, our largest product category.

items.statement: Inventory losses of Rs 10 cr in Q1 due to steel price correction in May-June; Q4 FY26 had Rs 15 cr inventory gain
items.quote: I think that resulted in erosion of around 10 odd crores, which I think if I factored that in, we would have obviously been at a much another 0.5% bps would have probably gone up in the EBITDA.

items.statement: Target to reach 2 million tonnes steel volume in ~4 years with geographic expansion and market share gains
items.quote: And our target would be around 4 years to achieve the 2 MT target.

items.statement: Focus on value-added steel products (cut-to-length) and expanding private label products in retail
items.quote: One is we are working on infrastructure addition where we can focus on value-added products in steel. So, this would be more cut to length and more products which customers would help us increase our customer base with OEMs.

items.statement: Acquisitions on the table if suitable opportunities found
items.quote: Definitely on the table. If we find any suitable acquisitions, definitely it will be there.

items.statement: Target to sustain EBITDA margins between 37% and 38%
items.quote: As these conditions gradually normalize, we believe our international business remains well-positioned to continue growing while contributing positively to our overall margin profile and supporting our target to sustain EBITDA margins between 37% and 38%.

items.statement: Phase 1 commissioning targeted by April 2027, major equipment deliveries by October 2026
items.quote: Construction remains on schedule, and we continue to target commissioning of Phase 1 by April 2027. Deliveries of all major long-lead equipment are expected to be completed this October.

items.statement: Greenfield facility at Navsari expected to start supplies in Q3 FY27 after FDA and customer approvals
items.quote: We expect that approval to come in this quarter as well, and for supplies to start from this facility in Q3.

items.statement: 21 customers at lab validation, 16 at pilot scale, 7 at pre-commercial/commercial validation for battery materials
items.quote: Today, 21 customers are at the laboratory validation stage, 16 customers have progressed to pilot-scale evaluation, and 7 customers have successfully completed pre-commercial or commercial validation and are currently engaging in active off-take discussions.

items.statement: Expect to conclude two significant binding off-take agreements for battery materials later this year
items.quote: Based on the progress of ongoing commercial discussions, we remain optimistic about concluding two significant binding off-take agreements later this year.

items.statement: Core specialty ingredients margin in mid-30s; NSS dragged consolidated specialty margin to 26%
items.quote: The business without NSS still was in the mid-30s in terms of margin profile. NSS has had a tough, challenging quarter, and that has kind of dragged down the profitability to the 26% level.

items.statement: Target to return to 37%-38% EBITDA with greenfield utilization and sales growth
items.quote: Historically, we before we kind of made the investment in building out the sales team and all, we were maybe tracking around 37% -38% EBITDA, and with the right level of utilization of the new greenfield and sales coming from both these markets, we're comfortably we can kind of achieve those levels.

items.statement: Phosphoric acid price increased ~50% in Q1; price pass-through largely in Q2
items.quote: Continued logistics disruptions, elevated freight costs, and a sharp increase in sulfur prices resulted in phosphoric acid price increasing by approximately 50% during the quarter.

items.statement: Majority of phosphate price pass-through to reflect in Q2 FY27
items.quote: So, I think a lot of the pass-through has happened later in Q1, so I would say marginal benefit or kind of we would have received in Q1, but in Q2, majority of the sales would happen with the pass-through.

items.statement: Phosphate demand exceeds current manufacturing capacity, providing visibility for balance of FY27
items.quote: Customer demand for our phosphate portfolio continues to exceed our current manufacturing capacity, providing us with excellent visibility for the balance of the financial year and reinforcing our confidence in the sustainability of this growth.

items.statement: Specialty ingredients demand healthy; LPG shortage was supply-side constraint only
items.quote: It is important to highlight that this was purely a supply-side constraint rather than a demand issue. Customer demand remained healthy throughout the quarter, our order pipeline continues to strengthen, and production has now normalized.

items.statement: Absorbis Bisglycinates Q1 sales already surpassed full FY26 total
items.quote: Sales during the first quarter have already surpassed the total sales achieved during the entire previous financial year, reflecting strong customer acceptance of our differentiated specialty ingredients.

items.statement: NSS Europe facing energy cost headwinds; expect flattish FY27 with single-digit growth
items.quote: I would say FY'27 continues to -- they may have a more like a flattish year with, I would say, maybe single-digit growth.

items.statement: Target steady-state working capital cycle of ~150 days long-term (ex-battery)
items.quote: In the near term, the long-term sustainable would be closer to 150 days.

items.statement: Targeting ~70% capacity utilization in FY27 and EBITDA margin ~17% by FY28
items.quote: We are targeting to hit a margin of about 17%. By FY28.

items.statement: Core garment EBITDA margin turned positive at 3.4% in Q1 FY27 vs negative last year; targeting pre-tariff levels
items.quote: Our core EBITDA margin i.e. the garment business alone excluding our other income, turned positive at about 3.4% against a marginally negative number in the same quarter last year

items.statement: Expect demand in India to strengthen substantially to absorb planned capacity expansion to 38 lakh pieces
items.quote: We see demand going up in India substantially to be able to use up these capacities that we plan.

items.statement: Offered price discounts to US customers to share tariff burden and retain volumes; margins took a hit
items.quote: We had to partner with our U.S. customers on prices, on discounts. This is in order to hedge the increase in cost so that they don't have to pass too much of a cost on to the end consumer as well.

items.statement: Expanding into women's bottoms, outerwear and athleisure to supplement premium men's bottomwear; not moving away from core
items.quote: We aren't looking to move away. We are intending to supplement our capabilities. Women's wear is an obvious easy entry because a women's wear bottom and a men's wear bottom aren't too different in terms of product.

items.statement: MOU with Sri Lankan contract manufacturer as contingency for adverse US tariffs; evaluating own plants in Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Nepal for geographic diversification
items.quote: We have got an MOU with a Sri Lankan contract manufacturer that helps you change the country of origin. So, if something were to happen on goods made in India, we can offer our customers goods made in Sri Lanka as well.

items.statement: Target to collect minimum Rs. 380 crores from legacy government receivables in remaining nine months of FY27
items.quote: remainder of nine months minimum, and this I am talking minimum, target is Rs. 380 crores will come from that in total

items.statement: Biochar plant recently started; revenue impact expected from next fiscal year
items.quote: You will start seeing because project has recently started any impact on numbers from the next fiscal

items.statement: Hi-Tech margin fell to 14.4% from 16.6% YoY due to unabsorbed fixed costs; plastic improved to 11% from 10%; Agro-Processing down 3%
items.quote: Hi-Tech division delivered about a 14.4% margin versus similar period at 16.6, so approximately 2% reduction, and plastic, in fact, improved by about a percent or so from 10 to 11, and Agro-Processing also came down by 3%

items.statement: July revenue already positive vs April-June; August-September look good; institutional large-diameter pipe negotiations indicate surplus demand
items.quote: We have registered already positive revenue growth in July as against April to June, significant revenue growth here. And August and September also seem to be good

items.statement: One large Pune water supply project with triple-digit billing remaining; other projects only Rs. 40-50 crores left
items.quote: In the other projects apart from the one project in Pune, I think total billing left is about approximately closer to Rs. 40-50 crores only

items.statement: Expect to cover Q1 EBITDA margin reduction in second half; full-year profitability better than last year
items.quote: we believe we should be able to catch up in the second half of the current fiscal year to cover what is lost

items.statement: Targets 8-10% top-line growth for FY27 and FY28, assuming industry grows 6-7%
items.quote: you can assume from all the businesses put together, we are looking at between 8% to 10% growth, quarter-on-quarter. That is the number we are looking.

items.statement: Lighting solutions margin temporarily hit by legacy professional lighting contracts; expects return to double-digit EBIT in a quarter or two
items.quote: once we are off this legacy project, we will go back to double-digit margins in overall lighting.

items.statement: Cost inflation 6-12% across categories; managed via selective price hikes and savings; no major further price increases needed for rest of year at this stage
items.quote: it is as high as 13% in some categories, coolers were the highest in terms of cost, like, yes. So, it is anyway between 6% to about 11%-12%. And most of that, between pricing and savings, we have managed to sail through

items.statement: Consumer products returned to growth (1.7% YoY) after multiple declining quarters; non-summer categories and Morphy Richards grew double-digit; fans declined due to supply issues
items.quote: consumer products growing at 1.7% after a decline for multiple quarters

items.statement: BLDC fan contribution 30-35% industry-wide; company under-indexed but growing faster; premiumization driving margin improvement
items.quote: the estimates which we have on BLDC vary between 30% to 35%. We are slightly under-indexed versus the industry, but it is growing much faster and we will be in our rightful share as we progress.

items.statement: Wires business progress better than expected; will play significant role in lighting segment going forward
items.quote: in wires, our progress is better than what we were expecting. And that gives us confidence that it can play a significant role moving forward to our business.

items.statement: No major capex guidance given; focus on brand investment and distribution expansion (direct dealers in South/West, e-commerce, quick commerce)
items.quote: we are equally mindful about our counter share and the focus is on that also. The second piece was on e-commerce. E-commerce contributes to approximately 15%.

items.statement: Commodity price volatility remains a risk; legacy professional lighting contracts pressuring margins temporarily; fan supply chain issues (gas, PCB) largely resolved
items.quote: the external environment continues to remain volatile. And we will assess the impacts before taking any pricing decisions.

items.statement: Working capital hovering at 50-60 days; inventory slightly up due to seasonal stocking; Q1 operating cash flow negative due to Morphy Richards acquisition tax payments
items.quote: it is largely hovering around between 50-60 days. So, that's the larger trend. And we see some buildup to happen because of the seasonal business.

items.statement: FY27 DI+CIP volume guidance lowered to ~575,000 tons from earlier 650,000-700,000 tons due to slower JJM fund releases
items.quote: So, Sir, we had erstwhile indicated the volume of I think 650,000 tons to 700,000 tons. But due to the slower initial release of JJM, we are expecting to reach a quantity of around 575,000 tons.

items.statement: Export mix target 22-25% of total volumes for FY27, with 60-70% focused on Europe/UK and rest on Middle East, Africa, Southeast Asia
items.quote: And we are expecting that at the end of the year, we will be exporting around between 22% to 25% of our total volumes.

items.statement: Current executable order book ~300,000 tons (~5 months), ~50% from JJM; Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, UP, Rajasthan most active
items.quote: So, we have a total order book of around 3 lakh tons, which works out to around five months. So, JJM, this order book, JJM would be around close to 50%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 9.5% in Q1 FY27; targeting 12-13% by Q3/Q4 FY27 on cost optimization and volume recovery
items.quote: Going forward, I think Q3 FY'27, Q4FY'27, we should be hitting EBITDA number of 12% to 13%.

items.statement: DI pipe net realization improved to ~Rs 55,000/ton in Q1 FY27 from ~Rs 50,500/ton in Q4 FY26; management sees rock-bottom pricing behind
items.quote: These are net realizations of around Rs. 50,500 per ton for Q4 FY'26and in Q1 FY'27 is around Rs. 55,000 per ton.

items.statement: Target DI pipe revenue share down from ~85% to ~55% in 4-5 years via valves (double revenue to Rs 800-1,000 cr), paints (Rs 800-1,000 cr in 5 yrs), ferroalloys, railway rubber
items.quote: From today, it's around 85% and in the next four to five years, you will go to around 55% or so.

items.statement: T.I.S. Italy: FY27 revenue target EUR 42-45 mn (vs EUR 38 mn avg last yr), EBITDA margin 14-15%, PAT ~8%; Q1 FY27 revenue EUR 10 mn, EBITDA margin 13%
items.quote: Sir, by the end of this financial year, we are expecting, as mentioned, it was going to be 20% above last year's average of around EUR 38 million. So, we should be, hopefully, we'll reach a number of EUR 42 million to 45 million in revenue.

items.statement: Long-term FY30-31 target: Revenue Rs 7,000-8,000 cr, EBITDA margin 13-13.5%
items.quote: I am very certain that we can look at a growth of revenue to around Rs. 7,000-8,000 crores with EBITDA level of 13%-13.5% by FY30 & FY31.

items.statement: Saudi anti-dumping duty impact minimal: Saudi sales only 2-3% of total, expected to drop to 1.5%, easily diverted to other GCC/Africa markets
items.quote: The total sales of Electrosteel Castings to Saudi Arabia was to a total of, it is about 2% to 3% of our sales. So, that is a quantity that can be diverted to other markets pretty easily.

items.statement: Term debt Rs 340 cr, scheduled to reduce to Rs 230 cr; net debt Rs 876 cr (Jun 2026) down ~Rs 1,100 cr in FY26; Rs 700 cr cash available for bolt-on acquisitions
items.quote: We have around Rs. 700 crores of capital on our books which we are ready to invest.

items.statement: Valves: India facility operational by end FY27; target 40-45% Asia contribution in 3-4 yrs; Q1 FY27 valve revenue grew 18% YoY
items.quote: We also expect our valves manufacturing facility in India to commence operations by the end of this financial year, supporting future growth and improving profitability.

items.statement: Railway rubber components: Board approval taken; registration 4-6 months; additional equipment under installation (3 months); leverages existing gasket plant in Andhra Pradesh
items.quote: So, possibly, it will take four to six months time for us to get it registered.

items.statement: Regulatory cost impact for this fiscal is here to stay; next fiscal will annualize this fiscal's impact
items.quote: I think on the regulatory part, regulatory part for this fiscal is here to stay. Next fiscal, obviously, we'll annualize this fiscal.

items.statement: Margins significantly impacted by war-led crude oil and forex costs plus regulatory energy and e-waste changes; pricing could not fully recover combined impact
items.quote: One thing in the quarter that did happen, partly expected, partly unexpected, was our margins were significantly impacted due to both the impacts of the war, basically in two areas: one is in anything that was influenced by crude oil, which obviously pricing went extremely high and continues to be quite high, and the second part of it was all the energy changes. Regulatory changes, which included

items.statement: Took multiple price increases in April and May to partly cover war-led commodity inflation and regulatory inflation but not fully
items.quote: We were able to take up in April and May pricing, which partly covered the war-led inflation and the regulatory inflation, but not fully, like I said, thereby impacting margins.

items.statement: Industry volume growth in mid-single digits; company grew revenue 11.4% driven by market share gains, premium mix and pricing
items.quote: Our industry, which is the refrigerators and washers, multi-brand outlets volume grew in mid-single digits, which also helped us. But that was not the only factor which drove our top-line. On top of the industry growth, our market share also grew, and we grew market share in double basis points across both the categories of refrigerators and washers, which helped our top-line growth.

items.statement: Invested INR 245 crores in Pune plant for four-door premium refrigerator (Luxuriem) production
items.quote: We are extremely proud that this entire thing is made in India, thought through by India, executed by India, and it's rolling off our Pune lines where we've invested INR 245 crores on this technology.

items.statement: War impact on crude oil prices and forex (USD from 88 to 95-96) significantly increased costs; e-waste accounting at higher rate than commercially procurable
items.quote: The dollar used to be 88 last year, now is sitting at about 95, 96, and obviously, that's quite an extraordinary increase. So, these two things basically have impacted significantly on top of the regulatory costs that I spoke of. And of course, we continue accounting for e-waste at the higher level.

items.statement: Achieved record revenue of INR 2,582 crores in Q1 FY27, highest ever quarterly revenue in company history
items.quote: We delivered a top-line revenue of INR 2,582 crores. This is the highest ever revenue for the quarter in the history of Whirlpool, which we've delivered.

items.statement: Maintained negative net working capital in Q1 FY27; recovered all air conditioner working capital invested last quarter
items.quote: We have a net negative net working capital this quarter, and all the investments we made in the Whirlpool of India Limited August 06, 2026 last quarter in air conditioners have been fully recovered, as you'll see later

items.statement: Launched Luxuriem 654-liter four-door premium refrigerators with triple evaporator, 6th Sense AI freshness detection, glass-steel finish, Obsidian interiors; fastest convertible (<30 min) in class
items.quote: We are very, very happy to introduce to you Whirlpool Luxuriem, which are the four-door premium refrigerators. We're introducing the 654-liter four-door premium refrigerator. These have several, several firsts, fantastic products. This is India's fastest convertible in its class. It converts in less than 30 minutes from a freezer to a fridge, which is unmatched in India.

items.statement: Launched 11 kg top load Bloomwash in Juniper Green with load-sensing quick wash (30/35/40 min) and Soft Sense auto softener dispensing
items.quote: We also launched large size in top load Bloomwash, which is our hero, we launched the 11 kg in a completely new color, which is being quite well-received in the market, it's called Juniper Green. And what is really cool about this is that typically, if there's a quick wash cycle that other machines have, whether you put in a small load or a medium load or a large load, typically other machines was

items.statement: Dynamix dispenser technology now in 50% of semi-automatic washer portfolio including new 8 kg capacity; guarantees zero detergent patches
items.quote: We have now launched even 8 kg capacity in the Dynamix dispenser, and now 50% of our semi-automatic washing machine has this Dynamix dispenser, which is re-commoditizing semi-automatic washing machines.

items.statement: Elica subsidiary revenue up 26% and profits up 22% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Elica, we're very pleased to say, continues with a very strong performance. Revenue is up 26% and profits are up 22%.

items.statement: War-related supply chain constraints (LPG, oil-based products, components) in April-June; no production stoppages despite daily stock uncertainty
items.quote: We have navigated the challenges on supply chain, which were extremely high in April, May, June, whether it was availability of LPG, or whether it was availability of oil-based products, whether it was availability of components and parts. There were a lot of challenges that happened because of this situation that we have in the Middle East. But we were able to, in fact, very proud to say, deliver

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin squeezed 377 bps to 4.6% in the quarter due to unprecedented cost increases from geopolitical instability and currency depreciation.
items.quote: The EBITDA came in at INR 120 crores at 4.6%, and we saw squeeze of margins, wherein EBITDA margin squeezed by 377 basis points, and we delivered profit before tax of INR 120 crores at 4.6%.

items.statement: Multiple price increases taken in the quarter were insufficient to fully offset the magnitude of commodity and forex-driven cost increases, resulting in net under-recovery.
items.quote: We took a couple of price increases in the quarter, but then the price increases were not sufficient enough to mitigate the 100% of all the cost increase, which was like of a very different magnitude which we saw in the quarter, and as a result of this, there was a net under-recovery, and hence, the squeeze on margins.

items.statement: Management expects the next quarter (JAS) to be financially tough due to seasonally weak volumes for refrigerators and ACs while commodity costs and forex remain high.
items.quote: I think going forward, July, August, September, to answer your question, will continue to be very challenging, because very simply, we are a refrigerator, air conditioner company is more than two-thirds of our revenue. And this is the weakest quarter for refrigerators and air conditioners. But the commodity costs are very high. The forex is very high.

items.statement: Capex budget is not a constraint; decisions are driven by project ROI. Base ongoing capex is about INR 100+ crores annually, with additional investment for new products, innovation, and automation.
items.quote: So, it's very difficult to pinpoint a number to say that this is what we're looking at from an exact number perspective. But yes, the base ongoing capex is about 100 plus, we keep investing based on specific initiatives, innovations, automations, etc.

items.statement: No immediate large capacity capex needed in next 6-12 months as overall capacity utilization is at 70-75%; front-load washer capacity has significant headroom with no three-shift operation yet.
items.quote: Our capacity on an annual basis across all products is about 70%, 75% utilization. So, there is no immediate requirement to put a large capex, immediate, I mean, the short-term, let's say, next 6 months, 12 months, to a large capacity capex.

items.statement: Full-year revenue growth outlook is highly uncertain; management is figuring out production and availability on a month-on-month basis and cannot predict market growth accurately.
items.quote: I would say without exaggeration that even now, we are literally figuring out how to manage on a month-on-month basis in terms of production, in terms of availability, etc. We are not out of the woods as an industry on all of these things.

items.statement: E-waste provisioning has been a drag for 18 months; resolution depends on government-industry-recycler negotiations and would provide a significant margin benefit if settled at lower levels.
items.quote: It's been a very long time. It's been like what, 18 months since we've been accruing the higher amount. And obviously, releasing that up would be a big benefit for people like us who are accruing at the highest value, right?

items.statement: Premium portfolio (front-load washers and air conditioners) performed well, supporting top-line growth through higher ASPs, while the company pursues premiumization in top-load washers via High DC strategy.
items.quote: Our premium portfolio, which is the front load washing machine and the air con business, has done pretty well, and which also aids, given that these are high-value products and higher ASP products, aids in the top-line growth.

items.statement: Whirlpool Corporation (parent) stake is at 39.75%; Whirlpool India operates at arm's length with no business discussions, only technology licensing and brand/quality forums.
items.quote: Ever since the stake of Whirlpool Corporation went down to below 50%, they're at 39.75% now. The way we're working is that, and this is for all our shareholders and investors to know, the way we're working is completely at arm's length.

items.statement: Board is cognizant of large cash balance; aims to finalize a capital allocation blueprint within 12 months covering capacity, new products, automation, and inorganic opportunities.
items.quote: within the next 12 months, I need to have a very clear plan on how to utilize the cash, including any other options which, you know, I don't want to get into Whirlpool of India Limited August 06, 2026 the detail, but whatever I'm not able to use, then there could be other options for that as well

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin also squeezed ~300+ bps to 5.1% in the quarter; Elica business delivered 26% revenue growth and 22% PBT growth.
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, we delivered a top-line growth of INR 2,727 crores in this quarter, again a double-digit growth of 12.1%. We delivered an EBITDA of INR 139 crores at 5.1%, and delivered a PBT of INR 139 crores at 5.1%. Again, on a consolidated basis, we saw a similar margin squeeze of about 300 plus basis points.

items.statement: Regulatory energy efficiency changes for refrigerators and ACs occur every three years (next due Jan 2029); India's standards are already among the world's highest, adding recurring cost pressure.
items.quote: Technically speaking, if '26 January is the refrigerator one now, as per the calendar, the next one should be '29 January. So, other than that, we know we don't have, we don't expect anything else.

items.statement: Management took price hikes in April and May 2026; full reflection expected in Q2 FY27 (July-September).
items.quote: we have taken up prices in April and May, as I said before. I'm not going to say exactly what the numbers are, but we have taken up prices two consecutive months because we had to. And it was not fully reflected in April, May, June, but it will be fully reflected in July, August, September and beyond.

items.statement: Gross margin compression driven primarily by war-related commodity/forex impact (larger) and energy regulation charges on refrigeration business (about half of war impact).
items.quote: let's say there are two big things which impacted us a, war-related stuff which is a combination of all the things between the oil prices, the effects and a lot of other things and then the second big element especially on materials or gross margins was on the energy regulation of charges impact on refinery or con business. If I just split broadly to say that in the order of magnitude, the war imp

items.statement: P4G program continues on BOM, engineering and supply chain costs but cannot fully offset Black Swan event impact due to material availability constraints.
items.quote: we are absolutely doing that, but we are not able to get substantial savings to offset all the impact of this Black Swan event.

items.statement: Refrigerator and washing machine market grew 4-5% in Q1 FY27; Whirlpool gained 30-35 bps market share.
items.quote: the market itself hardly grew, so the mathematics, as you rightly pointed out, the market grew about 4%-5% across refrigerators and washers. And our market share, as I told you, grew about 30-35 basis points.

items.statement: Elica business growing strong double-digits driven by market responsiveness, dual strategy (mass + premium), and pricing covering cost increases closely.
items.quote: We expect to see strong growth coming out of Elica, obviously always strong double-digit growth.

items.statement: Commodity and forex outlook uncertain; management hopes for resolution within FY27 but cannot comment.
items.quote: of commodity pricing, excuse me, commodity and forex, this is anybody's guess, you know, your guess is as good as mine. We all pray and hope that this gets resolved soon for the good of the world, and frankly, also for the good of industry. And that is something that we are absolutely unable to make a comment on. But hopefully it's not too far away, and it happens within this fiscal

items.statement: No industry-wide pricing agreement possible (illegal); each player decides independently based on competitive dynamics and volume-profitability trade-off.
items.quote: the law for anybody to come together on pricing, which is why we decide what to do on pricing independently. Obviously, we check what's happening in the market, which is just basic market intelligence when consumers are being offered prices, obviously, you know what the pricing is. So, there is no, absolutely no chance of any industry-wide agreement on pricing, because that would be

items.statement: ESOP scheme for senior management: 100% performance-based cliff vesting after 3 years at face value, stricter than prior time+performance vesting from Whirlpool Corp.
items.quote: What we've done now is made a 100% of the shares for senior management vest only after 3 years, which is cliff vesting. And completely based only on performance.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 revenue growth guided at high single-digit with EBITDA margins around 25%
items.quote: We would like to reiterate our earlier guidance of high single -digit revenue growth for the organization with EBITDA margins of around 25% during the year.

items.statement: U.S. business expected at USD 1.1-1.2 billion for FY27
items.quote: For the full year, we expect the U.S. business to be in the USD 1.1 billion to USD 1.2 billion range, aided by growth in base business, our injectable launches, and contribution from Pegfilgrastim offsetting the additional competition in products like Mirabegron and Tolvaptan during the year.

items.statement: U.S. quarterly revenues expected at USD 250-280 million for next couple of quarters
items.quote: We expect revenues to be anywhere between USD 250 million to USD 280 million a quarter over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: U.S. business expected to return to growth trajectory from FY28
items.quote: We believe that all these initiatives should help in the U.S. getting back to its growth trajectory from FY28 onwards.

items.statement: India formulations to outperform IPM by 1.2x-1.3x
items.quote: We remain confident that our India Formulations business will continue to outperform IPM by 1.2 x - 1.3x to supported by a strong sales force of more than 11,000 people and pipeline of more than 80 new product launches over the coming years including innovation in-house and in-licensed products.

items.statement: Chronic share target 70% in India over next five years
items.quote: The Chronic segment accounts for around 67% of our portfolio, up from around 65% in FY26, and we have set ourselves a target to increase the share to 70% in the next five years.

items.statement: Novel proprietary products to contribute one-third of India revenues in 10 years
items.quote: We have set ourselves a target of novel proprietary products contributing one third of our India revenues in the next 10-year timeframe.

items.statement: R&D spend expected around 8% of sales for full year
items.quote: For the full -year, R&D is expected to be around 8%.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected 27-28% for full year
items.quote: For the full -year, however, we expect it to be in the region of 27% - 28%.

items.statement: Other Developed Markets growth 10-20% over next couple of years
items.quote: We are looking at potentially double-digit growth, in some years., higher than others, but anywhere between 10% to 20% over the next couple of years.

items.statement: VISUfarma acquisition closed, net cash reduced to INR 2,831 crores
items.quote: Net cash stood at INR 2,831 crores as of 30 June vis-a-vis INR 4,636 crores as of 31 March quarter, largely due to closure of our VISUfarma acquisition.

items.statement: Gross margin 74.6% in Q1FY27, up 330 bps YoY
items.quote: This quarter was at 74.6% up from 71.3% in Q1FY26 last year. This 330basis points YoY improvement is driven by multiple factors, which includes better product mix, higher profitability in India, increased volumes , cost improvements and efficiencies which we have undertaken over the last several quarters.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 30% in Q1FY27, full year guided around 25%
items.quote: EBITDA excluding forex and other income during the quarter was INR 2,464 crores vis-a-vis INR 1,641 crores in the same period last year , an increase of 50% YoY. Margins were 30% vis-a-vis 26.6% last year in the same period, an increase of 340 basis points over the last year. For the full year, as indicated by Vinita, we expect EBITDA margins to be around the 25% mark.

items.statement: Plan 50+ U.S. launches in 3 years with 10 exclusive FTFs, 5 biosimilars, 2-3 505(b)(2)s
items.quote: In the next three years, we expect to launch 50 plus products in the U.S. with 10 exclusive first-to-files, five biosimilars, as well as two to three 505(b)(2)s.

items.statement: Increased competition on Mirabegron and Tolvaptan to impact U.S. sales in FY27
items.quote: However, we anticipate the business to revert to its growth trajectory from FY28 largely led by a rich pipeline of products including exclusive first-to-files, biosimilars and 505(b)(2) products.

name: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 80 bps QoQ to 26.4% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA margins at 26.4% improved by 80 basis points quarter-on-quarter and profit after tax grew by 27.7%.

items.statement: Gross margin declined 90 bps YoY to 52.5% due to higher VAM costs
items.quote: Gross margins at 52.5% were lower than last year same period by 90 basis points.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance corridor maintained at 20-24% for operating flexibility
items.quote: And of course, they recovered and the world that we are living in with all these risks and uncertainties, we would still prefer to keep a corridor, which gives us enough operating flexibility. So no need to change it at this stage.

items.statement: VAM consumption cost rose to $1,370 in Q1 FY27 from $924 YoY and $800 range in Q4
items.quote: VAM consumption in the quarter was at $1,370 as compared to last year $924 and the fourth quarter was in the $800 range.

items.statement: Price increases of 2-12% taken across C&B categories with time-weighted impact flowing into Q2-Q3
items.quote: It could go from, let's say, 2% to about 12%, to be fair. And some of it has a component of the time-weighted component. So therefore, it all didn't go on April 1, to just put it in perspective.

items.statement: Consumer & Bazaar underlying volume growth at 12.5% in Q1 FY27, above 3-year CAGR of ~9%
items.quote: And against that, we are now in quarter 1 at 12.5%. So therefore, just the quarter 4 I think is one data point.

items.statement: Growth businesses (Dr. Fixit, Roff, Projects) seeing accelerated momentum at 2-4x GDP
items.quote: I think for our growth businesses, particularly Dr. Fixit, Roff, even our projects business, if you look at Pidilite Projects Group and others. Some of our other growth businesses, we are seeing accelerated momentum. I'm saying so that's good news. We are in the range of 2x to 4x, but we are seeing accelerated momentum in the underlying volume growth in some of our categories.

items.statement: Tile adhesive penetration only 25-30% in India; Roff growing fastest and gaining share
items.quote: Just to give you a sense, the penetration of tile adhesives in India is still not more than 25%, at best 30%. So, the room for growth exists for all players. We can only confirm that we are growing fastest amongst all the players, which means we are gaining share in a fast-growing category.

items.statement: Export volumes declined due to geopolitical issues; expected to recover as situation normalizes
items.quote: B2B exports UVG for the quarter was -8.4%. And overall exports for the company also degrew in the first quarter, largely because of geopolitical issues in some of our key markets.

items.statement: VAM prices volatile ($800-$2,000 range); may pass rebates if raw material costs decline
items.quote: So it's far more dynamic than maybe we've seen in the past, maybe we have seen it once or twice. But even there, the fluctuation is, I think, quite unique. And as you know, is a little bit decoupled from directly crude as well.

items.statement: Expanding plant network for tile adhesives; Nio Pro production scaling from 1 to 4 plants
items.quote: We are now going beyond 1 plant to 4 plants to ensure that this is available in wider geographies.

items.statement: UnoFin (decorative finishes) seeing green shoots in commercial and high-end residential projects
