items.quote: Only for quarter 2 because the shutdown cost also gets added in the cost in quarter 2 and also because in Northeast, the rain is more so of course, the fixed costs are getting absorbed by a lower volume. So it may be about INR1,400 for quarter 2

items.statement: Q1 capex spend of INR93 crore; full-year FY27 capex plan unchanged at INR500 crore
items.quote: This quarter, we have spent around INR93-odd crores. And our planning what we have given INR500 crores for this quarter this year, that will continue. That will still holding on the same.

items.statement: Total North expansion capex estimated at INR2,600-2,700 crore (ex-GST), INR2,900 crore with GST
items.quote: The overall capex of this thing is about INR2,600 crores to INR2,700 crores is that what we are expecting. And I think we are focusing in the next 2 years to primarily get this capex going in North.

items.statement: Assam subsidy income for FY27 revised down to INR115 crore from INR145 crore due to new payout formula
items.quote: So what I expect for this year is not about INR145 crores, but about INR115 crores.

items.statement: Fuel cost per ton rose to INR1.55 in Q1 from INR1.33 in Q4 FY26; expected to fall to INR1.45 in Q2
items.quote: So in the fuel cost in F Y26, quarter 4 was about INR1.33, which has gone up to INR1.55. We expect in Q2 onwards, the cost should come down to about INR1.45

items.statement: Cement prices broadly stable in Northeast and outside markets (Bihar, West Bengal) in Q2
items.quote: And on the prices, the prices, I think if I compare -- I think the prices are broadly stable in Northeast as well as in outside Northeast markets of Bihar and West Bengal, even in the quarter 2.

items.statement: Northeast demand muted in Q1-Q2 due to elections and floods; pent-up demand expected to drive pickup in H2
items.quote: So I think that because of the lack of demand in the first 2 quarters, like quarter 1, quarter 2 and because of the floods, which have completely on the Northeast at the moment, I think that when the floods subside, which is basically quarter 3 and 4, I think there should be some pent-up demand which gets released in those 2 quarters in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Northeast industry growth expected ~7% in FY27; Star Cement targeting 8-9% growth in Northeast
items.quote: I think for the industry, I would say that the growth rate should be about 7%. For us, I hope that we can do about 8% to 9% in Northeast.

items.statement: Assam government changed subsidy payout to equal annual installments over remaining 12-year period, reducing annual accrual by INR20-30 crore
items.quote: But now what we've done is that they have divided the number of -- the amount of subsidy by 12 years, right? So out of that, 2, 3 years have already gone through whatever remaining subsidy was there, they divided it by the remaining number of years, right, as per the new circular. So the impact of that is about INR20 crores, INR30 crores

items.statement: Not actively considering QIP; can fund North capex at 1.5-1.6x net debt/EBITDA
items.quote: So we are not at the moment actively thinking of QIP. We will do it at the opportune time in case there's opportunities available for which we need to further raise money that may be organic or inorganic.

items.statement: Building Solutions (AAC/RMC) revenue target of INR150 crore on ARR basis by Q4 FY27
items.quote: And I think we should be able to reach that ballpark figure. At least on an ARR basis, we should be able to reach that 150 number by the quarter 4.

items.statement: Green power share at 3% in Q1 (incl. WHRS); evaluating solar/group captive for Q3-Q4
items.quote: Green shares for this quarter was about 3%. This, of course, includes the WHRS as well. Shravan Shah: Tushar Bhajanka: And this we are planning to introduce solar some group captive opportunities that we're evaluating. I think in quarter 3 or quarter 4, we will also share the details of those contracts

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of INR8,100 crores, meaningfully higher than outlook communicated 9 months ago
items.quote: Our current FY27 revenue target of INR8,100 crores is meaningfully higher than the outlook we had communicated 9 months ago.

items.statement: Aspiration to reach INR18,000 crores to INR19,000 crores revenue by FY30
items.quote: We remain firmly on track to achieve our aspiration of INR8,100 crores by FY27 and INR18,000 crores to INR19,000 crores by FY30.

items.statement: Will revise revenue target after Diwali, analyzing one more quarter before giving new guidance
items.quote: We will revise our target after Diwali. We'll analyze one more quarter, and we will give our new guidance post Diwali. That's our plan.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin increased to 9.3% in Q1 FY27 vs 9.1% in Q4 FY26, driven by Advance Gold and non-22 KT jewelry mix shift
items.quote: Our consolidated gross margin increased to 9.3% in Q1 FY27 versus 9.1% in Q4 FY26, an improvement of 27 basis points.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance maintained at 8.5% to 9% despite mix improvement due to volume discounts on 22 KT jewelry
items.quote: The guidance of 8.5% to 9% gross margin we are giving, because, in the journey of business, you can see if 22 karat is somebody is taking volume, we have to pass on some 0.25% to 0.5% discount also to the customers.

items.statement: PAT margin guidance of 5.25% maintained, with aim to reach INR1,000 crores PAT
items.quote: From the overall guidance to the Street, 5.25% of the PAT margin still holds, while we plan and aimed at how we can reach the magical number of INR1,000 crores of PAT going forward.

items.statement: Advance Gold sales at 17% in Q1 FY27, significantly ahead of 15% expectation for FY27
items.quote: I am pleased to share that we have achieved 17% sales on the Advance Gold model, significantly ahead of our expectation of 15% of the Advance Gold model for FY27.

items.statement: Non-22 KT jewelry share increased from 10.5% to 14% of volume, studded jewelry from 1.65% to 2.1% of revenue
items.quote: the share of non-22 KT jewelry has increased from 10.5%in Q4FY26 to 14% in Q1 FY27 due to structural shift in customer preference towards lower Karatage jewelry. Sky Gold & The share of studded jewelry has also increased from 1.65% in Q4 '26 to 2.1% in Q1 '27

items.statement: CEO target: Advance Gold 15% average this year, 20% next year, 25% third year, 30% by 2030
items.quote: We have achieved 18% Advance Gold business, and we have given him the target for this year to be average of 15%, next year 20%, and the third year of 25%. In 2030, we will achieve 30% of the Advance Gold business.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 55%-60%, sufficient until 2028; future expansion via leased model with INR80-100 crores capex (12%-20% of PAT)
items.quote: Currently, the capacity utilization is close to 55%- 57%. And looking at the current projection numbers, we are good till 2028. And post that, we may look at a new facility, but that we will continue on the leased model, and capex will not be very big. It will be close to INR80 crores to INR100 crores.

items.statement: Q2 better than Q1 due to Navratri-Diwali orders, Q3 better due to marriage season, Q4 strong with Akshaya Tritiya deliveries
items.quote: So, we follow Q2 is better than Q1, and then Q3 is better. And again, the fourth quarter, March is better than that because Akshaya Tritiya's major delivery goes in March.

items.statement: International expo generated prospective order pipeline of INR30-45 crores across U.K. and European markets
items.quote: The response was highly encouraging, resulting in strong initial interest and helping us to build a prospective order pipeline of approximately INR30 crores to INR45 crores across the U.K. and European markets.

items.statement: Cyber fraud incident involving INR10.7 crores; INR3.5 crores recovered, legal proceedings ongoing for balance
items.quote: Out of that, INR10.7 crores was the total amount involved, but such incidents have unfortunately become increasingly prevalent across many organizations which are listed on the BSE and NSE.

items.statement: Generated INR30 crores operating cash flow in Q1 FY27, marking milestone towards cash flow positive model
items.quote: I am pleased to report that during quarter, the company has generated approximately INR30 crores of operating cash flow, marking an important milestone in our journey towards building a stronger and more self-sufficient business model.

items.statement: Net working capital cycle at ~60 days, targeting 2 days improvement YoY to reach 52 days by 2030
items.quote: We are at close to 60 days. And in terms of strategy, we are looking at reducing or improving on the working capital days by 2 days year-on-year, with an overall target to reach 52 days by 2030.

items.statement: Target mid-teens revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: our full year projection continues that we are targeting to hit around mid-teens kind of growth. There is a seasonality also which makes a difference. So we still stick to our projections of mid-teens 17-19

items.statement: Target 14% EBITDA margin by Q4 FY27
items.quote: our target still remains that by quarter 4 of this financial year, we get to our 14% EBITDA target. So that's the journey plan we have

items.statement: Target 15-16% EBITDA margin by FY30
items.quote: So over a period of next 3 to 4 years, say, by 2030 financial year, we want to hit EBITDA closer to 16%. That's the aim as of now. So somewhere between 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Price increases of 2-2.5% in consumer business; input inflation impact ~1.5% in Q1, higher in Q2
items.quote: taken so is around 2%, 2.5% in the consumer business, which is English Oven and Cremica. And this quarter has seen a partial impact of that because the price increase was taken during the quarter. Amit Purohit: Okay. And inflation -- cost inflation was just 1% on a Y-o-Y basis? Manu Talwar: About 1.5% approximately was the inflationary impact for this quarter, the next quarter is higher. So, the q

items.statement: No long order book; month-to-month orders for bakery and exports
items.quote: we -- in both these businesses, we don't have any long order book. We get orders on a month-to-month basis, right? So it's not that like projects and other things where you get 6 months or 9 months orders, it's nothing like that. It's a month-on-month order we get.

items.statement: Capex funding 60% internal, 40% debt; debt-equity comfortable
items.quote: in terms of cash flow side, if you would have looked at our debt equity ratio is more than comfortable. We normally do a bridge between borrowing and investing our own money even in this year, the additional capex, which we are planning to do in this particular year, it will be almost 60% -- 60% coming out of our own funds and 40% would be borrowed funds.

items.statement: Bakery EBITDA above company average; biscuit EBITDA slightly below average
items.quote: our Bakery business EBITDA is above our company average and our Biscuit business EBITDA is slightly below our company average. That's how the EBITDA margins of both the businesses stand out.

items.statement: Full-year services revenue guidance trimmed to INR2,650-2,750 cr from INR2,700-2,800 cr due to cash supply squeeze; total revenue guided at INR2,750-2,850 cr
items.quote: We are setting our full year services revenue goal at INR2,650 crores to INR2,750 crores against the INR2,700 crores to INR2,800 crores earlier. The total revenue, including product revenue, is estimated accordingly at INR2,750 crores to INR2,850 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance raised to ~27% from 25-26% guided in May, reflecting pricing discipline and tech-driven productivity
items.quote: Against this, we are raising our EBITDA margin guidance to about 27% from the 25% to 26% we had guided in May.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin expanded 170 bps QoQ to 27.2%, driven by automation, pricing focus, and higher-margin Tech & Payments mix; management aims to maintain ~27% for FY27
items.quote: EBITDA came in at INR173 crores, up 8.9% on a year-on-year basis and 6.8% sequentially, with margin expanding 170 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 27.2%.

items.statement: Steep state minimum wage hikes (6-60%) and 8% fuel cost increase necessitate larger price increases; private bank discussions progressing, PSB repricing via IBA committee expected by end-Q2
items.quote: On the cost side, this year has seen very steep increases in state-level minimum wages, ranging from 6% to as much as 60% in certain key large states. Fuel costs are up 8% this year. Now this will all necessitate a larger price increase than average.

items.statement: Currency supply at ~70% of indents in Q1, recovered to ~80-85% currently; expected to normalize by end-Q2. Currency in circulation up 12% YoY, same-store retail volumes flat
items.quote: As of today, the currency fulfillment has recovered partially through Q2 to about 80% of indented volume. And in our plan, we now assume that this should improve gradually by the end of the quarter.

items.statement: Won INR500 cr orders in Q1, led by HDFC Bank mandate (6,000 ATMs, 5 years, INR400 cr TCV); now have long-term contracts with all 3 largest banks
items.quote: On the contract wins, we won INR500 crores of orders in Q1. The largest of these is the HDFC Bank mandate, which we announced in May, 6,000 ATMs over 5 years at a TCV of INR400 crores.

items.statement: Tech & Payments segment at 18% of services revenue in Q1, expected to cross 20% by Q4 FY27; growing 35-40% vs 11-14% for ATM/Retail platforms
items.quote: Technology and Payments segment, which was 7% of our services revenue in FY22, has grown to 16% in FY26, is 18% in this quarter, and we expect this to cross 20% contribution by the end of Q4.

items.statement: Persistent currency supply shortfall may lead to pruning of underperforming ATMs from BLA estate; EBIT impacted by INR18 cr revenue drop in BLA business
items.quote: If the currency supply and the transaction levels do not improve, we will prune the persistently underperforming ATMs out of our BLA estate.

items.statement: Completed share buyback of 49.39 lakh shares at INR340/share (INR168 cr) on June 19, 2026; ~INR400 cr cash on books; surplus capital to be returned via dividend/buyback after inorganic needs
items.quote: As you are aware, we completed a share buyback on June 19, 2026, for 49.39 lakh shares at INR340 per share, totaling to INR168 crores.

items.statement: Services revenue growth guided at 15-19% for FY27; ATM/Retail platforms 11-14%, Tech & Payments 35-40%; double-digit revenue and profit growth expected
items.quote: Combined, the services revenue growth should be in the 15% to 19% range.

items.statement: HAWKAI Enterprise proven at national scale in large PSU bank; bidding into strong pipeline for next 18-24 months; ALGO MVS deployed at SBI, going live at ICICI in Q3
items.quote: The demanding AI use cases developed there were tested and deployed over a national network, and this will be key for us in competing for a large pipeline of similar bids across banks in the next 2 years.

items.statement: FSS acquisition integration on track; synergy benefits expected from H2 FY27; INR20 cr revenue accrual in Q1 from FSS contracts being novated
items.quote: In Q1, I think it will be roughly close to a INR20 crores accrual from FSS.

items.statement: No plans to enter merchant acquiring/payment aggregator space; view it as highly competitive with established leadership and difficult to make money
items.quote: As of now, we don't have any plans to be in the merchant acquiring space. We find that space to be very competitive and very difficult to make any money.

items.statement: Express volume growth tracking towards upper end of 20-30% range for FY27
items.quote: Broadly looking at where we are at the start of Q1 and the early part of Q2, we're towards the mid or upper side of the range that I spoke about, which is a 20-30% range.

items.statement: No structural change expected to FY27 margin trajectory despite Q1 headwinds
items.quote: I don't anticipate any structural change to our margin trajectory for the year or beyond either.

items.statement: PTL yield improved to nearly Rs 12 in Q1FY27, up 37 paisa YoY with only 6 paisa from fuel
items.quote: More importantly, yield continued to improve in the PTL business and has risen to close to nearly Rs. 12 for Q1FY27, leading to a revenue growth of over 20% year-on-year.

items.statement: PTL yield improvement is structural and sustainable across all distances
items.quote: On PTL yields, this isn't a seasonal improvement in yields at all. This is actually a planned and delivered improvement in yields.

items.statement: Fuel surcharge contracts cover 97-98% of volumes; full pass-through impact visible in Q2
items.quote: We are covered upward of 97, 98% at this point in time.

items.statement: Minimum wage increases to be passed through to customers; negotiations underway
items.quote: As minimum wages get revised, we do anticipate that they will continue to get revised. We will pass that on in the form of price increases to customers down the line.

items.statement: Express volumes grew 55% YoY in Q1FY27 to 322 million packages; D2C volumes growing 40-45% YoY
items.quote: Our express business delivered 322 million packages in Q1, which represents a growth of 55% year-on-year.

items.statement: Delhivery Direct GMV at Rs 150 Cr in Q1, ahead of FY27 plan of Rs 250 Cr
items.quote: As things stand, we are currently at a GMV ahead of plan at close to about Rs.150 Cr GMV and expect that we will close the year higher than originally planned.

items.statement: Automation investments in industrial systems, ASRS across fulfillment centers to address labor shortages
items.quote: We continue to bring in new industrial automation systems across both our key transportation facilities in terms of in-facility movement and automated storage and retrieval systems across our fulfilment centers.

items.statement: Chronic labor shortages, election and weather disruptions, geopolitical uncertainty, fuel inflation, statutory labor code changes impacted Q1
items.quote: There have been chronic labor shortages across the industry throughout the period of April, May and June. We also had significant disruptions due to both elections as well as weather in this quarter.

items.statement: Supply chain services revenue near Rs 200 Cr in Q1; new large contracts starting up, expected to stabilize by Q2-Q3
items.quote: Our supply chain services business came in at nearly Rs.200 Cr of revenue for Q1. Profitability was affected by the start of two new large contracts, which we expect will stabilize over a combination of Q2 and early Q3.

items.statement: Delhivery Maps launched based on proprietary GIS; initially for internal use, later for external customers
items.quote: technology standpoint, we launched Delhivery Maps, which is based on our proprietary GIS information. Obviously, we've been deploying Delhivery Maps across internal operations for a while now but intend to also make this available to external customers going forward

items.statement: NBFC initiative asset-light; will facilitate fleet financing via lending partners, not lend from balance sheet
items.quote: Our intention is not to lend heavily off the Delhivery's balance sheet at all. We have a number of high quality lending partners who we intend to work with.

items.statement: Express service EBITDA margin target 16-18% for FY27, confident of reaching higher end in H2.
items.quote: In Express, our target has been in that 16-18% service EBITDA range. We continue to maintain that and we remain confident that in the second half of this financial year, we will be in that range, in fact, closer to the higher end of that range.

items.statement: PTL internal objective to exit FY27 at 15-15.5% service EBITDA margin, up from 13.4% exit last year.
items.quote: This financial year, our internal objective will be to exit closer to 15-15.5% service EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 normalized EBITDA would have been 30-35 Cr higher but for fuel pass-through delay and service quality spend.
items.quote: So normalised, it would have been at least probably about 30-35 Cr higher compared to where we ended up.

items.statement: Strong volume growth across Q3, Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27; 55% higher volumes in Q1 FY27 vs Q1 FY26.
items.quote: We are also carrying 55% higher volumes in Q1FY27 as compared to Q1FY26.

items.statement: Labour availability complexity, changing statutory labour codes, wage inflation, and difficult climate operating environment are key risks requiring mitigation.
items.quote: Labour availability is going to get more complex, statutory labour codes are changing. Doesn't matter whether it's for fixed employees, or whether it's for gig workers. And either way, wage inflation is a reality. The reality is that the operating environment from a climate standpoint is becoming more and more difficult to operate in.

items.statement: New initiatives investment earmarked 160-175 Cr for FY27, largely for Delhivery Local; on track to stay within budget.
items.quote: The amount that we had earmarked, up to about 160-175 Cr for the financial year, at least looking at current trajectory, we should be well within that.

items.statement: Delhivery Local ARR at 150 Cr in July, ahead of 250 Cr FY27 exit target; contribution margins better than expected.
items.quote: We were expecting to exit the financial year at a 250 Cr ARR. But, here we are, we're sitting in August and we're already hitting, sorry, in July, and we're hitting a 150 Cr ARR.

items.statement: Supply chain services margin dip due to two large new contract ramp-ups (industrials and consumer durables); existing contracts remain profitable.
items.quote: The major change is the start of two new big contracts. At the start of the contract, what typically tends to happen is that we will commission the fulfilment centers across multiple sites. Inventory starts rolling in. There's a period where there's a mismatch between inventory inbound and inventory outbound.

items.statement: Network structural shift: opening freight service centers withdraws heavy loads from delivery centers, reducing average DC size and rental/supervisory/storage costs.
items.quote: When you activate a freight service station in Patna, which now has the ability to do PTL freight as well as heavies, what's happening is you're withdrawing the average weights from the DC network back into a gateway or a service center. And when you do that, the average size of delivery centers that you need in that specific city suddenly crashes.

items.statement: Ahmedabad city for Delhivery Local set to break even in Q3 FY27
items.quote: the first city that we launched in Delhivery Local, for example, which was Ahmedabad, in fact, looks set to break even most likely at some point within quarter three.

items.statement: Delhivery Local revenue run-rate expected to exceed FY27 target of Rs 250 Cr
items.quote: We had anticipated that we would do 250 Cr in this financial year. It does look like we will exit with a higher ARR than that given where we are today.

items.statement: Corporate overheads stable at 9.3-9.4% of sales; increase due to business development team build-out and technology costs
items.quote: corporate overheads as a percentage of sales has been stable at around 9.3, 9.4%.

items.statement: Contractual manpower expense Rs 371 Cr in Q1 FY27, up to 12.8% of revenue from 12.2% YoY
items.quote: That number would be 371 Cr for this quarter, this first quarter of FY27.

items.statement: Integration depreciation on unused assets recurring; cash integration cost guidance remains Rs 300 Cr
items.quote: our initial guidance of 300 Cr was a cash integration cost guidance.

items.statement: Record express volumes and high PTL volumes in Q1 FY27; external environment easing
items.quote: this decent start to Q1 with record volumes on express and high volumes on PTL continues.

items.statement: Heavy freight loads over 200 kg withdrawn into gateways; structural network change reducing service center size
items.quote: loads that weigh over 200 kgs have now been withdrawn wherever possible into gateways as opposed to being delivered from forward service stations.

items.statement: Network capacity additions in first half of financial year ahead of peak Q3/Q4
items.quote: your first quarter onwards, we would also have our network expansions coming in, because the first half is where the capacity is added.

items.statement: Fuel and minimum wage increases impacting linehaul, last-mile, and consumables costs
items.quote: fuel cost increases and minimum wage increases and the oil price linked items cost increases, which was more specific to this financial year.

items.statement: Cross-sales team fully active across 100 cities generating volumes for express, PTL, and cross-border
items.quote: the cross-sales team is fully active now. And we're already seeing strong traction on cross-sales in terms of generating volumes for the express business, generating volumes for the PTL business, and generating volumes for the cross-border business as well.

items.statement: Management is skeptical demand will go higher rather than lower; sees no demand issues for next few years in Mumbai redevelopment
items.quote: The demand has never gone down in Bombay. So, demand in terms of demand, I'm very skeptical that it is going to go on a higher side rather than on a lower side.

items.statement: Sold 44,000 sq ft in Q1 FY27; inventory sell-through: Rashmi Square ~80%, Rashmi Signature ~65%, Rashmi Delight ~40%, Rashmi Manorath ~20-25%, Rashmi Icon and Avenue just started
items.quote: One number I want to specifically mention is the area sold, which in Q1 FY27, we have sold around 44,000 square feet.

items.statement: War-related material/labor cost spikes in April-May 2026 have subsided; Govind Dalvi project on hold due to government stay on 500m section; no other operational challenges
items.quote: The war thing which has now subsided, initially during the first quarter in April-May, there were few challenges, but now everything has subsided.

items.statement: Revenue recognition follows Ind AS percentage completion method; 6 ongoing, 5 upcoming, 14 completed projects
items.quote: Accounting standard we follow the Ind AS, wherein we follow the percentage project percentage completion method. And currently, we have six projects ongoing, furthermore five are in pipeline, and 14 we have completed.

items.statement: Brand building through timely delivery, word-of-mouth, digital presence, channel partner meets, sales lounges; management focuses on project completion over marketing
items.quote: Our major for customer confidence has been delivery of timely. That has been our core. So, we focus more on completing completion of the projects rather than making just the brand visibility.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 10-12% (INR16-17/kg) for FY27; Q1 achieved INR19.6/kg but may not be sustainable each quarter
items.quote: Our targets of INR16 to INR17, or in percentage you can say 10% to 12% of EBITDA margin, is something which we always aim

items.statement: FY27 committed capex of INR150-175 crores for HFFR capacity expansion to 20,000 tons, medium voltage cable capacity in East, Vapi consolidation, and BESS
items.quote: Overall, we expect the year's committed investment will be in the range of INR150 crores to INR175-odd crores

items.statement: Export order book is spot-based (10-20 days visibility); July good, August okay but uncertain due to geopolitical situation
items.quote: Today, if you see, our order books are generally spot, and it is not beyond 10 to 15 days or probably 20 days. So we can comment probably up to August only

items.statement: Cable industry growing 12-13% YoY; Ddev targets 15% volume growth via market share gains in medium/high voltage XLPE and exports
items.quote: In the category -- product category in which we are servicing to all the cable customers, they are growing at a rate of average 12% to 13% only

items.statement: XLPE drives growth (72% mix); Bhiwadi adds 48,000 tons XLPE; HFFR target 20,000 tons; engineering plastics niche (10-15% margin) but low volume
items.quote: You can understand that we have added the capacities for XLPE of 48,000 tons and almost 25,000 tons for PVC. So proportionately if you check, the XLPE will always drive the growth

items.statement: BESS Phase 1 capex INR150-200 crores + working capital INR100-150 crores funded from internal accruals; no substantial debt increase expected
items.quote: The amount of investment will be comparatively limited and will be within the range of INR150 crores to INR200 crores, both considering capex and working capital margin

items.statement: Topline ambition INR5,000 crores by FY30; India power capacity to double to 900 GW by FY32 with INR9 trillion transmission investment
items.quote: We remain firmly on track to achieve our top line ambition of INR5,000 crores by FY '30

items.statement: Zero rejections maintained; 50% Sioplas market share; ~33% XLPE market share; exports 16% CAGR FY22-26; cash conversion cycle normalizing to 55-60 days
items.quote: Importantly, this growth has been achieved while maintaining zero rejections, a robust balance sheet and a consistent record of sustainable value creation

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins to recover to FY26 levels and surpass them before end of FY27
items.quote: We expect to recover to last year's EBITDA margin levels shortly and then hopefully surpass them. We remain confident of achieving this before the end of FY27.

items.statement: Higher blended grape cost impact to subside in Q4 FY27 and fully normalize from Q1 FY28
items.quote: As we have guided previously, the higher blended grape cost is expected to subside in Q4 FY27 and fully normalize from Q1 FY28 onwards, so the full impact will be felt in FY28 as the grape mix rebalances following harvest '27.

items.statement: Expect table grape prices to moderate to less than INR 20/kg in harvest 2027 vs INR 35/kg in harvest 2026
items.quote: We do expect that those grape prices would moderate to less than INR 20 a kilo this time. That's what we really have in our sights, which will definitely lead to a much better margin in terms of our Popular & Economy wines.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of former Chandon estate (Domain RASA) for INR 20 crores; winery ops to start Q4 FY27 harvest 2027
items.quote: A key highlight for the quarter was the completion of the acquisition of the former Chandon estate at an attractive price, as mentioned earlier, of INR 20 crores.

items.statement: Amphitheater expansion at Nashik completed July 2026; new bottle shop at Domaine Dindori opening next week; 5,000 sq ft events pavilion at Nashik on track for Q3 FY27 completion
items.quote: The amphitheater expansion at our flagship Nashik campus was completed in July. And we have our new bottle shop at Domaine Dindori, set to open next week, which is in line with our guidance. Additionally, the construction of our new 5,000 square foot events pavilion at our Nashik campus is on track for completion in Q3

items.statement: Received preliminary approval for 5 additional brand listings in CSD, taking total to 14 from current 9; expect listing process completion by Q3 FY27
items.quote: We have received preliminary approval for five additional brand listings in CSD, taking our total approved wines to 14 from the current 9 when those brands are launched in CSD. This is a very positive development, and we really hope to complete the listing process by Q3 FY27 and introduce the new wines in CSD before th

items.statement: Operating costs reduced 3% YoY in Q1 via organizational optimization and lower ESOP cost, partially offsetting margin pressure
items.quote: Employee benefit expenses reduced by 6% year -on-year, supported by organizational optimization initiatives and a lower ESOP cost. The actions resulted into 3% year -on-year reduction in the operating expenses, helping to partially offset the impact on EBITDA.

items.statement: Elite & Premium portfolio grew 6% in Q1, share expanded 310 bps to all-time high 78% of Own Brands
items.quote: The Elite & Premium portfolio, which is our focus, led the way, growing by 6% in Q1 with its share in Own Brands expanding by 310 basis points to an all-time high of 78%.

items.statement: Economy & Popular segment under pressure from unsustainable competitor discounting; consciously deprioritized to focus on Elite & Premium
items.quote: Coming to our Economy & Popular portfolio. This segment continued to face pressure during this quarter, owing to continued unsustainable discounts by competitors in the market. At the same time, we also consciously prioritized our Elite & Premium portfolio as we have been doing for the past couple of years now.

items.statement: Net debt declined to INR 319 crores (June '26) from INR 345 crores (June '25); expect net debt to continue trending lower by end FY27 vs FY26
items.quote: Our net debt at the end of June '26 stood at INR 319 crores against the INR 345 crores as on June '25. Looking ahead, we expect the net debt levels to continue trending lower by the end of FY27 compared to FY26.

items.statement: Annual new launch guidance of Rs. 150 billion for FY27
items.quote: our overall guidance stays firm to come up with new launches worth Rs. 150 billion for this year

items.statement: Annual pre-sales guidance of Rs. 100 billion for FY27
items.quote: we stay confident of achieving about Rs. 100 billion of pre-sales for the current year

items.statement: Revenue recognition guidance of Rs. 50 billion for FY27
items.quote: we anticipate completing projects in excess of Rs. 5,000 odd crores and recognizing revenue of like Rs. 5,000 odd crores, about 50 odd billion INR

items.statement: Land capex guidance of Rs. 1,500-1,800 crores for FY27
items.quote: the number could be in the range of around Rs. 1,500-Rs. 1,800 odd crores for the year

items.statement: Development and SG&A costs at 30-35% of sale value for new projects
items.quote: Our Signatureglobal ( development costs and SG&A costs do not cost 30%-35% of the sale value for these projects

items.statement: Q1 FY27 average realization Rs. 17,000+ per sq ft vs Rs. 15,000+ in FY26
items.quote: we achieved a per square foot realization in excess of Rs. 17,000 a foot. For the whole of last year, this number stood at a little above Rs. 15,000 odd a foot

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY27 maintained at 30-40% despite demand headwinds
items.quote: We are definitely waiting to maintain the 40% growth guidance and we are already on the track but unfortunate situation due to this war and everything, the demand was a bit on the downside. But yes, we will be maintaining. There is growth already. So, we will be maintaining 30 to 40% of growth this year.

items.statement: Oleo Chemicals revenue target of INR 65-70 crore for FY27 and INR 150-200 crore over 3 years
items.quote: So, from the first year that is the current financial year '27, we are expecting somewhere around INR65 cr. to INR70 cr. of revenue from OLEO. If we see a 3-year horizon, we are targeting somewhere around INR150 crores to INR200 crores of revenue from Oleo itself.

items.statement: Palghar expansion capex ~INR 71 crore, adds 60,000 TPA capacity, fully commissioned May 2026
items.quote: So, it is very much there in the financial. So, it is around –INR 67 crores in the Egypt and INR 71 crores in Palghar.

items.statement: Egypt facility expected to contribute INR 30-35 crore revenue in FY27 (last quarter)
items.quote: Initially we estimated around INR 50 crores to INR 60 crores from Egypt. Now, we are targeting around INR 30 crores to INR 35 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 13-15% and PAT margin target 11-12% going forward
items.quote: In our previous call, we have mentioned that we will expect a margin, EBITDA margin around 13% to 15% going forward.

items.statement: CPVC segment margins currently 18%, targeting 20-21% by Q4 FY27 as utilization improves
items.quote: So, right now, we are on 18%, we wish to be on 20%, 21% by the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Pipe demand picked up from August 2026, expecting good demand through December as PVC prices stabilize
items.quote: The demand has just picked up from August, and we see that from August until December, there's going to be a good demand for pipe sector because right now the PVC prices have been stabilized.

items.statement: Shift to higher-value lead-free and CPVC additives; CPVC started at low margins (3-7%) now at 17-18%
items.quote: We started with a very, very lower contribution margin of 3% to 5% to 7% just to start the business. And that is what has the product mix has changed the dynamics of that. But if you remove, say, for example, CPVC, okay, from our current turnover, you will see that the margins and the contribution margins in our calciu

items.statement: Freight cost spikes from shipping disruptions cannot be fully passed to customers, impacting margins temporarily
items.quote: In scenario like where the war scenario, the shipments are not coming on time, in this case, we are unable to pass on, like the sudden freight cost rise, the sudden CFS charges or sudden any transportation costs, we are unable to pass it on to the customer.

items.statement: Stearates capacity (6,000 TPA) at Palghar delayed to September/October 2026 from August
items.quote: This includes stearates capacity of 6,000 tonnes per annum, which is likely to commence commercial production in September/October 2026.

items.statement: 3-year revenue CAGR target ~35% with commensurate profitability from new capacities
items.quote: Over a period of three, we have already given the guidance that CAGR will be around 35% over a period of three years with commensurate profitability.

items.statement: IPO proceeds utilization: INR 15 crore in Q1 FY27, cumulative INR 165.9 crore, balance INR 45.9 crore as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: During Q1, ~ INR 15 crore of IPO proceeds were utilized, taking cumulative utilization to ~ INR 165.9 crore. The balance unutilized IPO proceeds stood at INR 45.9 crore as of 30 June, 2026.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue INR315.7 cr, up 44.8% YoY; EBITDA INR36.3 cr at 11.5% margin; PAT INR26.1 cr at 8.27% margin
items.quote: For Q1 FY27, our consolidated revenue from operations stood at INR315.7 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of 44.8% and increasing 10.3% sequentially over Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Expect higher sales in Q2 FY27; volume growth in mid-teens for current quarter
items.quote: We are continuing to witness strong demand in the current quarter as well and expect higher sales in the current quarter.

items.statement: Dahej greenfield project (40,000+ MTA) with INR100 cr investment, Phase 1 (15,000-17,000 MTA) targeting November 2026 commissioning
items.quote: With an investment of about INR100 crores, the estimated revenue potential will be INR900 crores. Phase 1 of the zinc oxide production is targeted for commissioning, as I mentioned, in Q3 FY27.

items.statement: Naidupeta brownfield expansion adding ~5,000 MTA, also targeting Q3 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: The brownfield expansion at our Naidupeta facility is also progressing well in parallel, and we expect to commission that also in the Q3 of the current financial year.

items.statement: Structural EBITDA margin range 10-12%; target 14-15% with higher value-added products and Dahej ramp-up
items.quote: Going forward, our target would be to get to an EBITDA margin level of about 14% to 15% with the higher share of value-added products that we are foraying into now.

items.statement: Dahej Phase 1 EBITDA margins expected at 11-12%; revenue potential INR300-400 cr
items.quote: Phase 1, as I just mentioned in the previous question, would be in the range of 15,000 to 17,000 tons per annum, and the revenue potential would be in the range of INR300 crores to INR400 crores, and the EBITDA margins that we expect to generate from that project would be in the 11% to 12% range.

items.statement: Tire industry demand robust: PV +26.6%, 2W +16.5%, CV +16.48%, 3W +11% YoY in Q1 FY27; ~INR25,000 cr capex announced by tire majors
items.quote: As per ATMA, the Q1 FY27 saw volume growth across major vehicle categories: passenger vehicles growing up to 26.6%, two-wheelers 16.5%, commercial vehicles 16.48%, and three-wheelers more than 11% year-on-year.

items.statement: Realizations at new normal due to higher commodity prices; zinc price neutral to EBITDA; cost optimization initiatives yielding sustainable margin improvement
items.quote: I think the new normal in terms of realizations because the prices of all commodities have increased. Zinc is also gone up in Q1, and I don't see any reason why commodity prices would go down in the near future.

items.statement: Geopolitical supply chain disruptions for zinc dross managed via scale, financial strength, supplier relationships; uninterrupted supply maintained
items.quote: Despite the ongoing global supply chain disruption, which has been quite severe over the last quarter because of the war, etcetera. However, JGC's scale, financial strength, and the long-standing supplier relationships have ensured that your company has had uninterrupted supply of raw material.

items.statement: Dubai subsidiary (BDJ Materials and Metal Trading FZCO) proposed for raw material sourcing and global distribution
items.quote: Recently, the company has also proposed to incorporate BDJ Materials and Metal Trading FZCO in Dubai, UAE, which upon incorporation will become a wholly owned subsidiary of BDJ Oxides Private Limited.

items.statement: Reaffirmed minimum 20% revenue growth for FY27 over FY26, targeting INR 1,800-1,900 crores full-year revenue
items.quote: For the full financial year, in terms of top line increase, we said we would be ending somewhere between INR 1,800 crores to 1,900 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 8-9% for full FY27 with exit run rate close to double-digit
items.quote: As far as EBITDA margin is concerned, it's between full year average between 8% to 9% with an exit run rate close to double-digit.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin target of 11-11.5% expected by mid FY28-29
items.quote: The sustainable EBITDA margins which we are targeting is somewhere around 11% to 11.5%, that's what is sustainable EBITDA margins we are targeting.

items.statement: Rajkot main facility recommenced operations, production consolidated from Gondal, expected to lower power, fuel, transportation and operating costs
items.quote: The recommencement of the Rajkot main facility also marks the completion of an important phase in our operational recovery. With production now consolidated from Gondal to Rajkot, we expect further improvement in manufacturing efficiency through lower logistics, power, and operating costs.

items.statement: 5% raw material inflation in Q1, passed on 4.2% via price hikes and grammage reduction, 0.8% absorbed; further 0.2-0.3% pass-through planned in Q2
items.quote: Total inflation which hit us in terms of raw material, it was 5%, out of which 4.2% we have passed on to the consumers and 0.8% sit as an hit to our P&L in the current quarter.

items.statement: Insurance claim of INR 30-40 crores expected in Q2 FY27, documents submitted, process ongoing with PSU insurers
items.quote: We are expecting those things to fall in Q2. However, since this is coming from the insurance company, from the PSUs, but we are quite confident enough because whatever necessary documents were required already submitted to the insurance company.

items.statement: Distribution expansion: 1,000+ distributors, 38% outlets on biweekly servicing, targeting 6 lakh retail outlets by end FY27
items.quote: By end of this year, we'll definitely be present at 6 lakh outlets.

items.statement: Trade discounts reduced to 2.5% in Q1 from 3.5% previously; marketing spend at 1% of revenue in Q1, budgeted 2.2% annually
items.quote: Current quarter it is 2.5%.

items.statement: FY28 EBITDA margin target 10-11% with exit near 11%; PAT margin 7-7.5%; revenue CAGR minimum 20% sustained
items.quote: Similarly, next year, which would be next it would be FY27-28, somewhere around 10% to 11% with an exit to near to 11%. And in terms of PAT margin, it would be around 7% to 7.5%.

items.statement: Chana stocked till Q3 end, potato stocked, palm oil and laminate purchased at market prices with no meaningful near-term increase expected
items.quote: Chana we have stored almost till Q3 end, so there also there has been inflation, but that is not hitting our P&L. Potato we have stored it. Palm oil and laminate prices, we are continuously buy from the market, but we don't foresee any meaningful price increase over there in an immediate near future.

items.statement: E-commerce revenue INR 2.79 crores in Q1 FY27 vs INR 2 crores in Q4 FY26; Modern trade flat at INR 1.85 crores
items.quote: E-commerce, we did exactly INR 2 crores number in Q4 and we did INR 2.79 crores in Q1 of FY27. Modern trade is at par, it was INR 1.85 crores in Q4 FY26 and it remained flat.

items.statement: Management does not give guidance on brand marketing spend but aims to keep overall customer inducement cost (brand, performance, discounts) in the 4% of GTV range when possible
items.quote: we try to stay in the 4% of the GTV range, right, whenever we can. Now, there could be quarters where we go above this, and there could be quarters where we stick to this range.

items.statement: AI investments are front-loaded in platform development, model training, and small language models; technology costs as percentage of revenue expected to become more efficient year-on-year over the long term
items.quote: From a longer-term perspective, our objective remains for technology costs as a percentage of revenue to become more efficient year-on-year, although individual quarters may continue to reflect investments in new capabilities.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA declined 7% YoY to Rs 29.24 crore due to reinvestment of operating leverage from core businesses into hotels and AI
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA came in at Rs. 29.24 crores, lower by 7% than the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Contribution margin grew 13% YoY to Rs 144.94 crore with margin percentage stable at 40.6% vs 40.5% last year
items.quote: Contribution margin grew to 144.94 crores, up 13%, with contribution margin percentage at 40.6% against 40.5% last year.

items.statement: GTV reached all-time high of Rs 5,524.33 crore, up 19% YoY
items.quote: Gross transaction value, or GTV reached INR 5,524.33 crores, a 19% increase over 4,644.66 crores in Q1 last year.

items.statement: Bus passenger segments grew 33% YoY to 0.89 crore with GTV up 39% to Rs 947.43 crore; bus GDP growth 39% YoY, exceeding 60% in 17 states
items.quote: On buses, passenger segments grew 33% to 0.89 crores. GTV grew 39% to Rs. 947.43 crores.

items.statement: Flight segments grew 4% YoY with GDP up 27% YoY; domestic ATV up 22% YoY, international ATV up 38% YoY; industry passenger growth negligible domestically and international market contracted
items.quote: In flights, we booked 0.29 crore flight segments, up 4%, with a GTV of Rs. 2,341.84 crores, up 27%.

items.statement: Train segments down 8% YoY to 2.44 crore due to category constraints; GTV up 4% to Rs 2,138.86 crore; OTA market share increased from ~60% to 63%
items.quote: For trains, we booked 2.44 crore train segment, down 8%. GTV was Rs. 2,138.86 crores, up 4%.

items.statement: Hotels crossed 0.5 million heads on beds in Q1; 90% of hotel bookings from existing captive user base; direct partnerships with 10,000+ hotels across 700 towns
items.quote: During the 1st Quarter, we put half a million heads on beds across our hotel network. We now have direct partnerships with more than 10,000 hotels across nearly 700 towns

items.statement: Acquired 54.66% stake in Brevistay to accelerate hotel supply, on-ground experience, and access double-digit gross take rates across conventional and flexible stays
items.quote: The acquisition of a 54.66% stake in Brevistay accelerates this journey. Brevistay adds direct hotel relationships, feet on the street, supply capabilities and expertise in flexible stay inventory.

items.statement: Aviation capacity cuts by Air India (~20%) and IndiGo (~10%) in JAS quarter leading to year-on-year decline in flown passengers; meaningful capacity restoration may begin only in festive period (Q3)
items.quote: Airline commentary also suggests that meaningful capacity restoration may begin only when the festive period starts in the 3rd Quarter. Therefore, we remain cautious about aviation passenger growth in the near term

items.statement: Train category constrained by Tatkal access changes, lower waitlist inventory, and additional authentication requirements; no immediate policy relief assumed in planning
items.quote: We are not going to predict the timing of policy or platform changes that are outside our control. We are planning the business without assuming any immediate relief

items.statement: Domestic flight ATV increased 22% YoY and 13% sequentially; international ATV increased 38% YoY and nearly 30% sequentially due to Iran conflict impact on oil prices and capacity reductions
items.quote: Domestic average transaction values or fares on our platform increased 22% year-on-year and 13% sequentially. International average transaction values increased 38% year-on-year and nearly 30% sequentially.

items.statement: AI chatbot resolved 92% of customer queries in Q1 FY27, up from 88% last year
items.quote: 92% of our customer queries were solved by the AI chatbot this quarter, up from 88%.

items.statement: Monthly active users 8.5 crore, monthly transacting users 0.42 crore, MTU to MAU ratio nearly 5%, app downloads 3.27 crore in Q1 FY27
items.quote: monthly active users were 8.5 crore, monthly transacting users were 0.42 crore, with our MTU to MAU ratio up to nearly 5%. App downloads for the quarter were 3.27 crore

items.statement: Annual EBITDA margin expected to remain in 14% to 15% range, inclining towards upper bracket given strong Q1
items.quote: Margins are expected to remain at similar levels, right? So we have always guided for a 14% to 15% margin. And obviously, quarter -- as we've always discussed, it's difficult to rate the business quarterly. But overall, at an annual level, we expect that the margins should remain in the 14% to 15%.

items.statement: Volume growth expected to be at least double digits for FY27 and next year
items.quote: So as of now, the expectation is we'll at least be double digits in our volume growth for this year, the next of the year.

items.statement: API segment expected to turn monthly EBITDA positive by end of February-March FY27 and contribute positively to profit in FY28
items.quote: Absolutely right, Abdul. So the whole target is on a monthly level, at least by the end of February, March, we should be monthly EBITDA positive in this business. And then next year, we should start positively contributing to the profit from this segment.

items.statement: Zambia order of $25 million (approx INR240 crores) expected to be delivered in H2 FY27 and similar amount in FY28
items.quote: Zambia is something we expect in the H2 that we deliver for this fiscal, the $25 million, which will roughly translate to almost INR240-odd crores in our revenue. And similar in the next financial year as well.

items.statement: New oral manufacturing facility in Baddi expected to go live by end of FY27
items.quote: We are in the process of setting up one more facility in Baddi, which will go live in the -- almost at the end of this financial year itself, which will significantly boost our oral manufacturing capabilities, right?

items.statement: CDMO model is cost-plus with API price increases passed through at every purchase order
items.quote: So the model has always remained a cost plus, right? So it is at every purchase order or whatever is the prevailing price of the input materials that gets passed through.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven largely by high-value product mix, not inventory gains; sustainable at current levels +/- 0.5%
items.quote: So very limited would be of inventory gains per se. Most of it is largely through high-value products being getting added.

items.statement: Q2 volumes also healthy in high teens; momentum continuing with strong visibility
items.quote: So Vivek, look at the volumes for Q2, right? So the volumes also look healthy in high teens, at least for this quarter as well. As the momentum continues, we can update how the rest of the year also goes.

items.statement: API segment shifting to non-cepha products like linezolid and montelukast, reducing COGS from 90%+ to ~75%
items.quote: Our cepha business, we have been able to come out of the low-margin products and as well as increase our basket of non-cepha products, including linezolid, montelukast and so on, which are helping us improve our margins, right?

items.statement: Management confident in API business turnaround; no plans to exit despite shareholder feedback
items.quote: So the management is fully confident, right? So this is a business we have been investing for over 3, 4 years now. The fruits of which are very visible as we speak, right? So the quarterly losses have been gradually coming down.

items.statement: Acquired Oriflame India's manufacturing business (Roorkee and Noida facilities) to expand into skin care, cosmetics, wellness and color cosmetics
items.quote: On 23rd of July, we announced the acquisition of Oriflame India's manufacturing business. The transaction covers two manufacturing facilities, one at Roorkee, Uttarakhand and other one at Noida, Uttar Pradesh, along with a leased warehouse situated at Noida, Uttar Pradesh.

items.statement: Cash surplus of INR1,616 crores (98% in fixed deposits with nationalized banks); net worth over INR3,400 crores with zero debt; will pursue value-accretive M&A
items.quote: Most of the money, in fact, 98% of the money is parked in fixed deposits with nationalized banks, right? And the money is safely with these banks. There was another question on inorganic. So our net worth sits at more than INR3,400 crores and there is no debt on the company.

items.statement: Auto gross margin sustained at 30.5% in Q1 FY27 despite commodity upcycle
items.quote: Despite a challenging commodity environment, we sustained Auto gross margin at 30.5%, reflecting the underlying strength of our product economics.

items.statement: Expect gross margins to remain around 30-32% over next quarter or two and improve further as commodity prices ease
items.quote: We expect margins to remain in this range over the next quarter or two and to improve further as commodity prices ease.

items.statement: Target opex to come down into ₹300-325 crore range over next couple of quarters
items.quote: Over the next couple of quarters, we expect opex to come down into the ₹300-325 crore range, which is where our target is.

items.statement: ASP expected to remain broadly around ₹1.25 lakh plus or minus 5%
items.quote: Overall I would say ASP should remain broadly around 1.25L, plus or minus 5%.

items.statement: Capex beyond Cell project completion around ₹30-50 crore, use ₹50 crore as target number
items.quote: Except for the Cell project that is now being completed, capex beyond that will be around ₹30-50 crore. You can use ₹50 crore as a target number.

items.statement: Deliveries increased to approximately 39,200 units, nearly doubling quarter-on-quarter, while orders increased to approximately 44,000
items.quote: Deliveries increased to approximately 39,200 units, nearly doubling quarter-on-quarter, while orders increased to approximately 44,000.

items.statement: About 20% of Auto portfolio to remain NMC-based for higher-performance products, everything else moving to LFP
items.quote: Within Auto, about 20% of our portfolio will remain NMC-based for higher-performance and top-end products. Everything else will move to LFP.

items.statement: Electric two-wheeler market grew ~17% QoQ while Ola registrations grew 97%, taking market share from 5.1% to 8.4%
items.quote: The broader electric two-wheeler market grew approximately 17% quarter-on-quarter, while Ola registrations grew 97%, taking our market share from 5.1% to 8.4%.

items.statement: Cell yields were in high-70s to around 80% range when production paused, roadmap to above 90% within a quarter of restarting
items.quote: Yields were in the high-70s to around 80% range when we paused production. There is a clear roadmap to move from there to above 90% within a quarter of restarting.

items.statement: Shakti Gen 2 using LFP cells to be announced 15 August, expected gross margins healthier than Auto segment
items.quote: With Shakti Gen 2 using LFP cells, we expect gross margins to be even healthier than in our Auto segment. It will be announced on 15 August.

items.statement: Mahashakti MoU with Axis Energy for 20 GWh over next five to six years, more demand pipeline expected
items.quote: This MoU is for 20 GWh over the next five to six years, and I feel confident that more demand pipeline will be announced as it develops.

items.statement: Service revenue roadmap targeting approximately ₹400-500 crore by FY2027-28
items.quote: Our roadmap targeting service revenue of approximately ₹400-500 crore by FY 2027-28.

items.statement: Gigafactory expected to be operational at 6 GWh by September, supporting own-cell integration and energy storage opportunities
items.quote: The Gigafactory is expected to be operational at 6 GWh by September, supporting greater own-cell integration in our vehicles as well as opportunities across energy storage and other applications.

items.statement: First batch of dealerships to go live on Janmashtami (early September), meaningful scale targeted before Diwali season
items.quote: We will announce the first set of dealerships, with stores already being set up, to go live on Janmashtami, which is early next month. We look forward to havin g a meaningful scale before the Diwali season

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted operating EBITDA improved from negative ₹326 crores in Q4 FY26 to negative ₹195 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Consolidated adjusted operating EBITDA improved from negative ₹326 crores in Q4 FY26 to negative ₹195 crores in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain EBITDA margins of 29-30% (+/- 100-150 bps) over the next 2-3 years driven by backward integration and scale.
items.quote: we have consistently, you know, informed that the margins of 29%, 30%, plus-minus 100, 150 basis points, we will be maintaining.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex was INR 1,500 crores, with INR 1,250 crores on solar (Seetharampur and Naidupeta) and INR 250 crores on Transcon.
items.quote: So the total capex in the quarter was about INR1,500 crores. Bulk of the capex was incurred on solar, on solar projects, basically both Seetharampur and Naidupeta. And then the remaining was incurred on Transcon, INR250 crores.

items.statement: New orders of INR 3,011 crores for cells and modules in Q1 FY27, taking total order book to INR 15,000 crores including transformers.
items.quote: We won new orders totalling INR3,011 crores for cells and modules, taking our total order book to INR15,000 crores, including transformers.

items.statement: Transformer business EBITDA margins historically 15% across cycle, PAT 8-10%; Premier expects slightly ahead due to low-cost base and synergies.
items.quote: profit margins historically, across the cycle for the transformer businesses have been about 15% in terms of EBITDA, and about 8% to 10% at the PAT level. And we expect that our margins should be slightly ahead of this

items.statement: Expects 1.2-1.3 GW/month avg for PM Surya Ghar and 6-8 GW AC (higher in DC) for KUSUM over next 9 months; C&I demand from Q4 FY27 post ALMM 2.
items.quote: In KUSUM, you know, the government has already given a deadline of March '27 for implementation of all the ongoing projects. So, actually we are expecting a huge step up in the KUSUM scheme. And I would expect the installation over the next nine months to be something between 6 to 8, possibly higher than 8 gigawatts.

items.statement: DCR module share to rise steadily over next 18-24 months; cell sales to decline as 10 GW cell / 11 GW module capacity comes online.
items.quote: over the next 18 to 24 months, is expected to go up steadily.

items.statement: 7 GW TOPCon cell line at Naidupeta in advanced commissioning; trial runs expected later this month; first revenue targeted September, 70% utilization by March quarter.
items.quote: The 7 gigawatt TOPCon cell line is in advanced stages of commissioning, with trial runs expected to start later this month.

items.statement: Non-DCR module business currently unprofitable due to oversupply (250+ GW capacity vs 30 GW demand); DCR segment remains strong and sold out till FY28.
items.quote: non-DCR business is not profitable as we speak. And we can see this in the industry that the non-DCR business, because there is about 250 odd gigawatt of module lines and the entire demand in India is about 60 gigawatt

items.statement: No concrete plan to raise primary capital in near future; enabling resolutions taken annually for flexibility.
items.quote: As we speak, I can confirm that there is no concrete plan to raise any primary capital in the near future.

items.quote: this year also, we'll be in the range of say, for the year somewhere around INR400 or so.

items.statement: Lead acid battery business revenue growth estimated at 9%-10% in medium term, predominantly volume-driven
items.quote: lead acid battery business as a whole, both industrial, mobility, exports, every opportunity put together can still achieve a revenue growth rates anywhere between 9% to 10%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex spend was INR450 crores, majorly towards new energy business
items.quote: Out of the planned INR1,700 capex outlay, during Q1 FY27, we have spent around INR450 crores, with major outlays towards new energy business.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 10.1%, consolidated 9.6% in Q1 FY27; margins impacted by elevated material costs, brand promotions, Amaron Assist, Factory of Future
items.quote: During Q1, the standalone EBITDA margin is around 10.1% and consolidated margin stood at 9.6%. items.quote: Four-wheeler and two-wheeler aftermarket volumes have grown by around 15%, and OEM segments continue to retain the volume growth momentum of around 24% in 4 -wheelers and more than 35% in 2 -wheelers on Y -o-Y basis. items.quote: New Energy business during Q1 Amara Raja Energy and continued to deliver strong performance with revenue growth supported by increased demand for telecom packs and 3-wheeler packs. items.quote: The other important aspect which also led to the moderation in profitability is a significant increase in the procurement costs of alloy, sulfuric acid, and poly. items.statement: BESS plant has reasonable order book visibility in India from major EPC players; expects 5 GWh utilization within 6-7 months of commissioning
items.quote: There is a reasonable order book that we are seeing in India itself, and it may also throw some e xport opportunity as we move ahead in other markets as well. So I don't see a major challenge of maybe in within a period of about 6 months from the time the factory is completed, at least getting to a level of 5 gigawatt kind of a

items.statement: BESS project initial capital outlay INR250-300 crores for 10 GWh capacity; operating margins expected 5%-8%
items.quote: the initial capital outlay for the BESS project could be in the range of, INR250 to INR300 crores, and its capacity will be around 10 gigawatt-hour. So, with the current day's price at the containerized solution level could be anywhere between USD100 to USD120. So asset terms-wise, it will be, definitely higher. But operating margin-wise, it might mimic the way the current pack business is doing.

items.statement: Recycling plant battery breaking in trial production; scrap prices higher than LME lead, causing cost pressure; benefits depend on scrap cost normalization
items.quote: the battery breaking operations is still in the trial production, and also recently the way these scrap prices in the country have moved substantially higher. items.statement: PLI 10 GWh tender application process started; company reviewing qualification criteria and will participate
items.quote: Yes, we are looking at the tender documents, and then depending on the qualification criteria that they have put in, so we will be participating in that tender while we are now weighing our options in terms of how to go about it.

items.statement: China supply chain dependency for cathode material; no specific export restrictions on battery cathode/anode material currently but monitoring geopolitical risk
items.quote: Processed battery material, at this point of time, we have not heard anybody saying that they will not supply. Supply. But from a broader supply chain development point of view, it is definitely a factor that needs to be monitored not only by any one company but at the industry level.

items.statement: R&D spend on cell development estimated at INR100-150 crores in FY27; LFP development prioritized for ESS over EV cells; 16 GWh by FY30 target flexible based on demand signals
items.quote: Even in this year towards the R&D of cell development, we may spend close to about INR100 crores to INR150 crores kind of money. So that kind of expenses we need to incur until some of these cells that we are currently talking about are available for commercialization.

items.statement: Management declined to provide specific revenue or EBITDA guidance, stating it is too early for forward-looking statements and turnaround will be phased.
items.quote: we have not in my earlier question answer, we have given any forward-looking statement or a guidance because Hardik, you have to understand, we are looking for a complete turnaround and that comes in a phased manner.

items.statement: CFO indicated approximately 30% revenue increase from current levels could start contributing handsomely to bottom line, but called it a ballpark number with moving goalposts.
items.quote: from where we are currently, another 30% increase probably we should give somewhere headway into started contributing handsomely to the bottom line.

items.statement: CFO said investments will be calibrated, focusing on small tooling and mould investments financed internally, with no aggressive capex planned.
items.quote: we are not looking for very much aggressive investments to carry out in any of the product categories as such. Some small investments in tooling and the moulds will be carried out and that will be financed largely through internally.

items.statement: Management highlighted strong Q1 branded business growth of 35.8% YoY to Rs 175 crores, driven by LED TV and AC categories.
items.quote: during Q1 Financial Year' 27, our branded business stood at Rs. 175 crores that recorded 35.8% year-on-year growth, primarily driven by strong performance in our LED TV and AC categories.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 100 bps YoY to 17.3% in Q1 FY27 due to better sales mix and improved realizations in AC and LED, partially offset by washing machine margin decline.
items.quote: Our overall gross margin improved to 17.3%, compared to 16.3% in Q1 Financial Year' 26, an improvement of 100 basis points, primarily supported by a better sales mix and improved realizations in AC and LED.

items.statement: Management aims to remain competitive on pricing while managing value chain to protect margins, focusing on product mix optimization.
items.quote: from a pricing perspective, we want to remain competitive in the competitive set we are operating in, while trying to manage the value chain in a manner that we are also protecting our margins.

items.statement: CEO sees strong structural demand across AC, TV, and washing machine categories driven by low penetration, rising incomes, and premiumization trends.

items.statement: AC contributed ~60% of Q1 revenue, LED TV 25-30%, washing machines low single digits; focus on strengthening core categories and launching new products like 100-inch QD Mini-LED TV.
items.quote: AC being seasonal, it's contributing around 60% to the overall turnover, followed by LED, which is almost you can say about 25% to 30%. The rest is with the washing machine.

items.statement: CFO noted balance sheet is slightly stressed with Rs 38 crore borrowing repayable over 18 months; asset monetization not immediately on table.
items.quote: we do have a borrowing balance of around Rs. 38-odd crores, which we will be having the repayment schedule over the next 18 months.

items.statement: Company targeting doubling retail reach in 6-12 months and achieving retail excellence in 800-1000 outlets by end of FY27.
items.quote: we are looking at really doubling our reach in the next 6 to 12 months. That's clearly one of our objectives. And the other objective is achieve retail excellence in a select set of outlets and we have an internal target for us between 800 to 1000 outlets by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Institutional cooling vertical newly set up with active inquiries; expected to become a key growth pillar going forward.
items.quote: we have set that up and we currently have a few good inquiries, and this would become one of our key pillars going forward.

items.statement: CFO targets net working capital days of 30-45 on average for the year, acknowledging seasonality may push it slightly higher during peak periods.
items.quote: somewhere between 30 to 45 net working capital days should be a good benchmark to at least to be there.

items.statement: Wada plant not shutting down; production scaled down to align with branded focus, but facility remains operational and may be utilized for optimum space usage later.
items.quote: we do not have any such plan to close Wada in immediate future. We have scaled down a little production to align with the strategy what we have. And the plant is still on much presence there.

items.statement: PLI scheme participation not actively pursued; company leveraging OEM/ODM partners for component manufacturing benefits.
items.quote: As far as our participations are concerned, we are not currently actively looking into this. Rather, we work with our OEM and the ODM partners to leverage upon the same.

items.statement: Committed 25% organic growth in aerospace for FY27

items.quote: We currently have a robust 10-year order book of INR5,960-plus crores and an active RFQ pipeline of INR1,632 crores.

items.quote: In Aerospace business, we aim that somewhere around 25%. That's our aim at a mature level. And then in our precision manufacturing business, somewhere around 12%-13%. That's a decent margin that we are looking. And

items.quote: So, our goal is definitely to continuously upgrade and go up the value chain. There are several stages that it takes to go up the value chain. items.quote: The dual benefit of the U.K. FTA implementation and rollback of restrictive U.S. tariffs has restored competitive export pricing. Global Tier 1 buyers are actively rebuilding inventory buffers, driving strong order inflows for complex machined components and drivetrain subassemblies.

items.statement: Logistics, tooling (carbide/HSS), and minimum wage costs rising; mitigating via efficiency, operating leverage, and customer pass-through

items.quote: Our estimated numbers earlier were at the INR600 crores range, but we do believe that we will go more than INR600 crores at this point in time and necessary improvements have been made.

items.quote: The consolidation will bring over 400 acres of land, several ongoing projects and some ready inventory at Futurex into the company's portfolio. Friends, our existing portfolio has an estimated unsold GDV of approximately INR 8,000 crores.

items.quote: Some serious order book is coming our way, almost about INR500 crores for 5 years, INR100 crores per annum.

items.quote: In next, by '30. Okay, by FY '30 like for gasket division, we've spoken about INR90O crores of revenue? Definitely. INR850 crore, forging INR600 crores revenue by FY '30.

items.quote: So, we will have a better picture for you around end of September. You know our strategy. So, 1 think they are in the middle of court proceedings. So, by 30 September, we'll have a better picture.

items.quote: Yes, We have received the order from JLR, we have received the order but for rubber components for EV vehicles, which is around INR15 crores to INR20 crores per annum, the supply will start from the first quarter or the second quarter of next calendar year.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin around 17% going forward
items.quote: Around 17%, you can assume.

items.statement: Stellantis chassis division production started in Q1 FY27, expected to bring more forging and heat shield business
items.quote: Stellantis, we started supplying from our chassis division. With this Stellantis, we will get more and more business into our forging business line and also heat shields.

items.statement: Plastic components order INR25 crores maturing from next financial year
items.quote: And we have plastic components, we are getting order of about INR25 crores for plastic components, more orders are coming that will start maturing from next financial year.

items.statement: Management will not provide EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 due to market uncertainty
items.quote: No, I mean, with this kind of uncertainty in the market, I will not be in a position to give you a guidance on the EBITDA margin for the year.

items.statement: Ad revenue declined 11% YoY in Q1 FY27 due to Middle East conflict impacting April and May
items.quote: Coming to advertising revenues. It declined by 11% year -on-year, largely due to the Middle East conflict severely impacting us during April and May as the advertisers remain very cautious.

items.statement: Green shoots visible in ad revenue in June post FIFA rights acquisition with advertisers engaging for premium sponsorships
items.quote: In June, there were some green shoots which were visible post the acquisition of FIFA 2026, digital and broadcasting rights wherein advertisers actively engaged with us to secure premium sponsorship opportunities across platforms.

items.statement: ZEE5 revenue grew 58% YoY to INR 4,571 million in Q1 FY27 with EBITDA of INR 44 million
items.quote: Revenue grew 58% year -on-year in quarter 1 to INR 4,571 million. Further, we continue to invest for future growth by increasing our marketing spend in Bullet which has a huge potential in capturing the attention of new age consumers.

items.statement: Digital business expects growth momentum to continue in Q2 FY27 accruing gains from FIFA
items.quote: The underlying unit economics of the business is intact, and we expect the digital growth momentum to continue in Q2 as well, as we further accrue gains on account for FIFA.

items.quote: Moving to subscription revenues. It registered a 16% year-on-year growth, as Punit mentioned, primarily driven by a higher ARPU and growth in subscribers in our digital business and increased pricing in our linear business.

items.statement: FIFA rights payments staggered over 8 years till 2034 with higher amounts attributable to 2030 World Cup
items.quote: Yes. So, Sameer, like you've noticed, we have 39 events till 2034. items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA was INR 789 million with 4.1% margin impacted by operating deleverage from Middle East crisis
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 789 million, impacted by operating deleverage due to Middle East crisis impacting the advertising revenue. As a result, EBITDA margins were at 4.1%.

items.statement: Significant portion of FIFA revenue and cost will flow through in Q2 FY27 compared to Q1

items.statement: Linear TV price hikes expected at next NTO cycle in February next year

items.statement: Fundraising timeline uncertain; company has written to regulator and filed appeal with Securities Appellate Tribunal seeking clarification
items.quote: So Abneesh, as far as the fundraising, we have already written to the regulator seeking clarification. And we have not received any response from there. We have also approached Securities Appellate Tribunal, and we have filed an appeal there.

items.statement: Star arbitration final hearing completed in July; outcome possibly in Q3 FY27 after final submissions in 1-1.5 months
items.quote: Yes. So Mr. Doshi, the Star arbitration hearings were held in July, which we have disclosed. And now further procedural steps will follow, and we are looking at an outcome possibly in Q3 of this year.

items.quote: So, on the B2C additions in the last quarter itself, we have more than doubled our subscriber base and a large part of that may be due to FIFA, but there is also a consumer base that comes in for non -sports is what I can say.

items.statement: Cash and treasury investments stood at INR 22.1 billion as of June 2026
items.quote: Cash and treasury investments as of June' 26 stood at a healthy INR 22.1 billion, comprising of cash balance of INR 4.4 billion, fixed deposits and other treasury investments of INR 5.9 billion and mutual fund investments of INR 11.8 billion.

items.statement: Expect high-teen revenue growth on base case over next 3-5 years

items.statement: Most capex completed, only INR10-15 crores left for last mile items

items.statement: Faucet exports not yet started; 95-97% of faucet revenue from India; investing in technology for world-class export quality
