I had said this in my last quarter also, but we need to build up our capabilities to start manufacturing world-class product for export.

items.statement: Stainless steel sink capacity utilization at 94% in Q1; new factory construction started for B2C and OEM customers like Kohler, Hafele, Grohe
items.quote: The company combined the additional 70,000 annual capacity, taking now the capacity to 250,000 units, approximate capacity utilization of 94%. The company acquired the adjacent land and we have already started the construction of new factory to cater new B2C, B2B OEM customers like Kohler, Hafele, Grohe, etc.

items.statement: Management declined to provide specific top-line or EBITDA guidance for FY27 but expects quarter-on-quarter growth driven by strong tailwinds.
items.quote: So, Gunit, we don't want to give any guidance as such. But what we can tell you is the tailwinds or growth drivers are very strong, and we are expected to show growth on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Internal target is to reach 30% EBITDA margin within two to three years on higher revenue base.
items.quote: Pranav, this is long-term. I mean, our target is to take EBITDA margins up to 30% and it comes from both. I mean, higher revenue as well as cost.

items.statement: Capex for next two years limited to normal repair and maintenance; refurbishment plans for Mumbai and Pune hotels being finalized with guidance expected next quarter.
items.quote: So, I mean, just to give you guidance, it will be normal repair and maintenance CAPEX for next two years.

items.statement: Pipeline of ~400 keys across Gwalior, Dehradun, Dwarka, Nashik, Rishikesh and Mandvi Kutch expected to open over next 12-15 months.
items.quote: So, we are looking at around 400 keys addition, maybe next one year or 15 months from now. That is Gwalior, Dehradun, Dwarka, Nashik, Rishikesh and Mandvi Kutch.

items.statement: Q1 occupancy trend expected to continue through remaining three quarters; business hotels typically cross 75-80% occupancy in second half.
items.quote: Q1 occupancy growth has shown good trend, and we expect this trend to continue for the remaining three quarters. Typically, business hotels cross more than 75-80% occupancy.

items.statement: New hotels in Tier-2/3 cities like Bhavnagar driven by industrial growth (Dholera), NRI weddings and tourism; no new supply in Mumbai/Pune to cannibalize existing assets.
items.quote: We are looking at new cities where we don't have presence. So, I don't think that will impact ARR. And when we look at new hotel project, we'll look at demand supply dynamics of that city.

items.statement: Pricing strategy is dynamic by micro-market; Mumbai hotel kept rates flat to drive occupancy to 91%, Pune driving both rate and occupancy.
items.quote: So, we decided to keep rates flat and sell more and more rooms. In Pune, we are driving both.

items.statement: Dehradun hotel delayed by another six months due to owner-dependent capex; Nashik delayed by technical issues beyond owner's control.
items.quote: Dehradun is delayed. There are challenges due to which they are delayed. That could be delayed by another six months. Nashik is going on. Work is going on. The target is to open before the main Kumbh.

items.statement: Net debt at INR 38-40 crore; balance sheet can comfortably support up to INR 300 crore debt at 3x forward EBITDA for growth funding.
items.quote: Even if I take three times multiple of my forward EBITDA, we can raise debt comfortably up to INR 300 crore on the balance sheet.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 530 bps to 27% vs 22% in Q1 FY26; flow-through exceeded 75% despite four new properties scaling up.
items.quote: EBITDA margins have expanded by a robust 530 points that is around 5.3% to 27% for the quarter compared to 22% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Domestic tourism CAGR estimated at 10-12% over next 3-4 years; Tier-2/3 cities contributing over 60% of new branded supply.
items.quote: According to industry estimates, India's domestic tourism is expected to grow, with a CAGR of around 10-12% over the next 3-4 years, supported by growth in business travel.

items.statement: Orchid Mumbai revenue grew 35% YoY with EBITDA up 50%; Orchid Pune revenue grew 27% YoY with cost rationalization underway.
items.quote: Orchid Mumbai revenue grew 35% year on year with EBITDA up 50% year on year. Orchid Pune revenue grew 27% year on year and we are rationalizing cost here to improve margins further.

items.statement: New CFO Milind Wadekar joined with 30+ years experience including 20+ years in hospitality (Leela, Chalet Hotels, Ventive Hospitality).
items.quote: I would like to welcome our new Chief Finance Officer – Mr. Milind Wadekar, who has joined us this quarter. He has extensive experience of more than 30 years in finance and in that particularly 20 plus years in the hospitality field.

items.statement: Expecting full-year FY27 operating margin in the range of 10% to 11%
items.quote: For the whole year, this will be dependent on the raw material prices, of course, but we are trying to maximize it. It may not be to the extent of what we have seen in the last financial year FY26 because of this first quarter. But yes, in the range of about 10% to 11%, if I have to make a guess.

items.statement: Took ~5% price increase in Q1FY27; expect further 8-9% hikes going forward; cumulative 11% in replacement market so far
items.quote: In the first quarter, we took price increase of nearly about 5%. And going forward , we are expecting to take price increases in the range of about 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Rs.4,980 crore expansion for PCR and TBR at Chennai plant; ~7% capacity addition by next financial year
items.quote: Keeping our optimistic outlook on the tyre demand, we stand committed to expand our manufacturing capacities as already announced in the previous quarter for Rs.4,980 crore for PCR and TBR at Chennai tyre plant.

items.statement: Q1FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 6.8% vs 10.9% YoY; expect recovery to 11-13% range in H2FY27
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for Q1FY27 was recorded at Rs.268 crore as compared to Rs.424 crore in Q1FY26. 3) EBITDA margins (Consolidated) in Q1 were recorded at 6.8% v/s 10.9% in Q1FY26

items.statement: Domestic volumes grew 25% YoY in Q1FY27; expect double-digit growth going forward
items.quote: Our domestic volumes which includes replacement and OEM, grew by 25% on a year-on-year basis from the corresponding quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated mix: TBR 56%, PCR 27%, 2/3W 5%, others 12%; PCR 16-inch+ now 35% of PCR volumes
items.quote: Product wise, the mix at consol level is Truck and bus is 56% and passenger line radial is 27%. 2/3-wheeler is 5% and others including industrial, farm and others put together is 12%.

items.statement: West Asia crisis drove ~20% sequential raw material cost increase; Mexico operations hit by shipping disruptions and IR issues (now resolved)
items.quote: The continuing West Asis crisis led to a steep increase in raw material prices by approx. 20% v/s Q4FY26, which impacted our gross and operating margins.

items.statement: Expect net debt to increase by Rs.500-700 crore in FY27 for capex and working capital
items.quote: So broadly, we are expecting an increase of Rs.500-700 crores overall in this financial year. But this will provide a lot of increased operating profits i.e. EBITDA going forward in absolute terms.

items.statement: Expect good double-digit revenue growth in FY27 on price increases and volume growth
items.quote: We are therefore expecting good double -digit growth on the back of the price increase s and the demand led increased volume, everything put together.

items.statement: India capacity utilization ~95% (TBR, 2/3W full; PCR 95%); Mexico back to normal production after disruptions
items.quote: Our capacity utilization has been around 95% in the India and on consolidated basis it is around 80%. Segment wise if I speak, we have been able to utilize nearly full capacit ies for TBR and 2/3W segments and for PCR it is 95%.

items.statement: EV tyre volumes grew double-digit QoQ; EV tyre life 5-10% shorter than ICE due to higher torque
items.quote: We have witnessed a double-digit growth in overall EV volumes over the previous quarter. W e offer a full stack solution for EV tyres and are well prepared to lead this emerging trend.

items.statement: Natural rubber prices softening; expect further decline next quarter; RM cost may rise 8-10% in Q2 due to high-cost inventory
items.quote: And we are hoping that these raw material prices stabilize barring some increase of between 8 - 10% in our RM cost in next quarter as we have been noticing because of the higher cost inventory which we have accumulated.

items.statement: USMCA agreement renewed for 10 years, favorable for Mexico-US duty structure
items.quote: Yes, the USMCA agreement has been renewed for 10 years. And therefore, we are hoping that the relations between Mexico and USA in terms of the duty structure is going to be favourable towards Mexico.

items.statement: Expect 10% gross margin increment from Jammu plant at full stabilization
items.quote: So, this is the first year like so we'll be stabilizing. And after a year and so when fully stabilized, we expect definitely a 10% margin up there.

items.statement: Target alkaline market share of 25-30% in 2 years
items.quote: My sense would be that we should be looking at anywhere between an exit share of 25% to 30% at the end of 2 years from now.

items.statement: Expect to become debt-free in 4-5 quarters
items.quote: But if you ask me, we see shorter in the next maybe in the 4 to 5 quarters, the company should be having a positive and should be a like-to-like debt free.

items.statement: Jammu plant commercial production started May 29
items.quote: An important milestone during the quarter was the commencement of commercial production at our Jammu facility on the 29th of May.

items.statement: Jammu plant and machinery investment INR 90-95 crores
items.quote: In Jammu, it will be around INR90 crores to INR95 crores will be our plant and machinery.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 15.1%
items.quote: EBITDA came in at INR61.5 crores while maintaining an EBITDA margin of 15.1%.

items.statement: Lighting segment broke even in Q1
items.quote: Yes. In quarter 1, we are broken even. Let's watch for it throughout the year. My sense is mostly it should hold.

items.statement: Zinc prices elevated at $3,500/ton vs below $3,000 last year
items.quote: Zinc prices continued to remain ele vated at around $3,500 per ton compared to levels of below $3,000 per ton during a major part of last year

items.statement: May need another round of price increases to manage zinc inflation
items.quote: I will not be very surprised if to manage the commodity inflation, we may have to do another round of price or margin corrections.

items.statement: Alkaline battery volume growth close to 48% in Q1
items.quote: Our alkaline battery portfolio continued to be the key growth driver, delivering close to 48% volume growth during the quarter.

items.statement: Rechargeable flashlight revenue growth over 20%
items.quote: Our rechargeable flashlight portfolio remained a key growth driver, delivering over 20% revenue growth during the quarter.

items.statement: Lighting business grew 13.7% with price stabilization
items.quote: Our lighting business delivered an encouraging quarter, registering healthy 13.7% growth. The business benefited from strong demand across key product categories, while the pricing environment showed signs of stabilization after a prolonged period of price erosion.

items.statement: Alkaline market share expanded to 18%
items.quote: We also strengthened our position in the premium battery segment with our market share expanding to 18% within the alkaline sector, reflecting results of our premiumizat ion strategy

items.statement: GST incentive for Jammu plant not yet approved
items.quote: There is no movement has happened on our GST approval at this point of time, but we are in a very advanced stage of the discussion with the industries department.

items.statement: CCI hearing scheduled for last week of September
items.quote: So, there is next hearing date around the last week of September. But I can't comment on the possibility of what you are saying because as of now, what we are holding at this point of time that management cannot estimate rightly.

items.statement: Noida plant sale not yet completed, second plot expected to close shortly
items.quote: Noida sale is not yet completed. As you see that there are 2 plots. One we have executed. And second, we are expecting to close shortly.

items.statement: No growth guidance given; trials ongoing, may take longer than anticipated, wait one more quarter.
items.quote: So, at this point in time, we are not giving any guidance. What we are saying is, trials are going on, it is work in progress. We are getting decent responses, but there are technicalities which entail our team to engage more, give some more solutions.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance raised to INR350-400 crores, including corporate house and land.
items.quote: This year, we are in fact -- we had discussed this at the board level, we are upping or increasing our capex guidance to now almost over about INR350 crores to INR400 crores because we've just recently contracted for a dedicated plot of land for our corporate house

items.statement: INR170-200 crores to be spent on new corporate house this year and next.
items.quote: we will be spending about INR170 crores to INR200 crores over this year mainly and something over next year, that is an additional part.

items.statement: INR50-100 crores may go for extra land for further expansion.
items.quote: Another INR50 crores to INR100 crores might go for extra land that I will procure for further expansion. We have already started that process.

items.statement: Operating margin guidance maintained at 20-22%; this quarter remains above that.
items.quote: I think our guidance continues at 20%. I don't think we're going doing a bridge for any margin that we do above that. 20% to 22% is our operating margin. I believe this quarter continues to remain above that.

items.statement: Gross margin consistent around 60-61%; no margin guidance given.
items.quote: Yes, yes, general in the range of around, you know, 60%, 61%, that is our consistent kind of a gross margin scenario. But, whether there should be an improvement or not, let us see.

items.statement: Freight and raw material cost increases are passed through, raising realizations and other expenses.
items.quote: as the freight goes up, as the raw material prices go up, as we do the pass-through, the realizations will go up, other expenses will also go up, correct.

items.statement: Freight still elevated but dropping; container availability and transshipment ports are issues.
items.quote: Freight is still elevated levels, but dropping rather than going high. So, we believe it has started to come down a little bit, but it all depends.

items.statement: Ferrochrome and steel scrap prices are fairly elevated; passing through.
items.quote: No, it is a little elevated, but we are passing through, so we are not actually worried about it, but, yes, it is fairly elevated right now. Even ferrochrome is on the higher side currently.

items.statement: Chile high-chrome order supplying 3,000-3,500 tons per quarter and expected to continue.
items.quote: I think that's going well. That is adding to I think about 3,000 tons. And as we speak, because there's a whole supply chain and invoicing, but between 3000 tons and 4,000 tons, 3,000, 3,500 tons -- per quarter.

items.statement: South America could become a 300,000-400,000 ton market for the company.
items.quote: we continue to believe that the strategy to focus on South America, which can become a 300,000, 400,000-ton market for us, 300,000, 400,000-ton market for us, and solve for a few things at the same time is something that excites us.

items.statement: Total opportunity in gold, copper, iron is 1-1.5 million tons; overall 2-2.5 million tons.
items.quote: but yes, broadly speaking, 2-2.5-million-tons total opportunity. If you narrow it down between gold, copper, and iron at maybe 1, 1.5 million tons, it includes grinding media, it includes liner, it will include some tons of this particular product also

items.statement: Q4 to Q1 EBITDA decline due to lower FX gain, unfavorable product mix, higher trial and freight expenses.
items.quote: Second is you would have seen major contributor is the product mix. So, in the past, we have said that in a given quarter, if the product mix is extremely favorable in terms of bigger castings going more, then the needle will move into a much better margin.

items.statement: NGDS will be sold as part of a package with grinding media and liners, not standalone; margin profile unchanged.
items.quote: Grinding media, liner, and NGDS together forms a package that gets sold to the customer.

items.statement: Trials are iterative and uncertain; could take 3 months to 2 years, updates may be bland for 3-4 quarters.
items.quote: this journey of doing a trial, the iteration is uncertain in a way that it could take 3 months, it could take 2 years because every mine site is different, operating conditions are different

items.statement: Chinese forged media has made dramatic entry; no Chinese presence in high chrome currently.
items.quote: Chinese are Chinese today have made a dramatic entry into the forged space where, you know, as much as the top two mines, I think, in Chile today use Chinese forged media.

items.statement: 99acres expected to become cash-generative during FY27.
items.quote: With leadership established across traffic, supply, and customer engagement, significant headroom for monetization, and disciplined m arketing investments, we believe 99acres is well positioned to sustain healthy growth while becoming cash-generative during FY27.

items.statement: Shiksha headwinds expected to persist over the near term.
items.quote: We expect these headwinds to persist over the near term.

items.statement: Job Hai revenue targeted to more than double this year.
items.quote: Last year we did about Rs.15 crores. We would like to more than double this year in Job Hai.

items.statement: Job Hai could reach Rs.100 crores in two to three years.
items.quote: If we execute well, can it get to a hundred crores in maybe two, three years and more? Yes, it can.

items.statement: Job Hai burn of about Rs.50 crores per year should remain same or moderate.
items.quote: Of course , we are investing in Job Hai, s o we are burning close to Rs.50 crores a year. As top line starts to grow, this burn should either remain the same or start moderating.

items.statement: Margins should improve if topline grows in the teens.
items.quote: If you're able to grow topline in the teens, margins should improve. But if for some reason, top line growth comes at 8, 9, 10%, then it'll be hard to improve margins.

items.statement: Headcount may start growing once business grows in the teens.
items.quote: Our headcount may start growing once again, once our business starts growing in the teens.

items.statement: Invested in 135 companies with about Rs.5,000 crores invested value.
items.quote: So far, we have invested in 135 companies with an invested value of approxim ately Rs.5,000 crores through our balance sheet directly or through our AIFs.

items.statement: AI-Rex live across more than 4,000 enterprise customers and recruitment firms, over 10% converted to paying.
items.quote: As of the end of June, AI-Rex was live across more than 4,000 enterprise customers and recruitment firms, with over 10 % already converted into paying customers.

items.statement: Talent Pulse serves more than 600 paid customers.
items.quote: Our AI-powered Talent and Salary Intelligence Platform, Talent Pulse now serves more than 600 paid customers, ranging from large enterprises to smaller organizations.

items.statement: Recruitment business operating PBT margin at 58%.
items.quote: Recruitment billings grew by over 17%. In Q1, revenue grew by 13%. Operating profit grew by 25%, at an operating PBT margin of 58%.

items.statement: Jobseeker business PBT margin at 63%.
items.quote: The business also operated at a healthy PBT margin of 63%, aided by the increasing share of self-serve offerings.

items.statement: AI-Rex priced at Rs.3,500 per mandate for companies and Rs.2,500 for consultants.
items.quote: Yes, the pricing is Rs.3,500 rupees per mandate for companies and Rs.2,500 rupees per mandate for consultants.

items.statement: Hiring activity stable, led by replacement hiring with some improvement in incremental hiring.
items.quote: Hiring activity remained largely stable, led primarily by replacement hiring, with some improvement in incremental hiring.

items.statement: Newer monetization levers like AI-Rex and Talent Pulse contributed to higher ARPU.
items.quote: Additionally, newer monetization levers such as AI -Rex, Talent Pulse, and other value -added offerings contributed to significantly higher ARPU and expanded our revenue opportunity per customer.

items.statement: AI-driven search changes affected Shiksha traffic and billing.
items.quote: AI-driven changes in search behaviour have been affecting Shiksha's traffic for several quarters, in line with expectations. This is translating into a billing impact as reduced referred search traffic from Google affected client delivery outcomes.

items.statement: Expect operating leverage to return as volume normalizes and investments commercialize
items.quote: And we expect operating leverage to return as volume normalizes and these investments commercialize.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 9.7% vs 15.7% previous quarter due to one-time costs and front-loaded investments
items.quote: Total EBITDA is at Rs. 116.3 crores, with a margin of 9.7%, as compared to 15.7% in the previous quarter, and 13.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Expect margin improvement as new tech-heavy offshore contracts replace labor-priced runoff
items.quote: The contracts we are winning carry technology content and offshore-weighted delivery. We expect that to show in the margin structure ahead of revenue cycle in following quarters.

items.statement: Intend to move growing share of contract value to outcome-linked non-headcount commercial structures
items.quote: First, the pricing shift – We intend to move a growing share of our contract value onto outcome-linked and non-headcount commercial structures.

items.statement: Strong pipeline in Agentic AI, process automation, contact center, digital modernization, platform services
items.quote: Our pipeline remains strong in areas such as agentic AI, process automation, contact center, digital modernization, and platform services.

items.statement: Added 19 new logos in CX and digital services and 8 in HRO and payroll processing in Q1
items.quote: We added 19 new logos across CX and digital services, and 8 clients in HRO and payroll processing.

items.statement: New deals smaller in size but higher margin due to AI; existing clients drive FY27 growth
items.quote: As we add these new clients, they are going to be smaller in size compared to the past clients because with AI, the actual revenue size goes marginally smaller than in the past. But on the other hand, margin is higher.

items.statement: Funding growth initiatives including Project Ganga primarily through internal accruals
items.quote: Collection discipline continues to hold, and we are funding our growth initiatives including “Project Ganga” primarily through internal accruals.

items.statement: CelerityX adding new prestigious logos and securing repeat enterprise contracts with longer duration
items.quote: we have seen not just new prestigious logos being added in the last quarter, but also more importantly, and this is very important, we have been able to get in, corporates for repeat orders and repeat contracts are very, very critical

items.statement: Broadband high-speed adoption (101+ Mbps) rose from 11% to 15% YoY on expanding subscriber base
items.quote: pretty much high -speed adoption, which was barely in the low single digits, about a year and a half ago, already it's risen from about 11% last year, this time to 15% on an expanding subscriber base.

items.statement: Macro uncertainties and client prudence may persist near term; clients not fully ready on data governance for AI production
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain cautiously optimistic, m acro uncertainties and client prudence may persist in the near term and our 1st Quarter reflects

items.statement: Expect largest FY27 expansion growth driver in AI digital space from existing client adoption
items.quote: I expect the largest expansion growth driver is in the AI digital space. But as always, existing clients drive growth because establishing a new client, gaining the credibility with that client and driving growth from that takes time.

items.statement: Incorporated HGS MENA IT Consulting LLC in Dubai to build technology and consulting capabilities across MENA region
items.quote: Another important development was the incorporation of HGS MENA IT Consulting LLC in Dubai. This will help us build technology and consulting capabilities across the MENA region and support our expansion strategy.

items.statement: New logo ramp-up takes 6-8 months; initial $150k-$300k work with training costs impacting margins early
items.quote: typically, once we add new clients, it takes around 6 to 8 months before you start seeing the benefits of that revenue and scale. Initially, it starts off as a small amount of work around $150,000 to $300,000 and then eventually it scales up.

items.statement: Project Ganga not negative cash flow; enabler role uses in-house resources, ISP pricing competitive with market
items.quote: It is not a negative cash flow at all. That is the reason why we looked at it from a no profit, no loss perspective because for one simple reason, the process, see, let me put it differently. The expertise that we are bringing are from in -house people.

items.statement: Vertical mix more diversified with lower dependence on largest vertical; BFSI, Retail, Public Sector broader base
items.quote: Our vertical mix has become more diversified compared with prior quarters, with lower dependence on our largest vertical and broader bas e across BFSI, Retail and Public Sectors, which is exactly the portfolio rebalance we have committed at the start of

items.statement: For FY27, excluding Pril and FA, expect double-digit revenue growth.
items.quote: For FY27, excluding the Pril business, we expect double -digit revenue growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margins likely to remain under pressure during FY27 due to elevated crude-linked input costs, though H2 should be substantially better than H1.
items.quote: EBITDA margins are likely to remain under pressure during the year due to elevated crude -linked input costs, though H2 should be substantially better than H1, subject to demand momentum and commodity price stability.

items.statement: Gross margin stood at 38.5%, down 950 bps YoY, impacted by abnormally high input cost inflation and lower realizations.
items.quote: Gross margin stood at 38.5%, down by 950 basis points year -on-year, impacted by abnormally high input c ost inflation and lower realizations.

items.statement: EBITDA margin stood at 8.4%, down about 820 bps YoY, flowing through from gross margin decline.
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 8.4%, down about 820 basis points year -on-year, which is flowing through the gr oss margin.

items.statement: Total price increases of 4-4.5% taken since start of war; 3% flowed through Q1, remainder visible in Q2.
items.quote: So overall, about 4%, you can say, 4%, 4.5% out of that, 3% has flown through quarter 1 and the remaining will be visible in quarter 2.

items.statement: Personal Care saw 9-10% price increases; Fabric Care ~5% portfolio basis; Dishwash competitive.
items.quote: in segments such as Personal Care, the price increase is roughly 9% to 10%. We have gone up to 9%, 10%. And in other business segments, 4% to 5% price increases have been taken.

items.statement: Rural demand relatively resilient; urban markets subdued due to higher household expenses, pressure on discretionary spends, cautious consumer sentiment.
items.quote: Rural demand stayed relatively resilient, while urban markets after showing signs of recovery in the second half of FY26 remained subdued during the quarter.

items.statement: Crude oil and crude-linked derivatives highly volatile; West Asia conflict kept global energy markets unsettled; input cost pressures emerging with soap noodles price increases from June.
items.quote: During the quarter, crude oil and crude -linked derivatives remained highly volatile. The West Asia conflict kept global energy markets unsettled. This affected input costs, packaging materials, and the supply - chain planning.

items.statement: Margin recovery expected to be progressive and closely linked to top line growth; benefit from lower crude-linked inputs likely visible only gradually and more meaningfully from October if commodity prices remain stable.
items.quote: Any benefit from lower crude -linked inputs is likely to be visible only gradually and more meaningfully from October, provided commodity prices remain stable. Margin recovery is therefore expected to be progressive and closely linked to top line growth.

items.statement: Working on diversification and reducing dependence on crude-linked raw materials for last 1-1.5 years; innovation and new products scaling up to support margin recovery.
items.quote: Having said that, we understand that the heavy dependence on crude -linked material is a risk. And accordingly, we have been working on it for the last 1, 1.5 years. There is a lot of work which is happening in diversification and reducing the dependence on crude-linked raw material.

items.statement: Exo Liquid launched 3-4 months ago, ramping up as per expectations; Maxo incense sticks launched in July, priced at par with competition.
items.quote: So, Percy, we have it's only been 3, 4 months that we have launched it. And from a launch perspective, it has done reasonably what as per expectation. So far, so we'll be able to probably give you more this thing maybe end of the year.

items.statement: Endeavor to deliver double-digit revenue growth from current quarter itself; high single-digit volume growth expected through the year.
items.quote: See, our endeavor is to deliver double -digit revenue growth from current quarter itself. This is what we are aiming for. But of course, 3%, 4% price increase will be sitting over there. So high single digit is the volume growth that we are expecting throug h the year

items.statement: M&A evaluation ongoing with stringent filters; TTK opportunity evaluated but 2 divisions not aligned to strategy and significant overlap in remaining 2.
items.quote: On the specific point that you raised about TTK business, yes, we had looked at the business, but the 4 divisions of the business, 2 of them were not aligned to our business strategy, and there was a significant overlap in the remaining 2. So, we did not take it forward.

items.statement: Secured lifetime orders worth INR131 crores in Q1 FY27, up 51.8% YoY, with EV programs contributing INR64 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured lifetime orders worth INR131 crores, representing a growth of 51.8% year-on-year. Importantly, the EV programs contributed nearly INR64 crores out of this INR131 crores

items.statement: Expects sales numbers to increase quarter-on-quarter in FY27, with strong growth momentum continuing from Q1 into Q2
items.quote: This year, even quarter 2 till date, we are seeing strong growth coming in. So that momentum is still continuing. And quarter-on-quarter, I think what we are expecting is the sales numbers to increase.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 focused on EPDM capability development (3 new lines, one operational in Q2), toolroom expansion, and land near Sambhaji Nagar
items.quote: So investment would be in this financial year in 3 areas. One is the capability development in the EPDM product. Second, in the expansion of the toolroom and for the land requirement on the west area near Sambhaji Nagar.

items.statement: Raw material costs up ~4%, passed on ~2% to customers; balance 50% under discussion, expected to settle by end of Q2 or early Q3
items.quote: So approximately 4% of the raw material cost has gone up due to these increases. Out of that, we're able to pass on around 2% of the raw material prices to the customer. For the balance 50% price increases, we are in the discussion with the customer. And we are hopeful that by end of Q2 and the start of Q3, we will be able to settle those price increases also with the customer.

items.statement: Sustainable long-term EBITDA margin target for automotive ancillary business is 12-13%
items.quote: If you talk about the automotive ancillaries, like us and so, because where we have the OEM customer where we need to be most cost competitive, 12% to 13% margins would be on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Aftermarket business grew 30% YoY in Q1 FY27, launched 345 new SKUs, expanded to 155 distributors; expects similar 30% growth rate to continue
items.quote: Tanya, last year also this business grew by 30%. And this year also, we are expecting that this business will continue growing at that rate.

items.statement: Technology partnership with Hutchinson for advanced body sealing systems, focused on glass run channel; targeting Indian market initially, expecting breakthroughs by end of FY27
items.quote: Through this partnership, PPAP will offer modern and advanced body sealing system solutions to all the customers in India, enabling access to global technologies and next-generation sealing solutions.

items.statement: Raw material inflation remains a near-term watch item; portion of recent cost increases still under discussion with customers
items.quote: However, raw material inflation remains an important near-term watch item across our businesses. While we have made progress in securing cost pass-through arrangements with customers, a portion of the recent cost increases is still under discussion.

items.statement: Tooling business capacity utilization at 84%; received orders for 30 molds with pipeline of 124 molds; targeting 20% output increase in FY27
items.quote: While last year, this division has successfully developed 148 molds, this year, we intend to increase our output by 20%.

items.statement: Received INR100 crores from JV exit; INR8 crores used for taxes; 25% retained for working capital, rest for strategic capex
items.quote: So on the sale proceeds, which we got from the exit of the JV, so around INR100 crores we got. So out of that, around INR8 crores has been utilized towards the payment of taxes. So out of that balance amount, 25% would be retained for the working capital requirements and rest would be used for the strategic capex requirement of the company.

items.statement: Targets net debt-free status within next 3 years
items.quote: So for the short-term side, our target is that in next 3 years at the net level, we would like to be debt free.

items.statement: Battery business remains loss-making; focus on minimizing losses; expects improvement from Q2 FY27 but still a concern
items.quote: Battery business, that is why in our opening comments also we've categorically said that the focus is basically on minimizing the losses which are contributed by this business. And we are continuously working towards that. We are engaging with customers, getting new customers on board, especially in the energy storage area. And I think quarter 1, contribution was not that good, but we are hopeful

items.statement: Tooling business restructuring into Meraki Precision Tools Engineering Limited expected to complete by Q3 FY27
items.quote: As part of this restructuring, the tooling business is proposed to be hived off into a wholly owned subsidiary of PPAP under the name of Meraki Precision Tools Engineering Limited. This process is currently underway and is expected to be completed by quarter 3 of financial year '27.

items.statement: Merger of Avinya Batteries Limited with PPAP expected to complete by Q4 FY27
items.quote: The merger process is in progress and is expected to complete by quarter 4 of financial year '27.

items.statement: Industry outlook encouraging with festival season, GST 2.0, easier financing, and positive consumer sentiment supporting demand momentum
items.quote: The upcoming festival season, lower vehicle ownership costs following the new improved GST 2.0, easier financing conditions and overall a positive consumer sentiment are expected to support the continued demand momentum.

items.statement: One new EPDM line operational in Q2 FY27, two more lines to be added in FY27
items.quote: And out of that, one new line would be operational in the Q2 itself. And we would be further investing in another 2 lines in this financial year.

items.statement: Order book grew 23% year-on-year to ₹6,095 crores, reflecting continued customer traction and healthy pipeline
items.quote: Our order book has grown 23% year-on-year to ₹6,095 crores, and this reflects continued customer traction and a healthy pipeline of business.

items.statement: Management committed to delivering another healthy quarter in Q2 and will revisit guidance mid-year
items.quote: We continue to be positive. We are committed to have quarter 2 reflect the similar trend. So I think this is what the focus is.

items.statement: New vertical investments reduced 8% year-on-year to ₹37 crores; full-year investment expected to be broadly in line with prior expectations
items.quote: Total investments during the quarter reduced by 8% year-on-year to ₹37 crores from ₹41 crores last year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 111 bps to 2.8% driven by 63 bps gross margin improvement to 20% and operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA increased 90% year-on-year to ₹96 crores with EBITDA margin expanding from 1.7% to 2.8%, an improvement of 111 basis points.

items.statement: Interest cost flat in USD terms; early payment discounts used to enhance gross margin while keeping finance cost directionally flat or lower
items.quote: Directionally, flat interest cost or going south.

items.statement: North America revenue grew 48% year-on-year; Europe revenue grew 21%; new mandates from marquee customers represent $330 million annual potential over 3-4 years
items.quote: During this quarter, we enhanced our customer base and new mandates from marquee customers, representing an annual business potential of approximately US $330 million.

items.statement: Sourcing-as-a-service GMV of ₹1,700 crores in Q1 yielded ₹42 crores revenue (2.5% of GMV) and ~₹10 crores PBT (25% of revenue); model expected to scale similarly for 2-3 years
items.quote: We had close to ₹1,700 crores of GMV that was under execution in the sourcing as a service business in quarter one. And that translated into approximately ₹42 crores of revenue, about 2.5% of the GMV.

items.statement: Ted Baker losses ~$2 million in Q1; full-year losses not expected to exceed $2-3 million; resolution with Authentic Brands Group underway
items.quote: We believe that on the whole for the entire year, the losses from Ted Baker should not exceed more than $2-$3 million.

items.statement: Net working capital improved to 1 day from 4 days; net debt reduced 73% to ₹29 crores; net debt/equity 0.02x, net debt/EBITDA 0.07x
items.quote: Net working capital reduced from 4 days at March 2026 to just 1 day at June 2026. This improvement, together with strong operating cash generation helped us reduce net debt from ₹105 crores to ₹29 crores, a reduction of 73% during the quarter.

items.statement: AI and digital transformation underway to enhance productivity, improve decision-making and create operating leverage; SAP upgrade to S/4HANA in progress
items.quote: By embedding AI and digital capabilities across sourcing, pricing, supply management, data and operation, we are very positive and expect to enhance productivity, improve decision-making and create greater operating leverage as we scale.

items.statement: Manufacturing margin ~6.5% currently from value retailers; Busana partnership to upgrade customer profile to fashion customers and improve margins
items.quote: As you know, we make at present EBIT margin of close to 6.5% on our manufacturing, that is largely coming in from catering to value retailers. With this Busana partnership, we get to engage with more and more fashion customers, and we also get to benefit from the skill set that Busana brings in.

items.statement: PDS Ventures investment restricted to sub-₹10 crores annually ($1-1.5 million); exploring external fund to leverage platform without additional PDS capital
items.quote: We're restricting that investment to sub ₹10 crores a year, so between $1 million to $1.5 million.

items.statement: Sourcing concentration in Bangladesh not expected to decline in absolute terms; percentage share to decrease as India, Egypt and other geographies scale
items.quote: We do not anticipate the absolute amount of sourcing we are doing from Bangladesh to go down. But at the same time, we see more and more traction building up from some of the geographies I just mentioned.

items.statement: Maintained FY27 revenue guidance of INR 6,000 crore and FY28 guidance of INR 7,500 crore; order inflow target INR 12,000-15,000 crore for FY27
items.quote: No. As of now, we are not contemplating any change in the guidance, what we had given during the last con-call. So, we are maintaining the same guidance. So, we received 5 new projects during the current financial year. So, we expected to secure a total new business worth of INR12,000 crores to INR15,000 crores in FY27

items.statement: Full-year FY27 bookings growth guidance of 35% to 40% over previous year, targeting INR2,100-2,200 crores
items.quote: So in terms of our guidance for the bookings, we've said we expect to grow by about 35% to 40% over previous year, which takes us to a range of INR2,100 crores to INR2,200 crores in terms of a number for the current year.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 business development target of INR4,000-5,000 crores GDV
items.quote: When it comes to business development, INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores was the GDV target or the aim we were looking at.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 EBITDA margin guidance on new sales of 22% to 25%
items.quote: We continue to hold our guidance for the full year FY27. So we expect to reach a bookings growth of 35% to 40% over previous year, business development of INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores during this year and EBITDA margins on new sales in the range of 22% to 25%.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 launch pipeline guidance of INR3,000-3,500 crores booking value across 6 projects
items.quote: So Amit, we have guided for about INR3000 crores to INR3,500 crores of booking value that we are intending to pu t in terms of the fresh supply in the market

items.statement: Full-year FY27 operating cash flow target of INR400-500 crores
items.quote: So last year, we had done about INR400 crores of OCF. And what we mentioned even in our prev ious call that this year, we are targeting to be somewhere in the range of INR400 crores to INR500 crores on the OCF front

items.statement: FY27 land acquisition outflow guidance of INR600-900 crores
items.quote: So today, when we look at the land outflows, we might be closer to in the range of INR600 crores to INR900 crores.

items.statement: Added projects with aggregate GDV of approximately INR2,600 crores in Q1 FY27 including Goregaon redevelopment and South Ahmedabad horizontal development
items.quote: We added projects with an aggregate gross development value of approximately INR2,600 crores, which includes redevelopment project in Goregaon, Mumbai and the horizontal residential development in South of Ahmedabad.

items.statement: Portfolio EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 22-25%, with JD projects at lower end and outright projects at higher end
items.quote: Largely, I think, more than horizontal and I would say, vertical, I think for us, the margin percentage has varied, whether it's been an outright project or a JD project. When we give a range of 22% to 25%, probably I think our JD projects are slightly on the lower end of this pa rticular range and our outright projects are on the higher end of the range

items.statement: Underlying demand remains strong across core markets of Gujarat, Bengaluru and MMR
items.quote: Yes. I would say, Amit, the underlying demand is still quite strong.

items.statement: Price increase cycle stabilizing, underwriting not dependent on large price hikes, expecting moderated price increases
items.quote: My personal view is, I think now the price increase cycle, I think, is stabilizing. While be cause the demand remains strong, there are pockets where there are opportunities to pull up the pricing. But at least when we are underwriting, our business plan, we are ensuring we are not dependent on very large price hike

items.statement: Comfortable with debt-to-equity up to 1:1, currently at 0.29x, providing headroom for growth
items.quote: So we have said also in the past, and we are maintaining our comfort at 1:1 debt equity. So till that le vel, we are quite

items.statement: 4-5 year growth plan targeting 25-30% CAGR, with balanced inventory across Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Mumbai markets
items.quote: When we look at, firstly, our 4- to 5-year plan, I think our guidance has been that we can continue to grow at about 25% to 30% CAGR. And I think we remain quite confident that we should be able to achieve this.

items.statement: Unrecognized revenue of INR3,825 crores expected to be recognized over next 4 years, with plotted projects over 2-3 years and high-rise over ~4 years
items.quote: Broadly, I would say that all of this would get recognized over the next 4 years.

items.statement: Estimated operating cash flows of over INR5,119 crores from existing portfolio over next 4-5 years
items.quote: Looking ahead, our existing project portfolio provides strong cash flow visibility with estimated operating cash flows of over INR5,119 crores expected to be realized over the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Long-term credit rating upgraded to AA- with stable outlook by India Ratings
items.quote: Another encouraging development during the quarter was the upgradation of our long-term credit rating by India Ratin g to AA- with a stable outlook

items.statement: Goregaon redevelopment project: 6.7 lakh sq ft carpet area for sale, ~200 units for members, ~4 years to complete after launch
items.quote: So the carpet area that we are generating for the market is about 6.7 lakh square feet. It's a redevelopment project. So this is the area that we will be putting for sale. Remaining, of course, there is a redevelopment component that we are building for the members.

items.statement: Targeting net EBITDA margin well above 47% for FY27 and at least 50% for FY28 on a consolidated basis
items.quote: Patanjali Keswani: 2027 will not be 47%, it will be better. But fiscal 2028, if we do not do 50%, then we have underperformed.

items.statement: Expecting around 2,000 managed and franchised room openings in FY27, broadly confident despite potential minor slippage
items.quote: Broadly, I am pretty confident to be around the 2,000 Keys mark and, things happen. But from the pipeline that we have today and, and the kind of relationships we have with our, with our owners, I feel largely confident unless something large falls on our head, but 2,000 should be okay

items.statement: Targeting Rs. 60 crore EBITDA from Keys portfolio once fully renovated and operating at full performance
items.quote: Basically, I said we are targeting a Rs. 60 crore EBITDA from Keys, and I think that is something that we will achieve

items.statement: Balance renovation spend on remaining 300 Keys rooms estimated at Rs. 13-14 crore at Rs. 4-5 lakh per key
items.quote: I would say that we would end up when we finish the full portfolio, the balance spend on 300 rooms would be about Rs. 13 - Rs. 14 crore

items.statement: Fleur pursuing ~2,500 rooms for capital deployment with Warburg's Rs. 960 crore infusion and Rs. 200-300 crore balance sheet funds
items.quote: Last quarter also we had said that we are pursuing rooms of around 2,500 Keys. So that pursuit is still on, and we are very hopeful to achieve that in the few quarters ahead. We are very confident on the capital side

items.statement: Signed 13 managed and franchised hotels with 1,020 rooms in Q1 FY27, over 3x the inventory opened
items.quote: In this quarter, we also signed 13 managed and franchised hotels with 1,020 rooms, which is over 3x of the inve ntory that we opened

items.statement: Combined operational and pipeline inventory stands at 23,381 rooms across 279 hotels in 170+ cities
items.quote: Our combined operational and pipeline inventory now stands at 23,381 rooms across 279 hotels in 170+ cities, of which 135 hotels, which is 11,946 rooms across 80-plus cities are already operational

items.statement: Q1 FY27 net EBITDA margin at 43.8%, down 99 bps YoY due to SAR provision and GST input credit loss adding 3.1% of revenue to expenses
items.quote: Our net EBITDA margin for Q1 FY27 stood at 43.8%, which was 99 basis points less than 44.8%, which we achieved last year in Q1 FY26. This drop was due to Provision for Stock Appreciation Rights and the loss of input credit in the GST levied, which increased our expenses by 3.1% of total revenue in Q1 this year versus zero in the previous year same quarter

items.statement: Pro forma Lemon Tree (post-demerger) Q1 FY27 net EBITDA margin improved to 58.1% from 54.2% YoY, up 383 bps before SAR provision
items.quote: For Lemon Tree on a pro forma basis in Q1 FY27, revenue stood at Rs. 65.7 crore versus Rs. 54 crore in Q1 last year, which is up 22%. Net EBITDA before provision for stock appreciation rights was Rs. 38.1 crore versus Rs. 29.3 crore and Net EBITDA margin improved to 58.1% from 54.2%, up 383 basis points

items.statement: GST mitigation strategy focuses on shifting rooms above Rs. 7,500 ARR to reduce GST impact, currently estimated at ~2% of net revenue
items.quote: Our GST impact broadly, I would say, you could still say this is ballpark in the range of 2% of net of our overall revenue

items.statement: Q2 FY27 significantly better than Q1 with July showing great recovery and August continuing solid
items.quote: Neelendra Singh: Absolutely. I think Q1 sounds like everybody caught a little bit of a cold. Q2 is significantly better, and July was great, good recovery in July and August continues to be solid as well.

items.statement: West Asia conflict reduced inbound travel causing corporate demand softness in CBD locations like Mumbai and Gurgaon, partially offset by retail strategy in Delhi, Hyderabad, Bengaluru
items.quote: That led to the biggest impact of that was lesser inbound traffic and the uncertainty. Now that had second order effects. And in our segment, that translated largely towards lesser domestic travel as a second order effect of less inbound travel

items.statement: Fleur debt-to-EBITDA target to hover around 2x long-term; may briefly exceed during 6 big hotel developments but currently comfortable at ~Rs. 1,275 crore group debt vs Rs. 700 crore EBITDA
items.quote: We are very clear. See, occasionally, we are building 6 big hotels, which is what our plan is, debt may briefly cross 2x existing EBITDA. But our long-term plan is that in Fleur debt-to-EBITDA should hover around 2x, and that is a good sign because it means we are able to productively deploy capital

items.statement: Fee income from third-party managed hotels grew 42% YoY to Rs. 22.8 crore in Q1 FY27; total management fee up 21% to Rs. 45.4 crore
items.quote: income from management and franchise contracts from third - party owned hotels stood at Rs. 22.8 crore in Q1 this year, an increase of 42% year- on-year. Fees from Fleur Hotels stood at Rs. 22.6 crore, up 6% year-on-year. Total management fee from Lemon Tree stood at Rs. 45.4 crore, an increase of 21% year- on-year

items.statement: Expect acceleration in Lemon Tree fee income over next 8-12 quarters driven by signings trajectory (5,000 rooms signed in FY26 opening in FY29) and Fleur developments
items.quote: And I think over the next 8 -12 quarters, you will start seeing acceleration in the fee income of Lemon Tree

items.statement: Q1 was an aberration; Q2 issues resolved, revenue improvement expected via ARR and balanced occupancy mix
items.quote: Q1, as I said, was an aberration. I still feel and maintain we could have done better. But in Q2, I think all these issues will be resolved. and we will go back to the expected level of improvement in revenue through a mix of ARR and a more balanced mix of ARR and occupancy.

items.statement: Renovation of 487-room Delhi portfolio nearly complete; 37 rooms under renovation, both hotels at 90%+ occupancy, opening by end of Q2
items.quote: I think in the entire portfolio of 487 rooms, 37 rooms are balanced, which are currently under renovation. And the sad thing is both the hotels are doing over 90% occupancy. So there is a real loss of revenue, but we will open this by the end of Q2.

items.statement: Renovated hotels showing RevPAR improvement; confident of significant RevPAR improvement by end of year
items.quote: And wherever we have renovated, we see that customer response is good. So now local market conditions may be X, Y Z, but we are confident that this renovation is going to lead to a significant improvement in RevPAR as it plays out by the end of this year.

items.statement: International expansion targeting 3-hour flight markets where Indians travel; UAE, Nepal, Thailand, Maldives identified; 32M Indians travelled overseas, 12M+ to key markets
items.quote: So what are the markets where Indians go? The biggest and best market is UAE. You will be surprised to know that in spite of war, the Indian movement to UAE was not significantly affected other than a few days, it is still very much there.

items.statement: Keys target: Rs 6.5 lakh per key EBITDA, 50% margin, Rs 13-14 lakh per room revenue, Rs 115-120 crore revenue, Rs 60 crore EBITDA
items.quote: I would not say RevPAR uplift. I would say simply that we have a simple target, Keys should generate Rs. 6.5 lakhs per key EBITDA. And if Keys has an EBITDA margin of 50% when it is stable, it means Rs. 13 lakhs - Rs. 14 lakhs per room. So that is what we want. We want a revenue of about Rs. 115 - Rs. 120 crore from Keys and a Rs. 60 crore EBITDA.

items.statement: Managed portfolio same-store revenue growth 9-10%; new hotels adding incremental fee income; fee income growth rate to accelerate as signed rooms catch up
items.quote: Same-store revenue growth for managed portfolio was in the late single digits; I think it was 9 %-10%. One of the reasons is some of the hotels, which we opened last year were not stable in the managed portfolio. So they stabilized this year. So on a low base, there was a higher impact of revenue.

items.statement: Renovation spend tapering: next year OPEX and CAPEX in renovation will meander towards 1% of revenue from past 3 years' levels
items.quote: But what I can say is that next year onwards, OPEX and CAPEX in renovation will meander towards 1% of revenue from what it was in the past 3 years.

items.statement: High-value renovations (Rs 10-12 lakh/key) mostly done except Delhi and Bengaluru; Q3-Q4 will see refurbs (Rs 2.5-3 lakh/room); full portfolio new by FY27, norm from FY28
items.quote: As far as Lemon Tree goes, we will have finished the full renovation of the main hotels and refurbishment of a lot of Keys and other hotels that needed intervention in FY27. In FY28, we will revert to norm, which is really no renovations, but a continuing thing on refurb.

items.statement: Q1 renovation spend Rs 9.8 crore (2.25-2.3% of revenue) vs normal Rs 3 crore (1-1.2%); incremental Rs 6 crore; EBITDA margin to recover 2-2.5% next summer, targeting 50% net EBITDA margin
items.quote: We spent about Rs. 9.8 crore in renovation in Q1 which is about 2.25 %-2.3% of revenue. So that was the total spend. Now normally, what would we have spent? Normally, we would have spent Rs. 3 crore, which is 1% or 1.2%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin deteriorated 1% on revenue but renovation spend was 2.25%; waterfall shows Rs 5 crore reduction vs last year; margins should recover as renovation tapers
items.quote: So, if you ask me, our EBITDA margin versus last year deteriorated by 1 % on revenue, but our spend in renovation was 2.25%. And if you see the waterfall change, it was a reduction in Rs. 5 crore over last year.

items.statement: Debt for new hotels matched to operating EBITDA, not presumed EBITDA; 1:1 debt-equity; first 2-2.5 years funded from equity, debt needed only in final year matched with cash flows
items.quote: So, we use operating EBITDA, known EBITDA to really look at debt for new hotels rather than fund new hotels based on a presumed EBITDA. So that is a standard risk mitigation practice that Lemon Tree has had from the beginning.

items.statement: Below-the-line expenses (corporate, talent, technology) will not grow at revenue rate; target 75-80% EBITDA margin long-term as fee income doubles and corporate costs drop to 20-25% of revenue
items.quote: When we say that we are targeting in Lemon Tree to ultimately have an EBITDA margin of 75%-80%, it means really, we are saying we will double our management fee income and our below-the-line expenses, which is basically talent and technology as a percentage of revenue will then drop to 20%-25%.

items.statement: GST impact reduction strategy: increase % of rooms sold above Rs 7,500; currently 52% below, 48% above; target weighted average reduction from 2% to 1.7% and lower; some hotels will never reach Rs 7,500
items.quote: Our intent is not that we will be able to get rid of all the rooms will not go to Rs. 7,500. Our intent is that this percentage should ramp up so that a larger and larger percentage of rooms are sold at over Rs. 7,500.

items.statement: Negotiated vs non-negotiated room mix balance improving; better balance visible in July-August; Q2 onwards will see better balance between retail/negotiated and non-negotiated
items.quote: I guess like I said, as we achieve more balance, which is already visible in July and August, you can certainly see in the next presentation, you will potentially notice a better balance of negotiated and non - negotiated b usiness, no doubt about it

items.statement: Fleur demerger: Warburg investing USD 100M at USD 1B valuation for 10% primary; post-demerger shareholding Lemon Tree 41%, Warburg 36%, public 33%; 2,500 rooms acquisition target
items.quote: It is a valuation which is fixed at, I think, USD1 billion. So they are investing in Fleur at USD1 billion. So they are giving USD100 million for 10% primary.

items.statement: Fleur to grow rooms by over 50% by FY30 (from ~6,000 to ~9,300); revenue growth higher as incremental rooms are mostly Aurika brand; Lemon Tree reinventing as asset-light player at scale
items.quote: So we are saying Fleur will increase by over 50% in rooms by FY30 approximate, but much more in revenue because the incremental rooms that are being bought are all Aurika's other than some operating assets.

items.statement: Demerger approval process with SEBI, then NCLT, shareholder vote, creditors, GST; completion targeted first half of calendar 2027, conservatively late second half of next year
items.quote: So currently with SEBI, post we got the CCI approval and some scrutiny by the stock exchanges. So that is in process as of now, post which the NCLT process filing and meetings and hearings would start.

items.statement: Order backlog at end of Q1 FY27 was INR 32,222.1 crs, representing strong double-digit growth vs Q1 FY26
items.quote: As a result, we closed the quarter with an order backlog of INR 32,222.1 crs, representing strong double-digit growth compared with Q1 FY26 and providing good revenue visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA grew 135.0% YoY to INR 399.9 crs in Q1 FY27, including unrealized forex loss of INR 36.37 crs
items.quote: operational EBITDA grew 135.0% YoY to INR 399.9 crs. It is important to note that this EBITDA performance includes an unrealized foreign exchange loss of INR 36.37 crs recorded during the quarter.

items.statement: Profit before tax margin was 15.6% and profit after tax margin was 11.8% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: As a result, our profit before tax margin stood at 15.6%, while profit after tax margin was 11.8%.

items.statement: First BESS order (165 MW/330 MWh) received in Andhra Pradesh; modular scalable solution excluding batteries; margin profile to mature over time with localization
items.quote: The second project marks a major milestone for Hitachi Energy India. It is a 165 MW / 330 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project in Andhra Pradesh, reflecting strong validation of our capabilities in grid integration, power quality, and advanced energy solutions.

items.statement: Multiple data center orders secured including 40x2500 kVA project in Hyderabad; launched Grid-to-Rack solution for data centers
items.quote: In addition, we secured multiple data center orders from hyperscalers during the quarter. A notable project among these is a 40 × 2500 kVA data center project in Hyderabad, awarded by a leading Indian multinational conglomerate

items.statement: Railway and metro projects progressing slower than anticipated; expected to pick up from second half of FY27; transmission dip is temporary timing issue
items.quote: Railway projects are progressing slower than originally anticipated. Based on the discussion with the rail and metro authorities -- we expect it should pick from the second half of the year. Transmission is just a timing issue.

items.statement: Chinese players allowed in GIS/transformer market with 60-65% local content; management sees no material impact if level playing field maintained
items.quote: view is clear. More competition is welcome to meet the demand and supply challenges or perceived demand and supply challenges, if any. As long as there is a level playing field, we do not see any issue in competing and ensuring that our margin ambition is met in that

items.statement: Plant 6 commercialization on track for H1 FY27; mechanical completion done, validations and customer audits ongoing
items.quote: We are on track for the commercialization of Plant 6 in H1 of FY27, which will further strengthen our manufacturing capacity and enable us to support future growth opportunities.

items.statement: Plant 6 expected to be fully online by end of H1 FY27; quarterly depreciation ~INR30 million initially
items.quote: Quarterly depreciation, we have yet to do the thorough calculation, but should be around 30 million, plus/minus, I don't know, 10%, 15%, but around 30 million per quarter should be the number initially, initial 1 year and then it goes down as you have seen the quarter depreciation reduction.

items.statement: Plant 6 revenue potential INR1,100 crores; can grow 10-15% more via efficiency initiatives and maintenance capex of INR12-15 crores annually
items.quote: In terms of utilization, we have mentioned earlier that with Plant 6 we can deliver INR1,100 crores kind of a number in terms of revenue. However, we have always in past seen that the initial estimate that we give in terms of revenue that can be delivered with our plants can be grown to a large extent, 10% to 15% more

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA grew 26% YoY to INR34 crores ex-ESOP; reported EBITDA INR27 crores including INR7.2 crores ESOP expense
items.quote: Excluding the impact of ESOP expenses, which are non-cash in nature, INR7.2 crores, our EBITDA grew 26% Y-o-Y to INR34 crores.

items.statement: Gross margins driven by business mix, operational efficiencies, value-added products in CDMO, and Exports growth; Trade Generics decline offset by better CDMO product portfolio
items.quote: The gross margin that we have been able to deliver, they are mainly driven by business mix, operational efficiencies that we have been able to bring in, and the product portfolio within -- especially within CDMO vertical that we were able to convert in this quarter.

items.statement: Indian pharma market volume growth 3.4% in Q1 FY27; Windlas delivered 18% YoY revenue growth to INR248 crores, highest ever quarterly revenue
items.quote: The Indian pharma market witnessed a volume growth of 3.4% in Q1 of FY27, reflecting a steady yet measured industry environment. Against this backdrop, Windlas Biotech continued its growth trajectory, delivering its highest ever quarterly revenue of INR248 crores, representing 18% Y-o-Y growth.

items.statement: API price volatility persists due to crude situation and geopolitical factors; inventory increased during quarter but normalized by end; cost-plus model with transparent pricing to customers
items.quote: The prices have been varying quite a bit with the crude situation. And early on, what we had seen was that even people who had stock of their past lower costs were taking an advantage and increasing prices when the crisis started in West Asia. Thereafter, many times, there was corrections and things stabilized. So very

items.statement: Completed INR47 crores buyback in Q1 FY27 (promoters did not participate); declared FY26 dividend of INR13 crores (INR6.30 per share)
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, the company also completed INR47 crores buyback in which promoters did not participate and declaration of FY26 dividend of INR13 crores, INR6.30 per equity share.

items.statement: Current utilization 60-65%, peak stretchable to 70%; capacity expansion decisions based on customer visibility, not pre-emptive large blocks; brownfield expansion ~1 year timeline
items.quote: As such, we have said that 60% to 65% is the highest peak utilization level for our kind of business, which can, of course, be stretched to 70% or so. But as we increase the operational capacity, this number does not really remain that important.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA margin 11.4%; management targets improvement in H2 FY27 but defers specific guidance by one quarter due to cost volatility
items.quote: We want to improve it, however given the extremely volatile situation on the cost front, we have not given any specific guidance but we will give a specific guidance in the next quarter, but be clear the target is to improve over what we have achieved today.

items.statement: Export margins at 15% worst-case at current peak freight (USD10-12k/container), normal 16-17%; domestic ~11%; delta ~4-5% vs historical 8-9%
items.quote: At the current freight costs, assuming that nothing goes down, we still calculated that that should still give you around 15% EBITDA margins. Now, in a good situation, it could be 16%- 17%, in the worst situation, it is 15%.

items.statement: IPO proceeds utilization 57% (INR146.69 crores of INR259.32 crores) as of June 30, 2026; INR8.88 crores utilized in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Out of the net IPO proceeds of INR259.32 crores, INR146.69 crores have been utilized so far, that is 57% of the funds have been utilized as on 30th June 2026. During the quarter, INR8.88 crores was utilized out of the IPO proceeds.

items.statement: Targets INR3,000 crores turnover in about 3 years, maximum before 5 years, with ~30% YoY growth and INR1,000 crores PAT
items.quote: My turnover of INR3000 crores in about 3 years and I will achieve it maximum before 5 years. And I will main tain a growth of about 30% year-on-year

items.statement: Aims for 27-30% net profit margin and 40%+ EBITDA margin in future
items.quote: I would like to remain a company with 27% to 30% net profit and EBITDA of 40% plus in future also.

items.statement: Plans 3,000-3,500 operational beds in FY27, up from 2,400 currently; targets 7,000-10,000 beds in 3-5 years
items.quote: In FY27, I had said I will do 3,000 to 3,500 operational beds. I will do 3,000 plus this year. We will do 3,000 to 3,500, and in three to five years, I have given the number of 7,000 to 10,000.

items.statement: Product revenue steady at INR118 crores in Q1 FY27; OTC sales up INR3 crores QoQ; Entero distribution to start within 15 days
items.quote: medicine sales were INR80 crore s in Q1 and INR118 crores in Q4, and this quarter too it is INR118 crores. So product business is steady

items.statement: Total patient touchpoints grew 10% QoQ to 534,000 in Q1 FY27; daycare volume up 31% YoY to 19,400; e-commerce orders up to 264,000
items.quote: In the last quarter, a total of 4,87,000 people connected with us across OPD, IPD, daycare, COD, e-commerce, and consultations. If I look at quarter 4 to quarter 1, then 5,34,000 people are connected to us in this quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 41%, PAT margin 28%; one-time other income of INR7 crores (INR5 cr warrant valuation, INR2.5 cr capital gains)
items.quote: In this quarter, our revenue from operations stood at INR224 crores, while EBITDA was INR92 crores and PAT was INR65 crore s. We delivered a 41% EBITDA margin and a 28% PAT margin

items.statement: Deliberately reduced government/credit business from INR15 crores to INR5 crores to avoid receivables risk; building cash-rich model
items.quote: I have reduced government business. If I continue business where money gets stuck in receivables, that bad debt risk persists. When you look quarter-on-quarter, I have scaled down government business to one-third on a yearly and quarter-on-quarter basis, while maintaining and regularly growing our private business.

items.statement: Ultra-luxury wellness center in Manali (108 rooms + 22 villas) starting Sep-Oct; leased 3-year renewable contract; minimal operating cost (only marketing & doctor wages)
items.quote: Its name will be, sir, Jeena Sikho Premium. We are planning that. Arjuna Wellness was its name earlier, so that name is coming in the agreement.

items.statement: Manali center: Year 1 - 50% occupancy, ADR INR32-35k, EBITDA 35-40%; Year 2 - 60% occupancy, ADR INR35-37k, gross margin 60-62%, operating cost 9-10%
items.quote: With an average occupancy expected for the first 12 business months would be 50%, with an ADR of 32,000 to 35,000, and with overall gross margins of around 50% to 55%, with an EBITDA coming to approximately 35% to 40% plus for year one.

items.statement: Plans 3-4 similar luxury wellness centers across India, each targeting INR3-5 crores net profit
items.quote: We are looking for more such deals in India, so we are planning to launch three to four such luxury premium wellness in four different corners of all over India, which will give us at least around INR3 crores to INR5 crores profit from each center, as we have thought. Net profit.

items.statement: IPD patients up 33% YoY to 11,500; daycare volume up 31% YoY; OPD/consultation volume up 143% YoY; ticket size reduced for affordability
items.quote: Within our Ayurveda healthcare service business, underlying demand remained strong, with Panchakarma revenue growing 13% in Q1 FY27, supported by a 33% YoY increase in IPD patients and a 31% increase in day care volume.

items.statement: Reduced ticket size for underprivileged patients; launching discounted scheme for BPL/Ayushman patients at INR4,000-5,000 per bed to boost occupancy
items.quote: We have made it a little cheaper for the poor man. That is one factor. The poor man who is unable to pay, we have started a new segment for him to give a discount.

items.statement: Entered partnership with Entero Healthcare; products to appear across all distributors within 15 days after completed testing and software integration
items.quote: They have completed their testing, and within 15 days, our products will start appearing across all their distributors. Their software integration and testing took the last 2 months.

items.statement: Satkartar partnership active; will run new ads and direct patients for admissions once ads ready
items.quote: Meetings with Satkartar are ongoing regularly. As soon as our new advertisement is ready, Satkartar will run it and direct patients to us for admission. That agreement is active and sustained; there is no issue with it.

items.statement: ZeroTouch expected to contribute 20-22% of revenue within next two years
items.quote: So, we are planning to achieve this target by maximum in two years. So, this year will have a very good potential coming into this financial year and the next financial also will achieve a greater.

items.statement: Expect minimum Rs. 5-6 crore ZeroTouch orders in current financial year
items.quote: The upcoming, as per your questions, on this year, we are expecting to have a minimum Rs. 5 crores to Rs. 6 crores order on ZeroTouch in this year only.

items.statement: Current order book stands at Rs. 75 crore for next two years including ARAM contracts
items.quote: So, we have as of now Rs. 75 crore order book for the next two years. That is the new order as well as our ARAM, which is our long-term contract with the government

items.statement: ZeroTouch EBITDA margin expected at 55-60% vs traditional ERP business
items.quote: From ZeroTouch, EBITDA margin is expected to be between 55% to 60% compared to the ERP.

items.statement: Target consolidated EBITDA margin range of 42-46% over next few years
items.quote: So, our focus has always been to range between 42% to 46%.

items.statement: Revenue split 60% education ERP, 40% manufacturing ERP in Q1 FY27
items.quote: So, last, we have a like total revenue is distributed into the, 60% is coming from our education ERP and entire vertical of education and 40% is coming from the manufacturing.

items.statement: ZeroTouch currently has only pilot orders; confirmed orders awaited from university and government tenders
items.quote: As of now, we have only pilot orders and the confirmed orders, we have bidded the tender and we are in process of it.

items.statement: LLM-based AI features to launch to existing customers in Q3 FY27; revenue expected before March 31, 2027
items.quote: So, for the 2 nd Quarter of this year, sorry, 3 rd Quarter of this year, we want to launch that is our timeline EBITDA launching, sorry, BITA launching into our existing customers. And by end of this financial year, we are expecting to start our revenue

items.statement: Strategic acquisition plan focused on technology, education, FinTech, AI and data center with disciplined approach
items.quote: So, we are currently planning to have a strategic acquisition for various focus areas that is technology, education, FinTech, AI and data center. These are the five areas.

items.statement: Intangible assets at Rs. 10 crore; may increase 10-20% with two products under development
items.quote: So, sir, as of now, we have a total Rs. 10 crore intangible assets, that is including of hardware machine of ZeroTouch, the software part of the ZeroTouch, and complete AI engines, what we are building.

items.statement: ZeroTouch follows DaaS model charging per question paper printed and delivered
items.quote: The ZeroTouch machine is completely DaaS model. So, device is a service. So, we are not selling this machine to any of our institutes or any customers. We provide completely end-to-end service.

items.statement: AI LLM features initially free with query limits; paid plans for additional queries
items.quote: So, our revenue model will be initially to stick to open them in free, number of requests will be free in the initial stage and top up to that they can buy a plan to have more queries.

items.statement: Q1 revenue declined ~25% sequentially due to seasonal business patterns
items.quote: It will be compared to the last quarter; it is around 30%. Pravesh Saxena: 30%? Bhaveshkumar Gadhethriya: Sorry, 25

items.statement: Major AI LLM investment already made; additional 15-20% capitalization expected for training and deployment
items.quote: So, major part of the investment we have already done like building our LLM and all the things. Now, as I mentioned to your previous questions around 15% to 20% will be add-on to train them and making it to the live.

items.statement: Sales and marketing team expanded to Chandigarh, Odisha, Bihar, Jaipur, Pune, Mumbai, Indore, Bhopal, Gujarat, Rajkot
items.quote: we have expanded our team to Chandigarh. So, we are now present in Punjab and Haryana, we have expanded our team into the Odisha, we are into Bihar, we have a team in Patna, we have a team in Jaipur, Pune, Mumbai, we have a team in Indore, Bhopal

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins to improve to 14-15% in Q2 FY27 and reach 18-20% run rate by Q4 FY27, subject to stable raw material prices
items.quote: Accordingly, we expect EBITDA margins to improve to between 14% to 15% in Q2 FY27 and reach the normal state of 18% to 20% on a run rate basis by Q4 '27, subject to raw material prices remaining broadly stable.

items.statement: Expect full-year FY27 volume growth of 8-10% and revenue growth in high teens
items.quote: So, the volume growth estimate for full year would be close to, between 8% and 10%, I think. Minimum. More, actually it is closer to 10%.

items.statement: Expect FY28 standalone volume growth of 13-14% and price realization growth of 3-4%
items.quote: So roughly 13% to 14% should come from volume and 3% to 4% should come from price realization for the next year.

items.statement: Expect FY28 revenue growth of mid to high teens on standalone basis
items.quote: Yes, so FY28 we expect a growth of again mid to high teens.

items.statement: New capacity of 1.5 million helmets annually expected operational from September-October; current utilization 81% at 1.95 million units
items.quote: Our first phase of 1.5 million helmets of additional annual capacity is progressing as planned and is expected to become operational beginning October and September.

items.statement: Raw material cost impact expected to soften from 600bps in Q1 to ~300bps in Q2; further improvement in Q3-Q4 as styrene prices moderate
items.period: Q2 FY27, Q3 FY27, Q4 FY27
items.quote: On the raw material side, we had an impact as you said, was 600 bps for Q1. We expect this to soften, close to 300 bps in this quarter. And then as material prices soften, we expect Q3 and Q4 to be better.

items.statement: Added 27 new COCO stores in Q1 FY27, total network now 165 stores across 100 cities; on track for 80 COCO store additions in FY27
items.quote: We remain on track to achieve our target of adding about 80 company-owned, company-operated stores during FY27.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 57.1% in Q1 FY27 from 55.8% YoY; EBITDA margin 13.9%; operating EBITDA margin 9.1%
items.quote: Gross profit for the quarter stood at Rs. 231 crore, up 19.4% YoY, with gross margin improving to 57.1% in Quarter 1 FY27, from 55.8% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Raw material inflation (polyol, TDI) up 70-160% on spot prices, but net inflation only 30-40% due to supplier relationships; passed on via two ~5% price hikes
