items.quote: Although it went up 70%, 80%, 160% we actually saw net inflation only by about 30-40% at various points in time when we acquired it. And that is the reason when we passed on the price to end consumer it was two increases of about 5% each approximately.

items.statement: Mattress revenue grew 27.3% YoY (66% of revenue); two-thirds volume, one-third price; furniture to return to mid-to-late teens growth over next two quarters
items.quote: Mattress contributing 65.9%, about 66% for Q1 FY27 revenue with a healthy 27.3% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Own channels 72.3% of revenue (growing 20.5% YoY); online 52.7%, offline 47.3%; premium mattresses ~15-20% of company sales, ~50% of offline mattress sales
items.quote: Our own channels contributed 72.3% of total revenue, with revenue from these channels growing 20.5% YoY.

items.statement: Full impact of raw material cost increases to flow through H1 FY27; expect ~100 bps gross margin compression in Q2 vs Q1 unless Middle East situation worsens
items.quote: When you look at the overall H1, it might not be more than 100 to 120 basis points unless something else happens in the rest of August and September in terms of driving up the prices.

items.statement: A&P spend to remain 7-8% of revenue for FY27; rental outgo ~Rs. 80-90 crore; ESOP expense Rs. 10-12 crore (lower than earlier Rs. 12 cr guidance)
items.quote: Yes, please because the festive season will also come up now so in that range, it should be this.

items.statement: External marketplace channels grew 7.6% YoY in Q1 after prior declines; benefited from platform growth focus and sale events
items.quote: Our external channels contributed 27.7% of total revenue and delivered 7.6% YoY revenue growth.

items.statement: Jumbo store construction underway: first store targeting June-July 2025, second August-September 2025, both in Bangalore; furniture growth step-jump expected post launch
items.quote: In terms of going live, we target next year June-July for the first store and August-September for the second store, both in Bangalore.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin 9.1% in Q1; steady-state target ~7.5% for FY27 given volatility; 16-17% reported EBITDA margin 2-3 years out
items.quote: We should aspire for the same number this year given the huge volatility in all of the things. Channels, competition, raw material prices.

items.statement: Store catchment areas show 2.7x-3x monthly run-rate growth after offline store opening; 36% revenue from repeat/cross-sell customers
items.quote: That catchment area, which includes online and offline, that growth has remained at about 2.7x-3x. So, if a town was at Rs. 3, it is now at Rs.10 per month.

items.statement: Raw material inventory 3-4 weeks; current inventory cost below spot prices; price hikes paused unless unforeseen increases occur
items.quote: We do have about 3-4 weeks of raw material that is parked with us based on different types of raw materials.

items.statement: Management expects to sustain EBITDA per ton of approximately INR75,000 for FY27, depending on product mix, exports, and currency.
items.quote: We therefore believe that we should be able to sustain approximately INR75,000 per ton for FY27, though the actual performance will depend on the product mix, exports, and currency.

items.statement: Management targets export revenue to return to historical peak of around 40% of total revenue over time.
items.quote: And what we have said is over time, so not specifically in this period of this year, the target is to increase it back to its historical peak of around 40% of total revenue.

items.statement: Management aims to reduce net working capital days to 30-35 days, in line with industry standards.
items.quote: But we feel that 30, 35 days is something that is fairly achievable, and that is what our aim in the going forward will be to do better than that also if possible.

items.statement: Phase 2 expansion at Supa is on track for completion by March 2027 with overall project cost of INR150-160 crores, largely funded by IPO proceeds.
items.quote: See the overall project cost for phase two like we had mentioned, part funded through the IPO funds, was around INR150 crores to INR160 crores.

items.statement: Board authorized evaluation of acquiring additional 10 acres of land within Supa MIDC for long-term expansion requirements.
items.quote: our board last night authorized management to evaluate acquiring an additional 10 acres of land within Supa MIDC for its long-term expansion requirements.

items.statement: Entered into a five-year supply framework agreement with Hitachi Energy Global for winding wires to their Indian and global plants; details still being finalized.
items.quote: We are very pleased to announce that we have entered into a five-year supply framework agreement with Hitachi Energy Global to supply winding wires to their Indian plants as well as their some of their global plants.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA per ton was approximately INR93,000, up from INR74,000 in Q4 FY26 and INR66,000 a year ago, driven by record CTC contribution, higher exports, improved utilization, and weaker rupee.
items.quote: In Q1 of FY27, we reported EBITDA per ton of approximately INR93,000 per metric ton, up from roughly INR74,000 in Q4 and INR66,000 a year ago.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month EBITDA per ton was approximately INR74,000; management believes INR75,000 per ton is sustainable for FY27.
items.quote: We reported an EBITDA per ton of approximately INR74,000 for the trailing 12 months period. We therefore believe that we should be able to sustain approximately INR75,000 per ton for FY27.

items.statement: Transformer OEMs have order books of 3-5 years and are expanding capacity; strong demand pipeline in EV motors, AC compressors, DG set alternators for data centers, and localization due to BIS standards.
items.quote: if you look at the T&D side of it, you know, like we mentioned, you know, a lot of the customers locally and globally, we find them, they are sitting on an order book of anything that could be from say, 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: CTC contribution within specialized wires reached record levels in Q1 FY27; 765 kV and HVDC products represent above 25% of CTC volume.
items.quote: In fact, in Q1, CTC's contribution to the total revenue reached record levels in the last several years.

items.statement: Specialized wire revenue grew 113% YoY in Q1 FY27; standard wire revenue grew 83% YoY; overall volume was under 8,000 metric tons, up 30% YoY.
items.quote: Overall, sales volume was a little under 8,000 metric tons in Q1, up from roughly 7,600 metric tons in Q4 and 6,100 metric tons a year ago.

items.statement: Some transformer OEM customers in active capacity expansion mode have delayed order pickups by a few weeks; expected to normalize as bottlenecks resolve.
items.quote: we have seen a few of the transformer OEM customers who are in active capacity expansion mode, delay picking up their orders by a few weeks.

items.statement: Upcast backward integration facility at Chakan commissioned with 5,000 MT capacity to recycle own copper scrap; expected to provide modest operating efficiency and sustainability benefits.
items.quote: Last week, we completed yet another one of our IPO objectives on time by commissioning our upcast backward integration facility in Chakan. This facility will have a capacity of 5,000 metric tons and be used to recycle our own copper scrap.

items.statement: Installed capacity at June 30, 2026 was 43,445 MT; expected to reach roughly 59,000 MT by end of FY27 after Phase 2 completion.
items.quote: once phase two of our Super expansion is complete by the end of this year, this financial year, we would have an installed capacity of roughly 59,000 metric tons.

items.statement: Consolidated utilization improved to 73.5% in Q1 FY27 from 70% in Q4 FY26 on unchanged capacity of 43,445 MT.
items.quote: With capacity unchanged, consolidated company utilization improved to about 73.5% in Q1, up from 70% in Q4 of FY26.

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 60 days in Q1 FY27 from 65 days in Q4 FY26 and 71 days a year ago; further improvement targeted.
items.quote: After showing a five-day average working capital day improvement in Q4, we were able to improve it by another five days in Q1 during Q1, resulting in an average working capital days of 60 days during the quarter compared to 71 days a year ago.

items.statement: Reiterated double-digit revenue growth guidance for FY27
items.quote: For FY27, we reiterate our double-digit revenue growth guidance.

items.statement: DG set order book at INR1,700 crores as of 31st July 2026, with INR900 crores data center orders
items.quote: Within our DG set business powered by Cummins, the order book as of 31st July 2026 stood at INR1,700 crores, providing strong visibility for future growth. Out of this, data center -specific orders within this business stood at INR900 crores.

items.statement: Data center order book increased to INR1,100 crores by August 7th from INR900 crores on July 31st
items.quote: as on July 31st, the data center order book stood at INR900, but literally just in the past week, that order book now, like if you would take August 7th as the timestamp, that number would be 1,100.

items.statement: Genset EBITDA margin impacted in Q1 and part of Q2 due to West Asia crisis, expected to improve from Q3 onward
items.quote: due to West Asia crisis, this will be -- the margin will be impacted for Q1 and part of the Q2. So, so this is the period that where the margin will be subdued, but we believe that from Q3 onward, it is going to improve.

items.statement: Two-phase price hike implemented: small increase mid-Q1, balance at start of Q2; quantum not disclosed
items.quote: we took a two-phase approach. We based on the market conditions and, you kno w, acceptance, feedback from our sales team, etc., we took a small price increase in the middle of Q1, and the balance in the start of Q2.

items.statement: Wind IPP portfolio to grow from 330 MW to 633.55 MW (corrected to 638.35 MW); 50 MW in FY27, 150 MW in FY28, 100 MW in FY29
items.quote: Including above projects, we have clear visibility to take our IPP portfolio to 634 megawatt, or to be more precise, it is 633.55 megawatt. (Wrongly said on call. The correct number is 638.35 megawatt)

items.statement: Data center is fastest-growing segment; manufacturing remains top market segment; rental is second fastest growing
items.quote: data center, of course, is our fastest-growing segment, but manufacturing still continues to be our top market segment in terms of percentage, and that's followed by real estate. The second fastest growing is the rental segment.

items.statement: Wind revenue mix: IPP 11.5%, EPC & O&M 7.1% of Q1 FY27 revenue; DG set 81.4%, Allied 9%, Wind 18.6%
items.quote: Within this segment, the IPP business contributed around 11.5% to Q1 FY27 revenues, while the EPC and O&M for BOP contribute approximately 7.1%.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties and commodity price inflation impacting margins with time lag for cost pass-through
items.quote: As flagged on our last call, the geopolitical uncertainties and e nergy prices have had an impact on our performance. Commodity price inflation weighed on our margins this quarter as there is typically a certain time lag before we can pass rising input costs through to our customers.

items.statement: MSLG pipeline strong with INR41 crore order won, international inquiries resuming, PSU second phase in technical discussions
items.quote: recently, we have won one tender of INR41 crores, which is to be executed between 12 months to 15 months. The others are in pipeline.

items.statement: RECD revenue INR16-17 crores in Q1 FY27, impacted by crisis and GRAP implementation, expected to recover in coming quarters
items.quote: retrofit emission control devices business, it is strong enough, but this time we have we have about 17 crores, 16 crores of a revenue during the quarter, primarily because of one is the crisis, second is on the GRAP implementation, which was there in the Northern Capital.

items.statement: EPC wind business executing ~450 MW currently, adding 250-300 MW annually with ~INR400 crores yearly revenue
items.quote: you can say approximately the top line would be around INR400 crores of the this EPC business.

items.statement: Wind IPP EBITDA margins: new projects 82-83%, old 330 MW projects 62-63%, EPC 10-11%
items.quote: generally, the new projects take comes with the 82 %-83% of the EBITDA level of a total revenue side, and our old projects of 330 megawatts, generally we get 62%-63% of the EBITDA, and in the EPC business, we get generally 10% to 11% of the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: No orders lost due to supply constraints; capacity increases underway across industry to meet data center demand surge
items.quote: I mean, we're not losing any orders or anything because of supply constraints. This is a phenomenon that, every engine maker, every DG supplier is facing, just because -- not supply constraint, but because of how quickly the demand in DCs shot up.

items.statement: Net cash INR193 crores; capital allocated to 300 MW wind projects under construction; open to other deployment opportunities
items.quote: we already mentioned about the 300 megawatt, which is under construction, including 50 will go live this year and 250 new project that we won. So, one is that the capital will be allocated towards that. Further, the we always open to any of the idea that comes into fore.

items.statement: Platino business focus on India due to strong domestic demand; export possibilities to be explored later
items.quote: right now the focus is on India per se because the demand is very strong per se in India. And definitely, as we discussed earlier about the export possibilities which is there, so we will look forward for that, but right now the focus is in India

items.statement: Management says numbers will go up and they will not let them go down, citing strong Q1 and positive response from IPO roadshows.
items.quote: We are really working hard. We will not let the numbers go down anyway. Numbers will be going up as our first quarter you can see.

items.statement: Flagship store in Jaipur requires approximately INR24-25 crores total investment for interiors; land and building already ready.
items.quote: So, approximately we were going for the BOQ with the BOQ, I think it's around INR25 crores will be invested in that. The land is already being procured before. The building is already ready. Now the interior part is happening. I think approximately we wer e counting around INR24 to INR25 crores invested into that in

items.statement: Company-owned boutique stores outside Jaipur estimated at around INR5 crores each excluding inventory.
items.quote: We are calculating in each store around INR5 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue split was 78% B2B and 22% B2C, both driven by bridal demand.
items.quote: So, we had around 78% of B2B in this Q1 as I have come to know, 22% we have done B2C and both the demands were connected to bridals.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 33.12% and PAT margin at 23.12%.
items.quote: EBITDA increased 33.02 to INR11.72 crores with a healthy margin of 33.12%, while PAT grew 37.86 to INR8.19 crores with a PAT margin of 23.12%.

items.statement: Gold price locked at order booking with advance; hedged immediately to protect margins; procurement matched to sold stock.
items.quote: Most of the time, it is order booking and when if we get a good advance from the client, we just immediately hedge the gold so that we don't get any kind of fluctuation in our margins and prices.

items.statement: Bridal season growing strongly; Gen Z and millennials driving demand for designer branded jewellery beyond HNIs.
items.quote: Industry is growing. In fact, bridal seasons are growing like anything. People are asking for designer jewellery a lot. We were thinking of only HNIs going for designer jewellery. Now, it's not like that. Everybody wants a taste.

items.statement: Expanding into contemporary men's jewellery and lightweight pret jewellery for Gen Z and millennials alongside core bridal.
items.quote: We are introducing new collections across emerging categories, including contemporary men's jewellery and lightweight pret jewellery. Basically, we deal in bridal jewellery, but now we are starting few more categories of jewellery, that is pret and men's jewellery.

items.statement: Working capital may increase with retail expansion but ample capital available for current plans; will seek funding later if needed.
items.quote: So, working capital requirement may increase, but at this moment, we have ample capital to do the current kind of expansion we are looking for. So, I think this is enough yet. If it is needed later, strategically we will go for more fundings.

items.statement: IPO proceeds used to become debt-free; balance funds (approx INR52-57 crores) held for future expansion and inventory.
items.quote: So, the first thing which was there was getting debt-free, that we are already done. And the balance fund, I think we have around -- I think around we have still -- we have around 52 and the 7, I think it is. So, it's around -- we have a chunk of fund which we have kept for further expansion and there's a amount which is already used for the new inventory made.

items.statement: Flagship store in Jaipur targeting operational by November 2025, delayed by rains; brand ambassador to be announced at launch.
items.quote: Trying to get it done by November, but interior is going on. Let's see what happens. Jaipur is getting good rains. So, the work is getting delayed, but I feel we will be able to get it done by November.

items.statement: Franchise model under development with protocols expected within a month; franchise partner funds inventory (est. INR6-8 crores per store).
items.quote: We are really working hard, I think by a month, we will be ready with our franchise models. What because at this moment, we are not even inviting franchises till the time we are not ready with the strong protocols on that.

items.statement: Inventory can be rotated across company-owned stores; designs easily reworked or recycled if not selling.
items.quote: It can be rotated because it's our own store. So, the best part of this is that the inventory rotation will give us more business. So, that is for sure will be happening.

items.statement: US prioritized for export expansion; also exploring UK and Middle East with exclusive pieces for art-loving UK market.
items.quote: US is anyway a big market, actually. If we talk about UK yes, it's a good market, but I feel US is a bigger market and we are working on some new shows, we are working on some new partners who can do some exhibitions there, private exhibitions there with our stuff.

items.statement: Revenue expected to grow at 15-16% CAGR consistent with last 5 years; EBITDA margins to remain stable
items.quote: we expect the margins to remain stable and the Laser Power & revenues also to grow at a steady level as we have been growing in the last 5 years at around 15% to 16

items.statement: Order book at INR27,884 million as of June 2026 comprising INR14,327 million manufacturing and INR13,557 million EPC
items.quote: Our order book stood at approximately INR27,884 million as of June '26. This comprises of INR14,327 million of manufacturing order and INR13,557 million of EPC order.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 12.6% in Q1 FY27 from 11.5% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA grew by approximately 26% to INR659 million, and EBITDA margins improved to 12.6% from 11.5% in Quarter 1 of FY26.

items.statement: HT cables carry 2-3% higher EBITDA margin than normal cables; specialized HTLS conductors expected to fetch higher margins
items.quote: So, it's roughly like 2%, 3% of margin difference between the normal cable and HT cables at EBITDA level. That's how we look at our business, yes.

items.statement: Participated in INR1,250 crores of HTLS re-conductoring tenders out of INR3,500 crores floated in last year; high-voltage cable sales grew from 9% to 29% of revenue in 9 quarters
items.quote: Over the last 1 year, utilities have approximately floated tenders worth INR3,500 crores involving HTLS conductors and re- Laser Power & conductoring. We have participated in approximately INR1,250 crores of these tenders

items.statement: Manufacturing split 90% cables / 10% conductors; HT cables grew from 9% to 29% of revenue in 9 quarters; EPC-manufacturing mix to remain similar
items.quote: In manufacturing division, our cable and conductor split usually between 90% and 10%. And that's how, because till now we are selling those conventional conductors, and with this HTLS segment coming into the picture, that proportion may increase with this specialized conductor.

items.statement: Finance cost absorbed 55% of Q1 EBITDA; INR4,900 million IPO proceeds used for debt repayment; gross debt now INR3,600 million with net debt negligible after INR2,400 million fixed deposits
items.quote: Finance cost absorbed approximately 55% of quarterly EBITDA and remained a principal factor moderating the conversion of operating profitability into PAT.

items.statement: IPO completed July 2026; INR4,900 million proceeds utilized for loan repayment; gross debt reduced to INR3,600 million
items.quote: Approximately INR4,900 million of IPO proceed was utilized towards the repayment of loan outstanding. Gross debt currently stand at approximately INR3,600 million.

items.statement: Interest savings of ~INR40 crores annually at PBT level from debt repayment at ~9% cost of capital
items.quote: So, the interest saving typically our cost of capital is roughly 9%, and we have repaid INR490 crores of debt. So, accordingly, the interest saving will come through, and that should be nearly somewhere INR40 crores in a year at PBT level.

items.statement: Working capital typically 100-120 days; Q1 spike due to EPC project mobilization and FG/WIP inventory buildup of INR90 crores expected to normalize
items.quote: Our working capital typically range between 110 to 120 days, 100 to 120 days, actually. And there could be some spike in a particular reporting date because of various reason, the EPC project at what stage it is.

items.statement: EPC EBITDA margins broadly 15-20% but vary by project milestone timing; not representative of steady run-rate
items.quote: EPC margin roughly stands between somewhere 15% to 20%, but EPC margin can't be look at a particular quarter or at a particular moment, because that will depend on a single project milestone.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity 85,000 metric tons; utilization ~62% overall, cables ~80%; capacity expanded ahead of demand; can reach 90-95% utilization
items.quote: expanded installed capacity meaningfully over last 3 years, our immediate focus is on improving utilization, increasing the productivity of our existing assets, and growing the contribution from higher value-added products

items.statement: TS Conductors AECC technology patented; carbon core imported from US; Laser manufactures conductor and handles installation in India
items.quote: The technology provider is a US-based company called TS Conductors, and that is the company which manufactures the carbon core, and it is a patented technology, and they produce this carbon core from U.S. and export it to India.

items.statement: Deferred tax benefit of ~INR125-130 crores from carry forward losses to be fully utilized in FY27; normal cash tax from FY28
items.quote: On INR500 crores, the tax saving, entire tax saving would be roughly somewhere INR125 crores, INR130 crores. And for accounting purpose, we are showing that as a deferred tax, but there is no cash outflow since then on my taxes.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 45-50% YoY driven by full-year execution of recent orders
items.quote: And we will be doing a revenue growth of about 45% to 50% Y -o-Y. This is driven by full -year execution of orders which we have won recently.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA growth targeted at 35%+ YoY subject to fuel cost normalization
items.quote: Apart from that, we are targeting to have an EBITDA growth of 35% plus year -on-year subject to fuel cost spikes which we are expecting to normalize.

items.statement: FY27 PAT growth expected at 35%+ YoY reflecting interest cost savings
items.quote: PAT growth we are again expecting to be in the range of 35% plus year-on-year reflecting a margin which will be having because of savings in interest cost as well.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 9,124 crores including GST as of June 30, 2026 with 46-month average duration
items.quote: Our order book stood robust at INR9,124 crores including GST as of June 30, 2026. Out of the revenue of INR657 crores, INR597 crores, that is approximately 91%, came from coal mining services.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin for Q1 FY27 is 20.02% after excluding INR 10.57 cr diesel escalation revenue; steady-state margin guided at 23%+
items.quote: However, our revenue for the quarter includes a revenue of INR10.57 crores related to diesel escalation which has been given to us by Coal India. So if we report that, our EBITDA margin stands at 20.02% for this quarter.

items.statement: Diesel prices spiked from INR 90 to INR 154 during Iran war; currently at INR 110-120 range and expected to normalize
items.quote: See, initially the diesel which was at INR90 scaled up to INR112, then in the range of INR130 to INR140, and then it also picked up to INR154 rupees, sir. Now, that same diesel also touched a low of INR98, and then today it is standing at INR110 to INR120 range, sir.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR 450 crores (INR 167 cr cash, INR 283 cr debt) for current orders; no new tenders assumed
items.quote: Sir, if we are talking about the current orders which we have secured, we in the complete year we will be adding up INR450 crores sir. Out of that INR450, INR167 will be in the cash part, sir. So on the loan part if we don't add up any further tender from here on, sir, INR283 will be in the form of loan.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of INR 208 crores used for debt repayment; year-end debt expected at INR 750 crores
items.quote: We started off the year with INR1,024 crores of debt, and we will do some run -down as well in the current year by paying EMIs. And we are ad hoc payment of INR208 crores. So we expect that by year -end we should close at roughly around INR750 crores worth of debt.

items.statement: No slowdown in coal demand; power sector growing daily; contracts not dependent on coal volume but on overburden removal
items.quote: No. We are -- one thing is very clear that there is no weakening demand for coal, because you see the power sector, and power sector is growing every day and demand is growing every day.

items.statement: Actively bidding for 8-10 coal/OB tenders; evaluating iron ore, MDO and critical mineral opportunities
items.quote: We do started bidding for other coal contracts already from last month itself. And there are a couple of contracts -- couple of tenders which are in pipeline right now. We have participated in more than 8 to 10 tenders right now and we are awaiting results. Apart from that, we are actively looking for opportunities in

items.statement: Key scaling risk is maintaining execution discipline and building senior professional team as sites grow from 10 to 15-20
items.quote: Apart from this sir, we will have to keep building up a good, sound, senior professional team which will keep the work at the site happening at the momentum and at the discipline we need sir.

items.statement: Fuel escalation clauses cover 86% of revenue (coal mining); timing mismatch causes partial pass-through; logistics also affected by diesel spikes
items.quote: Sir, a major, if you see 86% of our revenue comes from coal mining. So all our coal mining projects are covered with fuel escalation costs.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded from BBB+ to A- with positive outlook post-IPO; cost of debt 8.5-9% expected to decline
items.quote: I'm happy to share that we have got one notch improvement from BBB positive to A minus with a positive outlook. The outlook has also been upgraded.

items.statement: Q2 overburden removal target ~34 million cubic meters vs 43.37 in Q1; Q3-Q4 expected to be strongest quarters post-monsoon
items.quote: Sir, the monsoon is a weak quarter for our sector sir. And number 2 sir, as we have done 43 million cubic meter in quarter 1, we wish to do approximately 34 million cubic meter in quarter 2 sir.

items.statement: Cost push of 5% to 6% seen; similar price increase taken to protect margins.
items.quote: So broadly, the cost push what we have witnessed is in the range of about 5% to 6%. And as Gunjan mentioned that we have taken a similar price increase to ensure our margins are protected.

items.statement: No margin dilution expected in subsequent quarter from cost push.
items.quote: But as I said, with the cost push, we have also corrected the pricing. So, largely, we expect that even in the subsequent quarter, we should not have margin dilution on account of cost push.

items.statement: New price stock to hit market at large scale around September.
items.quote: So by that time, the new price stock will start hitting the market at a large scale, that would be sometime towards, let's say, September. So still there is time.

items.statement: Channel mix diluted gross margin by about 100 bps this quarter.
items.quote: Just to add on what Gunjan mentioned for the current quarter, the channel mix dilution is close to 100 basis points.

items.statement: Same channel mix would have improved gross margin by 230 bps versus 130 bps.
items.quote: So if assuming the same channel mix would have been there, the gross margin percent would have seen an improvement of 230 basis points versus 130 basis points what you see.

items.statement: Product funnel reimagined; significant portfolio change by March 2027.
items.quote: So by March '27, you should see a significant change in the portfolio of products we are offering to consumers, right, with, as I mentioned, a significant amount of authority from Bata on design and comfort, backed by technology.

items.statement: Average lines per store at 68% of two years ago; expected to settle around 60%.
items.quote: But an average of about 68x will come down to about 60x, and I think that would be the right balance.

items.statement: Vendor consolidation expected to give 0.2% to 0.3% annual savings over longer period.
items.quote: But yes, typically, we have witnessed over a longer period of time, we should have got a delta savings from consolidation at an overall level of about 0.2% to 0.3% at a year-on-year basis, right?

items.statement: Manufacturing partner rationalization and kit rationalization expected to give about 200 bps over multi-year journey.
items.quote: So all this clocked together over this journey period, right, which is spanning across multiple years, should give us about 200 basis points thereabouts.

items.statement: A&P expense currently about 3% to 3.5% of sales versus 2.5% a year back.
items.quote: Right now, you can look at whatever is the current trend line, which would be about between 3%, 3.5% versus about 2.5% a year back.

items.statement: Elevated marketing spends expected over next couple of years to back product range.
items.quote: And I don't see a reason why the next period that is coming ahead, I wouldn't say only the quarters, but even the next couple of years, you will see elevated marketing spends to back up this -- the product range that is coming.

items.statement: Some revenue deferred last quarter due to delayed monsoon, seen coming through in July and early August.
items.quote: We -- in the short term, we did see some deferral of revenue last quarter due to the delay in the monsoon. And that we can obviously see coming through in July, etc., and early August.

items.statement: Premium and premiumization remain an agenda; higher growth seen on premium side.
items.quote: However, we still see higher growth on the premium side of our products, right? So ASP has gone up, right? So I think while the drag has come down on lower price points, premium and premiumization will remain an agenda for us.

items.statement: Franchise partners get about 18% to 24% ROI.
items.quote: Broadly, a franchise partner gets in the range of about 18% to 24% ROI. Some are smarter and more efficient, so it gets a little better if they get a good deal in terms of the real estate piece.

items.statement: Franchise like-for-like growth close to high single digits for last four quarters.
items.quote: We are, I would say, basically in the range of ballpark about close to high single digits like-for-like growth for an extended period of time for the last, let's say, 4 quarters.

items.statement: Potential franchise trade areas in excess of almost 600.
items.quote: We right now have potential trade areas just for franchise, which are in excess of almost 600 right now. So there's a huge, how do you say, belly to fill on that front also.

items.statement: Company expects about 60% of company to comprise products, chemicals and services, treatment solutions about 40%.
items.quote: We believe that with this reclass ification, about 60% of the company will comprise of products, chemicals, and services, and the treatment solutions will be about approximately about 40% of the company.

items.statement: Roha and Ankleshwar de-bottlenecking to take total resin capacity to about 5x pre-Roha capacity.
items.quote: After these works, total resin capacity across the two sites is expected to reach approximately 5x the capacity that existed before construction of the Roha plant.

items.statement: Phase I Roha expansion will double resin capacity versus original baseline.
items.quote: Phase I (Roha expansion) will double capacity (2x versus the original baseline).

items.statement: Phase II Roha expansion plus de-bottlenecking to raise total output to roughly 5x original Ankleshwar capacity.
items.quote: Phase II (fur ther Roha expansion), together with the de‑bottlenecking gains, will raise total output to roughly 5x the original capacity of Ankleshwar.

items.statement: Company aspires to take 10% of global resin volume through Roha and Ankleshwar plants.
items.quote: But what we are trying to say is we expect through the Roha plant and the ong oing Ankleshwar plant, that we are aspiring to take 10% of the global resin volume, which I think is a fairly big aspiration from that perspective.

items.statement: Pharma resin capacity expansion plan is 6x at FDA-approved Ankleshwar facility.
items.quote: Our pharma resin factory is FDA approved, and the capacity expansion plan is 6x.

items.statement: Membrane business plan is 3x business growth over the years.
items.quote: Overall, the plan is to have a 3x business growth over the years.

items.statement: Zero B home water solutions growing at 30% plus rate.
items.quote: The last part of building scale, you have witnessed that, is through our Zero B home water solutions range, where we have been growing at a significant rate of 30 odd percent , 30% plus.

items.statement: Margins in Portugal/Europe business expected similar or better than India.
items.quote: That varies segment to segment. But overall, the margins will be similar, if not better than what we see in India.

items.statement: Company sees significant upside opportunities from Portugal acquisition over next two to three years.
items.quote: The company continues to see significant upside opportunities from that acquisition for Ion Exchange. And we continue to work towards that, and we believe that the success from those countries, those geographies in the next two to three years will be significantly more.

items.statement: Treatment solutions segment facing headwinds from large legacy projects now in final stages.
items.quote: I think we have borne a brunt of that pain of those projects as is evident in these numbers. But they are kind of in the final stages.

items.statement: Company working on PFAS absorption and destruction technologies; sees no significant threat to polymer-based resin business.
items.quote: Apart from that, we don't right now see a significant threat to our polymer-based resin business. Having said that, we continue to look at various basic chemistry of seeing how those applications can be made.

items.statement: Company appointed leaders for Americas, Asia Pacific, Middle East Africa; Europe leader in process.
items.quote: While we kind of highlighted the appointment of our North Americas leader, our Americas leader rather, we have also appointed a leader for our Asia Pacific business. We have appointed a leader for our Middle East Africa business, and we are in the process of appointing a leader for our Europe business.

items.statement: WQA certification is a must to sell resins in Americas market; company has obtained it.
items.quote: For us to be able to sell in the Americas market, the WQA certification is a must, and that is what the company has gone and done.

items.statement: Company expects uptick in global businesses with WQA certification, Roha plant and leadership in place.
items.quote: So, yes, with the WQA certification, with our Roha plant commission, with our leadership team in place in some of these global markets, we will see an uptick on the businesses, based on which premise the investment was approved.

items.statement: Company to be selective on projects with better risk profile and execution predictability to improve solutions profitability.
items.quote: A, in terms of being selective and picking up projects which are definitely much better risk profile, much better execution predictability in terms of improving and strengthening our solutions business further from a competency standpoint in walking away from difficult projects, being a lot more selective.

items.statement: Expects at least 50% increase in specialty chemicals capacity over next couple of years.
items.quote: So, we expect a substantial increase of at least 50% in this capacity over the next couple of years.

items.statement: Pharma resins capacity expansion to be completed in next 12 months.
items.quote: And we believe that we have the necessary actions being put in place to get this up and done in the next 12 months.

items.statement: Roha plant 25% utilization guidance maintained despite softer year so far.
items.quote: So, we continue to hold on, ma'am. This is about four months of the year gone. It has been softer than what we expected. But at this point in time, we are not throwing in the towel. We are still holding on and working with our teams in the overseas geographies and with our plants to see that we are able to meet the guidance.

items.statement: Consumer segment aims to break even this financial year.
items.quote: So our plan is to see if we can break even in this financial year. That is the first target for us.

items.statement: UP legacy project to spill over to next financial year due to fund flow constraints.
items.quote: As of now, the way the funds flow are happening, it will spill over to the next financial year because there is a huge amount of work that is still left to be done.

items.statement: Significant part of other large legacy project to be completed this financial year.
items.quote: But leaving UP project out, the other legacy projects, we believe a significant part of the work will be completed in this financial year, especially for the large project.

items.statement: Pharma resins expansion is asset-light, CapEx manageable, focused on knowhow and IP.
items.quote: The CapEx is manageable. It is not so much the CapEx-CapEx as to the knowledge and the technical knowhow that helps us unlock that potential and the value.

items.statement: Order book INR 2,473 crores as of June 2026; excludes Hyundai $52 million contract.
items.quote: Across these three businesses, our order book stood at INR 2,473 crores as of June 2026, providing healthy execution visibility. However, this order backlog d oes not include the recent contract win of Hyundai of around $52 million, which was announced post the closing of the quarter

items.statement: Bid pipeline INR 9,777 crores provides strong opportunity funnel.
items.quote: In addition, the bid pipeline stood at INR 9,777 crores, providing a strong opportunity funnel for future order inflows.

items.statement: Roha plant impacted chemical segment margin by approximately 6%.
items.quote: The impact of Roha on the chemical segment margin was approximately 6% at the segment level.

items.statement: Input cost increases passed on with time lag; expect margin clawback if crude softens.
items.quote: As we mentioned that because of the input cost increase, we have gone for the price increases across all the customers and the segments, but there is a time lag in passing of the cost increases. So that also has contributed to the overall margin erosion.

items.statement: Input costs to improve as crude prices stabilize at lower levels.
items.quote: But over time, as things stabilize, as the benchmark crude prices come down and settle down at a much lower level or at a level before the geopolitical crisis level, definitely our input costs will also start improving.

items.statement: Significant part of Roha volume to cater to North American market growth.
items.quote: So, there is a significant assumption that, not a majority, but a significant part of the Roha volume will be used to cater to the North American market growth.

items.statement: Focus on advanced and emerging solutions to improve treatment solutions mix.
items.quote: So, all of these are steps that we are taking to fundamentally improve the mix profile of the treatment solutions business, move away from commoditized EPC towards more where we can add value, work on areas around resource recovery, around new technologies in hydrogen, ultra-pure water, high-purity water.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation may cause delay in Hyundai contract if crisis continues.
items.quote: We don't anticipate any delay as of now. However, if the crisis geopolitically continues, then there will be cause for worry.

items.statement: UP project unexecuted portion around 11% of order backlog as of June.
items.quote: The UP unexecuted portion is around 11% of the order backlog as of June. Our order backlog was around INR 2473 crores.

items.statement: Birla Opus revenue growth over 50% year-on-year for FY27.
items.quote: Yes, on a Y-on-Y basis we are guiding over 50% revenue, which is the second part of your question.

items.statement: Birla Opus to become INR10,000 crores brand by FY28.
items.quote: We took a cost shock on the chin this quarter and continue to invest because we are not optimizing for one quarter, building Birla Opus into a INR10,000 crores brand by FY28, and every leading indicator tells us we are firmly on that path.

items.statement: Birla Pivot to achieve EBITDA break-even by exit of FY27.
items.quote: Birla Pivot remains on track to achieve EBITDA break-even by exit of FY27.

items.statement: Standalone capex plan for FY27 is INR3,157 crores.
items.quote: Coming to capital expenditure, the standalone plan for FY27 is expected at INR3,157 crores.

items.statement: Grasim to invest less than INR1,000 crores in renewables in FY27.
items.quote: Renewable we will be investing not more than INR1,000 crores in the current financial year.

items.statement: Chemical margins to face pressure in Q2 due to expensive inventory.
items.quote: Having said that, second quarter we will of course be selling material from stocks which we purchased in the first quarter which were more expensive, so there will be pressure on our margins, but it's a volatile situation.

items.statement: Paint price increases cumulative impact 8.8% in Q1 FY27, some flowing to Q2.
items.quote: We chose to manage it through phased price increases rather than one blunt correction, and the cumulative impact in quarter one FY27 was 8.8% and some of the price increase impact has flown to quarter two of

items.statement: Q2 typically weaker due to monsoons, but good volume growth expected once season sets in.
items.quote: Also quarter two typically is a weaker quarter because of monsoons and once the season sets in, we are expecting good volume growth to be returned back.

items.statement: Premium and luxury portfolio contributes approximately 65% of Birla Opus sales value.
items.quote: Importantly, the premium and luxury portfolio now contributes approximately 65% of sales value, reinforcin g the strength of our premiumization journey and improving the quality of our revenue mix.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments and trade policies increase uncertainty and disrupt supply chains.
items.quote: The ongoing conflicts in parts of Europe and the Middle East, coupled with the evolving trade policies and supply chains realignme nts, have increased uncertainty across global markets.

items.statement: Royalty of 0.25% of standalone revenue starting June, estimated INR100 crores.
items.quote: Grasim will be paying on standalone revenues. So if you take standalone revenues, impact will be around INR100 crores.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA to be maintained below 2 times.
items.quote: We will be maintaining our net debt below two.

items.statement: Rental growth for remaining FY27 quarters will be based on existing contracts with no significant changes expected
items.quote: So, rental growth over the remaining quarters of FY'27 as of now will predominantly be based on contracts in place. So, whatever the contracted terms and conditions are, they will be followed as is usually happening in NKP.

items.statement: No significant lease expiries or renewals expected in FY27
items.quote: 26-27 is a fairly quiet year in terms of any significant leave and license agreements expiring or getting off in terms of any of the existing leave and license agreements expiring.

items.statement: Only routine CAPEX for maintenance and upgrades at NKP, no significant redevelopment or expansion
items.quote: Nothing significant in NKP apart from the routine CAPEX that we have for upgradations and to ensure that licensed premises and the Park in general is of an international quality, international standard, Grade A office standard.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain steady based on current contracts
items.quote: We feel that based on the contracts we have in place, they should not be very, they should not fluctuate greatly. Yes, very steady.

items.statement: New lease escalation clauses shifted to ~4.75% annually from previous 15% every three years
items.quote: Now, we are more foc used, as we have said in the past, on annual escalation, which are about approximately 4.75% somewhere there, +/- a few basis points

items.statement: Recent small office lease at Nirlon House at ~Rs 250 per sq ft per month
items.quote: So, approx., on the area was about Rs. 250 a square foot.

items.statement: High occupancy limits visibility into live market inquiries; Goregaon micro-market growth viewed positively
items.quote: Because our occupancy is +/- full, we have no significant vacancies. A lot of the demand is obviously going somewhere else. And because of this fact, we do not get a lot of the live inquiries or the serious inquiries as well, because there is no space here.

items.statement: No concrete plans for REIT conversion or Nirlon House redevelopment; co-owner consent required for latter
items.quote: As of now, we have no concrete plans of converting to a REIT. As we said in the past, if we have anything significant to say on this front in terms of any significant change in the structure of the company or restructuring, we will let you know.

items.statement: Debt repayment of 5% annually starting May 2027 per loan agreement; no decision on prepayment
items.quote: As per the existing agreement with the lender, we have to pay back for the next few years 5% every year totaling 25%. So, to that extent, we will be guided by the terms and conditions of the agreement with the lender.

items.statement: Dividend increased to Rs 30/share for FY26; no guidance given for FY27
items.quote: Over the past few years, it was Rs. 26 a share. This year, for the Financial Year 25-26, we have increased it to Rs. 30 a share. And going ahead, 26-27, Mr. Khan, it is a little bit, we just do not want to specifically say what the dividend will be.

items.statement: Business on books for Q2 is very positive versus same time last year.
items.quote: What I can say is for the next quarter, which is Q2, business on books vis-a-vis the same time last year is very positive.

items.statement: Expect foreign tourist arrivals to return to normalcy in Q3 and Q4.
items.quote: And we hope and expect the foreign tourist arrivals coming back to normalcy in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Continue to see increase in ARR due to limited supply and MICE events.
items.quote: For the current year, we continue to see increase in ARR due to limited supply, and MICE events like BRICS as well as Aviation show, which will happen in the later part of the year.

items.statement: Spent Rs 148 crores on CAPEX and planned projects in Q1.
items.quote: We spent, out of that, Rs 148 crores on CAPEX and the projects which were already planned.

items.statement: Working on expansion of almost 30 new properties by 2031.
items.quote: We are working on a robust expansion plan of almost 30 new properties, which will be in operation by 2031, which includes managed as well as our owned hotels.

items.statement: Managed hotels pipeline: 23 hotels, 1,833 keys.
items.quote: at the pipeline summary for managed hotels, total number of hotels which are in the Q1FY27 Result Webinar Transcript 6 Internal pipeline, both Oberoi and Trident is 23, with number of keys of 1,833

items.statement: Like-to-like EBITDA margin excluding Rajgarh was 30.6% vs 29% reported.
items.quote: So, if I just bifurcate that amount and look at last year EBITDA, on a like-to-like basis without Rajgarh itself, as against our 29% EBITDA for the current quarter, if I look at like-to-like basis and take out the Rajgarh, that brings our EBITDA to almost 30.6 %.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA impacted by Rs 9 crores from various factors.
items.quote: And if I compare that with last year, we have an impact of roughly ₹9 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: Power and fuel costs increased due to Hormuz crisis and Iran-US war.
items.quote: One is the power and fuel went up because of the Hormuz crisis, the Iran -US war. That had impact on our costs because of the increase in cost at the hotels.

items.statement: Spent Rs 4 crores extra on marketing to offset lower international tourist arrivals.
items.quote: We had done almost ₹4 crores of extra marketing expenditure to make sure that we get extra domestic bookings to offset the international tourist arrivals, which was actually below by 10% in Q1.

items.statement: Renovation write-off impacted Q1 by Rs 7.5 crores.
items.quote: Just sorry. Vineet, just one correction, and, again, if I have got this number wrong, please, please correct me, but the write-off from renovations was, if I remember correctly, ₹7.5 crores.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand offset lower foreign bookings due to geopolitical situation.
items.quote: The domestic demand offset the impact of lower foreign bookings on account of geopolitical situation.

items.statement: International guest arrivals fell 10% in Q1; expect trend to continue in Q2.
items.quote: In Q1, there was a fall in international guests coming to our hotels and we saw that in any hotel that has a dependency on foreign visitors staying at the hotel. In Q2 , that we would expect that trend to continue just given what's happening in West Asia.

items.statement: Oberoi brand RevPAR grew 8.2%, lower than industry due to Rajgarh ramp-up and West Asia crisis.
items.quote: Oberoi brand falls in the luxury segment and luxury segment saw a growth of 13.2% on RevPAR, while Oberoi hotels saw a growth of 8.2% in Q1.

items.statement: Trident brand RevPAR grew 13.8% vs industry 9.2%.
items.quote: For Q1, this segment saw a growth of 9.2% for the industry, while Trident hotels had a growth of 13.8%, both on account of occupancy and ARR.

items.statement: Kolkata Oberoi restoration delayed due to safety compliance and construction halt.
items.quote: So Kolkata is an unusual hotel because it's a very old historic building. And anytime you're doing a restoration of an old building, there are unknown factors.

items.statement: Additional 25 million pen capacity operational by end of September, total installed capacity about 75 million pens per annum.
items.quote: As committed earlier, our additional 25 million pen capacity is expected to become operational by end of September, taking our total installed pen injector capacity to approximately 75 million pens per annum.

items.statement: Should be able to go beyond 36 million pens.
items.quote: But yes, I think we should be able to go beyond 36 million. Short answer is we should be.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to return to normalized level by Q3.
items.quote: We expect that the gross margin would come back to normalized level by quarter 3.

items.statement: Semiconductor Trays investing about INR5 crores in existing facility for initial requirements.
items.quote: Semiconductor Trays, I think we have mentioned that we are looking at investing about INR5 crores in our existing facility, which would meet initial requirements.

items.statement: Consumer Electronics plant down south investment between INR80 crores to INR100 crores.
items.quote: On Consumer Electronics, again, we have said that once we set up a plant down south, we would be looking at an investment of somewhere between INR80 crores to INR100 crores in that facility.

items.statement: Abu Dhabi plant commercial sales by end of FY28.
items.quote: The plant is supposed to start selling by end of F Y28. So we should get into commercial sales by the end of FY28, which means the capacity, if you think about it, is really for the markets opening up in Europe in '28, plus insulin as well as the markets that will open up globally in 2030, '31.

items.statement: Consumer Electronics revenue to reach $10 million within 24 to 30 months.
items.quote: I think 24 to 30 months is the short answer. Again, this is not a guidance. So this is what our projections look like. We think we can get to that number within 30 months.

items.statement: Semiconductor revenue to start from Q4 of this financial year.
items.quote: Yes. That's the current Q4 Semicon revenue, yes.

items.statement: Consumer business expected to maintain FY26 level, not grow in current year.
items.quote: And I think what we also had said in the -- when we did the Q4 call, this business would probably not grow in the current year. So we will maintain, at a level which we did in FY26.

items.statement: Domestic business overall will grow as a percentage.
items.quote: Ishika, as we move forward, I think our Healthcare business is going to grow. We are going to look at more both on our Semiconductor and Consumer Electronics business, which will again be more domestic focused. So I think the domestic business overall will grow as a percentage.

items.statement: Chinese GLP-1 device pricing $1.50 to $1.70, ours above $2.
items.quote: Chinese competition, look, as far as my knowledge goes, Chinese are potentially putting their product on the market somewhere around $1.50 to $1.70. And again, copycat products, so not really anything novel. That's 20-year-old technology. Some products that the Chinese have put on the market do infringe not only our patents, but also other key suppliers globally.

items.statement: Pricing contracts are volume and market-driven with annual price review, not cost-plus.
items.quote: These are not cost -plus contracts. They're basically just volume and market -driven pricing contracts with the mechanism to do price review annually. So it all depends on the type of agreement. It's not a cost -plus business, first of all, right? It's an intellectual property -led business

items.statement: Emergency use auto-injector program to close by end of '27.
items.quote: On the emergency use auto-injector, it's a program that we've been working on for roughly 18 months, and we will bring it to a closure by the end of '27. It's based on the Toby auto-injector, but with key changes in design. So it's got an automatic needle insertion into the patient.

items.statement: Reusable auto-injector to be showcased at CPHI in Milan.
items.quote: The reusable auto-injector, we've gotten it to a point where we will be testing performance in the current month or early next month. And we will be showcasing it for the first time at CPHI in Milan. So let's say, it's quite advanced.

items.statement: Confident of securing partnership with major global pharmaceutical over next 4 to 6 quarters.
items.quote: Innovative side, like I said, I actually made it a part of my speech. I'm quite confident that we'll get somewhere over the next 4 to 6 quarters. We have dedicated staff now, senior industry leaders, both in the U.S. as well as in Europe. We're very hopeful that we can make some sort of an announcement in the next 6 quarters.

items.statement: Plan to deliver 2,500 units by end of FY27
items.quote: We plan to deliver 2,500 units by the end of financial year 2027.

items.statement: Expect to achieve a little higher than past year numbers this financial year
items.quote: we feel that the, at our level, we will be able to achieve a little higher than the past year numbers and , very exponential growth in terms of numbers will not be able to witness in this financial year

items.statement: Will deploy INR 500 crores over three years for club and hospitality projects
items.quote: For three years the company will deploy INR 500 crores of capital, by debt or by internal resources for these projects.

items.statement: Real estate EBITDA margins to gradually move up to 30%-35% once Town Villas and villa projects contribute largely
items.quote: Given the real estate sector, sell product of residentials and construct, build, and sell, the EBITDA margins would gradually move up around, 30 %- 35% once Town Villas and the villa projects contribute largely.

items.statement: Hospitality segment expected to contribute INR 50 crores+ PAT per year from third or fourth year
items.period: third or fourth year from now
items.quote: the hospitality sector would contribute say third or fourth year from now to an average of INR 50 crores of PAT per year. This represents an annuity income model, with both hotels expected to contribute INR 50 crores+.

items.statement: Comfortable giving PAT margins even higher than 20% over a run of two years from now
items.quote: But with an average we feel that we are comfortable and we would be able to give up a PAT margins even higher than 20% over a run of two years from now.

items.statement: Average selling price per square feet remained same at INR 7,500 per square feet, similar to Q1FY26
items.quote: Our average selling price per square feet has also remained same at INR 7,500 per square feet which is almost similar to Q1FY26.

items.statement: Average ticket size currently around INR 78 lakhs, projections show INR 95 lakhs to INR 1 crore
items.quote: Average ticket size today we already have mentioned that it is something around INR 78 lakhs and the projections and the numbers which we have, our average ticket size goes to around INR 95 lakhs to INR 1 crore

items.statement: Aspire to have 40%-45% premium, 30%-35% middle income, 20% affordable housing
items.quote: We still will have a mixed bag of it and going forward we can say that we would aspire to have 40%-45% as premium segment and around 30 % - 35% as middle income group segment and 20% as affordable housing.

items.statement: Pre-sales take around 90 days on average to convert to revenue recognition
items.quote: Hence, all the pre-sales which happen, it takes around 90 days on an average for them to get into the mode of revenue recognition so, we can put up a cycle of 90 days as an average for every pre-sales happening to contribute to the revenue

items.statement: No plans for new geographical diversification; will focus on MMR and Mumbai 3.0 region
items.quote: For the sake of new geographical diversification with new cities, there are no plans for it in those ways. We are able to consume and utilize our capital and man -resources in this area

items.statement: No program for new capital investments for business development this financial year
items.quote: Going forward for this financial year, we don't have any program for new capital investments for the business development as there is a good handsome size of projects in hand worth INR 14,000 crores

items.statement: Only past fundraise was INR 36 crores via preferential; any fund-raising program will change all ratios and numbers
items.quote: The only fundraise which we did in the past was INR 36 crores via preferential. With the borrowings which have increased, the GDV has also increased to a larger size

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio will gradually come down as projects mature and equity reserves build up
items.quote: The debt-to-equity ratio will gradually come down because once the projects get matured the equity gets on, the reserves and capital reserves get on adding up to every quarter-to-quarter or year-to-year basis.

items.statement: Capital deployed in hospitality currently INR 35-40 crores (7% of total), will increase as INR 500 crores deployed over three years
items.value: INR 35 crores - INR 40 crores currently; INR 500 crores over three years
items.quote: Today, today the capital deployed for the hospitality sector is something around INR 35 crores - INR 40 crores and going forward on every quarter basis, the total investments for these two projects is to a tune of INR 350 crores and with the club around INR 500 crores.

items.statement: Board approved raising Rs.137 Crores via CCDs, equity shares and warrants pending shareholder approval; management and HNAs participating
items.quote: we are able to raise Rs.137 Crores. Board has approved this particular raise through CCDs, equity shares and equity warrants. And of course, we have to wait for the shareholders' approval.

items.statement: Jonnagiri expansion to 2,500 tpd processing facility targeting up to 2 tons gold per annum around 2029-30; State government supporting land acquisition
items.quote: As of today we have 1010 processing facility approvals, but whereas we are going to increase it to 2,500 tons per day, which actually would take us at some point in time to 2 tons of gold, up to 2 tons of gold, that is the maximum anticipated from this project, 2 tons of gold per annum from this project, that could happen somewhere around 29 or 30.

items.statement: Kyrgyzstan Altyn Tor: completing larger leach circuit and new tailings dam for 10-year life; first phase revised mine design and life of mine plan by October 2026; underground resources expected >5 tons
items.quote: The first phase revised mine design and life of mine plan we are going to deliver by October 2026 and we are expecting that the underground resources are going to be more than 5 tons.

items.statement: Kyrgyzstan production commissioning imminent; MD visiting site next week to finalize arrangements and announce inauguration date
items.quote: In fact, next week I am personally I am going there, entire team is there. Once we go there, look at the final arrangements and then we will come back, we will commence the production part and then at a suitable date we will be announced to the market about the inauguration of this.

items.statement: Due diligence on three new gold assets targeting production by 2028; one in Kyrgyzstan (~10 tons) offered by government after Altyn Tor success
items.quote: we are currently carrying our due diligence on 3 assets. So, these assets once acquired could come into the production in the year 2028 at least by end of 2027 or 2028, that is the kind of strategy we have for the gold portfolio.

items.statement: Chhattisgarh Nickel-Copper-PGE: 15th drill hole ongoing, 2,500m completed, 1.3km mineralized zone identified; targeting 3,000 tpd plant; feasibility by mid-2026; capex from fund raise
items.quote: We are thinking of about 3000 tons per day processing plant, which effectively means this plant would be even bigger than what is going to be set up in Jonnagiri. So this would require a good amount of capex, but those details will come out only when we complete the process flow sheet, which we will do by mid next year.

items.statement: Ganajur project awaiting court verdict; recent Gadchiroli judgment restoring pre-2015 rights strengthens legal position; could produce ~1 ton gold in 2-3 years if lease granted
items.quote: Particularly, I can take a case that is in Gadchiroli iron ore case where the court has clearly ordered to restore the rights that have been accrued before 2015. So that gives us a strong legal position on that basis we are going to argue in the court.

items.statement: Company now has two defined verticals: Gold (Jonnagiri producing, Kyrgyzstan commissioning, Finland advancing) and Critical Minerals (Nickel-Copper-PGE, Tungsten, Lithium-Tantalum drilling)
items.quote: we have now clearly defined two verticals. We have always been talking about gold and critical mineral verticals that we have as projects, as a pro duct portfolio. But in this quarter, it ha s clearly been shown that these two verticals have their own value proposition

items.statement: Gold price at ~Rs.1,50,000 per 10 grams enabling price arbitrage; tungsten price increased significantly due to defense/space demand; government incentives for lithium/battery minerals
items.quote: you might be seeing that it is like almost like Rs.1,50,000 per 10 grams. So this is the right time at that kind of price arbitrage is always being done when you are into this business.

items.statement: Thriveni full-year EBITDA margin guidance of 28% to 30% remains intact.
items.quote: Having said that, I want to be very clear th at our guidance of 28% to 30% EBITDA margins on a full-year basis remains intact. We are confident of getting there as pass- throughs conclude and as volumes scale throughout the year -- through the year

items.statement: Planned foreign operations capex of about $300 million expected this financial year.
items.quote: So capex, currently, as Hemankur mentioned, we'll be having for the foreign operations, we are around $300 million is what is planned. This should be in this financial year is what it should -- what would be expected.

items.statement: Around INR8,500 crores capex this year apart from the Konsari ISP.
items.quote: Plus, as for the ongoing projects, we should b e having -- apart from the ISP in Konsari, we would be having around INR8,500 crores of capex in this year. So we've done around INR3,000 crores already in the first quarter

items.statement: Capex of around INR11,000 crores to INR11,500 crores over the next two years.
items.quote: And then, we -- so it should be at around INR11,000 crores, INR11,500 crores over the next 3 -- next 2 years, that should be the capex.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR11,000 crores for next two years and INR15,000-20,000 crores in the third year.
items.value: INR11,000 crores; INR15,000 crores to INR20,000 crores
items.quote: Yes. As I just mentioned, we should be at around INR11,000 crores -- close to INR11,000 crores for the next 2 years and a bit higher, around between INR15,000 crores to INR20,000 crores in the year after that, so the third year.

items.statement: Copper JV asset needs about $300-plus million capex to complete, targeted over next 9 months.
items.quote: And it would take a total capex of around $300-plus million to get it to completion. So as of now, we have done part of it, and we intend to complete that capex over the period of next 9 months.

items.statement: About 2.4 million tons of iron ore and pellet to be consumed internally by FY28.
items.quote: So at the moment, see, going forward to FY '28, we'll have our 1.2 million ton plant commissioned. So between the iron ore and the pellet around 2.4 tons -- 2.4 million tons on a round figure basis would be consumed within the company.

items.statement: BHQ beneficiation plant to produce around 16-17 million tons output in two phases.
items.quote: So we would be putting in around 16 million tons of output from that roughly, 16 million to 17 million tons, depending on the yield that we get from the material in 2 phases.

items.statement: First steel plant commissioning targeted by end of this year, March 2027.
items.quote: The first steel plant is already under commissioning -- is under execution. We hope to commission the plant by the end of this year, March '27.

items.statement: BHQ plant commissioning expected by March 2028 as per original schedule.
items.quote: In BHQ, we hope to commission it by March '28 as per our original schedule. The recovery of 38% against original 35% is more or less confirmed with all the tests that we've been doing on the test bench by the -- through the pilot plant.

items.statement: Slurry pipeline saving of INR500-550 per ton on pellet costing.
items.quote: Yes, it is -- Rajeshji has mentioned it around INR500 to INR550 per ton on the -- because of the slurry line -- slurry project. That is the saving what we are getting on the pellet costing.

items.statement: Thriveni pursuing pass-through of higher fuel costs to clients; negotiations underway.
items.quote: Our margins this quarter were marginally impacted by higher fuel costs due to this gulf crisis. We are actively pursuing pass-through of these costs to our clients, and those negotiations are currently underway.

items.statement: Odisha volumes expected to grow 39% year-on-year to 34-35 million tons in FY27.
items.quote: Several existing mines have been scaled up, and we expect Odisha volumes to grow 39% year-on-year to 34 million to 35 million tons in FY '27.

items.statement: Thriveni expects to maintain EBITDA level of around 27% to 30%.
items.quote: So we are pretty sure that we'll be able to maintain the EBITDA level of around 27% to 30%.

items.statement: Thriveni raising funds to reduce high-cost debt and fund capex and overseas subsidiaries.
items.quote: In fact, we just wanted to reduce our high -cost debt. And at the same time, we are going for capex, capital investment, and we have to invest in our outside subsidiaries also for doing the MDO contract.

items.statement: DRC copper export ban does not impact company as both assets produce final cathodes.
items.quote: So in our case, both the assets will be producing final cathodes. So it does not impact us. It might impact some of the players who might have to find extension and maybe put capacity to convert to cathodes ultimately.

items.statement: Revised annual Lamination volume target to 82,000 tons from 78,000 tons for FY27
items.quote: Therefore, we are revising our annual target to 82,000 tons for Lamination from 78,000 tons, as previously stated in Q4 Conference Call.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA of roughly ₹370 crores for FY27 based on current outlook
items.quote: If I start from current year, I would look at an EBITDA of roughly ₹ 370-odd crores based on current outlook.

items.statement: Targets turnover above ₹2,500 crores and EBITDA margin of 17%-17.2% for FY28 at 90,000 ton operating level
items.quote: For the next year, we should be looking at a turnover above about ₹ 2,500 crores if we don't do the Capex. I am obviously going to talk ex of the incremental Capex on Lamination. So, at a 90,000 ton operating level, we should be looking at a ₹ 2,500 crores turnover and an EBITDA margin of about 17%-17.2%.

items.statement: ₹150 crores Capex completed, increasing sheet metal capacity to 108,000 tons and augmenting Casting and Machining capacity
items.quote: We have recently commenced operations of the previously announced ₹ 150 crores Capex, which was announced last year, increasing our sheet metal capacity to 108,000 tons and augmenting our Casting and Machining capacity.

items.statement: ₹290 crores Greenfield Casting facility in Hyderabad underway, ₹60 crores already incurred, commissioning expected by Q1 FY30
items.quote: We are now progressing with the ₹ 290 crores investment for our Greenfield Casting facility in Hyderabad. This facility will help consolidate our foundry operations and provide the infrastructure required for the next phase of growth.

items.statement: Plans incremental Capex in FY28 and potential Bangalore facility in FY28-FY29
items.quote: definitely, for FY28, there will be some incremental Capex to increase the capacity, but we will do it closer towards Q3-Q4 timeframe, because we can still moderately expand in some of the facilities. Over maybe '28 and '29, we should be looking at doing the Capex in Bangalore for that facility which I mentioned.

items.statement: Strong visibility in Machining space, Machining capacity utilization at 86.33% is biggest bottleneck
items.quote: We have very strong visibility in the Machining space. So, part of the Capex that we have announced, ₹ 290 crores, taking the Machining capacity to 1,080,000 machine hours will be progressively implemented over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.8% in Q1 FY27, expects margins to improve as utilization inches toward 80%
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.8% for the quarter.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to reach 18%-18.5% in three years with Casting and Machining Capex coming online
items.quote: No, for sure it will be upwards of 18% for sure. With the Capex on the Casting and Machining coming online and the value-added products increasing as well as the co-drop products increasing, your margins should be closer to 18%-18.5%.

items.statement: Data Centers emerged as strong near-term opportunity with customers like Cummins, Marathon, Nidec; measured approach due to AI investment sustainability concerns
items.quote: Our Data Centers have emerged as a strong near-term opportunity given the significant power requirements for both primary and backup power generation. We are seeing strong demand from customers such as Cummins, Marathon, Nidec, and are also developing opportunities with a couple of more marquee customers.

items.statement: Strong visibility in railways, metros, Mining, off-highway equipment, and specialty industrial applications; Mining segment grew from 5% to 10% of revenue
items.quote: Beyond Data Centers, we are seeing strong visibility in railways, metros, Mining and off-highway equipment, and specialty end-use applications in industrial sector.

items.statement: Higher Value-Added Assemblies including Integrated Rotor Shaft and Stator Assemblies grew faster than loose Lamination, reflecting continued mix improvement
items.quote: Importantly, within Lamination, Higher Value-Added Assemblies, including Integrated Rotor Shaft and Stator Assemblies, grew faster than loose Lamination. This reflects a continued improvement in the product mix and increasing contribution from value-added offerings.

items.statement: Upward guiding Casting volume target to 17,000 tons from 16,000 tons; Machining share growing as customers prefer machined components over raw castings
items.quote: Casting capacity has gone to 24,000 tons. We would be upward guiding the Casting numbers to about 17,000 tons as well. Out of that, what will be the share of Machining would depend on how quickly our machines come in and we are able to put them to use.

items.statement: Measured approach to Data Center opportunity as AI investment pace may not be sustainable indefinitely
items.quote: We remain mindful that the pace of AI Data Center investments may not be sustainable indefinitely. Therefore, we are confident about the underlying growth in regular Data Centers driven by cloud adoption and data localization. We remain measured in our approach to the overall Data Center opportunity.

items.statement: Net debt around ₹491 crores as of Q1 FY27 end; potential to rationalize working capital by ₹25-30 crores
items.quote: Right now, the net debt is somewhere around ₹ 491 crores as of last quarter end. We have already incurred, like I said, about ₹ 60 odd crores of expenditure out of the ₹ 290 crores. Despite that, we have been able to meaningfully reduce the net debt, and I think there is still potential to further rationalize our working capital to the tune of about ₹ 25 crores to ₹ 30 crores.

items.statement: Full year tax rate expected to be 25% for FY27, not 33% as previously mentioned
items.quote: No, it will be about 25%, not 33%. This effective tax rate is about 25%.

items.statement: Transitioning to four verticals: Home Textile Solutions, Yarn Solutions, Fabric Solutions, and Apparel Solutions to diversify from U.S. and client concentration
items.quote: So in a sense, we are going to be adding 3 new product verticals to our port folio and in addition to Home Textile Solutions. And the 3 product verticals will be Yarn Solutions, Fabric Solutions and Apparel Solutions.

items.statement: Yarn Solutions and Fabric Solutions each target INR1,000 crores revenue at full capacity
items.quote: what I can tell you is that the overall revenues we are looking at from the Yarn Solutions vertical and the Fabric Solutions vertical are in the region of INR1,000 crores each at full capacities.

items.statement: Capex limited to maintenance and organic requirements using existing infrastructure
items.quote: We're keeping our capex limited to just maintenance and organic capex requirements, which is why I keep saying that all of these things are using our existing campus and infrastructure.

items.statement: NCDs raised for debt tenor balancing, not additional capital; net debt expected to reduce by fiscal end
items.quote: On the fundraising side, we have just raised some NCDs to make sure that our debt tenors are balanced and our maturity profiles are balanced. So it's not really additional capital as such at this point.

items.statement: U.S. demand altered by tariff uncertainty but stabilized; U.K. and EU FTAs to offer medium-term opportunities
items.quote: Vis-a-vis U.S. demand as far as Himatsingka is concerned. We have also seen some flip-flop on policies and therefore, the uncertainty. It's created an inflationary environment as far as our products are concerned, and therefore, the demand, let's just say, scenarios has been slightly altered, but I think the going-forward situation vis-a-vis tariff seems to have stabilized to current levels.

items.statement: Home Textile Sheeting faces pricing challenges and market share loss in U.S.; rightsizing planned
items.quote: We believe the home textile space will see pricing challenges going forward, especially on the Sheeting front. And we also believe that our new product verticals will offer better pricing power and market opportunities for us going forward.

items.statement: Yarn Solutions started revenue generation, ramping up; over 90% capacity to be sold externally
items.quote: So I believe that over 90% of our capacities will be placed externally because even today, we are not able to fulfill our internal requirements just by our captive plant.
