items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 16% driven by lower revenue, mix tweaks, raw material inflation
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA came in at INR101 crores. The EBITDA margin came in at about 16%, again, primarily driven by slightly lower revenues, some tweaks in product mix and some inflationary headwinds on the raw material front.

items.statement: Revenues to remain range-bound during transition; new verticals to compensate for Sheeting decline
items.quote: So while we go along, we will try to make sure or we are attempting to make sure that our revenues are range bound and don't take a knock as such.

items.statement: India to become largest or top-2 revenue jurisdiction in medium term via new verticals
items.quote: I will add here that in the medium term, India will probably become the largest jurisdiction for the company going forward, if not the largest, amongst the top 2.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated total income up 16% YoY to INR 495 crore, EBITDA up 17% to INR 88 crore with margins at 18%, cash profit up 56% to INR 76 crore, PAT up nearly 79% to INR 40 crore
items.quote: During the first quarter, we delivered a record quarterly performance, with consolidated total income increasing by 16% year-on-year to INR 495 crore, while EBITDA grew by 17% to INR 88 crore with margins improving to 18%.

items.statement: Flexible packaging capacity expansion of ~30% with capex of INR 50-60 crore, expected operational by Jan-Feb 2026
items.quote: We will be adding about a 30% increase to our existing capacity. You can say that the capacity will increase by about 30%. Abhisar Jain: And approx capex for that? Vidur Kanoria: We will be investing about INR 50 crore to INR 60

items.statement: FY27 non-separator capex budget of INR 100 crore, plus INR 30-40 crore for separator land, total INR 100-150 crore
items.quote: In FY27, we have about INR 100 crore budget and this does not include the separator. The separator spend will be over the course of the next 1.5 years. So this year, it will be probably more like the land cost and then everything else will pretty much be in next year's cost. So this will go up based on the separator announcement by maybe INR 30 crore, INR 40 crore. So between INR 100 crore to INR

items.statement: Battery separator Phase 1 revenue target INR 150-200 crore, long-term scale to 500 million sqm/annum with revenue potential INR 1,100-1,300 crore
items.quote: For Phase 1, the thing is that we are building infrastructure, so that, in future when we expand, as we have indicated, our vision is to make 500 million square meter. So we are buying a big land parcel, which we w ill do in Phase 1. So it is not fair to actually compare the asset turn, but still we expect pretty good margin and a topline of between INR 150 crore to INR 200 crore on this first pha

items.statement: Battery separator expected to deliver good double-digit margins and double-digit ROIC, better returns than existing packaging business
items.quote: Margin will follow, let us see, but I think it will be a good double-digit number. Akshay Kanoria: Basically, the return arithmetic on this from what our calculation meets very well our criteria as a Company. So definitely, if it works out well, it can be more attractive than our existing returns for sure

items.statement: Flexible packaging running at optimal utilization, folding cartons at ~70% utilization with headroom varying by plant, Chennai plant ramp-up on track
items.quote: We are at about 70-plus percent. But in different units, we may be at a higher or lower utilization. So as of now, it is fine. We are mostly concentrating on expanding area in a couple of our factories to make room for capex in the next year.

items.statement: Raw material price increases passed through with a lag of over a quarter, EBITDA margins maintained indicating pass-through effectiveness
items.quote: So there is typically like something of a lag when it comes to price increases being passed on. It is a bit of a difficult calculation because we always have some stocks and stocks on order and everything, whenever a price increase is initiated, it takes like over a quarter for it to get passed through. So, that is what has happened. Saket Kanoria: But basically, the EBITDA margin could not be mai

items.statement: No PLI scheme formalized yet for battery materials, qualification timelines for separator film expected to take at least a year (FY28-29), dependent on cell makers' factory ramp-up
items.quote: So far the government has not formalized any scheme and they have not opened any application. Beyond that, then we will have to discuss when the time for that comes. Otherwise I would not want to speculate on anything for a policy that is not there yet.

items.statement: No current domestic lithium-ion separator competitors, international market fragmented with China/Korea/Japan dominance, technology being developed in-house with R&D
items.quote: Right now, nobody, but Vidur, why don’t you answer. But I think there is nobody today in India who's manufacturing this material and nobody who has announced any plan to manufacture either. Vidur Kanoria: There are manufacturers of separators for lead acid batteries. But for lithium-ion battery today, there is no capacity online

items.statement: UK/EU FTAs provide slight duty reduction for flexible packaging exports, positive sentiment for India sourcing but limited direct benefit as products already at zero duty
items.quote: these FTAs do not really help in terms of our product because they were anyways going at zero duty. Flexibles it’s helped somewhat. There is a slight reduction in duties, which will make us mo re competitive than, say, if they were buying from a Vietnam or a Turkey, now we can be a little more competitive

items.statement: No specific FY27 growth/margin guidance given due to external factors, but domestic demand recovery seen as sustainable, packaging to remain major revenue driver for foreseeable future
items.quote: To give guidance is challenging in the current environment, there are so many factors out of control. But generally speaking, it is looking quite positive from where we sit today for the domestic as well as exports overall is alright, margins follow the top line typically. And over the next 4, 5 years, see the separator is going to be a long-term story. So once this scale and all really picks up,

items.statement: FY27 presales target of INR2,200 crores; H1 exit expected at INR1,050-1,100 crores
items.quote: I think INR2,200 crores is what we are targeting. Rohit: Sorry. INR2,200. Varun Gupta: INR2,200 we are confident of holding it this year. At this moment in time, it looks good. items.quote: And this year is expected around about INR2,000 crores of revenue.

While bookings moderated compared to the exceptionally strong preceding quarter, our collections remained healthy at INR409 crores, registering a 6% year -on-year growth

items.statement: Target project-level gross margin ~30%, SG&A ~12%, PBT ~18%, PAT ~12-13% to sustain 15%+ ROE

items.statement: Average realization improved 37% YoY to INR9,923/sq ft in Q1 FY27

items.statement: Vadgaon Pune Senior Living project underwritten at INR9,000-10,000/sq ft saleable area

items.statement: Inventory shortage in Gurugram, Jaipur, Bhiwadi may cause presales dip in near term; shifting capital to Senior Living
items.quote: A little bit of that is being driven by a little lack of inventory to sell coming up in Gurugram and Jaipur andBhiwadi, some of our key markets in the regular housing space. This is primarily happening because the company is shifting more and more capital towards the Senior Living space

items.statement: IFC partnership platform timeline expired; unable to deploy capital in non-Gurugram projects due to ticket size caps

Just because by the time we timed some of the projects and what their criteria for investment in these other cities outside of Gurugram were, we were not able to meet on the ticket sizes.

items.statement: Vadgaon Pune land acquisition: 28.55 acres, ~20 lakh sq ft saleable, ~INR1,800 crores potential sales value; launch in H2 FY28

items.statement: Bengaluru Kanakapura Road project CPs progressing; definitive documentation expected soon; team deployed for launch readiness

items.statement: Overall business growth guidance raised to 14% to 16% for the current financial year.
items.quote: So overall growth percentage from 12% to 13% may become almost around 14% to 16% overall for the whole of the current financial year, yes.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin guidance raised to around 23% from 22%.
items.quote: At the beginning of the year, we gave the EBITDA ma rgin guidelines of around 22% on a consolidated basis. I think because of better performance, overall EBITDA margins may remain around 23%. So I'm improving the guidelines by 1% here

items.statement: Capex of INR700 crores to INR800 crores planned for the current year.
items.quote: So largely, I think almost around INR700 crores to INR800 crores in current year will go in the CapEx side itself.

items.statement: Institutional business expected to remain single-digit growth, overall around INR260 crores to INR300 crores.
items.quote: Institutional business, we don't look for a very hi gh growth. It will be -- remain in single-digit kind of growth from the -- and overall business may be around INR260 crores to INR300 crores

items.statement: U.S. business growth of around 15% to 17% possible.
items.quote: Maybe around 15%, 16%, 17% kind of growth is possible, but currently looking at portfolio and other things.

items.quote: Normal Ipca launches will be almost around 3 to 4 p roducts and Unichem will also launch similar kind of products almost in a year where I t hink there will be around 7 to 8 kind of launches, both Ipca and Unichem put together will be there

items.statement: No margin pressure expected; material cost to sales may slightly decline versus sales growth.
items.quote: No, no. No margin pressure. I would see that your s ales -- compared to sales growth, material cost will little come down

items.statement: Prices are increasing, not being renegotiated lower.
items.quote: I think there are no such renegotiations of the pri ces where the prices are to be reduced, no. Rather we are increasing the prices everywhere because your costs are also moving up

items.statement: Ipca standalone margin could rise to around 30%; consolidated to 25-26% in 2-3 years.

items.statement: All dollar loans repaid; long-term debt around INR193 crores, no working capital debt.
items.quote: Last financial year, we had almost around close to USD50 million of dollar loans, which we have completely repaid before March itself. In fact, before these dollar depreciation started, we have almost every dollar loan prepaid every dollar loan.

items.statement: INR100 crores more to be invested in biotech piloting facilities and R&D this year.
items.quote: Current year also, we'll be investing almost around INR100 crores more on building up the piloting facilities and additional R&D investment i n biotech

items.statement: Biosimilar clinical work to start from next financial year; revenues expected in FY29-FY30.
items.quote: So overall, I think clinical things will start happening from the next financial year.

items.quote: Overall, I think volume growth is almost around 5%. Price growth is almost around another, I think, 4.5% to 5% and new product launches may be a round 2% or so. So overall growth is around 13

items.quote: We are almost around 7,000 people, medical reps aro und and expansion plan is already completed. items.statement: Management committed to 15-20% CAGR growth over next 3-5 years
items.quote: And the idea is that how we should grow between 15% to 20% CAGR in next 3 to 5 years. Management is committed for that number, and we are planning to do every bit in our scope to see that we achieve that growth.

items.statement: Annualized EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 40-42%
items.quote: But annualized basis, 40% to 42% margins are sustainable.

items.statement: Strong demand for DSVs expected for next 3-5 years, especially if Iran sanctions lift
items.quote: So for next 3 to 5 years, we remain quite bullish that DSVs are going to get a strong demand.

items.quote: See, around 35% to 40% contracts are short term and balance are on long-term. Basically, the EPC contracts that Naveenji mentioned are short term and IMR are generally mid- to long term.

items.statement: Gallant vessel sale to complete in September post shareholder approval
items.quote: So, post-shareholder approval, I don't think so there will be much formalities. And in the coming month, which is September, we should be able to complete.

items.quote: Yes, yes. Correct. Correct.

items.quote: No, 2 years will be too short a time because it is going to take, as I told you, it is 3 to 5 years to get a visible impact for Seamec because oil exploration activity is a long gestation kind of activity.

items.statement: Seamec Princess and Seamec III off-hire for monsoon (May-Oct); advanced talks for new contracts, will file with exchange when finalized
items.quote: No, no, the talks are going on and it is at quite advanced stage. So once it is finalized, we will be filing with the exchange so that everybody is aware about the contracts.

items.statement: MOU with DG Shipping for INR 1,000 crore fleet growth over 2 years on track; Seamec ANANT first acquisition
items.quote: So definitely, this is an MOU that we have signed knowing well our growth plans.

items.statement: Expects branded alco-bev business to grow approximately 60% to 70% for the full year.
items.quote: We expect our branded alco-bev business to grow approximately 60% to 70% for the full year, which is what we had indicated when we had done the Q4 call.

items.statement: Targets approximately 60% revenue growth year-on-year at company level.
items.quote: At the company level we continue to target approximately 60% revenue growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Confident of delivering company-level EBITDA margin of 23% to 24% for FY27.
items.quote: We remain confident in our ability to deliver a company-level EBITDA margin in the range of 23% to 24% for FY27, while continuing to invest behind our brands, new product launches, distribution capabilities, and international expansion.

items.statement: Chhattisgarh revenue guidance of 300 to 400 crores for the year is on track.
items.quote: So we gave a guidance in Q4 where we said that between I think 300 crores to 400 crores would be the revenue from Chhattisgarh this year. And I think we are well on the road we will be able to achieve that guidance definitely.

items.statement: No large capex planned this year; only ordinary course facility improvement and upgradation capex.
items.quote: There is no large capex planned this year. Yes in the ordinary course the capex which goes into improving facilities and upgradation only that will be there. Mostly all the heavy capex has already been executed.

items.statement: Plans to launch new products in this quarter and in quarter 3.
items.quote: So without disclosing what brands are coming we can definitely say that you will see some launches within this quarter and some in quarter 3 as well.

items.statement: Expects second half to be principal growth driver, contributing 60% to 65% of annual branded alco-bev revenue.
items.quote: With the second half expected to be the principal growth driver, in the last year it contributed nearly 60% to 65% of the annual branded alco-bev revenue.

items.statement: Indri growing 18% to 20% year on year; has 87,000 barrels of malt filled, largest in country.
items.quote: Indri is growing at a high digit, double digit number, we are growing between 18% and 20% year on year and that I think is the only company growing at that pace. And to be able to match that pace we have enough stock. For your question, we have 87,000 barrels of malt filled as on date.

items.statement: Camikara and Cashmir expected to grow triple digits this year on small base.
items.quote: Camikara and Cashmir this year are expecting, because see, the base is small, so they are going to see probably triple digit numbers grow.

items.statement: Aims to take Indri to top five global single malt in four to five years with about 1,200 crores top line.
items.quote: And we've kept a runway of four to five years for that. And at that point in time we should be doing a top line of about 1,200 crores on Indri alone.

items.statement: Ultimately wants 70% export and 30% domestic mix, a few years away.
items.quote: So we ultimately want to have 70% export and 30% domestic. But that goal will is a few years away.

items.statement: Facing inflation and price pressures in distillery operations excluding branded, but no pressure on branded side.
items.quote: Yes, inflations, and price pressures are there, but we are not in that really thin margin segment, so to say. So, our distillery operations minus the branded will have some pressures on pricing, but, on our branded side, we do not feel any pressures because the margins there are better.

items.statement: Expects to cross 1,15,000 to 1,20,000 filled barrels by March 2027, 18% to 20% above 1,00,000 barrel guidance.
items.quote: We had taken a guidance of 1,00,000 barrels by the end of this year, financial year that's March 2027. And looks like we will be we'll be crossing that by 18%, 20% we will be having a more than 1,15,000 to 1,20,000 barrels by that time.

items.statement: Reduced debt by about 10 crores this quarter; plans not to increase debt this year.
items.quote: So in this quarter we have reduced the debt by about 10 crores, but as you would understand that you know our growth trajectory continues, right? So we plan to not to increase the debt this year and all the cash from operation will be reinvested into growth and the gap.

items.statement: Ethanol margins usually 10% across the board; country liquor margins 15% to 18%.
items.quote: See ethanol usually across the board it's 10% for everybody give or take a bit depending on the prices. And country liquor again is very dependent on prices of grain fuel so anywhere between 15% to 18%.

items.quote: And a lot of that is also owed to you know there has been this court order from Chennai where all the ethanol plants have been put to rest right now and only orders will start flowing in from next month probably, quarter two and quarter three.

items.statement: FY27 Defence revenue target INR300-350 crores with EBITDA margin 30-35%
items.quote: In all, company aims to achieve INR300 crores to INR350 crores target this year with a marked EBITDA of 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth guidance 15-20% for FY27
items.quote: We maintain our guidance that it should be 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Defence capex ~INR400 crores; standalone capex INR100-150 crores for next couple of years
items.quote: Capex in the Defence sector, we have already given it should be almost INR400 crores. And for the current for the stand -alone division -- stand-alone unit, it will be -- it shou ld be almost INR100 crores to INR150

items.statement: Q1 FY27 Defence revenue INR80 crores at 38% EBITDA margin
items.quote: It was 80 crores and with a EBITDA of 38%.

items.statement: Value-added products ~60% of mix, increasing; legacy business declining
items.quote: Value-added, we have almost 60% we are already there. And in the coming years, this will increase and the legacy business, it will get reduced due to the increase in the value-added business.

items.statement: Hydraulic tube capacity utilization improved to 60-65% in Q1 FY27 from 50%; rapid expansion expected in coming quarters
items.quote: This hydraulic tube capacity, now it has started ramping up. In this quarter, it has come to almost 60%, which was earlier 50%. This quarter, it has come to 60% to 65%. And I hope in the coming quarters, it will be a rapid expansion, a rapid expansion in the percentage utilization.

items.statement: EBITDA per metric ton improved to INR9,000 in Q1 FY27 from previous quarter
items.quote: This quarter also, our EBITDA per metric ton is INR9,000 per metric ton. So we improved from the last quarter.

items.statement: Export growth 53% in Q1 FY27 from US and Europe; pipeline healthy but geopolitical uncertainty remains
items.quote: Was around 53% -- for this quarter, the pipeline of orders is pretty healthy for this quarter also. But again, geopolitical is a factor which should not be kept aside that we have to continuously monitor.

items.statement: Management confident of achieving approximately 10% revenue growth in FY27 with significant portion in second half
items.quote: Based on the visibility we have today, we remain confident of achieving approximately 10% revenue growth in FY27 with a significant portion of this growth expected to come through in the second half of the financial year.

items.statement: Current year estimates around 10% growth with EBITDA of 13%-14% and similar interest cost every quarter
items.quote: Current year estimates which is there is around 10% growth with EBITDA of 13%-14% with similar interest cost every quarter.

items.quote: As of June 30, FY26, our consolidated order book stood at Rs. 14,636 crores.

items.statement: Approximately Rs. 9,000 crores of bids under evaluation and near-term opportunity pipeline of approximately Rs. 60,000 crores
items.quote: In addition to our existing order book, we currently have approximately Rs. 9,000 crores of bids under evaluation. And more importantly, we have identified a near-term opportunity pipeline of approximately Rs. 60,000 crores.

items.statement: Targeting around Rs. 8,000 crores new orders this year expecting 10% growth in current year and 15% in corresponding year
items.quote: So, see we are targeting around Rs. 8,000 crores new orders this year which you know with that we are expecting 10% growth in the current year and 15% in the year corresponding.

items.statement: Consolidated operating EBITDA margin improved to 14.02% from 13.4% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Operating EBITDA has improved with a margin of 14.02% compared to 13.4% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Expect to maintain EBITDA margins between 13%-14%
items.quote: So, we expect to maintain our EBITDA margins between 13%-14%.

items.quote: Plus, maybe some working capital borrowings of Rs. 100 crores – Rs. 200 crores may be needed in between.

items.quote: This year, target for non-core is between Rs. 150 crores to Rs. 200 crores. That we are fairly confident to achieve.

items.quote: Right now, if I am not mistaken, around 85% to 90% of the shares are pledged. So, we expect that to come down by at least 15%-20%.

items.quote: We b elieve the next phase of India's infrastructure development will be driven by large, technically complex and capital-intensive projects across Hydropower, Pump Storage, Tunneling, Irrigation and Urban Infrastructure segments

items.quote: The order book remains well-diversified, with Hydropower contributing 62%, Irrigation 17%, Tunneling 4%, and Roads and Urban Infrastructure accounting for the balance 17%.

items.statement: Finance cost reduced by almost Rs. 10 crores compared to corresponding quarter due to debt reduction
items.quote: So, finance cost has come down during the quarter compared to the corresponding quarter by almost Rs. 10 crores.

items.statement: Long-term credit rating upgraded to A stable from A-, short-term rating upgraded to A1 from A2 in June
items.quote: In June, our long-term credit rating was upgraded to A stable from A-, while our short-term rating was upgraded to A1 from A2.

items.statement: Completed sale of Rs. 27 crores land parcel in Telangana during Q1 FY27
items.quote: As part of our stated strategy of monetizing non-core assets during Q1 FY27, we completed the sale of a Rs. 27 crores land parcel in Telangana.

items.statement: Subansiri Lower Hydroelectric Project on track for all eight units to become operational during this financial year
items.quote: We remain on track for all eight units to become operational during this financial year, which will be an important miles tone not only for the project, but also for Patel Engineering

items.quote: We have grown around nearly 12% at Q1. Our expectation for growth of gold loan this year is around 30%, because some quarters are as per season, some quarters are off seasons. We expect that to be some between 25%-30%.

items.quote: We expect the yield to be somewhere around 18%. It may go down by 25 basis points or go up by 25 basis. Beyond that, we do not expect anything. It will be around 18%.

items.statement: Targets ROA of 3.5% to 4% and ROE of 15% to 18%.
items.quote: We are targeting an ROA of around 3.5% to 4%, and targeting an ROE of 15% to 18%, which is the ROE target.

items.statement: Expects to take ROE to around 18% in three years.
items.quote: Yes, we expect the ROAs and ROEs to consistently grow. In three years, our expectation is to take that ROE to around 18%.

items.statement: Plans to open around 500 branches, including Manappuram Finance and Asirvad.
items.quote: Now, one good news for us is the requirement of prior approval from RBI has been removed, which facilitates the opening of the branches. So we have the plan to open around 500 branches now.

items.statement: Wants to maintain around 75%-80% of consolidated AUM in gold.
items.quote: I am very happy to say that our focus will be more on gold loan. We want to maintain around 75%-80% of the consolidated AUM in gold.

items.statement: Wants to contain microfinance between 8%-10% on a consolidated basis.
items.quote: As I said, the microfinance will be contained between 8%-10%. That will be the cap on a consolidated basis we will put.

items.statement: Pricing expected to be in a broad band around 18%.

items.statement: Incremental funding cost expected around 8.8 to 9.

items.statement: Interest rate on income-generating gold loan scheme ranges from 14%-16%.
items.quote: The interest rate on this scheme, it ranges from 14%-16%.

items.statement: Vehicle finance GNPA elevated at 13.3%; focus is on collections.
items.quote: Focus is now on collections as GNPA continues to be elevated at 13.3% versus 10.4% in prior quarter.

items.statement: Microfinance disbursement expected at INR400 crores to INR500 crores.
items.quote: The growth will remain at a level of, I feel like INR400 crores to INR500 crores, as a disbursement in MFI.

items.statement: No more vehicle loans to be disbursed this year; may reconsider in FY2028.
items.quote: We do not want to disburse any more vehicle loans during this year. After one year, that probably in FY 2028, we may consider whether to restart or not.

items.statement: New MD and CEO Ashish Singh expected to join by January 1, 2027.

items.statement: Management expects mid-single-digit volume growth for FY27 and aims to maintain or improve EBITDA margins above 11%
items.quote: We remain positive for the entire year for both the single-digit margin -- single-digit volume growth and also a double-digit margin or the margins which we've given today. We'll only better that going forward.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved 360 bps to 11.6% driven by higher capacity utilization and JV profitability
items.quote: As a result of capacity utilization, our EBITDA margins have gone up on operational efficiencies, both on capacity utilization in our plants and also on the JV performances. So EBITDA margins go up by 3.6% to 11.6% for the quarter.

items.statement: Management targets EBITDA margin of 12%+ and believes current 11%+ margins are sustainable due to operational efficiencies
items.quote: Yes, absolutely. That's the target that we achieve 12% and more. But currently, we are very confident of showing the 11-plus percent margins, which we showed last quarter and this quarter.

items.statement: Announced 9+ million sqm greenfield plant in South with INR 220 crore capex, operational by Q3/Q4 FY28, adding INR 350 crore potential revenue
items.quote: Because of that, we have announced setting up a 9 million square meter plant -- 9-plus million square meter plant in the South, which would be up and ready by in the next 12 to 15 months. This would give us a potential revenue of about INR350 crores.

items.statement: Total capex of INR 275 crore planned through FY27 end including South plant and balancing equipment across plants, 65-70% funded internally

items.statement: Adding 4-5 million sqm capacity via balancing equipment in existing lines (Bahadurgarh, Gujarat, Morbi, South) by mid-Q3 to Q4 FY27, focused on value-added products
items.quote: We are taking many more steps, which are all work in progress to augment further capacity by about 4 million to 5 million in our existing lines in Bahadurgarh in -- which is in Haryana and in Gujarat and in Morbi and also in the South.

items.quote: Fortunately, we've been able to pass on all the gas price increase until now. So the current price increase has been between 16% and 18%.

items.statement: Standalone capacity utilization improved from 72% in Q1 FY26 to 83% in Q1 FY27; JVs swung from INR 10 crore loss to INR 3 crore profit YoY
items.quote: So if you see same time last quarter, which is Q1 last year, it was 72%. We are at 83%, and that's an 11% increase in -- sorry stand-alone, yes. On a stand-alone basis from 72% capacity utilization to 83%.

items.statement: Morbi exports down 50-60% from peak due to geopolitical/freight issues; expected to continue through Q2 FY27 until freight settles
items.quote: The only negative in the quarter has been from a Morbi perspective is exports has been down due to geopolitical reasons, the export is down a good 50%, 60% from the peak. That's been a little bit of a downer for the quarter, and this would continue probably for this quarter until it starts settling, until the freight starts settling.

items.statement: Project business (currently 7-8% retail, 10-11% government) expected to grow 3-4% as a share of total
items.quote: Our total project was about 7%, 8% in retail and about 10%, 11% in government. This in totality will go up by about 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Working capital days improved from 17 to 12 days; inventory reduced significantly due to Morbi shutdown; receivables and creditor days healthy
items.quote: Our debtor days, inventory days, creditor days are all healthy. Working capital days also have come down from 17 to 12 days.

items.statement: South plant capex funded ~60% internal accruals; balance via JV-level debt with no corporate guarantee from Somany
items.quote: About 60% with internal accruals.

items.statement: Maximum revenue potential at current capacity and prices is ~INR 3,700 crore; balancing equipment may add ~INR 300 crore more by year-end
items.quote: Approximately INR3,700 crores, yes, more or less, give or take, INR50 crores at today's price.

items.statement: Targets top line growth of more than 15% year-on-year, about INR1,350 crores for this financial year.
items.quote: We are targeting a top line growth of more than 15% year-on-year, resulting into about INR1,350 crores for this financial year, maintaining a healthy bottom line.

items.statement: Next year revenue target INR1,600 crores plus/minus INR50 crores.
items.quote: Next year, you're looking at about INR1,600 crores plus/minus INR50 crores.

items.statement: Order intake over next 3-4 years should be at least INR8,000-9,000 crores, executed over 5-6 years.
items.quote: Our order intake over the next 3 to 4 years, I think should be in the region of at least INR8,000 crores to INR9,000 crores to be executed over the next 5 to 6 years.

items.statement: At least INR1,600 crores order inflow expected this year, may improve.
items.quote: M.V.R. confirms that we will see at least INR1,600 crores being added this year. And we may improve that number by the way, over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Total order book stands at INR4,300 crores as on date.
items.quote: So with this major win, our total order book sells to a record-breaking of INR4,300 crores as on date.

items.statement: Stand-alone order book INR2,156 crores; consolidated INR2,849 crores including service orders INR244 crores.
items.value: INR2,156 crores; INR2,849 crores; INR244 crores
items.quote: In terms of the opportunities, our stand-alone order book as of quarter end stands at INR2,156 crores, providing strong visibility for the upcoming period. Around 66% of this order book is from defense and the rest that is 34% is from space, metrology and hydrology sectors. Our consolidated order book stands at INR2,849 crores, which includes service orders of about INR244 crores, which are typica

items.statement: Secured INR2,205 crores order from HAL for Uttam Radar subsystems in July.
items.quote: Staying in the order book, I would like to highlight that in the month of July, we secured a significant order worth about INR2,205 crores from Hindustan Aeronautics Limited for procurement of critical subsystems for Uttam Radar.

items.statement: Expect INR700-800 crores orders from QRSAM for first 3 regiments.
items.quote: So that will leave at least INR700 crores, INR800 crores worth of orders to be added from for QRSAM for the first 3 regiments only, at least for now.

items.statement: Expect INR500-750 crores orders from Astra Rafael Comsys JV.
items.quote: We are looking at least INR500 crores to INR750 crores orders from our Astra Rafael Comsys, our joint venture, and at least INR3,000 crores worth of business coming in from Su-30, Virupaksha as well as Angad.

items.statement: Expect INR100-120 crores orders from BEL for Shatrughat and Samaghat programs.
items.quote: Approximately around INR100 crores to INR120 crores worth of orders we expect for these 2 programs put together.

items.statement: Margins expected similar to last year with positive increase.
items.quote: Definitely, definitely, the margins are going to be similar to last year. You can expect a delta increase on that -- positive increase in that margins.

items.statement: Expect to maintain current margin trajectory, but no commitment due to factors.
items.quote: So that gives us the confidence that we should be able to maintain more or less our current margin trajectory. But we don't want to commit to you on the margins because there are a lot of factors which will come into play from incremental products, number one.

items.statement: Invested in automated process engineering workflows and advanced infrastructure.
items.quote: To support this rapidly growing volume and complexity of work, we have invested steadily in automated process engineering workflows and advanced infrastructure.

items.statement: Stretch supply chains across borders due to global restocking; ensuring supply chains remain intact.
items.quote: So we are beefing up our purchase departments and other departments as the risk, which I also want to highlight is stretch supply chains across the border, across every country because everybody is restocking on their ornaments inventory. So we've got to make sure that our supply chains remain intact and stuff comes in within the defined time lines.

items.statement: No dilution for working capital; equity is expensive.
items.quote: Till we have accretive nonorganic opportunities, we will not dilute for working capital. We are fairly comfortable on that part, which goes on to increase our return on equity, which is already has moved up substantially.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue guidance to INR2,200-2,300 crores with EBITDA margin of 10-11% (INR220-230 crores EBITDA)
items.quote: So basically, what we are guiding is INR2,200 crores to INR2,300 crores top line and EBITDA margin in the range of 10% to 11%. So, it will be in that range between INR220 crores, INR230 crores kind of EBITDA.

items.statement: FY28 normalized EBITDA margin target of 12-14%
items.quote: In fiscal '28, I think it's in the region of 12% to 14% is what we can look at.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 4% from 45% in Q4 FY26 due to raw material cost increases
items.quote: You would have seen the details of our financial statements and you would have seen that our margins, which were plus 45% last quarter, has come down to 4%, and that's what has percolated down to our EBITDA for the quarter.

items.statement: Specialty Ingredients EBITDA margin at 6.35% in Q1 FY27, down from normalized 10%+ due to 4-5% gross margin hit from geopolitical issues and 1-2% from liquidity constraints
items.quote: If I had done this 4%, my normalized EBITDA at this moment of time and with all the pressures of putting the material to American markets and other things, I would have done 4% at least more on gross margin, which would have straight flown down to my EBITDA.

items.statement: Aroma segment EBITDA negative INR4-4.5 crores in Q1 FY27 due to low 25% capacity utilization on ethyl vanillin campaign; expects positive EBITDA in Q2 FY27
items.quote: As I said, we were cautiously increasing the ramp-up of ethyl vanillin. And you would have seen that we would have produced how many -- 400 tons only in this quarter, with a capacity of 1,500. So naturally, there was cost of the plant, fixed cost, which cannot be absorbed entirely on the 400.

items.statement: Performance Chemicals EBITDA at 2.5% in Q1 FY27 due to diphenol plant shutdown; expects positive EBITDA in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Naturally, the closure of diphenol plant is weighing down on Performance Chemicals, and that's why we have seen a 2.5% EBITDA there.

items.statement: Vanillin demand picking up; channel stocks cleared; U.S./Europe supply gap of 5,000-6,000 tons identified
items.quote: So basically, the demand is U.S. and Europe where the antidumping duties are. So our focus on these 2 markets. And there seems to be a gap of about 5,000 to 6,000 tons of material, which will have to be imported because the local production capacities are fully occupied at that level.

items.statement: Ethyl vanillin 95% customer approval achieved; 350 tons sold in Q1 FY27; switching to methyl vanillin in Q2 FY27 for better margins
items.quote: We are happy to announce that we have almost -- 95% of our customers have approved our ethyl vanillin. In this quarter, we have already sold 350. If you remember in last quarter, we have said that we are taking the campaign of 750 -odd metric tons of ethyl vanillin.

items.statement: Vanillin production guidance reduced to ~3,000 tons for FY27 from 3,600-4,000 tons due to slower ethyl vanillin ramp-up and 4 campaign changeovers
items.quote: So basically, we had guided for 3,600 to 4,000 and now we are saying 3,000 -- around 3,000. The change is basically in our ethyl vanillin run. The ramp-up we took was slower than what we had anticipated purely because we wanted to get the quality standards to be absolutely undoubtable.

items.statement: Diphenol plant remains shut; evaluating alternative uses; decision by Q3 FY27
items.quote: By third quarter, we will take a decision to either have an alternate use for that or maybe if the situation is right, we may shift back to the diphenol production.

items.statement: May need INR100-200 crores additional credit lines for working capital as revenue scales to INR2,400 crores
items.quote: We will try to use the internal cash, but it looks like as the year progresses, we may have to go and go and take credit lines from the market in the range of INR100 crores to INR200 crores plus.

items.statement: Working capital cycle elongated to ~100 days due to Red Sea shipping rerouting and slower customer collections
items.quote: As you know, with the Hormuz Strait and the Red Sea issues, we have to now ship it across the South Africa, and that has increased the working capital needs. The -- because of the global slowdown also the recovery from the customers have also elongated by a few days and that's weighing down on the working capital cycle.

items.statement: Raw material cost pressures persist in Q2 FY27; expects to pass on ~50% of cost increases in blends
items.quote: No, not fully. But in the blends, some of it upwards, we will be able to pass on. I'm not saying that we'll be able to pass on entirely the cost, but maybe half of the cost we'll be able to pass on.

items.statement: Expects double-digit EBITDA margins by Q3 FY27; Q2 FY27 all three segments positive EBITDA
items.quote: Q3 could be there. Rehan: Q2? Nirmal Momaya: Q3. Rehan: So Q3 would swing back to double-digit? Nirmal Momaya: Yes

items.statement: Ethyl vanillin campaign of 750 tons half completed; methyl vanillin orders in hand for Q2 FY27
items.quote: If you remember in last quarter, we have said that we are taking the campaign of 750 -odd metric tons of ethyl vanillin. Half of that is done. We have produced almost more than 300 metric tons.

items.statement: Expect positive sales growth impact visible from Q2 FY27
items.quote: Difficult to give the number, but we should be positive and that positive impact should be visible from Q2 itself, I believe.

items.statement: Target to reach 70% premium product contribution in next 3-4 years
items.period: next three years to four years
items.quote: Now we have reached to 60-plus percentage already and the target is to reach to 70% in next three years to four years time.

items.statement: Expect Granuvia INR20 cr and Spinoace INR10 cr+ in FY27, combined INR30-35 cr gross
items.quote: I believe Granuvia can touch about INR20 crores in this fiscal and Spinoace can go INR10 crores plus, so both products put together INR30 crores to INR35 crores range is possible in this fiscal, gross level.

items.statement: Kaeros targeting 100% CAGR initially, then 50-60%
items.quote: Kaeros is a new company which we had launched and the target is to grow at a CAGR of 100% initially and then it will come down to 50%-60%.

items.statement: Sotanala total investment ~INR200 cr (INR50 cr formulation, INR150 cr technical), INR70 cr spent so far
items.quote: It will be a project total investment. These total investment will go roughly about INR200 crores, out of which I think about INR50 crores will be going in the formulations and INR150 crores will be for the technical. And the total investment made so far is to the tune of about INR70 crores.

items.statement: Annual capex to normalize to INR30-40 cr maintenance after current projects complete
items.quote: Once the current projects are completed, we expect annual capex to normalize around INR30 crores to INR40 crores of maintenance capex, allowing us to increasingly focus on utilization, cash generation and returns.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 240 bps to 31.6% in Q1 FY27 despite volume decline
items.quote: If we compare the value year-on-year results, the revenue from operations has degrown by 12%, INR691 crores to INR612 crores, and the gross profit has decreased from 202 crores to 193.16 crores by 4% though the gross profit percentage has increased from 29% to 31.6%.

items.statement: Premium product margins: Focus Maharatna 35%+, Maharatna ~30%, Generics 10-15%
items.quote: generally I always tell that FMs are the products which have higher profitability, Maharatna have reas onable profitability, say in between, and generics are sales that are low profitability. If you have the price advantage over any generic, you can make some good profits than the normal, because normally generic end up selling the generic at 10% to 15% gross margins. So, there can be cases where

items.statement: Premium portfolio (Maharatna + Focus Maharatna) at 64% of B2C in Q1 FY27 vs 58% YoY
items.quote: if we see some mix here, then the premium product sales has increased during this quarter. Last year, it was 58% of total B2C contribut ion, this year first quarter it is 64% of the total B2C contribution

items.statement: Monsoon improved in August, reservoir levels up, crops healthy; South India rice sowing 40% pending
items.quote: If we talk about August monsoons, we see good rains across all country, the reservoir situation is improving and the crops are very healthy. The only gap what we see is majorly in the South India where the rice sowing is little delayed in many parts where the dams are not full. But the dam situation is improving now. 40-odd percent of rice is pending remaining are to be sown in Karnataka, Andhra a

items.statement: Sales returns possible but expect to reduce to at least half of prior year's INR200 cr
items.quote: Yes, sales return, possibilities are definitely there, but this year I see only 1 or 2 herbicides failing, not many, number 1. Number 2, we were very, v ery cautious looking at the last year. So, the placements were not that strong what we did in the last year. It was a strategic call what we had taken to place lower, otherwise I could have also achieved the sales number by placing more, but we di

items.statement: Took price hikes in March, April (2), attempted May but rolled back due to weak demand
items.quote: We tried, like, as I told you that there was a big expectation of price hike in the month of March, we had taken one hike in March, two hikes in April, and I believe in May also we tried to take one hike, but somehow we had to roll it back because the market was very much delayed and the sentiment of the network was very weak.

items.statement: Dahej technical plant can add at least INR200 cr production capacity
items.quote: At least INR200 crores is possible to be added into the technical production plant and formulation also is going to support in a good way.

items.statement: Volume degrowth ~13% in Q1 FY27 with ~2% price increase
items.quote: Yes, the volume degrowth is about 13%. There is a small value growth of about 2% actually, which is visible in Q1 results.

items.statement: Sotanala formulation facility expected April-May next year, technical by Diwali
items.quote: The formulation facility at Sotanala is expected to commence around April-May next year, followed by technical products-- production by Diwali, subject to the project schedule.

items.statement: Target to double company size in 4-5 years
items.quote: The idea is to double ourselves. In the past, we used to double in 3 to 4 years. Now I believe that we should be able to double in 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of at least 50% for FY27
items.quote: So I think revenue guidance remains the same. It will be at least 50%.

items.statement: SSSG guidance of 8% to 10% for FY27
items.quote: And the guidance for SSSG has always been 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Store opening target of 170 to 200 stores for FY27
items.quote: Yes, we are on track to open 170 to 200 stores this year.

items.statement: New store capex increased to INR1.2-1.22 crores from INR1.1 crores
items.quote: So earlier, the capex used to be about INR1.1 crores. So I think it is up because of the prices rising, it has moved up to INR1.2 crores, INR1.22 crores.

items.statement: Planning 4-5% price increase from Q3 FY27 to pass on raw material cost inflation
items.quote: So I think we'll start seeing that impact from the third quarter onwards, and it will be an increase of about, I would say, 4% to 5% increase in the overall garment cost, which we'll have to pass on to the consumer.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target to be maintained despite aggressive store expansion
items.quote: And we will try to maintain the EBITDA margins even after opening so much new area.

items.statement: Demand in July-August in line with expectations; festive season in Q3 will determine full year
items.quote: July and August are at par with how we see demand and how we forecast the demand. But again, it will completely depend on the October, November period that will have the bulk of the sales.

items.statement: Consumer demand considered inelastic due to necessity-driven categories like kids wear (25% of sales)
items.quote: We think we are selling necessity to the consumers. And for example, kids wear is 25% of our sales. So you have to buy new clothes for your kids every year.

items.statement: Internal accruals and vendor prepayment reversal (INR150-200 crores) sufficient for expansion; no QIP needed
items.quote: No, I think the internal accruals will be enough. And currently, we are using a lot of our cash in prepaying our vendors. So once we want to use that money for expansion plans, we just get the creditor days back to normal. So I think that releases almost INR150 crores to INR200 crores of capital plus the EBITDA we'll generate this year.

items.statement: Inventory target of 90-100 days and creditor cycle of 45-50 days
items.quote: We are looking to target inventory of 90 to 100 days and creditor cycle of 45 to 50 days.

items.statement: Full price sales at 90% in Q1 FY27 vs 92% last year due to Adhik Maas and fewer wedding dates
items.quote: So there was a 30-day period of Adhik Maas in quarter 1. And I think because of that, we saw our full price sales go down from 92% to 90%.

items.statement: New stores operating at INR730-740 per sq ft vs mature stores at INR1,070-1,100 per sq ft
items.quote: But it's at a very respectable level, all the new stores that we have opened, they are already operating more than INR730, INR740 per square feet of sale.

items.statement: Repeat customer rate within first year improved from 40% to 55% over last 3 years
items.quote: So in fact, in the last 3 years, people who came back to us within the first year has moved up from 40% to almost 55%.

items.statement: Lease terms: 9-11 years with 12-15% escalation every 3 years; mostly standalone stores
items.quote: The average lease period ranges anywhere between 9 to 11 years, and the escalation ranges anywhere from 12% to 15% every 3 years. So that's the standard lease format.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 16% to 18% by year-end FY27
items.quote: On our EBITDA margins, I should say that even if things go along the way they are, we should be reaching closer to about at least between 16% to 18% by the year-end.

items.statement: PM3 major rebuild underway, commissioning within a month; major capex program completed
items.quote: Further, Paper Machine 3 has been shut for the time being for a major rebuild, which will lead to enhanced production capabilities and improved quality in the final product.

items.statement: Peak debt estimated at INR 760-770 crores; repayment of INR 170-175 crores annually for next 2-3 years to reach under INR 300 crores
items.quote: Peak debt, we are currently looking at about INR760 crores or INR770 crores maximum. And we have repayments of about INR170 crores, INR175 crores for the next 2 to 3 years. And by the next 3 years, we will be at very, very manageable levels of debt under INR300 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 13.2%; cost increase of INR 4,200/ton offset NSR gain of INR 3,400/ton QoQ
items.quote: As a result, EBITDA stood at INR40 crores, broadly stable year -on-year basis with EBITDA margin at 13.2%.

items.statement: NSR increased ~INR 3,400/ton QoQ but cost rose ~INR 4,200/ton due to West Asia conflict impacting fuel, chemicals, freight
items.value: INR 3,400/ton NSR gain vs INR 4,200/ton cost increase
items.quote: However, the improvement in blended NSR by approximately INR3,400 per ton was more than offset by an increase in cost of around INR4,200 per ton on a quarter-to-quarter basis. Driven by higher raw material, chemical and fuel prices amid the ongoing West Asia conflict.

items.statement: Target NSR of INR 72,000-75,000/ton in next 4-6 months from current INR 68,000-69,000/ton
items.quote: Currently, we are at about INR68,000, INR69,000 per ton level. Ideally, going forward, sensing of how the market is growing and the kind of positivity that -- positive sentiment that we are getting, our price increase is likely to touch and reach about INR72,000 to INR75,000 level in the next 4, 6 months.

items.statement: Healthy demand in Q1 FY27 supported by education, publishing, office consumption; expect demand to remain supportive
items.quote: The paper industry saw a healthy demand suppo rted by education, publishing, office consumption and broader economic activity in the first quarter of the financial year 2027.

items.statement: Specialty paper contribution currently ~18-19% of revenue; targeting 30% with OGR paper launch and specialty grade focus
items.quote: Right now, our contribution from specialty paper is just under 20%. It's about 18%, 19%, but we will surely be making our efforts to reach that level of 30%.

items.statement: West Asia conflict driving raw material, chemical, fuel cost volatility; local wheat straw prices elevated but cooling; import competition diminishing due to shipping costs
items.quote: However, the West Asia conflict intensified cost pressures, particularly across fuel, chemicals and other raw materials, while also affe cting freight and logistics cost. This created a challenging margin environment for paper manufacturers even as demand conditions improved.

items.statement: Commissioned DDS Double Displacement Digester System for wood pulping; installed Folio Ream Wrapping Machine; produced OGR paper on PM2
items.quote: We successfully commissioned the DDS Double Displacement Digester System for wood pulping, which will help optimize pulp quality and yield while reducing utility chemical and overall pulp costs.

items.statement: Pulp capacity to increase to 410-415 TPD from 365 TPD; clonal sapling production at 17.28 lakh/quarter; added 1,300 acres social farm forestry (total ~19,650 acres)
items.quote: So pulp capacity should -- will increase to about 410, 415 tons per day, and that's all that we will require to produce the relevant quantities of paper.

items.statement: AI integration in manufacturing targeted for completion by March 2028; targeting 4-5% cost reduction
items.quote: We could target between 4% to 5% additions in -- or reductions in costs.

items.statement: Antidumping and anti-subsidy duty applications filed for writing/printing paper (40-140 GSM); government reviewing
items.quote: We have already done that. We are already in close coordination with the government, where our applications for antidumping duty and anti -subsidy duty has already been filed, and it is being keenly being looked at by the government.

items.statement: Wheat straw prices cooling; reduction seen in Q2 vs Q1; further decline expected post-September with alternate fodder availability
items.quote: We are seeing a reduction in wheat straw procurement prices for ourselves in Q2 versus Q1.

items.statement: With the capacity being completed in Q3, revenue should reach INR7,000 crores to INR7,500 crores in a normal market.
items.quote: Sir, with the given capacity probably which is getting completed in Q3 of this year, you can say end of the calendar year December 2026, with the given capacity it should reach INR7,000 crores to INR7,500 crores in a normal market.

items.statement: Overall project outlay revised from around INR1,000 crores to INR1,112 crores; balance INR35 crores to INR40 crores to be completed by end of 2026.
items.quote: We have already invested INR1,076 crores, mostly through internal accruals, while the overall project outlay has been revised from around INR1,000 crores to INR1,112 crores, primarily due to technical upgrades, additional ancillaries, some inflation, and some time overruns also. The balance of around INR35 crores to INR40 crores is expected to be completed by the end of this current year 2026.

items.statement: DI pipe order book is around four months based on current dispatch position.
items.quote: Madam, as per the current dispatch position, it is the equivalent of say , the current capacity utilization, it is around four months' order book.

items.statement: Ferroalloy margin expected to sustain between 15% to 20% as specialty share increases.
items.quote: See, for ferroalloy business, as the share of specialty ferroalloy increase in our overall mix, we expect the margin to sustain between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: DI pipe margin achieved around 12% in Q1, should go up to 18% if prices improve.
items.quote: Whatever we have achieved in first quarter around 12%, that is good enough and it should go up to 18% if the prices improve.

items.statement: Post-monsoon recovery expected in DI pipe dispatches and payments; from Q3 things should improve.
items.quote: So, we would be looking at a post -monsoon recovery in the dispatches and the payments, and from the third quarter things should improve now.

items.statement: Value-added products were 42% of total sales in Q1 FY27; plant designed to achieve 70%.
items.quote: Importantly, value-added products accounted for 42% of the total sales in Q1 FY27, highlighting the continued progress in our product mix.

items.statement: DI pipe prices have dropped 25% to 30% compared to a year and a half ago and are at rock bottom.
items.quote: Look, providing EBITDA guidance for the pipe business would be speculative at this stage, because prices have dropped by 25% to 30% compared to where they stood a year and a half ago. Prices have fallen by 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Ferroalloy capacity utilization was above 80% last quarter and expected to remain 80% to 90% after new module commissioning.
items.quote: In ferroalloys, we achieved a capacity utilization of more than 80% in the last quarter, and it is around 27% of the turnover currently. So, as we commission the new module by December -January, capacity utilization in ferroalloys will remain at around 80% to 90%.

items.statement: DI pipe capacity utilization was 30% in Q1; first target is to achieve 50% to 60%.
items.quote: Right now, in the first quarter, the capacity utilization was 30% of the enhanced capacity. Around 100 and going forward as per the orders improve, we are ready to encash this. Production in the first quarter was 41,000. The annual capacity is 5,50,000. It is somewhere in the range of 30%, 33%. And if the market improves, it should go or double up. We -- first target is to achieve 50% to 60% capac

items.statement: Competition intensity will persist until capacity utilization crosses 65% to 70%.
items.quote: See, the competitive intensity will be there because currently because the currently the industry with our pipe capacity utilization this particular quarter was only 30% on the enhanced capacity. Similarly, competitors, they also are operating somebody in 25% range, somebody in 30%, 35% range. So, competition intensity will be there till the time capacity utilization crosses 65%, 70%.

items.statement: Net term debt reduced from INR3,408 crores in FY21 to INR188 crores in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: We have also continued to make strong progress on deleveraging with our net term debt reducing significantly from INR3,408 crores in FY21 to INR188 crores in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: TMT bar sales in West Bengal expected to increase to 50% to 70% next year from 15% to 20%.
items.quote: So, these products in Bengal, we were selling hardly 15%, 20% of our material. Going forward in the next year, we are foreseeing that probably we'll be able to sell around 50% to 60%, 70% of our TMT bars in West Bengal.

items.statement: Conventional steel product margins vary between 5% to 7%, specialized ferroalloys around 15% to 18%.
items.quote: So, for conventional steel products, the margins vary between 5% to 7%, and for specialized ferroalloys it's around 15% to 18%.

items.statement: DI pipe capacity increased from 5 lakh tons to 5.5 lakh tons per annum.
items.quote: Our DI pipe capacity has increased from 5 lakh tons to 5.5 lakh tons per annum, positioning us well to ramp up utilization as the demand revives and market conditions improve.

items.statement: Specialized ferroalloy capacity being enhanced to 1.9 lakh metric tons per annum from 1.66 lakh tons; blast furnace to 7.5 lakh tons from 6.3 lakh tons; sinter to 12.08 lakh tons from 9.08 lakh tons, commissioning by Q3 FY27.
items.quote: In parallel, our specialized ferroalloy capacity is also being enhanced to 1.9 lakh metric tons per annum from 1.66 lakh tons, and our blast furnace capacity will increase to 7.5 lakh tons per annum from 6.3 lakh tons capacity, and sinter capacity to 12.08 lakh tons from 9.08 lakh tons. These enhanced capacities are expected to be commissioned by Q3 FY27.

items.statement: FY27 expected to be best year in company history; July revenue INR150 cr+ monthly run rate
items.quote: This quarter is the best quarter in the history of the company. We are ahead of the composite sales with Flipkart partnership that entered and ultimately terminated. This quarter we cross the highest turnover which we reported in during our Flipkart partnership era. And this year we believe that should be the best year in the history of Health X.

items.statement: RetailerShakti EBITDA expected to turn positive in Q3 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA number we are closer to break even and expect to make positive EBITDA in Q3 this financial year end.
