items.statement: Approximately INR 118 crores invested in fit-outs for current 1.13 million sq ft operational portfolio; additional deposits and refurbishment capital paid for 2.3 million sq ft signed future capacity
items.quote: Yes. INR 118-odd crores of investment in the fit-outs of probably the assets that we have. Now this would be all fresh investments. There would be obviously assets which would have turned older and we would have reinvested some more capital in that. And future deposits that we have paid for like as I covered earlier, there's almost 2.3 million square feet of assets that we have signed up for the f

items.statement: Raised INR 100 crores through senior, listed, secured, redeemable non-convertible debentures at 11.75% coupon with 36-month tenure; 1.85 crore shares (19.65% equity) encumbered but promoter holding not pledged or reduced
items.quote: Subsequent to Q1 ,DevX raised INR 100 crores through senior, listed, secured, redeemable, and non-convertible debt, carrying a coupon of 11.75% per annum with a tenure of 36 months.

items.statement: Enterprise clients contributed approximately 70% of revenue from operations in Q1 FY27, up from 52% in corresponding quarter last year; overall occupancy improved to 91.93% from 88.6%
items.quote: Another important development for us has been the increasing share of enterprise businesses. The enterprise clients contributed approximately 70% of our revenue from operations duringQ1 , compared to 52% in the c orresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Building technology-led real estate ecosystem through AI infrastructure launchpad partnering with pan-India media organization; investing in Eezily Networks for broker networks and demand insights; initiating tokenization platform outside I
items.quote: We are building a technology-led real estate ecosystem through our AI infrastructure launchpad where we would be inviting AI and PropTech innovators, that is sta rtups, to develop solutions around operational efficiency, process automation, customer experience, and data-driven decision-making processes.

items.statement: Noida center closed due to litigation towards end of FY26, resulting in revenue dip of INR 4.5 crores from that center; full year FY26 Noida revenue was INR 11.5 crores before closure
items.quote: Now today, while we speak, there's a dip of INR 4.5 crores from the center that has been closed.

items.statement: Capital One asset expected to generate INR 2.75 crores monthly revenue (INR 33 crores annually) at INR 87 per sq ft per month in first year due to rent-free and fit-out periods; full operational year expected at INR 110-125 per sq ft per mo
items.quote: This 1 ,044 that you are referring to, boils down to INR 87 per square feet per month in Ahmedabad. So, the first year that we are calculating right now has certain rent-free periods and fit-out periods. So this is the time that has been pre-leased, from that day when we start the fit-outs typically it takes three to four months of time frame for clients to come in and start paying the rentals.

items.statement: Ahmedabad development management project of approximately 8.6 lakh sq ft requires roughly INR 100 crores fit-out investment for 8,500 seats with potential revenue of INR 120 crores; 1.4 million sq ft planned under development management mod
items.quote: Once the building is ready and handed over to us, we will do investments into the capital towards fit-outs, which would be roughly around INR 100 odd crores, following which our property operations would commence with approximately 8,500 seats and it has a potential to generate revenue of roughly INR 120 odd crores.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced to INR 135 crores from INR 145 crores at end of FY26; net debt INR 81 crores with net debt to equity 0.4x and net debt to EBITDA (IGAAP) 1.04x; INR 100 crore NCD will reflect from Q2, offset by INR 55 crores existing debt
items.quote: At the end of quarter one FY27, our gross debt was INR 135 crores compared to INR 145 crores at the end of FY26. With cash and cash equivalents of INR 54 crores, our net debt was INR 81 crores compared to INR 89 crores at the end of FY26.

items.statement: FY27 guidance: 3.5-4 GW sales, INR 6,000 cr revenue, ~12% EBITDA margin, 6-7% PAT margin
items.quote: So our guidance remains as was given earlier, between 3.5 to 4 gigawatt sales, revenue around INR6,000 crores, with a EBITDA of about 12% and a PAT margin of about 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Phase 1 capex ~INR 1,850 cr (2.4 GW cell + 4 GW module); Phase 2 capex ~INR 1,600-1,700 cr (3.6 GW cell); total ~INR 3,500 cr
items.quote: So the right now the Phase 1 that we have of about 2.4 gigawatt of cell that is approximately and 4 gigawatt of module that is approximately INR 1,850 crores. And the Phase 2 of 3.6 gigawatt of cell would be approximately around INR1,600 to INR1,700 crores.

items.statement: Confirmed order book ~6.35 GW (~INR 8,200 cr), 132% of current 4.8 GW module capacity; 70% utility, 30% C&I/open access; 30% DCR orders
items.quote: Our confirmed order book currently stands at approximately 6.35 gigawatts, representing around 132% of our current operational module capacity of 4.8 gigawatt, and providing strong forward revenue visibility.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 8.33% vs 7.25% Q4 FY26; expect significant improvement in H2 FY27 as cell manufacturing ramps, targeting high-double-digit EBITDA
items.quote: We feel it will be a significant increase in our EBITDA and the bottom-line. Difficult to give a number, but it's going to be in the high-double digits that is what we can say right now.

items.statement: ~30% C&I orders fixed price; utility ~30-40% variable price, rest fixed; selective order execution to protect margins amid high input costs
items.quote: On the module side, I would say, almost 30% which are the C&I are fixed price and on the utility side I would say 30% -- 30%, 40% is variable price and the rest is fixed price.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility (Iran war) driving commodity, freight, forex costs; ALMM-2 delay to Jan 2027; customer wait-and-watch on policy; force majeure extensions
items.quote: The ongoing geopolitical situation and associated supply chain uncertainties continued to influence global markets. Commodity prices remained volatile, logistics costs remained elevated, and foreign currency fluctuations added further variability to the cost environment.

items.statement: Current debt ~INR 1,250 cr; net debt expected to peak at INR 2,200-2,400 cr; debt/equity 0.99; capex funded via balanced capital structure
items.quote: So net debt wait what we are looking at would be at around INR 2,200 crores, approximately INR2,200 crores to INR2,400 crores.

items.statement: Indonesia order of 70,000 units to be supplied over FY27 and FY28
items.quote: And yes, I can only say that the 70,000 orders will certainly be supplied over a period of two years, FY27 and FY28.

items.statement: Around 4,500 government bus orders and 850 e-bus orders on hand for delivery in Q2
items.quote: CV passenger, we still have around 4,500 government orders on hand, which we will continue to deliver during this quarter. As I spoke, there are 850 e-buses orders also on hand.

items.statement: 2.5% net price hike taken on July 1 to offset commodity inflation; confident it will pass through
items.quote: The net price hike in July, we have taken 2.5% increase and very confident that it should pass through as we progress during the quarter.

items.statement: Further commodity cost pressure expected from steel and rubber; will manage via cost actions and price hikes
items.quote: Yes, there is further cost pressure ahead of us in terms of commodities, few of the commodities, steel, rubber, etc. And it is our endeavour, of course, to ensure that the price hike and our own internal cost management actions enable us to tide over this tough commodity challenge.

items.statement: Underlying demand fundamentals strong with robust e-way bills, diesel consumption and FASTag collections correlated to GDP growth
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier, Pramod, I think the underlying demand fundamentals are pretty strong, right? We saw e-way bills, diesel consumption, FASTag collection. I think all the indicators indicate very high movement of goods, which means the underlying freight available is pretty robust.

items.statement: EV volumes grew nearly 3x YoY; SCV EV penetration reached double digits in May and June; over 3,200 SCV EV retails in Q1
items.quote: Therefore, we had more than 3,200 retails on SCV EVs in Q1, which alone is almost four times growth on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Q1 investment spending of ₹515 crore at 2.7% of revenue, within guided 2-4% range
items.quote: Total investment spending in Q1 was ₹515 crore at approximately 2.7% of revenue. This sits comfortably within our guided range of 2% to 4%.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 11.7%, down 60 bps YoY due to commodity inflation; EBIT margin 9.4%, down 20 bps
items.quote: EBITDA was ₹2,300 crore at a margin of 11.7%, down 60 basis points YoY. The moderation is commodity-led.

items.statement: Supply chain constraints in sheet metal, casting, forgings due to broad-based auto demand; debottlenecking actions underway
items.quote: As a result of which, some of the part categories like sheet metal, casting, forgings have become a constraint. To address this, a lot of debottlenecking actions have been taken place, few more in the pipeline.

items.statement: Cell supply from China is a bottleneck for Intra EV production; higher orders placed, supplies expected to debottleneck by end of Q2
items.quote: And the lead time for the demand or lead time for getting the cells in India and converting into batteries is currently pretty high. But I think we have placed higher set of orders already around two months back. So, towards the end of this quarter, I think we should have the supplies completely debottlenecked.

items.statement: Freight Tiger now a subsidiary after acquiring additional 18.1% stake for ₹96 crore in May 2026; total holding 63.6%
items.quote: On Freight Tiger - we acquired an additional 18.1% equity stake in May 2026 for around ₹96 crore, taking our total holding to approximately 63.6%. Freight Tiger is now a subsidiary.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu demand improving month over month, last month very close to normal post-election slowdown
items.quote: Yes, Tamil Nadu has been improving in demand month over month, and especially last month was pretty good, very close to the normal situation as far as Tamil Nadu demand is concerned.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of Rs. 750 crores for FY27 at around 17% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Let me close my remarks by recreating our guidance of Rs. 750 crores in revenue for FY '27 at an EBITDA margin of around 17%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue represents approximately 24% of full-year Rs. 750 crore target, ahead of 45:55 H1:H2 split
items.quote: The 1st Quarter therefore represents approximately 24% of our full-year revenue target of Rs. 750 crores. That is ahead of where the 1st Quarter needs to be, given our guidance that the year splits 45:55 between the two halves.

items.statement: Board approved redeployment of Rs. 101.85 crores IPO funds for 60% stakes in Saicriti Pharma and Prathyak Laboratories
items.quote: The Board has approved a proposed variation in the objects of the IPO issue. In substance, we propose to redeploy Rs. 83.83 crores originally earmarked for the capacity expansion and upgradation of our manufacturing facilities, that is, Unit-1 and Unit-2, and Rs. 18.02 crores originally earmarked for the establishment of new research and development center towards majority stakes in two operating

items.statement: Saicriti Pharma facility at Gummadidala targets April 2027 completion with 154.66 million units injectable capacity
items.quote: This proposed route delivers approximately 154.66 million units of injectable capacity against approximately 105 million units under the original upgradation plan. That is roughly 47% more capacity on a larger and long-lived asset, at an unchanged CAPEX outlet from the company and with the completion extended only about a month to April 2027.

items.statement: Australian facility physical completion targeted January 2027, TGA inspection by March 2027, Phase 1 manufacturing from April 2027
items.quote: Construction is on schedule with physical completion targeted for January 2027. The TGA licensing inspection anticipated by 31st March 2027 and Phase 1 manufacturing expected from April 2027.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin improved to 41.8% in Q1 FY27 from 38.1% in Q4 FY26, a 370 bps expansion
items.quote: Gross margin improved to 41.8% from 38.1% in the preceding quarter, an expansion of 370 basis points.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 14.9% in Q1 FY27 from 14.4% in Q4 FY26 despite lower revenue and elevated air freight costs
items.quote: EBITDA of Rs. 27 crores at a margin of 14.9% and improvement of 50 basis points over the 14.4% recorded in Q4 FY '26. I would emphasize that this improvement was achieved on a lower revenue base, and it was achieved despite absorbing elevated air freight cost in Australia.

items.statement: Contracts have 90-120 day lag for price revisions; raw material cost recovery partial in Q1, full benefit expected in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our contracts carry a window of 90-120 days between a price revision being notified and being realized. That lag is now beginning to unwind in our favor. The recovery of raw material cost increases remain partial at this stage, and we expect full further benefit to flow across the contract book through the 2nd Quarter.

items.statement: Renewed exclusive OTC supply agreement with EBOS Group valued at AUD 202 million (~Rs. 1,300 crore) for 7.5 years with 3-year extension option
items.quote: The agreement as a whole is valued at AUD 202 million, or approximately Rs. 1,300 crore at $1 to Rs. 64.5. The agreement is set in stone exclusively for 7.5 years. That works out to be around about AUD 27 million a year, and there is a further period of 3-year extension by mutual agreement, which would take the agreement out to 2036.

items.statement: EBOS network growing at 5-8% annually with net addition of ~16 pharmacies per year; Noumed expects more large order wins
items.quote: Their standardized growth year-on-year has been running at around about 8%, and what that comes back to is the number of new pharmacies that they bring into their portfolio and chain. So in a stabilized environment over a 12-month period, TerryWhite EBOS would bring on around about, say, 35 pharmacies. They may lose between 12-14 pharmacies, and they would have a net growth of around about 16 phar

items.statement: Prathyak Laboratories brings 150 SKUs across 86 molecules with capabilities in lyophilised, liposomal, nano-based complex injectables and oncology injectables
items.quote: Prathyak operates an established research and development center at the Genome Valley in Hyderabad with 3 years of operating history, 65 personnel including 28 research scientists and a pipeline of 150 SKUs across 86 molecules with proven capability in lyophilised, liposomal and nano-based complex injectables and in oncology injectables.

items.statement: West Asia situation delayed consignments from Indian CMO network to Australia, forcing air freight at elevated cost impacting Q1 margins
items.quote: The situation in West Asia delayed consignments from the Indian contract manufacturing network into our Australian market. This affected the industry as a whole, and we took the decision to move available inventory by air rather than by sea in order to protect our customer commitments. That decision carried a cost.

items.statement: Hyderabad Industrial Lands Transformation Policy prohibits upgradation of Unit-1 and Unit-2 within outer ring road, necessitating relocation
items.quote: Under the Hyderabad Industrial Lands Transformation Policy, which is called as HILTP policy, units situated within the outer ring road may convert that land and relocate outside it and materially for us, upgradations within the outer ring road are no longer permitted. Unit-1 and 2 at Jeedimetla fall squarely within that parameter.

items.statement: Australian facility funding of AUD 53 million complete; company contributing AUD 3.5 million via Singapore subsidiary
items.quote: to complete the Australian facility, AUD 3.5 million (erroneously AUD was not mentioned) is being contributed by the company through its wholly owned Singapore subsidiary and AUD 1.5 million (erroneously AUD was not mentioned) by the existing Australian shareholders which has already been invested. The company infused AUD 1.75 million (erroneously AUD was not mentioned) approximately 6 weeks ago a

items.statement: Board approved incorporation of US subsidiary through Singapore entity to evaluate US market entry at preliminary stage
items.quote: The Board also has approved the incorporation of the subsidiary in the United States to be held as a step-down subsidiary through Sai Parenterals PTE Singapore. The entity is being created to support the company's evaluation of an entry into the United States market. This evaluation is at a preliminary stage and we will make appropriate disclosures as and when there are developments to report.

items.statement: Peak debt year expected in FY27 with de-leveraging from FY28; gross debt-to-equity comfortably at 0.6x
items.quote: FY '27 is expected to be a peak year of debt growth for the existing business as we complete the ongoing CAPEX and Acquisition Program with de-leveraging from FY '28 as these assets begin to contribute to earnings and cash flows. Even at peak debt, the gross debt to equity ratio is comfortably placed at 0.6 times.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25%
items.quote: So this year we will be keeping a same growth trajectory what we have posted last year, around 20% to 25% growth range we will be trying to keep.

items.statement: Current order book of INR100 crores executable in Q2 and partly Q3
items.quote: Yeah, so like I said, the current order book stands at INR100 crores.

items.statement: INR25-30 crores capex for Nashik premix facility redevelopment over 1-1.5 years
items.quote: So overall capex -- so as you are aware that one strategic, there is a demolition happening at our Nashik factory for our premix facility, and it is redeveloping with the new infrastructure, for that we will be incurring a capex roughly around INR25 crores to INR30 crores in the coming one year or maybe one and a half years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 11.3% in Q1 FY27 vs 13.8% in Q1 FY26 due to raw material cost increase
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin stood at 11.3% during the quarter compared with 13.8% in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: MRP increased 10-15% on select branded products to pass through raw material cost
items.quote: Approx 10 % to 15% we have increased our MRP. So that will see a impact in the Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Q2 strongly supported by INR100 crore order book; seasonality drives higher growth in H2
items.quote: No, in fact our Q2 is very strongly supported by a strong order book of around INR100 crores. Okay. So there is definitely no sign of a slowdown in the quarter two.

items.statement: Branded segment at 28% of revenue, targeting 35% in couple of years
items.quote: So in the next couple of years we expect that to go to that 35% mark.

items.statement: West Asia crisis increased critical raw material costs and freight, impacting gross margin
items.quote: The major reason is the West Asia crisis where we have seen few of our critical raw materials in our segments in premix as well as branded has seen a rise in the cost.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 47% blended in Q1 FY27, up from 30% last year
items.quote: So overall, capacity-wise we have seen a volume growth this quarter, which representing around 47% of total capacity utilization at this stage.

items.statement: ESG order pipeline of INR75-100 crores for FY27
items.quote: Right. So we will be looking at around INR75 crores to INR100 crores. For the year. Yeah.

items.statement: Gross margin contracted >3% YoY due to raw material cost rise from West Asia crisis
items.quote: So, if you see the gross margin has contracted by more than 3% compared to last year quarter. The major reason is the West Asia crisis where we have seen few of our critical raw materials in our segments in premix as well as branded has seen a rise in the cost.

items.statement: Volume grew 25-40% YoY in Q1 across premix and branded segments
items.quote: So overall, if you see the volume mix, the volume has grown roughly around 25% to 40% for this quarter.

items.statement: Inventory days at 142 in Q1 FY27 vs 130+ last year due to order book and strategic stocking
items.quote: So inventory days still stands around 142 days as on the Q1. Okay. Varun: Okay. Mr. Soman: Compared to last year, around 130 plus days

items.statement: Field force increased >50% YoY in Q1 for Tier 2/3 expansion; operating leverage expected by Q3
items.quote: We have invested more than 50% in the field force capabilities on the ground. And that has bring impact in our employee expenditure also.

items.statement: 25-30% of raw materials imported; whey protein costs up, vitamins stable
items.quote: So, we have around 25 % to 30% of the raw materials which we are procuring internationally, and major of the raw materials we are procuring domestically.

items.statement: Management prefers not to give detailed revenue or profitability guidance due to structural uncertainties.
items.quote: As management, we would ideally prefer not to give you very detailed guidance on revenue or profitabilit y for the future. This is primarily because there are a few structural uncertainties in our business that we genuinely do not have control over.

items.statement: Expects FY27 EBITDA margin similar to FY25 and FY26 levels.
items.quote: So, if you look at ‘25 and ‘26, I think there would be reasonable guides for, I mean, we should expect very similar numbers in ‘27 for EBITDA as a percentage.

items.statement: Under normal circumstances margins should move a few percentage points, not as dramatically as before.
items.quote: But again, the world has continued to surprise us. So never say never, but under normal circumstances we should expect it to move a few percentage points and not as dramatic as you saw between let's say a Q4 of last year and the Q1 of last year.

items.statement: This year generally looks to be a steady, good year of growth with not too much volatility.
items.quote: At a present point in time, all I can say, sir, is that this year in general looks to be a steady, good year of growth, and with sort of, I would say, reasonably, with not too much volatility.

items.statement: Revenue expected to normalize progressively through the year as order books execute more evenly.
items.quote: We view Q4 as the anomaly, not Q1, and expect revenue to normalize progressively throughout the year as our order books execute on a more even cadence.

items.statement: No large capex planned in regular business; only maintenance capex needed.
items.quote: Within that sphere, we will largely be doing maintenance capex and there isn't any large capex planned. But we are exploring certain new areas of business to get into.

items.statement: Maintenance capex runs 5% to 10% of gross block at any point in time.
items.quote: So, one can say that between 5% to 10% of your gross block at any point in time you can assume is a maintenance capex that you have to keep doing.

items.statement: New technologies and areas being explored could require some capex, not yet materialized.
items.quote: What I would say is for new technologies and new areas that we are looking into, there could be some capex that could be coming up, which at this point in time are not fully materialized, so I cannot really talk too much about them.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization is between 55% and 60%.
items.quote: However, on utilization, I would be I would say we are currently between I would say 55% to 60% utilization. We did a very large capex, that sort of came fully online last year.

items.statement: Operating cash flow is positive and expected to remain positive this year.
items.quote: I think it will be positive sir. It is positive only, sir. Yes, sir.

items.statement: Outdoor and lifestyle brand projections are strong and should drive reasonable growth in that segment.
items.quote: But we -- if I were to say that right now the projections that we have in place with these brands are pretty strong, and should drive reasonable growth within that segment itself.

items.statement: Tariffs would affect business but less badly than last time due to arrangements with customers.
items.quote: So, if it happens, would it affect our business? Absolutely. And I think it's going to affect everyone. But not so badly as its last time because of some things that we put in place.

items.statement: Middle East situation hoped to increase defense spending, a longer-term tailwind.
items.quote: In general, I think we believe and we hope that the, the kerfuffle that's going on in the Middle East should lead to increased defense spending, and that from a longer-term perspective should be a tailwind for us.

items.statement: Stealth, camouflaging and lightweight carbon materials being developed as future growth drivers.
items.quote: All I can say is that in both the area of stealth and camouflaging, as well as lightweight materials that include carbon and its sort of forward goods, we are working on those and we hope that we continue to -- that these, the products that we develop become growth drivers in the future.

items.statement: Finished parachute systems are executed under a licensing agreement with a technology partner.
items.quote: Yes, they are, so it's under a licensing agreement. That's right. With one of our technology partners, sir.

items.statement: Aerospace and defense indigenization, global defense spending, and China plus one are key growth drivers.
items.quote: One is the entire focus on aerospace and defense in India and indigenization therein. If we believe that the aerospace and defense industry will develop supply chains in India, I think that is something that Kusumgar will continue to drive.

items.statement: Cumulative capex to reach approximately $1.2 billion in FY27; capex pipeline of approximately $5 billion through FY31
items.quote: I would like to reiterate that cumulative capex is to reach approximately $1.2 billion in this fiscal year, reflecting the pace of expansion across our port network. Looking further ahead, we have identified a capex pipeline of approximately $5 billion through the financial year 2030-'31.

items.statement: Mumbai Port: additional 64,000 cubic meters liquid storage at ~INR125 crores, commissioning targeted H1 FY27
items.quote: we are developing an additional 64,000 cubic meters of liquid storage at an investment of approximately INR125 crores. And I'm pleased to share that the progress is progressing as per schedule and with commissioning targeted during the first half of this fiscal year.

items.statement: JNPA Port: major expansion of ~318,100 cubic meters liquid storage, 77,236 MT LPG capacity, LPG bottling plant 35,000 MT/year, total capex ~INR1,675 crores; first phase 100,000 cubic meters liquid storage expected Q3 FY27
items.quote: we're executing a major expansion of approximately 318,100 cubic meters of additional liquid storage, 77,236 metric tons of LPG capacity and an LPG bottling plant with 35,000 metric tons of annual capacity with a total capital outlay of roughly INR1,675 crores. The first phase of this liquid storage expansion of approximately 100,000 cubic meters is expected to be commissioned in Q3 of FY '27

items.statement: JNPA Port: Board approved 52,000 MT refrigerated double-walled steel LPG tank
items.quote: the Board of Directors in its recent meeting has approved the development of a 52,000 metric ton refrigerated double-walled steel LPG tank

items.statement: Kochi Port: Board approved additional 49,577 cubic meters liquid storage, commissioning by early next financial year
items.quote: the Board has now approved this expansion and the construction of an additional 49,577 cubic meters of storage capacity at this site. And this new capacity is expected to be commissioned by early in the next financial year.

items.statement: Mangalore Port: LPG rail loading gantry and bottling plant with investment of INR52.5 crores; evaluating further 60,000 cubic meters liquids addition
items.quote: We are developing there an LPG rail loading gantry and bottling plant infrastructure with an investment of INR52.5 crores. This -- and furthermore, we are -- the 75,000 cubic meters of liquid capacity that was added last year is now fully operational with full utilization, bringing the total liquid storage to 193,000 cubic meters of capacity. And I'm pleased to say that we are -- we have secured a

items.statement: Kandla Port: CRL 4 liquid terminal adding 94,148 cubic meters storage, commissioning targeted next year
items.quote: The construction of the CRL 4 liquid terminal, which will add an additional 94,148 cubic meters of storage is progressing well with commissioning targeted for next year.

items.statement: 15-year take-or-pay agreement with leading conglomerate for petroleum products at Pipavav, committed volumes exceed 0.5 million MT/year, operations expected by end of year
items.quote: We are developing an additional liquid rail gantry and have already secured a 15-year take-or-pay agreement with a leading conglomerate for petroleum products. The committed volumes under this agreement exceed 0.5 million metric tons per annum with operations expected to commence by the end of the year.

items.statement: 15-year take-or-pay agreement with Hindustan Zinc for ammonia terminal at Pipavav to service DAP plant
items.quote: we have signed a 15-year take-or-pay agreement with Hindustan Zinc to service its upcoming DAP, that's Di-Ammonium phosphate, plant for part of capacity, providing long-term revenue visibility and a strong foundation for the asset from day 1.

items.statement: Distribution blended EBITDA margin of INR7,000+ per ton considered sustainable for FY27 and beyond, up from INR4,000 pre-FY25
items.quote: we believe the margin of INR7,000 looks sustainable. Of course, in '25, '26, it was driven and we have achieved probably on account of the geopolitics and the uncertainty and the difficulty that has come in this business because we are vertically integrated and we are in the entire value chain, we have been able to deliver this kind of margin, up from INR4,000, which in the past was a standard mar

items.statement: Logistics throughput EBITDA ~INR1,000 per ton; sourcing EBITDA ~$85-90 per ton
items.quote: If you come to LPG EBITDA, it's very standard that the throughput or the logistics volumes that we do delivers close to INR1,000 EBITDA. And then what is left, you divide it by the distribution margin, leave out sourcing, sourcing hardly matters as far as EBITDA is concerned, it is a very low contributor. So then you

items.statement: Logistics volume growth benchmark 25% YoY; potential step-up growth above 25% from enablers (pipelines, VLGC jetty, multimodal evacuation)
items.quote: We believe that year-on-year, we would always clock a worst-case scenario growth in the logistics volume of around 25%. But if these enablers are delivering on account of customers using these enablers, there would probably be a step-up kind of a growth you will see when customers start using these enablers, assuming that normalcy comes up.

items.statement: ITOCHU Corporation acquired 10% stake in Aegis Terminal Pipavav Limited; intends to increase to 25% over next 3 years
items.quote: ITOCHU Corporation, which has acquired a 10% stake in Aegis Terminal Pipavav Limited. And ITOCHU has -- representatives have joined the Board with a long-term -- have come on board, sorry, with a long-term strategic vision and has -- they have expressed their intention to increase their stake over to 25% over the next 3 years.

items.statement: CPG quarterly breakeven targeted in 4-5 quarters
items.quote: In terms of a quarterly breakeven for this business, we are working towards another 4 or 5 quarters. We should have a quarterly breakeven on this business.

items.statement: Jaggery plant commissioning in 6 months in Karnataka, will more than double capacity
items.quote: The plant will be commissioned in 6 months' time. It is coming up in Karnataka. It will more than double our current jaggery capacity.

items.statement: Jaggery turnover expected ~Rs 100 crore from both plants once running
items.quote: In terms of the turnover, once we have both plants running, we should be able to do closer to Rs. 100 crores in terms of turnover, just from both of these plants.

items.statement: Nutra steady-state EBITDA margin 12-15%

items.statement: Targeting INR1,000 crores EPC revenue for FY27
items.quote: We hope to achieve INR1,000 crores on EPC itself this year.

items.statement: EPC order book at INR2,850 crores as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: As of June 30, 2026, our total EPC order book stands at approximately INR2,850 crores, comprising an external EPC order book of INR2,531 crores and an internal order book of INR319 crores.

items.statement: Secured INR295 crores CPWD order for RBI Colony Guwahati and INR126 crores LOI for Wardha hospital
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured a INR295 crores order from CPWD for the construction of the RBI Colony in Guwahati. This further strengthens our presence in large government-led infrastructure projects. In addition, we further strengthened our EPC pipeline with an LOI worth INR126 crores, excluding GST from Maharashtra Public Works Department for the development of a 300 -bedded General Hospital at

items.statement: EPC EBITDA margin at 9% in Q1 FY27 vs 8% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA stood at approximately INR13 crores, translating into an EBITDA margin of around 9% compared to 8% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: EPC gross profit margin remains 13-15% on average
items.quote: at the gross profit level in all our EPC on an average, we are still at between 13% and 15%.

items.statement: Real estate booking value INR66 crores in Q1 FY27 vs INR113 crores full FY26
items.quote: Against a total booking value of INR113 crores achieved in FY26, we recorded INR66 crores of booking value in Q1 FY27 alone.

items.statement: Real estate pipeline ~1.74M sq ft with ~INR2,000 crores sales value (~INR1,000 crores Vascon share)
items.quote: Together with Prakash , these projects represent approximately 1.74 million square feet of salable area with an estimated sales value of around INR2,000 crores, of which approximately INR1,000 crores is attributable to Vascon.

items.statement: Royal Rides Goa project (INR225 crores) stalled with no client go-ahead; assuming no revenue this FY
items.quote: For this financial year, let's just assume there will be no revenue coming. On the conservative side, let's just assume that the next 3 quarters, we don't see revenue from this project.

items.statement: INR80 crores warrant fundraise (25% received) for real estate (60-70%), EPC working capital, corporate purposes over 18 months
items.quote: It's a combination of all 3 for general corporate purposes a little bit, but primarily for real estate and a little bit for the EPC working capital as well. Somnath Biswas: And eventually, that INR80 crores is not an upfront kind of thing. This is a warrant, which is having a time horizon of 18 months to get this money done

items.statement: Real estate long-term ambition INR1,200-1,500 crores annual booking value by FY31
items.quote: We have set ourselves a clear long-term ambition of building towards an annual booking value of INR1,200 crores to INR1,500 crores by FY31.

items.statement: Real estate project gross profit margin 25-30%; pending construction cost ~INR300 crores on INR530 crores balance collections + unsold
items.quote: So see, for us, all the EBITDA on our real estate projects or our gross profit on the real estate projects still continue to remain in the range of about 25% to 30%. So we have about 50% of the balance as construction cost of the balance cash flows, INR300 crores.

items.statement: Net working capital cycle increased from 45 to 65-70 days due to geopolitical/local issues; expected to normalize
items.quote: But over the last 6 months or something more due to some geopolitical instability, local issues and all these things, we are seeing that the net working capital cycle has been increased from 45 days to almost 65 to 70 days.

items.statement: Net debt INR152 crores as of June 30, 2026; INR355 crores unutilized banking limits of INR760 crores total
items.quote: From a balance sheet perspective, net debt stood at approximately INR152 crores as of June 30, 2026. We remain focused on improving liquidity, optimizing our funding structure and enhancing cash flow efficiency as project execution improves.

items.statement: Order book reached a historic high of INR 194 billion (INR 19,400 crores), almost $1.8 billion, over four times the revenue base, with 66% EPC and 34% O&M, evenly balanced between India and international markets.
items.quote: Our order book position reached a historic high of INR 194 billion, that is INR 19,400 crores, almost $1.8 billion, which is over four times of our revenue base, providing very strong visibility for execution over the coming quarters and years.

items.statement: Q1 order intake was over INR 34 billion (INR 3,400 crores), with INR 29.6 billion EPC and INR 4.7 billion O&M; 77% from international markets and 23% from India.
items.quote: Our order intake during Q1 was over INR 34 billion, over INR 3,400 crores, of which about INR 29.6 billion was EPC and INR 4.7 billion was O&M.

items.statement: Management expects net working capital days to stay in the 100-110 days range over the next few years despite top-line growth, with an endeavor to bring it down further.
items.quote: Yes, considering the growth that we are expecting over the next few years, we have always said that if we stay in the 100 days to 110 days range, despite the increased top line growth which will require some amount of investment, I think we are fairly doing well.

items.statement: Design-build (DB) projects generally carry better margins than EPC because construction is a pass-through; management aims to increase the DB mix in the order book.
items.quote: So, you are right, the Design , Build project will generally be better in margin because there is no construction. Construction for us is a pass-through. Our idea would remain that to see if we can have more design build orders.

items.statement: MEA pipeline remains healthy across desalination, wastewater treatment, reuse, and industrial water, with increasing focus on ultrapure water for semiconductors, data centers, solar PV manufacturing, sludge management, and resource recovery
items.quote: Looking ahead, our MEA pipeline remains healthy across desalination, wastewater treatment, reuse and industrial water. We are also broadening our portfolio beyond traditional municipal projects with an increased focus on industrial water and O&M alongside emerging segments such as ultrapure for semiconductors, data centers, solar PV manufacturing, sludge management and resource recovery.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia shows no slowdown in tender pipeline or project awards; 2027 declared as Year of Water, with more than half a dozen active inquiries and a good mix of government and private tenders.
items.quote: I don't think there has been any slowdown. We are in touch with the client. So yes, we are seeing newer and newer projects. We are seeing Sharakat, which is one of the main customers for us, they were called SWPC before. They have announced that a series of projects that are going to come out.

items.statement: Geopolitical events in the Middle East have had no material impact on projects, operations, or demand; projects are far from strike zones, social in nature, and generally insulated, with force majeure clauses and contractual letters issued
items.quote: I want to reiterate that the projects in the Middle East are far away from any of these strike zones. We don't do any of the sanctioned work. All these projects are social in nature, they are water, sustainable, and hence these projects generally remain fairly insulated from any of these issues.

items.statement: Management targets industrial order mix to reach 20-25% over time, driven by traditional oil & gas and emerging sectors like data centers, solar, semiconductors, and green hydrogen, developed through a special initiatives team.
items.period: over a period of three, five, seven years
items.quote: So, we would say over a period of time, our objective will remain to take industrial order mix to be around 20% to 25%. That would be a good mix to have. And the new industries also we are developing through a special initiatives team.

items.statement: Perur desalination project in Chennai crossed a milestone with 1 lakh cubic meters of concreting completed, the highest ever on a single project; critical marine works are complete and the project is progressing steadily towards completion.
items.quote: At our flagship Perur desalination project in Chennai, funded by JICA, we crossed an important construction milestone with 1 lakh cubic meters of concreting completed, the highest ever in our history on a single project.

items.statement: Kodungaiyur project refurbishment is expected to start anytime soon; agreement signed, project report submitted to Project Engineer for evaluation, while O&M continues during the 1.5-year refurbishment phase followed by 18.5 years of full o
items.quote: Kodungaiyur, we have signed the agreement. We also have submitted the project report to the PE. PE is currently evaluating. While the PE is evaluating, we are, of course, still maintaining running the plant. So, the refurbishment phase should start any time now.

items.statement: Other expenses increased due to stricter provisioning policies aligned with higher order book quality; provisions are standard, required by accounting standards, and reversible upon collection.
items.quote: Number two, on the other expenses, as we told you last time as well that we continuously evolve our policies to see that with the increasing quality of our order boo k and the quality of orders that we take in, the policies become more stringent in terms of making provisions for delay or anticipated default

items.statement: International project execution timelines are typically 24-30 months, about six months faster than the 36 months seen in India, due to more defined timelines and funded projects where water is sold on a tariff basis.
items.quote: When it comes to India or outside, it depends on the complexity of the order. But generally, the orders outside India are faster. These are more, I would say, more defined, the timelines. And you see a very good mix of consultants, clients, all pushing us to achieve the project to be faster because these are more funded projects where the water is sold on tariff basis.

items.statement: Company remained net cash positive for the 14th consecutive quarter with a net cash balance (excluding HAM) of INR 965 crores as of Q1 FY27.
items.quote: We continued our net cash positive position for the 14 th consecutive quarter with a net cash balance, excluding HAM standing at INR 965 crores as of this quarter.

items.statement: Forex gains/losses are transactional and part of operational results; they are factored in at the bidding stage and will be seen more frequently as the business becomes increasingly international.
items.quote: You raise an invoice, you collect the money, you get forex gains. You book a cost, you pay the money, you get forex gains or loss. So these a re part and parcel of the business and that is why we are very clear that forex gains or losses are part of our operational results.

items.statement: Entered Kuwait with a landmark 60 MIGD SWRO desalination plant (maiden project) in partnership with HEISCO, and won the third phase of the 60 MLD Ajman Sewage Treatment Plant in UAE as a sewage biorefinery integrating sludge management, dig
items.quote: During the quarter, WABAG secured a landmark 60 MIGD SWRO desalination plant from the Ministry of Electricity Water and Renewable Energy. This is WABAG's maiden project in Kuwait and has represented an important entry into a strategically significant water market in the GCC.

items.statement: Confident of meeting 15% to 20% revenue growth guidance.
items.quote: See we have already guided for a 15% to 20% growth, Shubham, and we are confident of meeting that. And I'm sure you know that our endeavor will always remain to be better than what we promised.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin outlook 13% to 15%, endeavor to grow towards 15%.
items.quote: And that is why in our medium-term outlook, we gave a blended EBITDA margin outlook of staying within 13% to 15% of EBITDA. And there, you have seen in the last three years, we have been consistently performing on that, and our endeavor is to continue growing that more towards 15%.

items.statement: Fair to expect 13% to 14% EBITDA band this year, improving over years.
items.quote: But I would also like to have 15% by the end of this year. But realistically, with the kind of projects we have, it is more fair to expect a 13% to 14% kind of band in this year. And over years, it will certainly improve towards 15% or more depending on the sizes that we are operating.

items.statement: Bid pipeline $2-3 billion Middle East Africa, $1-1.5 billion India.
items.quote: I think as the market is opening up in the Middle East and Africa, we see a strong bid pipeline, but obviously, keeping that around $2 billion to $3 billion. I don't have the number over the top of my head, but I think that's the bidding pipeline that we have.

items.statement: Order backlog multiple beyond 3x, already beyond 4x, confident of maintaining.
items.quote: See we have not given an order inflow target. We have already given an order backlog multiple to be beyond 3x, we are already beyond 4x. And that we are confident of maintaining.

items.statement: Order book INR 19,400 crores all ready for execution or under execution.
items.quote: Today, we decided to prudently remove it. And today, our INR 19,400 crores is all orders which are ready for execution, waiting for effective date or already under execution or O&M, which is waiting for EPC to be complete.

items.statement: Expect order book to be executed over next 36 months.
items.quote: So each of these orders will be in different phases. But broadly, our expectation is that these orders would be executed over the next 36 months.

items.statement: Endeavor to do at least 10% to 20% of revenues from EP on multiyear basis.
items.quote: So, on a multiyear basis, our endeavor would be to at least do 10% to 20%, at least coming out of EP, if not more. In the past, we have even done one-third of our revenues from EP.

items.statement: No slowdown in bid pipeline, good mix including private entities.
items.quote: We have more than half a dozen of inquiries that are actively, we are working on. So I don't see a slowdown in a bid pipeline. So and we are seeing a good mix.

items.statement: Domestic traction returning after many quarters of flood.
items.quote: Yes. On the domestic front, I think we have seen traction now coming after many quarters of flood. You've seen over the last three, four quarters that it has ope ned up whether on the industrial side and now on the municipal side as

items.statement: Minimal impact from Middle East war, confident of managing geopolitical situation.
items.quote: The Middle East war has been on for the last three, four, five quarters, I don't know how long. And you have seen our numbers, we have been delivering. So I don't really see that as an impact.

items.statement: Working capital 3 to 3.5 months, expected to improve with international orders.
items.quote: On working capital, what I mentioned was if you are looking at growth 15% to 20%, especially being in a construction sector, having a 3 to 3.5-month kind of working capital is something that is not abnormal. And that is what is our only growth and the only investment for the growth that is there.

items.statement: No capex required for taking orders, asset-light organization.
items.quote: We are an asset-light organization. There is no capex required for taking orders. And as we have said, we are a modular business.

items.statement: New long-term strategy Wriddhi 2.0 to be presented at Annual Investor Meet for FY27 in May next year.
items.quote: Currently, we are working on the next long-term strategy, which is Wriddhi 2.0. And I'm sure in the Annual Investor Meet when we meet for FY 27 in May next year, we'll be able to present to the investors our strategy for the next five years.

items.statement: New avenues like solar, semiconductor, data centers, green hydrogen expected meaningful over 3-5 years.
items.quote: So I would say look at it more from a three to five year scale over the next 12 to 18 months, I say one or two orders selectively, we like to pick high technology. But over a three to five year period, this is expected to be a more meaningful number.

items.statement: Disbursals planned at INR10,000 crores in H1, INR20,000 crores in H2.
items.quote: Disbursals for the first half are planned at INR10,000 crores. First quarter was bang on target, and that will increase to INR20,000 crores in the second half.

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds to decline to 8.5% by end of year.
items.quote: The incremental cost of fund is now down to about 9%. And we hope to make that further decline to by the end of the year at to 8.5%.

items.statement: Cost of funds to reach 7-8% over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: And as the ratings continue to move up and eventually stabilize, we hope to hit the 7% range, 7%, 7.5%, 8% range over the course of the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Cost-to-income to be around 50% this year, declining from H2 next year, reaching 30-35% by FY29.
items.quote: I would imagine that this year we would be in the 50% type of cost -to-income range. From second half of next year, that will start declining. Hopefully by fiscal 2029, we will come to a 30% to 35% range.

items.quote: And through the second half of this year and financial year '28, we are fairly confident that we will move towards domestic AAA credit ratings and internationally, BB+ type of rating.

items.statement: Recoveries to exceed internal projections for profit.
items.quote: Recoveries, we will exceed the projections that we have made internally, for the profit projections that we have made to all of you. This I can say with 100% of confidence.

items.statement: Disbursements on track to achieve INR10,000 crores in H1.
items.quote: I'm almost in the middle of quarter two and I can confirm to you that disbursements are bang on to achieve the INR10,000 crores of disbursements in the first half.

items.quote: By fiscal 2028, the network would also be ready to be able to physically deliver gold loans, digitally deliver two-wheeler loans, and also integrate with various e-commerce marketplaces to be able to do buy now, pay later type of facilities. items.quote: Similarly, in the years to come, both micro LAP loans and rural home loans will become part of our mainstay in terms of would be amongst the assets which will be contributing about two-thirds to three-fourths of the disbursement.

items.statement: Inorganic growth to be considered from next financial year.
items.quote: Inorganic growth will be on the table from next financial year.

items.statement: No P&L pain expected from security receipts resolution.
items.quote: Fortunately, we already have the buffers in place, we’ve already marked down assets and so on. So, don’t worry, there is no P&L pain which is going to come, but all I’m saying is that the success in resolution, 99%, 95% in a couple of years.

items.quote: However, what we have shared is that we are going to reach our INR 17,500 crores on the five or six pillars, which is on account of the growth of existing businesses in terms of the current volume that the industry is growing.

items.statement: Aiming to maintain margin between 11.5% and 12% for the rest of the year.
items.quote: Last year we delivered about 11.7%, this quarter we are trending at 11.5%, and we are seeing that during the rest of the year, if we can maintain a margin anywhere between 11.5% to 12%, we will be good.

items.statement: Long-term target to deliver 12.5% margin by 2030.
items.quote: I think we are falling in quartile one of our industry, and I think from a margin perspective, we have already given a longer -term target to deliver 12.5% margin by 2030.

items.quote: Yes. So, you know, we have given guidance that during this fiscal year, we intend to spend about INR 400-odd crore in capex across various businesses.

items.statement: Added lifetime order book of approximately INR 2,500 crore during the quarter.
