items.quote: So our Janakpuri center has been growing roughly 30% year-on-year and is still growing. You know, Delhi is such a huge market and it is still growing at 30% year-on-year.

items.statement: Cash and bank balances ₹8.12 crores vs borrowings ₹6.74 crores; debt-to-equity ~0.04x as of 30 June
items.quote: Cash and bank balances as on 30th June stood at ₹8.12 crores against the borrowings of ₹6.74 crores and our consolidated debt-to-equity ratio remains comfortably at approximately 0.04 times.

items.statement: Confident of long-term guidance of Rs. 15,000 crores pre-sales in three years.
items.quote: Amit, we are absolutely confident of our long-term guidance that we have given. We are all aiming towards that.

items.statement: Aiming to do over Rs. 10,000 crores to Rs. 15,000 crores of business development in this financial year.
items.quote: On an annual basis, I have guided you in the range over Rs. 10,000 crores to Rs. 15,000 crores is what we are aiming to do in this financial year.

items.statement: Overall construction cost for the current financial year expected at around Rs. 1,200-Rs. 1,300 crores.
items.quote: Yes, around Rs. 1,200-Rs. 1,300 crores will be the overall construction cost for the current financial year.

items.statement: BD pipeline has term sheets and advanced deals worth more than Rs. 60,000 crores, split across NCR, Mumbai, Pune and Bangalore.
items.quote: We have more than about term sheets and advanced deals worth about more than Rs. 60,000 crores in the pipeline. These are reasonably split between NCR, Mumbai, Pune, and Bangalore.

items.statement: Total residential redevelopment portfolio increased to approximately Rs. 4,300 crores after adding Vashi project.
items.quote: With this addition, our total residential redevelopment portfolio has increased to approximately Rs. 4,300 crores.

items.statement: Redevelopment project margins in the range of about 25%-30%.
items.quote: There ’s no worry for that. We are in the range of about 25%-30%.

items.statement: Vashi project expected margins around 25%-30%, with sales expected at Rs. 38,000-Rs. 40,000 per square foot.
items.quote: Around 25%-30% is what we expect. It is a very high margin, very high, very premium location.

items.statement: Increased prices for Silas Tower-A; Worli premium segment commanding good premiums.
items.quote: We have increased our prices for Silas - Tower-A. Market continues to show strong demand.

items.statement: Niyaara Tower C tentative launch price in the range of about Rs. 100,000 to Rs. 120,000 per square foot.
items.value: Rs. 100,000 to Rs. 120,000 per square foot
items.quote: It is too early to talk about a launch price, but tentatively it will be in the range of about Rs. 100,000 to Rs. 120,000 per square foot.

items.statement: Premium housing demand in Mumbai remains stable, strong and growing in price and volume terms.
items.quote: In Mumbai premium housing demand continues to be very stable, strong, growing, both in price terms and volume terms. So, we are pretty confident that we are betting on the right market.

items.statement: NCR market has some froth; Noida has no land supply and huge demand.
items.quote: I think NCR market has some froth, but it is a combination. If you get the right pricing and the right sizing, as I always mention, backed by a strong brand and good location, I think you can do very well.

items.statement: Planning to commence commercial development at Birla Niyaara with about 1.3 million square feet.
items.quote: First, about 1.3 million square feet. The design is in planning stage, and we are hoping to get the approvals and start commencement before the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Commercial development at Birla Niyaara expected to yield at least about Rs. 800 crores annual leasing when fully stabilized.
items.quote: I think a four -year time is what we are looking at getting into the leasing stage. Given the current market conditions, I thin k it should be at least about Rs. 800 crores annual leasing when it is fully stabilized.

items.statement: Net debt is virtually zero after receiving Rs. 3,325 crores, about 95% of consideration, from ITC deal.
items.quote: We have received Rs. 3,325 crores, which is approximately 95% of the consideration amount. The balance 5% will be subject to certain conditions subsequent, and certain working capital adjustments which are to be reviewed because it takes time for the working capital to be computed.

items.statement: Challenges in business development are right pricing, right location, right title and prudently risk-managed projects.
items.quote: As I have always mentioned, the challenges are the right pricing, right location to get the right product, with the right title and prudently risk-managed projects.

items.statement: Niyaara Tower-1 handover expected by 2027 Q3, within RERA timelines of March 2028.
items.quote: We are within the RERA timelines of March 2028. Hopefully by 2027 Q3, we should be ready to handover.

items.statement: Expect FY27 to close at a better level than previous fiscal
items.quote: Despite the impact of PVC in quarter 1, based on current visibility, we continue to expect FY27 to close at a better level than the previous fiscal.

items.statement: Expect legacy long-term debt fully repaid during FY27 and effectively net debt free by end of FY27
items.quote: We expect our legacy long-term debt to fully be repaid during this year. Before incremental borrowings for new growth projects, we remain on track to become effectively net debt free by the end of FY27.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA expected around INR300 crores, not INR400 crores previously indicated
items.quote: We think our steady-state profit roughly would be somewhere around INR300 crores. But given that, that's a steady state tied up for all the 4 quarters.

items.statement: Announced INR250 crores investment program over 2-3 years for SIOP expansion and captive power at Sahupuram
items.quote: Yesterday, we announced the first step in what we envisage as DCW's next 5-year growth journey, a INR250 crores investment program over the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: SIOP capacity expansion from 30,000 to 45,000 tons per annum; Phase 1 adds 7,000 tons targeted for Q4 FY28 completion
items.quote: The first part is the expansion of our Synthetic Iron Oxide Pigment capacity from approximately 30,000 tons to 45,000 tons per annum. Phase 1 will add 7,000 tons, which is targeted for completion by quarter 4 FY28.

items.statement: Captive power infrastructure investment at Sahupuram targeted for Q4 FY28 completion to lower power costs
items.quote: The second part is an investment in the capt ive power infrastructure at our Sahupuram facility, also targeted for completion in the fourth quarter of FY28, aimed at structurally lowering power costs and improving operating efficiencies acr oss both our Specialty and Basic Chemicals businesses

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals EBITDA grew ~20% YoY; margins dynamic due to PVC-CPVC spread volatility
items.quote: Our Specialty Chemicals EBITDA grew approximately 20% year-on-year.

items.statement: SIOP margins stable around 35-36%; realizations north of INR80,000 per ton
items.quote: I think the margins would be somewhere around 35%, 36% and has been stable ever since we have been communicating that. And that's the way to see. And the prices would be somewhere north of INR80,000 or around INR80,000 a ton

items.statement: Basic Chemicals EBITDA negative INR14 crores in Q1 due to PVC losses; caustic soda saw margin expansion
items.quote: The Basic Chemicals segment reported a negative EBITDA of INR14 crores, primarily due to losses in the PVC business arising from temporary supply chain disruption, elevated VCM prices caused by the West Asia crisis.

items.statement: PVC contribution swing of INR50-55 crores QoQ from profit in Q4 to loss in Q1
items.quote: It's a swing because quarter 4 had a profit. Quarter 4 PVC spread PVC/VCM spread was high. So from that to what impacted the variable cost or the contribution, we estimate that it would be around INR50 crores, INR55 crores.

items.statement: VCM availability improved, supply chains normalizing, import duties reinstated, MIP introduced for suspension-grade PVC
items.quote: VCM availability has improved and supply chain conditions have begun to normalize. Normal import duties have also been reinstated and the government has subsequently introduced a minimum import price framework for suspension-grade PVC.

items.statement: Current PVC prices at $820-860 levels, well above MIP floor of ~INR80/kg; VCM prices corrected significantly
items.quote: Today, the prices are in the vicinity of $820 to $860 levels. And even the domestic prices also have got adjusted to that level. So as we talk now, the prices are much higher than the MIP and MIP is an instrument only to protect the bottom.

items.statement: PVC-CPVC spread currently north of INR25,000 per ton
items.quote: It's difficult to really gauge. But having said that, the spread could be anywhere north of INR25,000 a ton.

items.statement: Domestic demand reasonably resilient supported by infrastructure, housing, water management and manufacturing
items.quote: Domestic demand, however, remained reasonably resilient, supported by infrastructure, housing, water management and manufacturing activity.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals revenue grew 38% YoY to 33% of total revenue; CPVC volumes up 59%, SIOP up 3%
items.quote: Revenue from operations grew 14% year-on-year, led by 38% growth in Specialty Chemicals.

items.statement: West Asia conflict caused VCM supply shortage and price spike; entire VCM requirement imported; no domestic merchant VCM seller
items.quote: It's natural supply shortage because the VCM was usually sourced from the Asian producers who in turn used to buy their crude feedstocks from Middle East. Because of the conflict, the feedstock supply to the Asian suppliers, there was a force majeure, which forced them to curtail their operations, which in turn resulted in lo wer quantities available from our traditional suppliers

items.statement: INR 8,000 crore revenue target by CY30 remains the north star, driven by organic growth (JVD, Volteron) and external acquisitions
items.quote: The INR8,000 crores target, it's not only a target for the complete organization and the management team, but this is the north stars we are following every night to find our way to success.

items.statement: CY25 consolidated revenue may not reach INR 2,000 crore target but should not be far if US entity included
items.quote: I think you will see a significant improvement in the revenue generation. In the second half and I think, okay, we may not be at 2,000, but I think we should not be very far if at all we include the U.S. in that.

items.statement: Consolidated order book stands at INR 4,500 crore as of June 2026; standalone order book is INR 2,200 crore
items.quote: Our order book continues to grow strongly during the quarter. We secured order worth approximately INR1,200 crores. With these wins, our total order book as of June 2026 stands at approximately INR4,500 crores.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline is up to three years
items.quote: So the timeline is up to three years, basically.

items.statement: Advanced Coating facility at Taloja operational since June; trial orders underway
items.quote: It has been put in operation in June. Management: Yes. The facility is now operational. We are doing some of the testing and we have some trial orders, so we will start exploiting that facility as we go forward

items.statement: New workshop in China planned for Q3 CY26 for assembly of special machines and equipment
items.quote: We are now preparing to open a workshop in China in the third quarter for the assembly of special machines and equipment.

items.statement: Profitability affected by early-stage execution of new orders and one-time consolidation costs; expect improvement over medium term as projects progress
items.quote: As the new projects progress and the benefits of these organizational changes start to come through, we expect profitability to improve over the medium term.

items.statement: Strong pipeline for new orders across India, Asia, Europe and USA; order wins expected before year-end
items.quote: The pipeline for new orders is still very interesting. We have a possibility for new orders in different regions that we are active on. That means that we are still very positive on the Asian regions. We are also positive on the European region and we still see quite interesting development also in the U.S.A.

items.statement: JVD technology commercializable; advanced discussions to close first project in Asia this year; Volteron still in R&D phase
items.quote: JVD is already commercializable, and we have very advanced discussion to close one project hopefully this year for JVD in Asia.

items.statement: Potential JVD order size in range of EUR 50-100 million
items.quote: The order that we are looking at is in the range of EUR50 million to EUR100 million.

items.statement: JVD offers significant customer savings vs hot-dip galvanizing: at least INR 1,000 per ton, up to 20x for automotive/advanced high-strength steels
items.quote: So, I would say in terms of savings for the customer, we are talking about cases where it is at least INR1,000 saving and it can go up to 20x this figure based on the case.

items.statement: One-time consolidation costs (transaction, forex, notional interest, legal, audit, compliance) to stop from H2 CY26; parent company agreed to share-based payment instead of cash
items.quote: Fortunately, the parent company has agreed to go for a share-based payment instead of a cash payment. To that extent, many of these costs will actually stop incurring. We will stop incurring from the second half of the year.

items.statement: John Cockerill SA reduced stake from 75% to 70.4% in Q4 CY25; will increase back to 72%+ via preferential share issuance
items.quote: So, they remain a very large shareholder, at almost 70%. And if as you are aware we will be now issuing the preferential shares to them which are convertible and to that extent they will again go back to 72 plus percentage.

items.statement: Top customers: Tata Steel and JSW (standalone); adding ArcelorMittal (consolidated); top five contribute ~80%
items.quote: On the standalone, the top contributors are Tata Steel and JSW and on the consolidated will be adding ArcelorMittal to the top contributors. Management: Yes and that will come to around no, I mean overall it will be 80%, yes around 80% the top five, yes

items.statement: Service revenue significantly lower in Q2 vs Q1 (about one-third) due to project progress timing, not lack of orders; margins remain strong
items.quote: So, the service one I think this quarter was significantly lower than the last time. You know we are talking about maybe around almost one-third of the first quarter and even in terms of the ratio to the total sales, the service values services was lower.

items.statement: B-80 production target of 11,000 bpd by June 2027 with range of 8,900-13,000 bpd
items.quote: In the offshore, in the reservoir, there are always uncertainties. So, when I say 11,000, it could be 8,900 or it could be 13,000. But that's the range that we're looking at on the basis of the technical work that have been done on the reservoir and the pr ospectivity of this reservoir to produce these

items.statement: B-80 workover and drilling campaign requires debt funding; rig award imminent for October mobilization
items.quote: We are in the market to be able to raise funds to deliver that. Again, there could be a challenge if we don't get the funds, but at least some part of it, we are funding from our own accruals.

items.statement: Kharsang gas pipeline route survey tender closes tomorrow; 24 km pipeline to connect to Oil India network
items.quote: So, we have to lay a 24 kilometers pipeline into the Oil India pipeline, which has been -- which has already been laid. That pipeline, 24 kilometers, we have started -- I mean the tender for the route survey will close tomorrow, and then we'll appoint a route survey agency.

items.statement: B-80 crude inventory liquidation expected to incur 7-10% loss on remaining volumes
items.quote: Now how much? I would put my number to around 7% to 10%, but please don't take it as a guidance.

items.statement: B-80 gas realization at $16.5/MMBTU; Dirok gas at $12.5/MMBTU; blended average $12/MMBTU
items.quote: If you, I mean, I hate to make you do this, but if you want the B-80 realization on an average is $16.5 per MMBTU. The Dirok is 12.5. Okay?

items.statement: Dirok production at 50-70% capacity due to evacuation constraints; DNPL pipeline capacity to double to 2.5 MMSCMD by December
items.quote: They are looking at hot tapping to tie back and get back the total capacity to back to 2.5 million standard cubic meters from the current degraded capacity of 1, 1-1.5 MMSCMD.

items.statement: Kharsang production doubled YoY; 5-6 workovers completed on 23 shut-in wells; second 9-well drilling phase imminent
items.quote: We have now, we had 23 additional wells there, we were sat for without production, and we have been working over on them. Five or six workovers have been completed and we are incrementally increasing production.

items.statement: PY-1 new wells contingent on take-or-pay gas agreement with IOCL/GAIL to avoid water-out risk
items.quote: So this time, we are trying to get it right. As far as possible, we'll have a take-or-pay agreement either with GAIL or with IOCL and only then we will spud the wells.

items.statement: Debt raise planned for B-80 program; current gearing 0.04 with INR20 crore bank loan
items.quote: are in the process of raising debt. By the quarter four of by November, December of next year, 2027, our cash flows will be sufficient to fund our growth for B -15

items.statement: B-15 FDP under preparation with 3-4 concepts evaluated; drilling planned for FY28
items.quote: The FDP is under preparation. We are looking at all concepts. We are evaluating three or four concepts at this stage. One of them includes connecting to the existing ONGC's platform to red uce our capital costs. So, all of that is being worked now, and we'll do the drilling in

items.statement: Kharsang virgin gas discovered in two wells; pipeline route survey tender closing tomorrow
items.quote: The problem remains that if we find gas, then we don't have a buyer and in fact, we have found virgin gas in two of the wells in Kharsang. That's a good problem to have, but the only thing is it delays the monetization of reserves because we don't have a pipeline. So we have started a pipeline route survey, as we speak, the tender is out, it will close tomorrow.

items.statement: Cambay assets (Asjol, Balol, Palej) targeting 20-30% production increase; 5-6% already achieved last quarter
items.quote: Then we have also debottlenecked our Palej facility to be able to increase production by using thermionic heaters and those kind of things. So overall, 20% to 30% increase in production we will see going forward, although we have already seen a 5% to 6% increase in the last quarter.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu protests on PY-1 drilling; central government approvals in place, state government engagement ongoing
items.quote: Yes. So look, these fields are all approved by the MOPNG. For as a matter of good practice, we keep the state governments informed. But the final arbiter on the approval to drill, etcetera, is the central government, which we have for the entire field.

items.statement: DNPL pipeline hot tapping completion targeted by December 2026 to restore 2.5 MMSCMD capacity
items.quote: So that gives us a level of confidence. But it could have started a bit early, the tender etc., but floods have made a lot of disruption in Assam as we speak. Things are getting back to normal and in talking to the service providers of the hot tap, they are saying 16 to 20 weeks. Although they are trying to bring it forward now, so we are hoping that in December, the hot taps would be completed an

items.statement: Q1 FY27 standalone revenue INR117.5 crore; net revenue INR107.6 crore after profit petroleum
items.quote: During the current quarter, the company recorded standalone revenues from operations of INR117.5 crores compared with negative of INR194 crores in the previous quarter. After accounting for profit petroleum and revenue share of INR9.83 crores, the net revenue stands at INR107.6.

items.statement: IGL Spirits targets EBITDA in excess of INR500 crores for FY27 and aims to become debt-free from FY28, targeting EBITDA in excess of INR1,000 crores in next four to five years.
items.quote: All of this naturally gives us a very encouraging outlook for FY27 and we expect to deliver an EBITDA in excess of INR500 crores.

items.statement: India Glycols (chemicals) aspires to deliver EBITDA of about INR400 crores and revenue of approximately INR2,500 crores in the next four to five years.
items.quote: The other thing I have some kind of aspirations to share with you, and the aspiration that we are looking at is to deliver an EBITDA of about INR400 crores and a business which is approximately INR2,500 crores in the next four to five years.

items.statement: Ennature Bio Pharma aspires to achieve EBITDA of INR130-150 crores over the next four to five years.
items.quote: In terms of our aspiration for EBITDA, I think over the next four or five years, we are aspiring to do a INR130 crores to INR150 crores EBITDA.

items.statement: NSU (New Strategic Unit) aspires to reach INR150 crores plus revenue this year and INR600-700 crores in four to five years, with gross margins targeting 30% by 2030.
items.quote: We aspire to be INR150 crores plus in this year. And we aspire that in 4 or 5 years, we see this business to be possibly INR600 crores to INR700 crores business.

items.statement: IGL Spirits expects healthy double-digit volume growth next year, aiming to double volumes from FY26's 3.4 million IMFL cases.
items.quote: The outlook for next year, we expect to continue to grow in healthy double digits.

items.statement: Capex for the current year expected to be incremental at INR5-20 crores; no major plant investment seen for next two years unless new technologies require it.
items.quote: So, there may be incremental capex, but we are talking about perhaps INR5 - 10 crores, maybe INR15 crores, INR20 crores based on the plans that we have right now.

items.statement: Thiocolchicoside sales grew 26% quarter-over-quarter supported by a strong order pipeline and improved price realization.
items.quote: Thiocolchicoside sales registered a robust growth of 26% over the prior quarter, previous quarter, supported by a strong order pipeline, improved price realization.

items.statement: IGL Spirits Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 22.9% (up 207 bps); Bio-Fuel EBITDA margin improved to 10.8% (up 250 bps).
items.quote: Spirits business had a net revenue of INR371 crores with an EBITDA margin of about 22.9%, which is an improvement of 207 bps.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 15.0% in Q1 FY27 from 14.3% in Q1 FY26, continuing a multi-year expansion trend.
items.quote: EBITDA margin is 15.0% versus 14.3% in the Q1 last year.

items.statement: Crude price spike reduced bio-based EO cost disadvantage versus Reliance, enabling greater offtake for specialty chemicals and glycols in India.
items.quote: Now, this is something which was not the case 15 years prior to 2021. However, this changed in the recent past and for the few months that I am talking about, we were either similar to Reliance's prices or slightly lower.

items.statement: Raw material availability and pricing for Thiocolchicoside remain volatile and a challenge in Q2.
items.quote: However, the raw material availability and pricing continue to be volatile and a challenge in Q2 as well.

items.statement: IMFL volume grew 55% year-on-year to 1.4 million cases in Q1 FY27; Prestige & Above segment doubled to 0.5 million cases.
items.quote: We have grown 26% year-on-year in terms of net revenue, doing 1.4 million cases, which is a 55% growth over last year.

items.statement: Nicotine sales grew two times quarter-over-quarter driven by customer conversions in Europe; crude processing started at Kashipur adding significant capacity.
items.quote: Nicotine sales grew two times quarter-over-quarter driven by customer conversions in Europe. Nicotine crude processing operations we also started in our Kashipur plant, adding significant capacity.

items.statement: IMFL growth driven by mass premium segment; future focus on Deluxe Whiskey, Semi-Premium Vodka, and White Spirits to improve revenue mix.
items.quote: Going forward in the outlook that I presented to you, I spoke to you about a couple of offerings in the Deluxe Whisky segment. I spoke to you about an offering in the Semi-premium Vodka segment, and I spoke to you about renewed focus on the White Spirits business.

items.statement: War-related freight volatility (5-20x increase) and raw material supply disruptions (propylene oxide) negatively impacted chemicals exports to Middle East and US.
items.quote: Freights for westbound cargos have been very, very volatile, going up anywhere between 5 to 20 times, which impacted some of our businesses.

items.statement: NCLT sanctioned scheme of arrangement on July 17, 2026; demerger will create three entities: India Glycols (chemicals), IGL Spirits (spirits & bio-fuel), Ennature Bio Pharma (nutraceuticals, APIs, biopolymers).
items.quote: NCLT has now sanctioned the scheme of arrangement on 17th of July 2026, and upon effectiveness, the Spirits, Bio-Fuel, and Bio Pharma undertaking transfer to dedicated resulting companies.

items.statement: Confident in ability to outperform the industry, per stated guidance.
items.quote: While global geopolitical developments continue to shape the market dynamics, we remain confident in our ability to deliver on our guidance of outperforming the industry and drive sustained value for all stakeholders.

items.statement: Confident in sustaining year-on-year margin profiles through FY27.
items.quote: The profitability outcomes achieved during the quarter reinforce our confidence in sustaining our y-o-y margin profiles through FY27.

items.statement: Aims for VNB growth outpacing APE growth, implying margin improvement.
items.quote: Going forward, we remain focused on delivering VNB growth that outpaces APE growth while maintaining disciplined execution and profitability.

items.statement: VNB margin rose to 23.2% in Q1 FY27 from 20.3% in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Consequently, our VNB margin expanded from 20.3% in Q1 of FY26 to 23.2% in Q1 FY27, driving a robust 33% growth in the value of new business or VNB.

items.statement: About 30% of margin increase from protection mix and operating leverage, 70% from yield curve.
items.quote: Now, in this 3% approximate increase, you can say 30% is linked to mix around protection and some bit of operating leverage and around 70%, you can say is the yield curve, which actually has also helped offset the GST impact.

items.statement: GST effect largely behind; no other GST effect to worry about.
items.quote: Now that is largely behind us. From a GST perspective, there is not any other effect we have to worry about.

items.statement: QIP enabling approval valid until May next year, to support growth capital requirements.
items.quote: The approval of the, enabling approval of QIP at MFSL was taken as an enabling approval and which is valid until May of next year. And t hat was largely to support the growth requirements of the company.

items.statement: Can stay above internal risk threshold for at least two to three quarters comfortably.
items.quote: And I think we can stay above the risk threshold for at least two to three quarters quite comfortably as we see it.

items.statement: Internal solvency risk threshold hovers around plus/minus 180% few percentage.
items.quote: That number hovers anywhere between plus minus 180% few percentage.

items.statement: Will recoup and re-raise sub-debt amount plus additional Axis infusion capacity.
items.quote: We will recoup and re-raise both that amount and also the amount that we got from an additional capacity of the Axis infusion that happened in the first quarter. Yes, we will be doing a sub-debt raise.

items.statement: If RBC framework delayed, QIP may eventually be done to support growth.
items.quote: Look, if RBC does not come on time, as we had indicated in the past as well, then your assumption is correct. But if there is a development which happens on that framework, maybe the number may go up.

items.statement: June yield curve moved lower, could take away some Q1 yield benefits.
items.quote: Your observation is correct. You are saying that at the end of the June, the curve has moved, which could take away not the entire, but some benefits that were available in the first quarter from a yield curve perspective.

items.statement: Hopes non-par de-growth moderates toward green as quarters progress.
items.quote: We do hope to get the trends even on the non-par to at least no longer be in such sharp de -growth. It should move towards more in the green as the quarter’s progress.

items.statement: Protection, annuity segments remain focus areas to tap India opportunity.
items.quote: But more importantly, I think the segments of choices, protection, annuity is where we continue to remain focused and we are keen that those trends hold and we are able to tap onto that opportunity that India presents with respect to those products.

items.statement: Commission regulation consultative process awaited; will welcome consumer-good regulations.
items.quote: And we will welcome those regulations, and it is a great initiative by the regulators and they will want to follow a very long drawn consultative process here, at least what we are picking up from the media news articles as well.

items.statement: Structure simplification scheme NCLT process takes 6 to 12 months once filed.
items.quote: Sir, we had always indicated that the moment we file a scheme document, given it is an NCLT process, will take anywhere between 6 to 12 months. Those timelines hold.

items.statement: Order book stands at approximately INR5,100 crores with only INR1,251 crores from legacy projects and the balance carrying expected operating margins of 10% or higher
items.quote: Our order book today stands at approximately INR5,100 crores, providing healthy medium-term revenue visibility. More importantly, the quality of order book continues to improve significantly, only around INR1,251 crores order related to legacy projects, while the balance consists predominantly of projects carrying expected operating margins of 10% or higher.

items.statement: Company targets order intake of more than INR5,000 crores in FY27, with INR1,293 crores already booked in Q1 and INR212 crores as L1
items.quote: The company is hopeful of surpassing its guidance of more than INR5,000 crores in order intake in the current financial year, against which we have taken INR1,293 crores order in Q1 and are L1 in INR 212 crores of orders.

items.statement: BESS manufacturing facility expansion from 2.5 GW to 5 GW with 600 container units capacity to be completed in H1 FY28, total capex INR236 crores fully financed
items.quote: We expect the capacity enhancement from 2.5 gigawatt to 5 gigawatt along with the container facility expansion to be completed in the first half of FY 2028, along with the order for the associate facility, which addresses a market potential of 208 gigawatt by 2030.

items.statement: BESS manufacturing facility at Supa MIDC Pune has 2.5 GW assembly line ready, targeting NTPC container supply in Q4 FY27 subject to approvals
items.quote: The first phase of our 2.5 gigawatt assembly line is fully ready. The company has also started obtaining various certification from IEC/UL for its battery pack, which are required for supplying the container to NTPC against its current order. And we are targeting to build the NTPC in Q4, subject to requisite approvals.

items.statement: Pipeline of 134 upcoming projects worth INR98,725 crores across 11 states tracked, with irrigation and water supply making up over 80%
items.quote: On the water and power front, we track a pipeline of about 134 upcoming projects, worth close to INR98,725 crores across 11 states, with irrigation and water supply making up over 80% of this value, reinforcing water infrastructure as the biggest growth driver in the public capex cycle.

items.statement: Strategy to not take orders below 10% EBITDA margin; recent orders Konar, Kekri and Indore all above 10% margin
items.quote: As we explained into our previous con-call that as a strategy, at this moment, we don't take any order less than 10%. So it is always more than 10%. Like at the moment, the 3 orders which we have taken, Konar, Kekri and Indore; all are more than 10%.

items.statement: India growth rates may be less attractive than Q1 but company will continue to grow.

items.statement: Demand=Match expected to be embedded in all products all over the world in another year.

items.quote: This year. Yeah, this year we will have it globally, yes.

items.statement: Margins expected to continue to improve barring unforeseen tariff shocks; 25% tariff absorbed effectively.

items.quote: Kilburn Engineering and M.E. Energy are expanding the manufacturing and execution capabilities, which are at advanced stage and expected to complete by end October this year.

items.quote: For us, maintaining a 20% operating margin in a quarter with lower revenue is significant. It reflects the great discipline we have brought into the project execution.

items.statement: FY28 revenue growth 15-20%, EBITDA margin 15-17%.
items.quote: Definitely, we have a plan to grow about 15% to 20% in top line and EBITDA to 15% to 17% in '28 approximately.

items.statement: Pricing actions initiated in market, will take time to fructify and have impact.
items.quote: The pricing actions in the market has been initiated. It will take some time to really fructify and have an impact.

items.statement: Underlying demand environment and opportunity pipeline healthy; forward-looking 3 quarters good.
items.quote: And what we see is the underlying demand environment and opportunity pipe is healthy for us. The pricing actions in the market has been initiated. It will take some time to really fructify and have an impact. What I can see is that we are seeing the forwar d-looking 3 quarters, including the one which half of which has gone by is good for us.

items.statement: More than 1/5 of order bank from new emerging segments like data centers and semiconductors.
items.quote: I can -- what I can state here at this point is more than 1/5 of what is coming is on this new emerging segment is what we hold in our order bank.

items.statement: Emerging segments coming with higher scope including installation and commissioning, longer gestation execution period.
items.quote: Yes. So -- not big mix change, but the one change is what is happening that emerging segments is coming with the higher scope, including installation and commissioning. So from supply, we are also getting into the larger the project execution cycle, where the mix is changing in terms of not supply, it's also coming with a more longer gestation in execution period, including installation and commis

items.statement: Capex of roughly INR 500 crores taken in last 3 years across 3 plants to enhance capacities and cut imports.
items.quote: We have typically -- in the last 3 years, if I may so, we have we have actually taken on a capex of roughly about INR500 crores in our 3 plants, which we have.

items.statement: Multiple capex programs in Baroda medium voltage and transformer factories and new Kolkata plant with staggered completion timelines; some completing in calendar year 2027, a few by 2028.
items.quote: And there are multiple capsules which we have actually embarked on in terms of capex infusion, and they have a staggered completion time lines and a ramp-up plan. What Mr. Omkar was saying that all of them -- all those programs are being tracked by the management, and they are well on track as we see today, and we don't see any hiccups coming on the way of their completion.

items.statement: Rupee depreciated about 8% since start of year; commodity prices of copper, aluminum, steel and labor going up.
items.quote: At the same time, there are certain headwinds, which all of us are facing and so is our company is also facing is the devaluation of rupee, which has gone down. And also it's about 8% is where the rupee has depreciated since the time we started this year.

items.statement: Imports 10% to 15% of COGS, naturally hedged by exports in same range.
items.quote: This will be in the range of 10% to 15%, not more than that.

items.statement: Export revenue currently 10% to 12% of revenue; Kolkata capex largely to cater export market, still at ramp-up stage.
items.quote: Today, our export revenue is in the range of 10% to 12% in the revenue. And you know that the capex we invested in Kolkata largely will cater the export market, which is just starting, okay?

items.statement: Set growth target of roughly 10%, with foreign expected to grow more than domestic.
items.quote: In terms of growth, we have set a target of roughly about 10%. It varies for domestic and foreign. In foreign, we would expect a more pronounced growth than the domestic market.

items.statement: Target combined ratio for domestic book at 103 and foreign book at 95.
items.quote: And we would like to have combined ratio target for domestic book at something like 103 and the foreign book at 95 in line with the global markets.

items.statement: Foreign combined ratio target of 95 expected in 2 to 3 years.
items.quote: Timeline, I think we are fairly close to 103. 95, again, we feel that probably in a span of 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Medium-term target of 60/40 domestic versus international mix; 50/50 is long-term.
items.quote: So 50/50 is absolutely long -term goal. What we are presently targeting with a medium -term in view is 60/40.

items.statement: Foreign portfolio expected to increase significantly, but no number given.
items.quote: We expect the foreign portfolio to increase significan tly. At this stage, we would refrain from putting a number to it.

items.statement: Credit rating upgrade to A expected in 4 to 5 years if things go right.
items.quote: It is not really possible to give any timeline, but if things go all right, probably one can expect in a period of, say, something like 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: GIC's losses from cat events tend to be around 30% to 40% of market losses.
items.quote: In terms of our experience, it has been our stance that whatever might be the market losses, our losses from cat events tend to be around 30% to 40%.

items.statement: Competitive behavior may continue as GIFT City players scale up; flood losses could influence behavior.
items.quote: We believe that to the extent the players in the GIFT City will try to scale up their operations, their competitive behavior may continue. But as you also pointed out that there are flood losses.

items.statement: IRDAI directive on property rates is guidance; impact to be seen over next 2 to 3 quarters.
items.quote: It is only a guidance, so let us see how the impact will be over next 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: Focus on growing non-obligatory book and retail health over corporate or group health.
items.quote: As far as health is concerned, our focus is more on the retail health segment rather than the corporate or group health segment, where we believe the profitability lies.

items.statement: Life portfolio has around 20% market share and will grow, backed by actuarial analysis.
items.quote: Our book in life has been fairly stable at around a 20% market share. Now that we are going to focus, it will grow.

items.statement: Domestic market share to be maintained despite competitive pressure; foreign business to be regained after rating upgrade.
items.quote: Our stand remains what we have earlier advised that in domestic market, despite the competitive pressure, our goal will be to maintain our market share. On foreign side, to the extent we have got our rating back, and we are in touch with all the cedents and markets where we lost our business, which we had prior to rating downgrade.

items.statement: Solvency ratio at 4.32 as of June 30, 2026, up from 3.85 a year ago.
items.quote: Solvency ratio improved to 4.32 as on June 30, 2026, as compared to 3.85 as on June 30, 2025.

items.statement: Investment book market value INR157,000 crores; equity around INR58,000 crores.
items.quote: Market value as told is INR157,800 crores. That includes only equity, which is around INR58,000 crores, because debt is kept at cost only in ours as it is held to maturity.

items.statement: Subsidiary losses: South Africa INR287 crores, Moscow INR29 crores in Q1.
items.quote: If you want to know subsidiary company -wise, South Africa, we have shown INR287 crores loss during this quarter, and Moscow some INR29 crores loss from the subsidiary.

items.statement: Confident of fully recovering steel price increases, with margin neutralization in coming quarters.
items.quote: So we are confident on the steel price increase particularly. We will be able to recover fully and you will see the margin neutralization will happen in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Guidance to grow EBIT margin in double digit, continuing after price recovery.
items.quote: Maybe like we have given guidance, we will be able to grow EBIT margin in the double digit. And post the price recovery, we are confident that double digit margin improvement will keep happening in the future also.

items.statement: Steel price increases including Q1 will be fully recovered.
items.quote: Yes, that assumption is right. For steel prices particularly, inc luding Q1, we will be able to recover fully.

items.statement: In discussions with OEMs to recover non-steel inflation like fuel and freight.
items.quote: So as of now, we are in the verge of discussions with all the OEMs to recover, which is a non-steel inflation, which is basically fuel freight etc.

items.statement: Already infused Rs.250 crores; another Rs.250 crores infusion anticipated in Q3.
items.quote: we have already infused Rs.250 crores in the last quarter, maybe basically Q4 of the last financial year and we anticipate maybe in Q3, we will infuse another Rs.250 Crores.

items.statement: Total guidance of about Rs.750 crores infusion over a period of time.
items.quote: We are given a guidance of total put together about Rs.750 Crores infusion will happen over a period of time. So, second tranche of that will happen in Q3.

items.statement: TI planning around Rs.350 crores capex for current financial year; Shanthi Gears around Rs.100 crores.
items.quote: In TI, we are planning around Rs.350 Crores of Capex for the current financial year. And Shant hi Gear will be around Rs.100 Crores.

items.statement: Group capex excluding CG Power around Rs.600-700 crores.
items.quote: And if you take group as a whole, if you see something like 600 to 700 Crores.

items.statement: Next one or two quarters expected to be bullish; exports momentum expected to continue.
items.quote: but at least for the next one or two quarters, we feel it is going to be bullish. And exports also has done pretty well in particularly quart er one.

items.statement: TI Medical confident of 20% revenue growth year-on-year with profitability.
items.quote: Overall basis for TI Medical, as we said in the previous calls, we are confident to do 20% revenue growth year-on-year along with the profitability.

items.statement: Cycle business targeting at least 2 basis points margin improvement for the year.
items.quote: So we are hopeful, like we shared maybe at least another 2 basis point in the cycle business, we will be able to improve margin for overall year in the current financial year.

items.statement: Cell availability and prices a challenge for at least two to three quarters.
items.quote: Yes, it is a genuine challenge which we are grappling with and has been one of the challenge for us in quarter one and going forward at least for two, three quarters, we see this as a challenge

items.statement: One EV business expected to breakeven this year, two next financial year.
items.quote: We are expecting one of our business es to breakeven this year and may be two of them to break even next financial year.

items.statement: CDMO 200 KL intermediate capacity commissioned; inspection expected next financial year.
items.quote: So the 200K intermediate capacity, the commissioning has already happened. The validation batches are going on.

items.statement: TI Clean Mobility CCPS conversion only at IPO; no fixed timeline.
items.quote: The conversion happens only at the time of IPO. IPO, we have a time and there is no fixed timeline for this.

items.statement: Exports about 14% of revenue at TI level.
items.quote: At a TI level, it is about 14%.

items.statement: Maintains volume guidance at 6% to 8% for full-year FY26-27.
items.quote: As regards to our guidance for the full year, we maintain our volume guidance at 6% to 8% for the full -year FY26 -27, but I, however, increased the range of the EBITDA per metric ton guidance from the current INR 19,000 to INR 21,000 per metric ton to INR 24,000 to INR 25,000 per metric ton.

items.statement: Capex for this year will be about INR 150 crores.
items.quote: We talked about capex guidance. So I think this year, we will be at about an additional listing of about INR 150 crores.

items.statement: Expects demand to remain healthy through coming quarters due to festive season and improving momentum.
items.quote: As we look ahead, demand indicators remain encouraging across many of our key markets. With the upcoming festive season in India and improving momentum across several international markets, we expect demand to remain healthy through the coming quarters.

items.statement: Remains watchful of West Asia developments impacting feedstock availability, freight, and supply chains.
items.quote: At the same time, we remain watchful of developments in West Asia and their potential impact on feedstock availability, freight markets and global supply chains.

items.statement: Specialty Care mix improved, contributing to higher EBITDA per metric ton.
items.quote: Specialty Care mix has improved, contributing positively to growth in EBITDA per metric ton, moving us steadily towards objective of improving the quality of our earnings through a richer and more differentiated product mix.

items.statement: No pressure on pricing; transparent engagement with customers on price increases.
items.quote: No. I would not say there's any pressure on pricing because one of the things that the way that we engage with the customers on any pricing discussions is being transparent.

items.statement: Order book position looks better from demand scenario.
items.quote: And the way things are and our order book position, we do see things are looking better from a demand scenario.

items.statement: EPC project in Mexico on track for commercialization over next 12 months.
items.quote: The project continues to progress as planned, contributing EPC service income during the quarter, and we remain on track for commercialization over the next 12 months.

items.statement: EPC service income recognition to be completed by end of this financial year.
items.quote: And this is going to be completed this year. And I think we will have the recognition completed by end of this financial year.

items.statement: New products expected to contribute >5% of total revenue by 2030.
items.quote: And we do look at all new products, -- this thing is by 2030, they should contribute to almost greater than 5% of our total revenue and our contribution margins.

items.statement: Inorganic growth in Beauty and Wellness; may announce in coming months.
items.quote: A lot of work has happened, but we have not been able to come up with any announcement. But it is suffice to say that a huge amount of work is happening. I do hope that we will be able to come up with something in the coming months.

items.statement: No acquisition planned in AMET; only debottlenecking investments.
items.quote: See, AMET market very clearly, we have already done our capex. We obviously will be -- any capexes that we'll be doing there will be more in terms of certain debottlenecking exercises we'll do investments. There is no acquisition we are planning in AMET for sure.

items.statement: No change in strategy to grow both performance and specialty businesses.
items.quote: So, first of all, I'd like to clarify there is no -- strategy to transition from performance to specialty. Our strategy is very clear that we have to grow both the legs of our business performance and specialty ingredients.

items.statement: Management aims to sustain double-digit revenue growth on average over the long term
items.quote: we have been saying for the past few investor calls that what we have been aiming at to sustain a double-digit growth

items.statement: Company remains asset-light; no major capex plans disclosed
items.quote: We also took a decision to remain an asset-light company

items.statement: EPR certificate exchange platform developed and ready; awaiting government notification to operationalize
items.quote: Developing a trade receivables discounting system, a treads platform has also been taken up as one of the areas showing commercial viability

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 69.05% in Q1 FY27; management expects margins to remain around current levels but may face pressure at higher volumes
items.quote: EBITDA percentage of total income was 69.05%, also nearly 3% higher than the corresponding period of FY26

items.statement: Revenue models vary: transaction-fee based for some products, event-based for others, plus software development charges
items.quote: For certain products, it is the percentage of the transaction done and for certain things, it is based on the events only

items.statement: Mineral block auctions and critical minerals driving growth; scrap sales cyclical but historically 50-55% of e-commerce revenue
items.quote: Regarding the 20% growth that you have seen compared to the last year's Quarter 1, it is mainly due to the higher number of the mineral blocks and the minerals that we are selling

items.statement: New verticals: EPR certificate exchange, TReDS platform, travel portal (B2B live, B2C pending IATA), coal/mineral exchanges exploration
items.quote: We have simultaneously looked to identify suitable opportunities which can be capitalized on by leveraging MSTC's domain expertise developed over the last 23 plus years through e-commerce application development

items.statement: JV with Mahindra (MMRPL) turned profitable in Q1; outlook positive due to EPR norms and OEM incentives
items.quote: For the first time in quite a few number of sequential reporting periods, the venture has shown a positive PAT

items.statement: Dividend policy guided by DIPAM: minimum 4% of net worth or 30% of PAT, whichever is higher
items.quote: Minimum that is 4% of the net worth or 30% of the PAT, whichever is higher. It is the minimum dividend that a government company has to declare

items.statement: TReDS platform at advanced stage; targeting operationalization in FY27 subject to RBI approval
items.quote: subject to regulatory approvals being obtained, we should be able to operationalize this sometime during this FY27

items.statement: Travel portal B2B operational for internal/PSU use; B2C rollout pending IATA empanelment
items.quote: The travel portal is ready. As of now we are booking tickets for our own corporate travel and we have approached other sister PSUs for using this portal

items.statement: Exploring setting up own coal/mineral exchanges; initial stakeholder discussions underway
items.quote: MSTC is also exploring various possibilities and the ways and methodologies for establishing its own exchanges

items.statement: Exited trading/marketing segment (110% BG model) completely in Q1 FY27; now single-segment e-commerce company
items.quote: We had taken a decision in FY26 to completely exit from the trading and marketing segment and have seamlessly recovered our dues on the 110% BG model, closing the chapter on this legacy segment in this quarter

items.statement: Reiterated consolidated revenue CAGR of 70-75% over FY25-FY28, EBITDA CAGR 40-45%, PAT CAGR 35-40%, with EBITDA margins stabilizing at 12-13% and PAT margins at 5-6% by FY28.
items.quote: We reiterate our earlier guidance of approximately 70% to 75% consolidated revenue CAGR over FY25 to FY28, supported by the phased commissioning and ramp-up of Bokaro, alongside continued strategic organic growth across our existing verticals.

items.statement: Refrained from giving specific FY27 guidance; color-coated segment commissioning in Q2 FY27, ramping over next 6 quarters to FY28.
items.quote: I cannot -- I mean, we have not commented individually on the FY27 numbers, and so I would refrain from doing that. The guidance remains on track for FY28.

items.statement: Bokaro project capital deployed INR341.6 crores, including INR139.2 crores internal accruals; color-coated line hot trials ongoing, to be capitalized in Q2 FY27.
items.value: INR341.6 crores total deployed; INR139.2 crores internal accruals
items.quote: Importantly, healthy and consistent operating cash flows enabled us to deploy INR139.2 crores of internal accruals towards the expansion, taking total capital deployed to INR341.6 crores.

items.statement: Bokaro 150,000 tons line expected to take 3-4 quarters to ramp up fully; cold rolling and Galvalume lines to follow.
items.quote: This is a 1,50,000 tons line. And I would guess it will take us at least three to four quarters to ramp it up all the way.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin expanded 536 bps YoY to 67.9%; EBITDA margin contracted to 20.3% from 21.2% due to sharp fuel price increase from Middle East conflict.
items.quote: Gross profit was INR112.7 crores with a gross profit margin expanding by 536 basis points year-on-year to 67.9%.

items.statement: Initiated discussions with customers to incorporate gas prices into price variation mechanisms to mitigate future fuel cost volatility.
items.quote: Given the volatility witnessed during the quarter, we have also initiated discussions with our customers to incorporate gas pri ces into our price variation mechanisms

items.statement: Steel consumption growing 10%+ vs ~7% GDP; strong government infra spend and private investment; East region demand from rural housing, warehousing, industrial buildings; antidumping, QCO, PLI support color-coated demand.
items.quote: For the first time in a very long time, we are seeing a higher than GDP increase in steel consumption. So if we look at our GDP growth at about 7%, 7.2%, you add about 3% to 4% of inflation, you're looking at about a 10% odd, 11% odd real growth.

items.statement: Bokaro will offer full basket of coated products: Galvalume, Galvanized, ZAM; ZAM encouraged by MNRE for rooftop solar; pre-galvanized pipes and PEB structures growing.
items.quote: We will be in a position to offer all three products in the top range or whatever is available in the country. So I do feel that this will create a fair bit of stickiness for our products.

items.statement: Rolling mill utilization ~83.5% annualized; pipes & tubes ~40.1% annualized with production increasing sequentially; expect further utilization improvement.
items.quote: The rolling mill business achieved an annualized capacity utilization of approximately 83.5%, reflecting healthy demand and stronger volume absorption.

items.statement: Fuel price volatility from Middle East conflict impacted EBITDA margin; mitigating via gas price pass-through mechanisms with customers.
items.quote: While gross profit margins improved meaningfully, the operating EBITDA margin contracted due to a sharp increase in fuel prices arising from the conflict in the Middle East.

items.statement: Net debt INR468.9 crores, net debt-to-equity 0.57x; INR202.4 crores long-term borrowings for Bokaro; ROCE 9.5%, ROE 9.4% annualized (transitory due to greenfield capital deployment).
items.quote: Net debt stood at INR468.9 crores at a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.57x, of which INR202.4 crores represents long-term borrowings drawn for the Bokaro project.

items.statement: Pipes & tubes stable-state utilization target 65-70% by FY29; current Q1 annualized 40.1% up from ~34% in FY26.
items.quote: My personal under belief is that in pipes and tubes, stable state utilization of 65% to 70% is at best possible. And that's what we hope to achieve in a stable state by, let's say, FY '29 odd.

items.statement: No exports planned currently; focus domestic; UK FTA not a priority.
items.quote: No exports planned for now Bhavesh, but again, I will refrain from commenting on Q2. Let's focus this call on Q1.

items.statement: Quality certifications (ISO 9001, 14001, 45001, 17025, IATF 16949) to be applied after Bokaro plant commissioned, stabilized.
items.quote: So it's too early because we are still in the project stage. It's very early to appl y for any certifications. These will only be done once the plant is commissioned and up and running and

items.statement: Aspirational FY30 revenue target INR4,000-4,500 crores from Bokaro plus legacy ~INR650-700 crores; capital allocation priority remains expansion over buybacks/dividends.
items.quote: So, that is now you see -- so, you know, of course, when you talk about FY '30 and all, it's not unfair to say that, that's something which we will be aspiring to achieve. And it is possible.

items.statement: Board approved INR 425 crore capex for new brownfield tower at Max Vaishali adding 202 beds.
items.quote: To further strengthen our existing Network, the board has approved a cap ital expenditure of INR 425 crore for a new brownfield tower at Max Vaishali. This will add 202 beds to the hospital's existing capacity of 387 beds.

items.statement: Max Smart remaining 50% of 400-bed brownfield tower to be handed to operations this quarter.
items.quote: At Max Smart, we have currently operationalized 50% capacity of the 400 -bed brownfield tower. The remaining 50% beds are expected to be handed over to operations during the course of the current quarter.

items.statement: Nanavati Max remaining 50 beds to be operationalized this quarter; Phase 2 expansion work commenced.
items.quote: At Nanavati Max, remaining 50 beds will also be operationalized in this quarter and work on the Phase 2 expansion has commenced.

items.statement: Kalinga hospital turnaround targeted over next 12 months via integration, renovation, technology and clinical upgrades.
items.quote: Going forward, our focus is on integrating operations, renovating infrastructure, upgrading technology, and enhancing clinical programs to turn around the hospital over the next 12 months.

items.statement: Oncology to start normalizing from Q3, fully normalized from Q4.
items.quote: So, one is that oncology will start to normalize from Q3 onwards. Since mid of Q3 FY26 is when we took this action of not supplying / using the ORC drugs for the institutional patients, after the new MOU was signed in October 2025.

items.statement: 6% automatic price revision agreed with insurance companies is going to happen.
items.quote: So, last time when we had this stalemate with the insurance companies, we had agreed a 6% automatic price revision and that is what is going to happen.

items.statement: Ongoing negotiations with GIPSA and other insurers; hopes for price increase in insurance segment.
items.quote: Yes, so there are on -going negotiations with GIPSA and some other insurance companies. Also, the insurance companies that we had discussion with last time, are up for renewal in September-October. So, we hope we will get some price increase going forward in the insurance segment.

items.statement: Medical college for 150 seats needs around INR 300 crore spend, to be funded through internal accruals.
items.quote: Now, we have done some back-of-the-envelope calculations and our take is that for a 150-seat medical college, you need around INR 300 crore of spend.

items.statement: Medical education business expected to deliver more than 25% to 30% ROCE.
items.quote: We are seeing a more than 25% to 30% ROCE at present and we intend to do this at scale.

items.statement: Medical colleges commercial operations to start over the next few years, funded entirely through internal accruals.
items.quote: I think you will see starting of commercial operations of medical colleges over the next few years. We would obviously be open to doing any meaningful acquisition if it is available to kick-start our process sooner than that as well. We intend to fund it entirely through internal accruals.

items.statement: Institutional patient share trend expected to continue declining for present infrastructure.
items.quote: We added capacity, and yet you have seen it come down. So, I think, trend-wise that should continue.

items.statement: No significant opex increase expected until Gurugram comes up; higher EBITDA flow-through expected.
items.quote: And yes, I think you will not see any significant increase and you will see increase in revenue and therefore you will see a higher amount of EBITDA flow through.

items.statement: Net debt may marginally go up by year end due to ongoing capex and possible loans.
items.quote: I mean, we have an ongoing capex plan, so we are spending money at Shaheed Path, INR 425 crore approval, etc. So , I would say whatever cash we generate, we will obviously consume that and maybe we will also take some loan to finance the projects, so this net debt will marginally go up if you asking at the end of the year.

items.statement: Thane and Shaheed Path approvals expected in about six months, then 30-36 months for delivery.
items.quote: For both projects after the approval, which is another six months from now, after that they will take about 30 to 36 months for delivery.

items.statement: Minority shareholders of Kalinga have gone to court seeking buyout of their shares.
items.quote: Their request or suggestion is to buy their shares also as part of the transaction, which we are okay to, and they have gone to the court that we should buy their shares.

items.statement: DSO rose from 87 to 95 days; AR build-up of around INR 250 crore impacted free cash flow.
items.quote: DSO is up from 87 days to 95 days. So, in a way there is a build-up of AR of around INR 250 crore in this quarter compared to Q4 last year.

items.statement: Organic revenue growth expected at 25% plus or minus a couple of percentage points.
items.value: 25 plus or minus a couple of percentage points
items.quote: So if you see, what we had also mentioned earlier in our call and this also, we believe that the number will continue to be in the range of 25 plus or minus a couple of percentage points in terms of our revenue growth on an organic basis.

items.statement: Jayhawk addition to contribute 10-15% additional growth.
items.quote: And with the addition of the Jayhawk, that number will be added because Jayhawk was not counte d in our last year's revenue, any significant revenue. So another 10% to 15% of additional growth will come because of the addition of Jayhawk's revenue line

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin guidance 24-26%, consolidated 22-24%.
items.quote: So typically, as I have been always guiding that on a standalone, we should be looking at anything between 24% to 26% on a standalone basis. And on a consol basis, we should be looking at anything between 22% to 24% EBITDA margin is what I would really guide at because there are multiple companies, multiple segments, multiple end markets.

items.statement: Capex expected INR70-80 crores.
items.quote: And to my mind, in the range of INR70 crores to INR80 crores may be the number that I would look at from a capex point of view, for now.

items.statement: Cumulative signed LOI and contracts represent INR18,000 crores potential business.
items.quote: With this, our cumulative signed LOI and contracts highlighted in the presentation represents roughly INR18,000 crores of potential business over their respective tenures with several new products scheduled for commercialization from FY27 onwards.

items.statement: BASQUEVOLT LOI potential opportunity approximately USD300 million over 10 years.
items.quote: The potential long-term opportunity of approximately USD300 million spread over a period of 10 years reflects the depth of our customer engagement and our ability to participate in em erging high- growth application

items.statement: Polymer business expected 20-25% standalone, 30-35% consolidated.
items.quote: But we believe that on a standalone, we should be able to get a polymer business to be in the range of 20% to 25%. And on a consolidated basis, it should be in the range of 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Agri demand recovery is there and stable.
items.quote: See, Agri side, we are seeing at least the products that we have been in the past, we have been in, we see a fairly robust demand. so the demand recovery is there. We see that whatever we had been forecasting at the start of the year, we are seeing it to follow through.

items.statement: Bliss acquisition funded by INR300 crores debt and equity-linked instrument.
items.quote: There, we will be taking a debt of around about INR300 crores. And the balance consideration shall be raised through an equity-linked instrument, which would be the total balance of the total consideration.

items.statement: Bliss acquisition expected to conclude by first half of September.
items.quote: We expect that by the first half of September, we should be able to conclude this transaction fully.

items.statement: ETFA market size estimated at USD0.5 billion for two molecules.
items.quote: As you said, in terms of size of the market, we estimate that it should be in the USD0.5 billion kind of revenue that these 2 molecules will have.

items.statement: Bliss asset utilization targeted to improve to 60-70%.
items.quote: So we continue to believe that we should be able to improve the utilization of the company's assets to 60% to 70%, and that would translate to the kind of numbers that are there, that would be there.

items.statement: BASQUEVOLT commercialization expected in second half of year.
items.quote: And we expect it to be commercialized by the second half of the year or the later half of the year.

items.statement: BASQUEVOLT revenue ramp-up expected in 2-3 years.
items.quote: So as we say, it will be another 2 to 3 years, you will see a larger revenue ramping up as we go because that's how any new product will take, and that's what you will see.

items.statement: Order book expected to contribute 25% of revenue this year, 30% going forward.
items.quote: This year, we are expecting it to be significantly higher, contributing a round about 25% of our revenue. And going forward, it should contribute around 30%-odd of our revenue with the higher base volume that we have.

items.statement: Expect high-teens top-line growth for FY27 with continuous focus on improving margin profile

items.statement: Krystal products expected to exceed 50% of overall revenue by FY28

items.statement: Currency depreciation not a tactical advantage or disadvantage due to hedging of foreign contracts and import-processing-export model for several segments
items.quote: it is not really a tactical advantage nor is it a disadvantage for us because we import, we hedge our foreign contracts in terms of what the export realization is and then we subsequently export it out.

items.statement: Brazil subsidiary approved to expand distribution reach in Latin America for essential oils, aromatic chemicals, and specialty chemicals
items.quote: The company has approved the incorporation of a Brazil subsidiary, representing another step towards expanding our distribution reach in Latin America and creating a dedicated platform for our essential oils, aromatic chemicals, and specialty chemicals.

items.statement: New products targeted to be more margin-accretive than existing products; operating leverage expected to support margins as utilization and newer businesses gain traction over medium term
items.quote: each new product that's coming in, we want it to be like more margin accretive than our existing products.

items.statement: Eugenol and derivatives ramp-up delayed early in year by Madagascar floods but ports reopened, material flowing, strong export demand expected to bring volumes close to planned numbers by year-end

items.statement: Working capital cycle for Krystal expected to be much lower than traditional Gem business due to synthetic products requiring less inventory and use of factoring services to reduce debtor days
items.quote: the working capital cycle, you know, Krystal being more towards, you know, synthetic products where we don't need to hold inventory a large inventory for a large number of days, the working capital cycle will definitely be lower than the traditional Gem business. So, in addition to that, we are also availing the factoring services which will reduce our debtor days.

items.statement: Consolidated profitability path depends on commercialization and ramp-up of new Krystal products; current loss due to timing mismatch of facility costs (depreciation, interest, manpower) kicking in before higher-margin revenue arrives
items.quote: currently we're facing a timing mismatch, you know, where the cost of the new facility, the depreciation, interest, manpower cost, they are all, you know, kicked in to the current financials due to the standby capacity which has already kicked in. items.statement: Compressor production to commence in Q3 FY27, followed by room air conditioner production in Q4 FY27 at Sri City.

items.statement: Localization target to reach 65% over next 3 to 4 years, improving 2-3% annually.
items.quote: Our target to reach the localization rate to 65% over the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Demand healthy across Home Appliances and Home Entertainment; TV and washing machine to contribute significantly to growth.

items.statement: 55-inch plus TV segment grew 53% in Q1 and contributes 50% of overall TV business.

items.statement: Essential Series sold over 5 lakh units in first 6 months; margins in line with B2C portfolio, not dilutive.
items.quote: So we have sold more than 5 lakh unit in first 6 month of this calendar year with a strong response from both consumer and channel partner.

items.statement: B2B business confident of delivering 20% CAGR growth trajectory as delivered from FY22 to FY25.
items.quote: Backed by these multiple growth catalyst, we are very confident of delivering 20% CAGR growth trajectory which we have already delivered from financial year 2022 to 2025.

items.statement: Sri City investment to be funded entirely through internal accruals without external debt.
items.quote: Preserving our internal accruals to fund this investment entirely without any external debt is a conscious and deliberate decision that we believe is in the best long -term interest of our shareholders.

items.statement: Data center cooling is a meaningful long-term opportunity for B2B, not a key driver in FY27.
items.quote: From a materiality standpoint, this is not a key driver for us in FY27 outlook, but yes, it aligns well with our long -term B2B growth strategy.

items.statement: Dividend plans to be reviewed as Sri City investment progresses and cash generation strengthens.
items.quote: As our Sri City investment progresses in a phased manner and our cash generation strengthens further through revenue growth and margin improvement, we definitely plan to review our dividend plans.

items.quote: Renewal from a service EBITDA point of view, if I were to compare renewal service EBITDA to new service EBITDA, renewal service EBITDA is about 2.5 times to 3 times higher than the new service EBITDA.

items.quote: For example, health has grown at about 45% plus. Term life has grown at about 60% plus.

items.quote: And whatever capex's are remaining, which are new capex's of around, if you put total all this will be around USD 100 million or less USD 80 million capex, we'll be doing going forward.
