items.quote: We completed a QIP placement raising INR1,640 crores, close to $195 million, achieving full minimum public shareholding compliance and welcoming marquee institutions into our register.

items.statement: Net worth turned positive by INR691 crores after QIP proceeds of INR1,614 crores.
items.quote: So, as on 30th June '26, our net worth is negative by INR922 crores. But after this QIP proceed from QIP, which is INR1,614 crores, our as on today, our net worth is positive by INR691 crores.

items.statement: Expect 18% revenue growth in FY27, targeting INR1,800-1,900 crores turnover
items.quote: We did about INR1,600 crores last year. We can expect the same 18%-odd growth for this year also. So we should be looking at turnover in the region of around INR1,800 crores to INR1,900 crores.

items.statement: Machining mix expected to hover at 65-68% for rest of FY27
items.quote: Yes. I think it should hover in the 65% to 68% range.

items.statement: FY27 capex approximately INR150 crores, with INR30-50 crores replacement/debottlenecking
items.quote: Yes, approximately INR150-odd crores.

items.statement: 16,500 ton press to go into production by Q4 FY27; 4,000 ton press recently started production
items.quote: They're adding the 16,500 ton press, which will go into production by end of this fiscal, in Q4. And we also have a 4,000 ton press that has gone into production in the last couple of weeks.

items.statement: Automation investment to reach INR30-50 crores by end of FY27 from INR7.5-10 crores currently
items.quote: Absolutely. This number should triple, if not reach about INR50 crores, INR40 crores to INR50 crores end of this fiscal. At least, it should be in the region of INR30 crores.

items.statement: Strong momentum in domestic CV, tractor, passenger car and US Class 8 truck markets
items.quote: We've seen growth in the U.S. market, and also the CV market, the CV tractor and past car market in India are all running pretty hot.

items.statement: Targeting 90,000+ tons in FY27 and 100,000-110,000 tons in FY28
items.quote: So we should as discussed or as we have been guiding, would expect to cross the 90,000 ton mark in this year. And next year, challenge the 1 lakh ton, 1,10,000 ton mark.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 20%+ (2-3% improvement from current 18%)
items.quote: I would say all previous listing, our target would remain a 20-plus goal. We have to squeeze out 2%, 3% from the system. 1% is I can. I have clear visibility for 1% to 2%. But I would say 2% to 3% that should be our goal.

items.statement: Gross debt to remain at INR750-800 crores; no plan to increase debt beyond current levels
items.quote: No, we do not plan to increase debt beyond these levels. INR750 crores to INR800 crores is gross debt levels will stand at this point of time.

items.statement: Power and fuel cost spike in Q1 due to West Asian conflict; stabilized post-Q1
items.quote: There has been a huge increase in fuel cost in Q1 on account of the West Asian conflict. That has been, of course, over after Q1, it has reasonably stabilized.

items.statement: QIP enabling resolution active; will consider at appropriate time for sharp market opportunity
items.quote: The QIP is largely centered around a sharp opportunity that we might see in market. So, we are certainly, it's on the cards, and we are mulling it. At an appropriate time, we would definitely consider it.

items.statement: Land sale proceeds (INR64 crores gross) to reduce working capital, capex and borrowings
items.quote: That will be used to reduce our working capital and our capex and our capital borrowings.

items.statement: Revenue target INR3,000 crores by FY30 remains intact
items.quote: 2 quarters ago, you had mentioned about reaching INR3,000 crores in revenue by FY30. Do we still look to that number

items.statement: Expects export volumes to recover progressively from Q2 and maintains guidance of meaningful export growth for the full year.
items.quote: We expect export volumes to recover progressively from the second quarter and we are mai ntaining our guidance and meaningful export growth for the full year.

items.statement: Confident of delivering approximately 10% growth in domestic volumes for FY27.
items.quote: For financial year '27, our outlook remains positive, and we are confident of delivering approximately 10% growth in domestic volumes.

items.statement: Targets annualized revenue run rate of approximately INR25 crores for masala portfolio by end of FY27.
items.quote: We are targeting an annualized revenue run rate of approximately INR25 crores by the end of the financial year '27.

items.statement: Expects 10% domestic volume growth to continue for the next 2 to 3 years.
items.quote: And that's the number we kind of commit to for the upcoming 2 to 3 years as well.

items.statement: Guides for FY27 gross margin of about 30% and EBITDA margin of 17% to 18%.
items.quote: Our view right now is that for the current year, we look at about 30% gross margin and at about 17% to 18% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Q1 margins not sustainable; FY27 margin should be slightly better than last year, about 1% to 2% better at EBITDA level.
items.quote: In general, the margin should be slightly better than that of last year is our view right now.

items.statement: Able to pass on extra freight cost and rice price increases in Middle East after benchmark prices increased.
items.quote: But now after the local rate incr eases, the benchmark prices have increased -- so now we are able to pass on the extra freight cost and also the rice pipe increases.

items.statement: No more price hikes in Q2; will watch paddy crop season and decide calibrated price hikes in Q3.
items.quote: And we are not going to be taking any more price hikes within quarter 2. As Ashish also mentioned earlier, we are going to be waiting and watching for the paddy crop season to unfold.

items.statement: Demand remains stable; expects bulk pack purchases to progressively materialize over coming quarters.
items.quote: Demand remains stable, and we expect these purchases to pr ogressively materialize over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Sees demand picking up; export numbers will be much better in Q2 as bulk business resumes.
items.quote: Yes, yes, we'll see better numbe rs because I think bulk business will also resume in the second quarter to some extent. So yes, export numbers will be much better.

items.statement: New facility at Gangavathi expected to become operational by end of Q3.
items.quote: Our new facility at Gangavathi is expected to become operational by the end of quarter 3, supporting the next phase of growth in this portfolio.

items.statement: Plans to enter more regional rice varieties in quick commerce later this year.
items.quote: So later this year, you will see us entering a lot more of these categories.

items.statement: Deficient monsoon and depleted pipeline expected to keep prices firm into new crop.
items.quote: What I would say is that the deficient monsoon on top of an already depleted pipeline are used for firm not soft credit prices into the new crop.

items.statement: If peace process completes and markets open, basmati prices will definitely increase further.
items.quote: There is no doubt if the peace process completes and the markets have opened up -- will open up, definitely, there will be an impact on the price. The prices are definitely going to shoot further.

items.statement: Will be buying more inventory this season.
items.quote: Yes. This year, we'll be buying inventory. Definitely, we'll be buying inventory.

items.statement: Expect Australia and Ireland revenue to reach million-dollar levels in local currencies next year
items.quote: We believe that next year the focus on Australia and Ireland will be high and then we expect it to be getting into the million dollars, both local currencies over the next year.

items.statement: International markets expected to remain under 10% of total revenue for next couple of years
items.quote: So, the next year, what we see is that it could be depending, right now we are about like less than 10% I would say for the next couple of years for sure is what would be because given the current revenue.

items.statement: Seeing growth in AI and cloud technologies with new U.S. government contract access
items.quote: So, we see a lot of growth right now in the AI and cloud technologies. We won based on the recent, we are getting into U.S. government projects, which we were not before.

items.statement: Admitted into general bidding for U.S. state government sectors with RFP participation expected
items.quote: Yes, we do have, we recently actually part of this quarter, but we got admitted into general bidding for a couple of state, sectors. So, we still have to participate in individual RFPs.

items.statement: Product revenue (Circulus AP automation) at 25% margin and F&A services at 14% margin are highest margin recurring streams
items.quote: The product, we have a 25% margin, 25% out of our total revenue, 25% is product, and around 14% is coming from finance and accounting services. Those are recurring in nature.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 7.6% sustainable due to onsite-to-offshore shift reducing costs
items.quote: Yes, that number is true, actually. Because the expense is also drastically reduced. When it comes to onsite vs offshore, the offshore margin will be higher.

items.statement: Targeting mid-market GCC customers in U.S. starting with 3-5 member teams scaling to 50
items.quote: And most of the mid-market that we are talking, they wanted to start with few resources or a small team to begin with. And then once they understand the delivery and then their internal processes, slowly adapt to a bigger set of team.

items.statement: Zoho implementation 90% complete covering 13 products/modules for paperless transformation
items.quote: We started Zoho implementation that has been completed 90% during the quarter, covering around 13 products and modules with the remaining focus and final goal is stabilization.

items.statement: Revenue impact from onsite-to-offshore shift as onsite $70/hr replaced by offshore $35/hr
items.quote: Because of that, suppose if you are building an onsite resource at $70, we have to build the same at $35 in India when we do offshore. So, in fact, that is the difference.

items.statement: Expects 60%-70% of current order book executed in FY27.
items.quote: So if you look at the overall order book, I think most of that order book currently, which we have should be executed in FY27 itself. We are looking at about 60%-70% of the order book being executed in the current financial year.

items.statement: Odisha axle line to be commissioned in FY27, wheel line in FY28.
items.quote: So in FY27, we expect the axle line to get commissioned. And FY28 is when we have targeted for the wheel line to get commissioned.

items.statement: Targets INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue once both Odisha lines are commissioned.
items.quote: Once both lines are commissioned, we are looking at revenue of anything between INR2,500 crore to INR3,000 crore, is our revenue target.

items.statement: Targets at least 15% EBITDA in the wheelset business.
items.quote: And definitely, we are targeting an EBITDA of at least 15 -odd percent in this business, if not higher.

items.statement: About 50% of wheelset capacity for internal use and domestic, 50% for exports.
items.quote: Definitely, I think as we have always maintained that about 50% of the capacity would be for our own internal use and the domestic requirements, and 50% of the capacity is earmarked for the export business.

items.statement: Wheelset project capex INR2,600 crore; Jupiter's infusion reduced to INR600 crore after new investor.
items.quote: The project capex remains at INR2,600 crore. Out of that, Jupiter was supposed to infuse INR900 crore. Now, out of the INR900 crore, the new investor brings in approximately INR300-odd crore. So now Jupiter's infusion now goes down to INR600 crore.

items.statement: BESS order book now about 500 MW valued over INR500 crore; targets INR1,000 crore by FY27.
items.quote: With these wins, JEM Energy's BESS order book now increased to approximately 500 megawatts, valued at over INR500 crore. We are targeting a BESS order book of approximately INR1,000 crore by FY27, reflecting our confidence in the structural opportunity presented by India's rapidly expanding energy storage platform.

items.statement: Expects BESS order books of at least INR5,000 crore over next 3 years.
items.quote: This year, we expect complete order books to be about INR1,000-odd crore. And next 3 years, we are looking at, at least INR5,000-odd crore of order books in this business.

items.statement: Stone India to turn profitable from Q3; all JVs positive EBITDA before end of Q3.
items.quote: I think from third quarter onwards, Stone India will become profitable , maybe in the second quarter, you may see a slig ht borderline negative numbers. But from third quarter, Stone India will turn positive because now, it's a question of ramping up the production.

items.statement: Jupiter Electric Mobility to turn EBITDA positive from FY28.
items.quote: On the Jupiter Electric Mobility, I think which we have continued to maintain is that from FY28 onwards the business is going to turn EBITDA positive for us because as FY27 for us is building on our core technology and building on order books.

items.statement: Stone India EBITDA to be 15% plus from FY28 onwards.
items.quote: Again, from FY28 onwards, definitely, the EBITDA will be 15% plus on the business.

items.statement: 100% of freight wagon brake requirements to be met by Stone India before end of this calendar year.
items.quote: Again, as I've told you, before end of this calendar year, 100% of our requirements will be met by Stone India.

items.statement: Indian Railways wagon requirements unchanged; new order books expected soon.
items.quote: Indian Railways has not reduced their wagon targets, whatever the order books which we have from Indian Railways, there is no reduction in terms of the requirements, which they have given us, that continues to remain the same.

items.statement: BESS C&I segment growing 80%-100% month-on-month; no demand challenges seen.
items.quote: On the C&I segment itself, we continue to grow very strongly. If you look at month-on-month, our growth is close to 80%-100% on the C&I segment itself.

items.statement: Lucchini RS and SIMEST to acquire 25% of JTRWF for about INR290 crore.
items.quote: Under the partnership, Lucchini RS and SIMEST, an Italian government financial institute, shall acquire a combined 25% stake in JTRWF with an investment of approximately INR290 crore.

items.statement: Passenger systems partnership expected to be announced before end of the year.
items.quote: We are at a very advanced stage. And I think before the end of the year, we will be announcing a partnership.

items.statement: Expects FY27 capex to remain similar to FY26 capex of ₹800 crores.
items.quote: We expect capital expenditure in FY 27 to remain similar to the FY 26 capex of ₹ 800 crores.

items.statement: Expects better Q2 and Q3 margins due to raw material and conversion cost settlements.
items.quote: So definitely , we see a better Q2 and Q3 for sure. But if you tell me to give an amount, to be honest, there are so many variables around it that I cannot give a figure right now. But I can definitely say - it will be better than Q1.

items.statement: Aluminium alloy rates softening by ₹12-17 per kg in this quarter, expected gain.
items.quote: As I mentioned, we are seeing softening of the aluminium alloy rates, not the Q4 base, but lower, by 12-17 ₹ per kg is what we are seeing as of now in this quarter, which will be a gain to us .

items.statement: Raw material increases from OEMs to be settled this quarter, effective this quarter.
items.quote: Aditya, we are surely going to get all the raw material increases from every OEM in this quarter. So basically, we'll get the Q1 FY 26 rates in this quarter.

items.statement: Cumulative 4W casting bookings at Shendra reached ₹513 crores per annum peak potential.
items.quote: With our focus on increasing 4W casting business at our AURIC Shendra plant at Chh. Sambhajinagar, order wins have continued to build, taking cumulative bookings to a peak annual business potential of ₹ 513 crores per annum.

items.statement: Europe booked orders worth €13.9 million in Q1 FY27, including Mercedes and Stellantis.
items.quote: In our Europe business, we have booked orders worth € 13.9 million in Q1 FY 27. This includes a large order from Mercedes for their hybrid program and an order from Stellantis for their internal combustion engine program.

items.statement: Adding 9 lakh ABS units per annum, reduced from 12 lakh due to brake assembly demand.
items.quote: In line with this, we are adding 9 lakhs ABS units per annum. Earlier, we had announced a figure of 12 lakhs units per annum to our existing ABS capacity of 6.4 lakhs units per annum.

items.statement: Battery pack plant started SOP for Hero MotoCorp in June 2026, ramp-up to peak by Q3 FY27.
items.quote: Our battery pack plant near Pune commenced SOP for Hero MotoCorp in June 2026. With this large order won, the plant is in a ramp -up phase to reach peak volumes by Q 3 of this financial year.

items.statement: Entering 4W battery packs with capex of ₹62 crores, SOP expected by Q4 FY27.
items.quote: We have also announced our entry into 4W battery packs from the same plant with a capex of ₹ 62 crores and we expect SOP by Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Suspension business adding assembly lines to reach 100,000 units per month by end FY27.
items.quote: With increasing uptake of inverted front forks by OEMs, we are adding assembly lines and are on track to reach a monthly 100,000 units by end of FY 27.

items.statement: Won suspension orders for Hero MotoCorp and Suzuki, SOP in Q3 FY27, order value ₹120 crores per annum.
items.quote: We are also happy to tell you that we will be starting SOP for our suspensions for Hero MotoCorp and Suzuki in quarter 3 of this financial year. This total order value is approximately ₹120 crores per annum.

items.statement: Adding fifth forging press with SOP expected next quarter.
items.quote: To meet this demand and as we have shared earlier, we are addin g a fifth forging press with SOP expected in the next quarter.

items.statement: Solar damper and actuator business won totaling ₹345 crores.
items.quote: The total business won is ₹ 118 crores for the solar dampers and ₹ 227 crores for solar actuators, totalling ₹ 345 crores of business.

items.statement: European industry challenging due to Middle East crisis, high energy costs, US duties, Chinese competition, muted growth.
items.quote: In Europe, the industry continues as mentioned earlier to operate in a challenging environment shaped by the Middle East crisis, high energy costs and interest rates, duties imposed by USA, increased competition from Chinese OEMs, and muted automotive market growth.

items.statement: Received Maharashtra incentive addendum increasing incentive from ₹600 crores to ₹858 crores over seven years.
items.quote: Under the Maharashtra Package Scheme of Incentives 2019, we had received an addendum taking our incentive up from ₹600 crores to ₹ 858 crores. These incentives will be availed through the I ndustrial Promotion Subsidy by way of a state GST refund, broadly over a seven-year period.

items.statement: Expect single-digit revenue growth for FY27 with EBITDA margin similar to last year, possibly slightly higher
items.quote: We do expect single-digit growth as far as the revenues are concerned. As far as the EBITDA margin is concerned, it should be similar to what we did last year. Maybe it could be a little bit higher, but that's more or less the guidance.

items.statement: Expect double-digit growth for French entity and India operations in FY28-29, targeting >10% group revenue growth and EBITDA margin near 25-26%
items.quote: We do expect at least double-digit growth in the French entity as well as the India operations. All of this should help us to achieve more than 10% growth in the revenue YoY. The EBITDA margin should be closer to the 25-26% that we were doing prior to the EDQM issues that we had at the India sites.

items.statement: Indian entity revenue to grow 30-35% in FY27 with operating margin near 10%
items.quote: The Indian entity, as such, for the current financial year, the revenue should increase by at least 30-35% as compared to the previous year. As far as the margins are concerned, at an operating level, we should be at close to about 10%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex was CHF 4.9 million
items.quote: The CapEx that was done in Q1 of the financial year stood at about CHF 4.9 million

items.statement: One commercial tech transfer contract signed with US company from Switzerland to Bavla, to complete this financial year; second major legacy project approved by Swiss MNC and initiated; three more tech transfers in advanced discussions
items.quote: I'm glad to inform you that a commercial contract was already signed with the U.S. company to tech transfer a legacy project from Switzerland to Bavla site. The activity has been already started, and the project should be completed within this financial year. I'm pleased to inform you all that second major legacy project tech transfer has been approved by a prominent Swiss MNC, thanks to the stron

items.statement: New commercial product approved by US FDA added to portfolio; Japanese co-investment on track to be operational next year
items.quote: Recently, a new commercial product from the big pharma has been approved by the U.S. FDA, which adds another commercial product to our portfolio. The co-investment with our Japanese clients is proceeding nicely and it's on track. We're still expecting operational to be in the course of next year.

items.statement: New wool grease sources secured at more attractive prices for cholesterol/Vitamin D business; cost reduction programs showing first signs
items.quote: Also, we got new Wool grease sources with more attractive prices, which could be accessed, and we are confident that this will continue talking to different suppliers. Still, the cost reduction programs across this business unit are still ongoing and result their first signs.

items.statement: Phase three (operating leverage) expected conservatively in about one and a half years from now
items.quote: I think phase three would happen if I speak conservatively, about one and a half years from now.

items.statement: Major capacity expansion done for next two years; no major capital expenditure planned unless windfall order pipeline emerges
items.quote: I think we are done for the next one to two years until unless suddenly we get -- we are seeing an order pipeline which is looking very, very healthy for our luggage plant.

items.statement: Additional INR10 crore investment can add 50,000 pieces per month capacity in existing building
items.quote: So net-net, just to give you a brief broad understanding, another INR10 cr. of investment can give us another 50,000 capacity.

items.statement: Plant EBITDA estimated at approximately 12% at 40,000 pieces per month; bulk of benefit currently passed to consumers via pricing
items.quote: I think the plant individually, if it was not applying to Brand Concepts, we would have easily made between a 11%, 13%, approximately a 12% kind of EBITDA at the plant level.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to continue healthy trend due to consolidation and balance sheet focus
items.quote: I foresee that EBITDA margins will continue to show a healthy trend.

items.statement: Secondary sales strong across channels; primary billing temporarily dented by e-commerce SKU realignment and store closures
items.quote: However, our secondary continue to be strong. So very confident that we should be able to bridge this gap in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Company expects to return to growth by October after consolidation completion by September
items.quote: Yes, 100%. I would love to see it earlier than that, but yes, by October, for sure.

items.statement: Luggage growing low single digits; travel care negative due to backpack SKU consolidation; new brands (Off-White, Superdry, Juicy) showing strong early traction
items.quote: But the growth is probably low single digits, growth in luggage. Overall, travel care, we are sort of in negative, but not because of luggage, because of backpacks where certain SKUs, we needed to consolidate certain high volume, but low throughput or low margin items were sort of -- we had to take a call and discontinue a few of them.

items.statement: Off-White limited to four stores total; Juicy to add a couple more stores then pause for metrics; Juicy apparel 70-75% in-house by Q3 next financial year
items.quote: See Off-White, we have thought of five stores in totality. I think we are done for now. By next Q1, we'll be opening the fourth one in Bombay. And I think we are done for Off-White.

items.statement: Pricing pressure intense from new PE-backed players selling luggage as low as INR900; raw material costs escalated due to war situations; travel demand curbed
items.quote: There still seems to be a lot of challenges in terms of pricing pressures and new incumbent players coming into our category, specifically when it comes to the travel wear category. The pricing pressure still remains to be there. External conditions are not very, very bright. At the same time, it is further fuelled with war situations, which have escalated the cost of raw material to go up.

items.statement: Tommy Hilfiger license renewal delayed at international level; paperwork pending but business terms and 10-year plan with same royalties closed
items.quote: So, I can officially on record say this, that our 10-year business plan, royalties, figures, numbers have been closed. So, it's just the paperwork that we are waiting.

items.statement: Promoters infused INR20 crore (INR15 crore already deployed) for new brands; no further equity raise planned; debt peaked in FY26, expected to decline by FY27 end
items.quote: Yes, we do not intend to, at the moment at least, we do not intend to sort of take more debt. I think we've availed the government scheme which was available and it was prudent to do so. But apart from that

items.statement: Manufacturing: PC unit at 80%+ utilization (25,000 pcs/month); PP unit trials done, targeting 75-80% by Oct-Nov; combined capacity 50,000 pcs/month; plant EBITDA positive at 20,000 pcs vs earlier 30-35k breakeven
items.quote: By, at best in the next two months, I think we should reach 75%, 80% capacity over there also. So to put in perspective the PC unit has about a 25,000 kind of production capacity and same would be a PP, right? So, both together would be about a 50,000 capacity.

items.statement: Inventory reduced from INR128 cr (Mar) to INR123 cr (Jun) ~130 days; target to improve working capital cycle further
items.quote: We had INR128 crores of inventory at March end. Currently, we have about INR123 crores by June end. So it's about 130 odd days of inventory, sir.

items.statement: Benetton strategy reset: distinct channel-specific products, CSD entry planned, manufacturing cost advantage leveraged
items.quote: And now we are able to sort of segregate two clear, distinct lines. One, which we've dedicated to e-commerce, where we're playing that a sharp price point game. And even on the offline side, where we are launching, as we speak, we are launching by next month.

items.statement: Aeropostale brand to be discontinued; focus on existing portfolio (Tommy, Benetton, Superdry, Off-White, Juicy)
items.quote: We'll focus mostly on these brands, Aeropostale. Yes, time to give up, to be honest.

items.statement: Maintain FY27 revenue growth guidance of 35% to 40% and EBITDA margin guidance of 9% to 10%
items.quote: We continue to maintain the guidance for this year. We hope that we can do that or better for the coming year.

items.statement: May revise FY27 guidance upward after Q3 depending on performance
items.quote: Depending on how Q3 effectively goes, we'll be able to see if we can upward revise the guidance. So, we will be in a better position to update you about that at the end of Q3.

items.statement: Total FY27 capex for VOEPL expected between INR80 crore and INR100 crore
items.quote: So, total CapEx, this year we are looking at about between INR80 crores and INR100 crores in VOEPL.

items.statement: Commercial refrigeration capex of INR20-25 crore planned for FY27 and similar amount next year to reach 400,000 capacity
items.quote: This financial year, we are looking to do about INR20 crore, INR25 crore CapEx in commercial refrigeration. And next year, we look at a similar number to achieve the 400,000 capacity that we have planned.

items.statement: Strong order book visibility for AC and compressor segments supporting FY27 growth
items.quote: We have a very strong order book size for the forthcoming season. And we should be able to achieve our numbers primarily through on the backing of this strong and healthy order book.

items.statement: AC margin improvement expected from next year as raw material pressure eases; ODM vs OEM margin difference ~1-1.5%
items.quote: because of the raw material pressure, I think the entire supply chain, including our customers and the distribution channel is slightly stretched for margins. I think this pressure will continue for maybe 6 months or 12 months till the global situation sort of stabilizes, Virtuoso Optoelectronics Limited (VOEPL) Q1 FY27 Post Earnings Conference Call August 17, 2026 12.00 PM IST post which we belie

items.statement: Compressor EBITDA currently 5-7%, expected to improve by 1-2% after backward integration in next financial year
items.quote: So right now, we are looking at about 6%, 5%, 6% EBITDA, maybe 6% 7% EBITDA or 6 plus minus 1% EBITDA in compressors. But once you backward integrate and once the inventory, which the other manufacturers are keeping, gets consumed, maybe we will be able to improve the EBITDA slightly by a percent or two. But I think that we should expect primarily in the next financial year.

items.statement: Raw material pricing stabilizing; price increases requested from customers expected to average out over next couple of quarters
items.quote: And because of raw material issues, which has persisted, we hope that now the pricing is a little more stable. And over the next couple of quarters, I mean, we hope that the price increase that we are requesting our customers and also the market will effectively even out or average out.

items.statement: RAC industry expected to grow 8-10% in FY27; commercial refrigeration demand deferred in Q1 but expected to recover over the year
items.quote: I mean, I believe this year, I mean, last year on a bad year, we saw growth, but I think on a good year this year, we will still see, I believe, 8% to 10% growth in the next season.

items.statement: FY27 revenue mix: AC 55-60%, EMS ~10%, commercial refrigeration ~10%, components/washing machine ~5%, compressor ~15%
items.quote: So this is how it appears. I think the revenue share that is expected in this FY27. AC will remain at around 60%, 55% to 60% of the overall revenue. EMS will stay at about 10% in terms of the overall contribution. Commercial refrigeration will be at par, at about 10%. The component washing machine and other businesses should contribute about 5% of the overall revenue. And compressor will move up t

items.statement: PLI benefits ending in 2027; impact ~1% of EBITDA; negotiating with customers for win-win solution over next 12 months
items.quote: The effective impact of PLI is about a percent on the overall EBITDA of the company. So, I mean, in the AC business specifically. But anyhow, so we are in discussion with our customers and over the next 12 months, we will find a win-win solution with them.

items.statement: Compressor expansion first phase funded by equity raise and INR150 crore OCD debt; next phase funding decision in 12 months
items.quote: now, the first phase we are covering with the investment that we have already done as part of equity raise or the ongoing equity issue. So this will cover us for the first phase, which is up to

items.statement: Peak revenue potential of INR3,500-4,000 crore with ongoing expansions at 60-80% utilization across segments
items.quote: With the ongoing expansion that we are doing, which we conclude till in the next 12 months, we are looking at a peak revenue of about INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: Net margin target for FY27 at 2% to 3% (previously guided 2.5% to 3%)
items.quote: Net margin is a function of multiple things, but we are looking at 2% to 3% net margins.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth guidance of 40% for FY27 maintained
items.quote: Our guidance was 40% on a consolidated basis, and we are not moving away from that guidance as yet.

items.statement: Stand-alone revenue growth guidance of 25% for FY27 maintained
items.quote: overall, it would be about in the 25% range is what we had projected for the stand-alone, and we still stand by that guidance that we would be able to grow to that number for the entire year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 14-15% over 5-7 years reaffirmed
items.quote: what we have guided that 14% to 15% margin is over a period of 5 to 7 years.

items.statement: Moderating new capitalization levels; expensing more costs going forward
items.quote: Rather than waiting for a full policy rollout, we took immediate proactive measures in Q1 FY27 to moderate new capitalization levels.

items.statement: DICE contract novation of 85+ clients underway, completion expected by end of Q2 FY27
items.quote: The contract novation of around 85-plus clients is underway, and we should complete by the end of Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin 8.2% in Q1 FY27 vs 10.1% in Q1 FY26; expected to improve as DICE revenue kicks in
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, our adjusted EBITDA margin stands at around 8.2% as compared to 10.1% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Propel points margin 7.1% consolidated, 5% stand-alone in Q1 FY27
items.quote: With reference to Propel points margin on a consolidated basis, we have reached a margin of 7.1% with heavy attribution to Greenedge higher margins. On a stand-alone basis, Propel margin stood around 5% with a significant improvement from our Q4 FY26 margins.

items.statement: Cash back as percentage of program fees 66.3% in Q1 FY27 vs 65.7% in Q1 FY26; increase due to higher credit card mix
items.quote: With reference to cash back as a percentage of program fees, we saw cash back of 66.3% in Q1 FY27, which is a marginal increase to the cash back of 65.7% in Q1 FY26, but a significant drop from our Q4 FY26 where the cash back was closer to 69%.

items.statement: Zagg.Money annualized new card acquisition run rate increased 2.3x to ~84,000 cards
items.quote: Now I'm happy to announce that we have increased the annualized run rate by almost 2.3x to now reach around 84,000 cards in a short span of time.

items.statement: Fleet business transactions up 43% YoY, transaction value up 5.8% YoY, annualized spend rate INR100 crores
items.quote: Compared to Q1FY27 -- comparing Q1 FY27 to Q1 FY26, we have seen a remarkable 43% increase in the total transactions, along with a resounding 5.8% increase in transaction value, which has reached an annualized spend rate of INR100 crores as of today.

items.statement: DICE acquisition adds AI capabilities to Save, Zoyer, Propel; revenue from novated contracts starts Q2 FY27
items.quote: we will start realizing the revenue from novated DICE contracts only from Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Signed 5-year agreement with HPCL as aggregator for Driver Track Plus program
items.quote: We signed a 5-year agreement with HPCL as an aggregator for their flagship Driver Track Plus, DT Plus program to facilitate purchase of petroleum products and enable additional discounts and benefits to the entire corporate and retail base of Zaggle.

items.statement: Opening ADGM subsidiary in Abu Dhabi in Q2 FY27; mindful of regional volatility
items.quote: Now we are in the process of opening a subsidiary in ADGM, Abu Dhabi Global Markets International Financial Center and Free Economic Zone within this quarter, which is Q2 FY27. While we remain mindful of regional volatility, our engagement with local government, banking and commercial partners has met with overwhelming interest.

items.statement: Intend to deploy QIP proceeds into adjacent sectors for value-accretive acquisitions
items.quote: Moving forward, we intend to deploy our QIP proceeds into adjacent sectors, ensuring every transaction drives meaningful synergies and accelerate our long-term growth trajectory.

items.statement: DICE acquisition cost INR68 crores excl. GST, down from initial INR123 crores valuation
items.quote: we have secured the complete spend management product suite and intellectual property, along with their entire enterprise and partnership contract portfolio for approximately INR68 crores, excluding GST, a significant INR55 crores optimization from the initial INR123 crores valuation.

items.statement: DICE revenue expected INR15-16 crores in FY27 with 90%+ gross margins
items.quote: Sir, last year, they had done about INR12-odd crores, okay? And we expect that at least we are able to achieve anywhere between INR15 crores to INR16 crores this year, okay? As you know, gross margins there are about 90% plus.

items.statement: Collections target for FY27 revised to Rs 2,500-2,700 crores from earlier Rs 2,500-3,000 crores
items.quote: And we expect our collections to be in the range of Rs. 2,500-Rs. 2,700 crores in the current year, which would be a combination of the projects which we have already sold, which will be hitting the construction milestones and the fresh sales which we are planning to do, which is in equal proportion to one of them.

items.statement: Remaining capex on commercial assets under construction is Rs 1,500-1,800 crores, fully tied up with equity and debt
items.quote: The remaining capital which we need to deploy on these assets is amount in the range of Rs. 1,500-Rs. 1,800 crores and which would be, which is completely tied up as we speak.

items.statement: Residential launch pipeline of Rs 16,100 crores, with Rs 4,000 crores already launched and Rs 12,000 crores planned for FY27
items.quote: Our residential launch pipeline, spanning both unsold launched inventory and future launches, stands at approximately Rs. 16,100 crores. Of this, Rs. 4,000 crores is already launched and available for sale this year, while the remaining Rs. 12,000 crores approximately represents new project launches planned through the course of FY '27.

items.statement: Embedded PBT from sold residential portfolio estimated at Rs 4,500-5,500 crores
items.quote: Translating the sold portfolio into profitability terms, the embedded PBT is estimated in the range of Rs. 4,500-Rs. 5,500 crores.

items.statement: Max Towers latest lease signed at Rs 156 psf/month vs weighted average rental of Rs 132, mark-to-market upside over 50%
items.quote: Max Towers continues to command a significant pre-leasing premium, the latest lease signed at Rs. 156 per square foot per month, against a current weighted average rental of Rs. 132, a mark-to-market upside of over 50% and a premium of more than 50% to immediate micro-market rentals.

items.statement: Delhi NCR residential launches at 8,800 units in Q2 CY26, Gurgaon 70% share; office leasing 4.1 msf in Q2 CY26
items.quote: Delhi NCR recorded close to 8,800 residential unit launches in Q2, 2026, with Gurgaon continuing to lead the region accounting for approximately a 70% share across the key vectors of Sohna Road and Dwarka Expressway.

items.statement: Estate 105 Noida revised to residential portfolio, GDV enhanced to Rs 6,000 crores with Phase-2 launch in FY27
items.quote: At Estate 105 Noida, driven by the strong response to the project, we have revised the development mix to a residential portfolio, enhancing our project GDV to Rs. 6,000 crores, with Phase-2 of this plan in FY '27 as a launch.

items.statement: No sales guidance for FY27 due to volatile microeconomic environment, focus on quality of sales
items.quote: We feel that giving guidance in the current microeconomic environment is not the best thing for the long-term health of the company and we are very focused on the quality of sales that we do, in how we sell, in who we sell to, etc.

items.statement: ICRA assigned first-time issuer rating A+ stable, assessed committed receivables Rs 9,500 crores and cash-flow adequacy 105%
items.quote: Last week, ICRA, one of the premium rating agencies of the country, assigned Max Estates a first-time issuer rating of A+, with a stable outlook, on a consolidated basis covering the company and its 14 subsidiaries.

items.statement: Sector 59 Gurgaon launch expected in Q3 FY27, 1.3 msf development potential, GDV over Rs 3,500 crores
items.quote: Sector 59 on Golf Course Extension Road, it has a development potential of 1.3 million square feet, with a GDV potential of more than Rs. 3,500 crores, and we are expected to launch in Q3 of FY '27.

items.statement: Target annual rental income of Rs 700 crores at peak occupancy from commercial portfolio
items.quote: As our under-construction pipeline progresses, we expect to achieve our annual rental income of approximately Rs. 700 crores at peak occupancy.

items.statement: Commercial assets at 100% occupancy, lease rental income up 5% YoY to Rs 40 crores in Q1
items.quote: All the commercial assets were 100% leased, and the total area stood at 1.2 million square feet, with the lease rental income from Max Towers, Max House, and Max Square up 5% year-on-year to Rs. 40 crores in Quarter 1.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 234 crores, gross debt Rs 1,960 crores including LRD of Rs 934 crores, cash Rs 1,727 crores as of June 26
items.quote: As on June 26, the net debt stood at Rs. 234 crores, with a gross debt of Rs. 1,960 crores, including lease rental discounting borrowings of Rs. 934 crores, while cash and cash equivalents stood at Rs. 1,727 crores, with a net debt of Rs. 234 crores.

items.statement: Antara development management fee 9.5% of topline on senior living portion, sells at 7-10% premium to Max Estates residences
items.quote: Antara acts as a knowledge partner to Max Estates for which they are given a fee, which is a fixed fee in the range of close to 9.5%, which is a development manager's fees given to them.

items.statement: Expect high single-digit ARR growth going forward as demand stabilizes and wedding season drives rates
items.quote: So, we can expect definitely high single digit ARR growth as we go forward.

items.statement: Expect quarters ahead to be distinctly better than Q1 with continued revenue and EBITDA growth trend
items.quote: So, we expect that the quarters ahead are going to be distinctly better than the quarter which has gone by.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at Rs.200-250 crores; total 4-5 year capex plan of Rs.1,500 crores net of EM Bypass funding
items.quote: Within this year there could be around Rs. 200 crores - Rs. 250 crore of the CAPEX requirement.

items.statement: Pipeline of 12 hotels with 472 keys for FY27, taking portfolio to 3,149 keys by end of FY27
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY27, we now have a pipeline of 12 hotels comprising of 472 keys for this year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 28.12%; PAT margin close to 7% due to higher finance costs and deferred tax
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs.47 crores up 3% year-on-year with EBITDA margin at 28.12%.

items.statement: ADR growth was muted at 6% market-wide in Q1 due to flat air traffic; expect high single-digit ARR growth ahead
items.quote: The All-India market growth in ADRs during the quarter has only been 6%.

items.statement: Demand outlook positive with BRICS Summit, 40 wedding dates, Aero Show and Bharat Mobility Expo driving occupancy and ADR
items.quote: There are about 40 wedding dates during the course from now to March'27, Aero Show at Bangalore and the Bharat Mobility Expo among others.

items.statement: Flurys at 111 outlets, targeting 140 by end of FY27 and 400 by 2030; F&B contributes ~43% of total revenue
items.quote: By the end of this year, we are working to deliver 29 additional outlets to take the overall Flurys store count to 140 stores.

items.statement: West Asia crisis and flat domestic air traffic pressured Q1 ADR; international air traffic into India declined ~10%
items.quote: International air traffic into India during this course of this quarter has declined by almost 10%.

items.statement: EM Bypass apartment sales to generate Rs.70-80 crores cash flow in FY27 (Rs.21 crores already received); total Rs.300-325 crores over 4 years
items.quote: This will lead to improved cash flow of Rs.70 to Rs.80 crores during the course of the year, of which Rs.21 crores is already received.

items.statement: Target to double hotels from 42 to 87 and keys from 2,677 to 6,719 by 2030; 2x owned asset growth, 3x+ asset-light growth
items.quote: Overall, over the next four years, we plan to double the number of hotels from 42 hotels with 2,667 keys to 87 hotels totaling to 6,719 keys.

items.statement: Malabar House acquisition in Fort Kochi (17 keys) expected to close by Oct-Nov 2026
items.quote: The acquisition of the Malabar House in Fort Kochi is currently in progress. The property comprises of 17 keys on approximately half an acre of land and this acquisition is expected to be completed by October-November of 2026.

items.statement: Pune FSI increased from 2.5 lakh to 6.7 lakh sq ft; plan 2.5 lakh sq ft for hotel, 4 lakh+ sq ft for residential development
items.quote: At Pune, the FSI available to us on our land has changed from 2.5 lakh square feet to 6.7 lakh square feet.

items.statement: Other income sustainable at Rs.3.5-4 crores per quarter; expected to increase from EM Bypass sales proceeds and EBITDA performance
items.quote: So, I think around 3.5 – 4 crores will be sustainable on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Tax rate to decline from ~40% in Q1 to 30-35% in Q2-Q4 FY27 under new tax regime, improving PAT
items.quote: So, at present our tax rate from next quarter will go down from 35 to 25% as we are coming under new regime.

items.statement: Expects 20-25% revenue growth for FY27, already achieved 20% in Q1 without new product contribution
items.quote: 20% is something we were expecting, 20 -25% to happen in the entire year, but it is already translated and the other products have not even contributed.

items.statement: Q2 revenue expected to grow ~30% YoY with 1,000 tonne monthly sales increase from TLT and crash barrier adding ~10 Cr/month
items.quote: In Q1, you've seen a 20% increase in turnover. In Q1? So, similarly, in Q2, you will see this 20%. Plus, apart from that, you will see growth on other subjects such as transmission line tower and crash barrier. So, those will also start reflecting. For example, we're expecting that we'll increase our sales by 1,000 tons. So, give or take around 10 CR, something like that, monthly. So, 30% increase

items.statement: New products: RSJ Pole (500 tonne order, job work initially, listed by Q3-Q4); solar structures, railway bridges in research stage
items.quote: There is one order booking that we have taken from RSJ Pole. It's a product called RSJ Pole. It's again distribution lines. It looks like it's 500 tons order. So, that is currently only processed as a job work on like a 20,000. So, revenue will be 1cr only from it. But that is purely job work. We are soon going to start getting a lot of order from RSJ, which is another product. But we are expectin

items.statement: North expansion to be housed in new subsidiary for clear visibility of turnover, depreciation, and performance
items.quote: It is done in a subsidiary in north for an arrangement so that the visibility is possible for everybody to see how that plant alone is performing. That is why the subsidiary is created so that the turnover of it, the depreciation of it and everything becomes clear to all the investors to us to reflect upon to see.

items.statement: Uniware expected to grow over 15% YoY from Q4 FY27 onwards
items.quote: As quarter 4 FY '27 will be the first full quarter of like-for-like comparison following this client exit, we are confident of delivering growth of over 15% from quarter 4 FY '27 onwards in Uniware.

items.statement: Shipway expected to grow 20%+ YoY from Q4 FY27 onwards
items.quote: With the investments that we are making, we are anticipating that this growth will improve to 20% plus from quarter 4 FY '27.

items.statement: Profitability improvement expected in H2 FY27 as investments front-loaded in H1
items.quote: Most of these investments will be front-loaded in H1 FY '27 with benefits expected to build through growth and operating leverage, leading to an improving profitability trajectory in H2 FY '27 and beyond.

items.statement: Investments of a few crores in sales, marketing, AI product development and talent for H1 FY27
items.quote: The investment in terms of absolute is in the range of a few crores and will continue for the current quarter, post which we anticipate some of these investments to start demonstrating results and show improvement in our growth percentage as well.

items.statement: Uniware standalone adjusted EBITDA margin 32-35%, previously reached 40%
items.quote: Uniware, even with investments, it has grown from 32% to 35% from an adjusted EBITDA run rate perspective. And we've always maintained that Uniware as a business has a very strong operating leverage. So we'll continue to demonstrate that further. Last year, it had gone to the 40% adjusted EBITDA margin levels as well.

items.statement: Shipway to operate at breakeven from Q3 FY27, profits reinvested for growth
items.quote: We are targeting to make Shipway breakeven in quarter 3 itself. And with the investments playing out, we are confident of delivering a 20% plus growth from quarter 4 FY '27 onwards.

items.statement: Added 115 enterprise customers in Q1 FY27, up 30.7% YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 115 enterprise customers, up 30.7% compared to 88 in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: 40-45% of Uniware enterprise customers use quick commerce and B2B modules; UniReco 6-7% adoption; UniCapture 3-4% adoption
items.quote: 40% to 45% of our Uniware enterprise customers are now using quick commerce and B2B modules. 6% to 7% have adopted UniReco within a year of launch and 3% to 4% have taken up UniCapture within 2 quarters of its launch.

items.statement: Shipway operates in INR 4,000+ crore courier aggregation market with single-digit share
items.quote: Shipway, as we've mentioned multiple times before that Shipway operates in courier aggregation, which is a large market opportunity. As per our estimates, it's INR4,000 crores plus market, where we are a relatively early-stage player, single-digit market share today with a significant headroom for growth.

items.statement: ESOP expense INR 2.5-4 crore per quarter for next year due to 4-year amortization of grants from last year
items.value: INR2.5 crores to INR4 crores per quarter
items.quote: As per the amortization cycle of the ESOPs, we expect the ESOPs to get amortized over a period of 4 years from the date of grant. We granted these ESOPs sometime last year. So over the period of next year, the spend would be trending in the similar range of INR2.5 crores to INR4 crores per quarter.

items.statement: No fund raise planned; cash balance INR 92.6 crore, growing 72% YoY, to be used for M&A if needed
items.quote: We are adding cash to our balance sheet on a regular basis. Cash balances increased to INR92 crores, 70% growth over last year. We will use -- we'll potentially use this cash for M&A, but Unicommerce e we don't foresee the need of doing a fund raise because we are adding cash flows to our balance sheet on a regular basis

items.statement: M&A exploratory stage; evaluating startups adjacent to business with 4 criteria
items.quote: We continue to evaluate inorganic opportunities. We continue to explore start-ups in respective areas, which could be adjacent to us. The 3 criteria that we look for inorganic are: one, it should make sense for existing customers. Two, it should be a good product, good team. Three, it should be available at the right valuation. And sorry, fourth, one more is that it should either be profitable or

items.statement: Uniware maintains premium pricing as market leader; brands value stability and scalability
items.quote: We continue to be a market leader on the Uniware side. We continue to be a premium player. So we continue to hold that position even now. The brands and the ecosystem values us for the stability and the scalability of the platform and that they know that they can trust this platform with the entire e-commerce operations.

items.statement: Shipway-Uniware customer overlap 10%+; absolute overlap growing as both bases expand
items.quote: The overlap of Shipway in the Unicommerce ecosystem continues to be 10% plus, while we have maintained this 10% plus number for the last couple of quarters. The number may seem stagnant, but actually, the absolute overlap of clients between Shipway and Unicommerce continues to increase because the client base is increasing at both Uniware and Shipway.

items.statement: Uniware growth levers: market growth, new customer acquisition (30-50% improvement since listing), and cross-sell of new modules to 1,100+ enterprise base
items.quote: compared to when we were listed, we are now seeing anywhere between 30% to 50% improvement in the number of clients being acquired. Unicommerce e We are also seeing good attach rates of UniReco, UniCapture. UniReco is now at nearly 7% of attach rate. UniCapture is at nearly 3% to 4% of attach rate within 2 quarters of

items.statement: Expects mid-teens revenue growth with stable EBITDA margins for Belrise as a whole.
items.quote: What we are guiding for is the business as a whole, which is for Belrise as a whole, which is mid -teens revenue growth with stable EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to remain broadly stable compared to FY26 levels.
items.quote: We expect EBITDA margins to remain broadly stable as compared to FY26 levels.

items.statement: Margins expected to go up in coming quarters to maintain EBITDA margin vs FY26.
items.quote: So across all three which is commodity, staff, and energy and transportation, we believe that we are largely through the cost pressure or cost pain that we felt in the first quarter, and we can expect our margins to go up in the coming quarters so that we are able to maintain our EBITDA margin as compared to FY26.

items.statement: Intends to deploy majority of INR17,000 million net proceeds this fiscal year towards inorganic and organic growth.
items.quote: And lastly, with respect to our fund raise of INR17,000 million, we intend to deploy a significant majority of these net proceeds within this fiscal year, primarily towards high -quality inorganic opportunities and also towards select organic growth initiatives.

items.statement: New chassis order expected to generate annual revenue in excess of INR650 million, production starting Q4.
items.quote: The program is expected to generate annual revenue in excess of INR650 million and will be added to our existing brownfield facility in Bangalore, with start of production expected in Q4 of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Renewable energy sheet metal assemblies order to generate annual revenue in excess of INR1,500 million at peak.
items.quote: At peak volumes, the facility is expected to generate annual revenue in excess of INR1,500 million.

items.statement: Two-wheeler chassis order for Sambhajinagar facility has annual revenue potential of approximately INR500 million.
items.quote: Supplies are expected to ramp up from Quarter 4 of this fiscal year, with the program representing an annual revenue potential of approximately INR500 million.

items.statement: Cumulative order book with one OEM in two/three-wheeler space is INR1,550 million annual run rate.
items.quote: So it's a INR1,550 million cumulative order book when I say annual revenue run rate, and this is only with one OEM in the two-wheeler and three-wheeler space.

items.statement: Already at INR2,000 million run rate with this OEM including suspensions and braking wins.
items.quote: So one can say that we are already at a INR2,000 million or a n INR2 billion run rate with this particular OEM, and there's further conversations ongoing, which will continue to build on top of this.

items.statement: Back-to-back pricing model passes input cost fluctuations to customers with slight lag, no material margin impact expected.
items.quote: As we have shared before, our back-to-back pricing model means these fluctuations are largely passed to our customers with a slight lag, and we do not expect this to have a material impact on our margin profile in this fiscal year.

items.statement: Commodity cost pass-through expected in coming quarters; worst cost pressures behind.
items.quote: We do believe that the commodity costs pressure that was there in quarter one, we will get the pass -through of that in the coming quarters, which means that the commodity cost cycle f or us has largely played out.

items.statement: Two/three-wheeler business benefits from industry volume recovery and new platform launches.
items.quote: On the demand side, our two and three-wheeler business, which remains the largest contributor to revenue, continued to benefit from the industry-wide volume recovery and from new platform launches at our marquee customers.

items.statement: Four-wheeler and commercial vehicle revenues grew 18% year-on-year in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: The four-wheeler and commercial vehicle business were the fastest growing segments of our portfolio in FY26 and this momentum has continued into Q1 FY27, with revenues growing 18% year-on-year driven by new business wins across an expanding customer base.

items.statement: Aerospace and defense target to reach 10% of manufacturing revenue in short to medium term.
items.quote: Sumedh, already mentioned in the last earnings call that we want aerospace and defense to get to 10% of our manufacturing revenue in a short to medium term.

items.statement: Operating headwinds from input availability, logistics, raw material, energy, and labor costs; no material margin impact expected.
items.quote: During the quarter, we also navigated several operating headwinds, including disruptions to input availability and logistics from the global oil situation, elevated raw material and energy costs, and higher staff and labor costs following the minimum wage hike.

items.statement: Hyva India tipper business acquisition expected to complete in Q3 FY27.
items.quote: The transaction is currently progressing through the closing process and we expect to complete it during Q3 of this financial year.

items.statement: Industry price increases unsustainable due to weak demand and elevated Chinese supply; packaging costs 40% higher YoY
items.quote: Prices of several molecules remained under pressure as global supply remained elevated, particularly with continued availability of intermediates and technical products from China.

items.statement: Delayed monsoon caused delayed sowing, resowing, and cautious dealer stocking; Q1 demand shifted to subsequent quarters
items.quote: The delayed rainfall resulted in delayed sowing across several important agriculture markets. In certain regions, farmers had to reassess their crop plans or undertake resowing.

items.statement: 189 global registrations (120+ valid, 10+ under renewal); new registrations in Taiwan, Vietnam, Sri Lanka, Saudi Arabia; expanding in Africa, LatAm
items.quote: Overall, we have 189 registrations globally, of which more than 120 are valid and more than 10 are under renewal.

items.statement: El Nino declared; weak monsoon outlook for remainder of FY27; channel inventories low; raw material costs remain incrementally higher than last year
items.quote: We are not expecting very promising monsoons even in the coming days because this El Nino has already been declared.

items.statement: Two of three planned specialty products launched; new fungicide on track for Q2 launch subject to patent expiry; ICAR-IARI collaboration for heat/drought resistant products
items.quote: Two of the three speciality products planned for FY27 are already in the market, while our new fungicide remains on track for launch this quarter, subject to the relevant patent expiry.

items.statement: 50 outlets under development to open this fiscal year, with meaningful uplift over 12-18 months.
items.quote: In terms of the 50 units you're referring to, those are more outlets we're actually constructing as we speak. So, those are not even online. Those will come online say in this fiscal year, a large part of those is the plan that they will open up.

items.statement: Existing 90 units to normalize over next 12 months, benefiting H2.
items.quote: Those, some of them which were in the early part of the year are hitting the little coming to normalization or maturity levels. A large part of those happened, in the last 2 quarters and those outlets will hit normalization over the next say 12 months approximately.

items.statement: LFL growth expected 5-7% above passenger traffic.
items.quote: So, in a sense, if you see, we tend to be in that range of more than passenger traffic, somewhere in the 5% to 7% above that at least in terms of performance.

items.statement: Normalized LFL around 14-15% with passenger traffic 8-9%.
items.quote: We've traditionally been where, we're used to passenger traffic somewhere around 8% to 9% in normal years, and drive maybe 5% to 7% more of LFL growth over that to kind of reach an LFL percentage maybe around 14% -15%.

items.statement: H2 expected good bounce back in passenger traffic.
items.quote: So, the expectation is H2 of this year should be a good bounce back on passenger traffic. And I think that's also been a call -out by many independent research , what they expect passenger traffic this year in India to be, a strong H2.

items.statement: Adjusted gross profit margin around 81%, within guided range.
items.quote: Adjusting for this reclassification of INR223 million of lounge aggregation cost from other expenses to cost of sales, the adjusted gross profit stands at INR3.65 billion, translating into an adjusted gross profit margin of around 81%, which remains well within our guided range.

items.statement: Other expenses to normalize to original numbers within 12 months.
items.quote: From that perspective, we believe that we should be coming back to our original numbers what we have been traditionally showing within another 12 month odd or so.

items.statement: Maturity period 12-18 months for existing airports, 18-24 months for greenfield.
items.quote: And for a greenfield, which is a brand-new airport constructed from scratch, it goes into the 18-month to 24-month type of horizon, where you get to those normalized profit levels.

items.statement: Net contract gains 15.9% year-on-year system-wide.
items.quote: We sustained strong momentum in new outlet openings, backed by recent contract wins and a robust pipeline, which translated into net contract gains of 15.9% year -on-year at the system -wide level.

items.statement: No significant price escalation this year, tempered due to challenges.
items.quote: So, I think what has been there is that just in terms of normal, initiatives that we've done around, we still kept that delta of around 5% to 7%. So, a combination is coming, from a part of it from price, but no as much, a part of it is coming from initiatives we would do around premiumization, initiatives we would do around , big bundles together, also in some cases, in few cases, brand edits or

items.statement: Delhi T3 contract expires September 2026; JV bid results pending.
items.quote: So at this moment, Delhi T3 which is a material subsidiary, the contract is till 30th September 2026. The JV GHL has bid for the contract, but the results are not out at this moment.

items.statement: Chennai and Kolkata airports up for renewal in March 2027 and Q1 FY28.
items.quote: So, like we had clarified in earlier calls as well, there would be Chennai and Kolkata airports which would be coming at the end of March 2027 and early quarter 1 of 2027-2028 for renewal purposes.

items.statement: Debt-free balance sheet with cash of INR9.7 billion.
items.quote: As of June 30th, we maintain a debt-free balance sheet and a consolidated cash balance of approximately INR9.7 billion.

items.statement: Expanding passenger services platform to additional airports.
items.quote: In parallel, we intend to progressively expand our passenger services platform to additional airports, building o n the encouraging early response at Noida.

items.statement: Focus on Asia for international expansion, Middle East on hold.

In Q1 FY26, the EBITDA margin for Q1 FY27 was 14.6% as compared to 17.8% in Q1 FY 26. The lower margins are primarily attributable to input cost inflation, particularly in fuel and packaging materials arising from the West Asia conflict.
